author: jhosm
body:
## In plain English

We scaffolded the actual Backstage portal application so it can be built into an image and render the governed catalogue. Backstage ships no turnkey image, so this is the real app source tree a later issue turns into a container. Out of the box it renders the event (AsyncAPI) and REST (OpenAPI) catalogue entries, and it now also renders the three reconciliation contracts as syntax-highlighted YAML instead of the raw, unstyled text they used to show — the one piece of custom wiring the repo had already specified word-for-word.

## Summary

- **`backstage/`** — a stock `@backstage/create-app@0.8.4` scaffold (`--skip-install`, non-interactive). We used the **`--legacy`** template deliberately: create-app's current default is the new *declarative frontend system*, which has no `apis.tsx` / `apiDocsConfigRef` seam, whereas the reconciliation-widget code the repo specified (verbatim in `infra/backstage/app-config.yaml`'s handoff block) is written for the **classic frontend system**. `--legacy` gives exactly that `packages/app/src/apis.ts` seam while still using the new **backend** system and bundling `@backstage/plugin-api-docs` (which natively renders `asyncapi`/`openapi`/`graphql`). Minimal scaffold — no extra auth providers, plugins, TechDocs, scaffolder templates, or CI beyond what create-app ships.
- **`packages/app/src/apis.tsx`** — carries the specified `createApiFactory` on `apiDocsConfigRef` **verbatim**: `spec.type: reconciliation` → a `PlainApiDefinitionWidget` with `language: 'yaml'`; every other type delegates to `defaultDefinitionWidgets()`. Renamed from the scaffolded `apis.ts` to `.tsx` because the factory returns JSX. The legacy template already renders `EntityApiDefinitionCard` (which consumes `apiDocsConfigRef`) on API entity pages, so the widget is actually consumed. This discharges the widget wiring of the **closed** handoff `babelstone-ax0b.6`.
- **`app-config.babelstone-dev.yaml`** — a clearly-labelled **DEV-ONLY** overlay pointing a single catalogue `Location` at the repo's real `contracts/catalog/catalog-info.yaml`, to prove ingestion locally. It does **not** fork or weaken the governed `infra/backstage/app-config.yaml` (left untouched) and restates no schema.
- Committed the fully-resolved `yarn.lock` (the lockfile the image build needs) and kept the `mise.toml` `node = "22"` pin (Backstage rejects the system Node 26).
- **Out of scope** (separate issues): the image Dockerfile (`zla1.6.3`), the image-build CI leg (`.6.4`), DB/secret wiring (`.6.5`/`.6.6`), and the live deploy (`.6.7`).

## Testing

All via `mise exec -- corepack yarn` (Node 22 through the worktree's mise pin; a writable `YARN_GLOBAL_FOLDER` to sidestep root-owned home caches):

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `yarn install` | **PASS** (exit 0; ~1.06 GiB, peer-dep warnings only) |
| `yarn tsc` | **PASS** (exit 0 — `apis.tsx` compiles with the reconciliation widget) |
| `yarn build:backend` | **PASS** (exit 0 — app + backend bundled into `dist`; bundle includes the `react-syntax-highlighter` yaml language the widget uses) |

## ADRs touched/honoured

- **ADR-IC-015** (Backstage as the catalogue portal; the §1–§2 **no-drift invariant**) — *honoured*. The app restates **no** schema: the governed production config remains the single source (`infra/backstage/app-config.yaml`, baked as `app-config.production.yaml` by the image build with `/catalog/catalog-info.yaml` as its only Location); the dev overlay mirrors that single-Location posture against the repo tree without forking it. No ADR is amended or superseded.

## bd issues closed on merge

- Closes babelstone-zla1.6.2

(Also discharges the widget wiring recorded in the already-closed handoff `babelstone-ax0b.6`; only `zla1.6.2` is closed by this PR.)

## Summary
- Fixes a mobile-only bug where the whole page appeared shifted/offset left on narrow viewports (e.g. iPhone 15, 393px width)
- Root cause #1: `html` was missing `overflow-x: hidden` (only `body` had it), so when the 3D skills globe rendered DOM icons slightly wider than the viewport, the browser expanded the entire layout viewport instead of clipping — shifting every fixed-position element (theme toggle, mobile section nav) off-screen
- Root cause #2: `.git-commit` is a CSS Grid item inside `.experience-timeline`; grid items default to `min-width: auto` (their min-content size), so a `white-space: nowrap` company name inside `.commit-company` forced the experience-timeline cards wider than their container instead of ellipsis-truncating, on mobile

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced with Playwright at 393×852 (iPhone 15 viewport) against the local dev server; confirmed `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` (449px) exceeded `clientWidth` (393px) and the fixed theme toggle rendered off-screen
- [x] Applied fix, re-ran the same script: `scrollWidth === clientWidth === 393`, theme toggle and mobile nav render in the correct position
- [x] Verified visually via screenshots across hero, skills, and experience sections — content centered, no offset, experience timeline company name truncates with ellipsis instead of overflowing

author: ajhpaynav
body:
## What & why

Docs-only 0.1.2. Answers the recurring question **"can I use this with my PSP?"** by showing, concretely, how to feed the engine from a real processor's response. **No engine or rule-table changes.**

### Added
- **`docs/processors.md`** — the processor-mapping guide.
  - Leads with the core principle and the one gotcha: the engine takes the **raw Visa/Mastercard network code**, *not* your gateway's abstracted decline status.
  - **Full field-by-field mapping for Worldpay Express** (Element Express), sourced from the **Express Interface Specification v3**: `HostResponseCode` → `declineCode`, `MerchantAdviceCode` → `merchantAdviceCode`, `CardLogo` → `network`, `PaymentType`/`SubmissionType` → `context`/`mitSubtype`. Includes the MAC value table (which values the engine recognizes vs. `22/40/41` that fall back to the raw code) and the `PaymentType` enum table.
  - General recipe + a pointer table for Stripe / Adyen / Braintree / Checkout.com (where the raw network code and MAC live).
- **`examples/`** — runnable walkthroughs against Worldpay Express:
  - `worldpay-express-mapping.ts` — reusable helper (`toReattemptInput`, `isExpressDecline`, `networkFromCardLogo`, `contextFromPaymentType`).
  - `worldpay-express-cit.ts` — checkout: allow-retry vs sanitized `customerMessage`, plus the velocity stop.
  - `worldpay-express-mit.ts` — dunning: retry delays (MAC 25), account-updater (MAC 01), permanent stop + decline fee (MAC 21), dead card.
  - `examples/README.md`.
- README "Using it with your PSP" section linking the above; bump to `0.1.2`; docs-only CHANGELOG entry.

## Verification
- Both examples **run** with correct engine output (transpiled via esbuild against the built `dist`) and **typecheck** cleanly (the only `tsc` gripe was `console` needing `@types/node`; the `@paynav/reattempt` self-reference and all engine types resolved).
- `npm run typecheck` clean · **94/94 tests pass** · `npm run build` succeeds.

## Reviewer notes
- Worldpay Express fields were verified against the linked primary spec (Appendix 1 "Response Codes", `PaymentType`, `CardLogo`). The other-processor pointer table is framed as **"verify against your processor's docs — starting points, not guarantees"**, since only Worldpay was verified from source this pass.
- `package.json` `files` stays `["dist"]`, so `docs/` and `examples/` live on GitHub and stay out of the npm tarball. README relative links still resolve on the npm page. Easy to flip if we'd rather ship examples.

author: alexschrader
body:
Two pure-render Ladder improvements from the backlog, kept together (same file, cohesive UX).

## 1. Lessons expand to preview their items
Each lesson row in a unit now expands to show its item list — the words/kana it teaches, learned ones lit, the rest dimmed — so a learner can see what a lesson covers before diving in. (`UnitRow` already showed lesson title + `canDo`; this adds the missing item list via a new `LessonPreview`.)

## 2. Collapsible stage sub-sections
The Units list already grouped by CEFR stage; now each stage group **collapses independently**. Only your **active stage** opens by default (or the last real stage if the whole track is done) — completed/future stages collapse to a one-line summary, so the Units tab isn't one long wall as it grows toward A2. Row numbering is assigned up front so it stays continuous regardless of which stages are open.

Both are pure presentation — no engine/schema/mastery change; read `rung` you already track.

## Gate
`validate` (21) · 78 unit tests · build · smoke dev + preview (Ladder render exercised: unit expands → lesson expands → item shows; word bank; tab nav).

author: ugurcanyagiz
body:
### Motivation
- Replace the original node-driven interactive atlas with a simpler, scroll-driven cinematic homepage to present curated phases of the atlas as scenes.  
- Move away from complex submenu/focus panel interactions and orbital particle system toward a performant starfield and camera-driven visual that responds to page scroll.  
- Simplify navigation surface while preserving top items from `atlasData` for quick entry points.

### Description
- Reworked `src/components/ScrollCinemaHome.astro` to replace the `.atlas` markup and behavior with a new `.cinema-atlas` structure, new phase content, a simplified nav (`navItems`) and a scroll-space driven UI.  
- Replaced per-node focus panel, submenus and many node-related DOM structures with a series of `phases` rendered in the DOM and a compact HUD/progress indicator, while still deriving `navItems` from `atlasData`.  
- Replaced the old canvas particle/orbital rendering and large interaction state machine with a new canvas/starfield renderer and a `render` loop that lerps a single `progress` value from page scroll into scene/camera CSS custom properties.  
- Updated event wiring to use `data-cinema-atlas` root, `scroll`/`resize` handlers, reduced-motion support, and removed many click/touch handlers tied to the old node/menu UX.  
- Comprehensive CSS rewrite to support the cinematic layout, new variables (e.g. `--scroll-progress`, `--accent-r/g/b`, `--camera-x`), responsive sizing, and reduced-motion fallbacks.

### Testing
- Manual previewed the component locally in the dev server to verify scroll-driven phase transitions, canvas starfield rendering, and responsive layout across breakpoints (no regressions found).  
- No unit tests or automated CI tests were modified or added as part of this change and no automated test run was triggered by this rollout.  
- Verified `prefers-reduced-motion` handling paths are present and that `reduce` media changes are observed by the new measurement loop during manual testing.

author: lemonforest
body:
## rc172 = orchestration→C spine, batch 2 — catalog registry/kernel-state/audit in C

The chain-runner's foundation. 6 of the 8 `amsc.catalog` owed_orchestration rows earn a C path:
- **4 dedicated C peers**: `list_registered_roots`, `get_local_kernel_state`, `use_local_kernel` (+ `clear_local_kernel` via `use_local_kernel(None)`), `attestation_audit`
- **1 thin composes_c** (no new symbol): `list_attested_sources` (compose over the descriptor parse + pure filter/sort/project — consistent with the already-composes_c `get_attested_dataset`/`get_attested_descriptor`)
- **2 deferred** (stay owed): `run_catalog_chain` + `list_catalog_chains` — they compose the `amsc.compose` chain-runner, not yet in C (rc173–175); left owed with a dated note, no stub

**C design (a) — caller-owned state**: stateless arena-backed logic peers, no global mutable C state, no long-lived handle. The host owns the registry/kernel state and passes it per call (mirrors rc171's stateless-peer pattern; byte-parity trivial to prove). The peers compose `srmech_json` (parser/canonical-writer/builder) + `srmech_sha256_hex` (the kernel cache_hash) — no new parser, no new hash. 8 new symbols (4 peers + 4 arena sizers); ABI stays 3.

**Bug caught+fixed**: the final writer-arena region was carved `end - cur` but `cat_carve` re-aligns first → unaligned intermediate sizes overflowed it (`attestation_audit` hit it; the other 3 passed on lucky even sizes). Fixed to align-then-take-remainder across all four peers.

### Verified (own build, both modes)
native==pure across register/list/lookup/kernel/audit (15 tests, incl. attestation_audit over every real attested source); consumers byte-identical (register_attested_root, tool_schema_coverage, genome register, format, descriptor). Ledger: owed_orchestration 15→9, composes_c 70→76, sum 114; `CEIL_NON_COMPUTE_OWED` 9 tight; transitive-reachability assert covers the 6 new composes_c. tools 403; ABI 3; version rc172; numpy-absent; no abs/libm; both C modes `-Werror -Wpedantic` clean; JPL green.

author: jonathandieu
body:
Registers the stage workload cluster with ArgoCD entirely through git + ExternalSecrets — no `argocd` CLI, no admin bearer token. See terraform ADR 0003 for the full design.

- `charts/platform/cluster-registrations`: one ExternalSecret per registered cluster, pulling a precomputed ArgoCD cluster-secret config blob (bearerToken + CA) from the 1Password item terraform creates alongside each cluster's dedicated `argocd-manager` ServiceAccount.
- Wires `cluster-registrations` into the existing `platform` appset rather than adding a new one.
- Tightens the `platform` appset's cluster selector to also require `argocd-active: "true"`, so a future second platform peer (failover) isn't treated as also-active. The live platform cluster's self-registration secret already has this label (applied via terraform).

Once this syncs, `dieubernetes-stage-do-atl1` should appear as a registered cluster in the ArgoCD UI, and the existing `workloads` appset (`purpose in [prod, stage]`, unchanged) should start generating Applications for mealie/plausible/changedetection on stage.

author: jesusroyeth
body:
Running `Heatmap` or `ObjectBlurrer` with an OBB model crashes on the first frame that has tracks:

```python
import cv2
from ultralytics import solutions

im0 = cv2.imread("boats.jpg")  # https://ultralytics.com/images/boats.jpg
solutions.Heatmap(model="yolo11n-obb.pt", show=False)(im0)
```

```
File "ultralytics/solutions/heatmap.py", line 59, in heatmap_effect
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = map(int, box)
ValueError: only one element tensors can be converted to Python scalars
```

`ObjectBlurrer` fails the same way at `object_blurrer.py:76` (`int(box[1])`). The same code with a detection model works fine, and the object counting guide shows OBB models for solutions (`model="yolo26n-obb.pt"`), so a user following the docs hits this directly.

Resolves #25057

**Root cause**

`BaseSolution.extract_tracks` (`solutions.py:175`) supports OBB explicitly: for OBB models it fills `self.boxes` with `xyxyxyxy`, a (4, 2) tensor of corner points per box, instead of the 4-scalar `xyxy` of detection models. `BaseSolution` already handles both shapes in two places — `store_tracking_history` (`solutions.py:199`) computes the centre with `box.mean(dim=0) if box.numel() > 4 else ...`, and `box_label` draws the rotated polygon for (4, 2) input. That is why `ObjectCounter` works with OBB models. But several solutions consume `self.boxes` assuming 4 scalars (`map(int, box)`, `int(box[1])`, `(box[0] + box[2]) / 2`), and calling `int()` on a 2-element row tensor raises the error above.

Following the "scan for other occurrences" pattern from #21816, I checked every solution that consumes `self.boxes` and ran each one with an OBB model in order to confirm which ones break. Six are affected — five crash on the first frame with tracks, one is latent:

| Solution | Crash site | Error on main |
|---|---|---|
| `Heatmap` | `heatmap.py:59` | `ValueError: only one element tensors can be converted to Python scalars` |
| `ObjectBlurrer` | `object_blurrer.py:76` | same `ValueError` |
| `RegionCounter` | `region_counter.py:117` | `ValueError: Point() takes only scalar or 1-size vector arguments` |
| `VisionEye` | `solutions.py:712` (`visioneye`) | same `ValueError` as Heatmap |
| `ParkingManagement` | `parking_management.py:250` | same `ValueError` as Heatmap |
| `DistanceCalculation` | `distance_calculation.py:62,108` | latent (mouse callback): `RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor ... is ambiguous` |

Not affected (verified with the same OBB model): `ObjectCounter`, `TrackZone`, `QueueManager`, `SpeedEstimator`, `SecurityAlarm`, `Analytics`. They only touch the boxes through `box_label` and `store_tracking_history`, which already handle the (4, 2) shape. `ObjectCropper` also fails with OBB models, but for a different reason — it runs its own `predict` and reads `results.boxes`, which is `None` for OBB. That is a separate bug with a separate cause, so I kept it out of this PR.

**Fix**

A small static helper in `BaseSolution`, `get_enclosing_box`, that returns the axis-aligned enclosing box `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` (min/max of the 4 corners) when the input is a (4, 2) OBB box, and returns the input untouched otherwise — same `numel() > 4` gate that `store_tracking_history` already uses. Each affected consumer derives a local xyxy from it and keeps passing the original box to `box_label`, so the rotated OBB polygon is still drawn.

Why this approach and not the alternatives:

- Converting inside `extract_tracks` would break the paths that need the (4, 2): `store_tracking_history` needs the corners for the centre and `box_label` needs them for the polygon.
- Repeating the min/max guard in six places would work, but the helper keeps a single source of truth, and `BaseSolution` already owns the OBB normalisation (`extract_tracks`, `store_tracking_history`).
- The centre of the enclosing box is exactly `box.mean(dim=0)` (verified on real boxes, max diff 0.0), so the centre-based consumers (`RegionCounter`, `ParkingManagement`, `VisionEye`, `DistanceCalculation`) stay consistent with the centre `ObjectCounter` already computes for OBB.

There is one behaviour change to mention: in `Heatmap` and `ObjectBlurrer` the enclosing box is also clipped to image bounds. This is needed for OBB and a no-op for detection. Detection `xyxy` is already clipped to the frame in post-processing (`ops.scale_boxes` → `clip_boxes`), so `max(x, 0)`/`min(x, w)` never changes it. OBB `xyxyxyxy` corners are not clipped, and tracked corners can end up outside the frame (on boats.jpg they reach x=2007.7 on a 1920-wide frame, and y spans -94.2 to 1151 on 1080; 18 of 169 enclosing boxes are out of bounds). Without the clip `Heatmap` raises `IndexError` on the heatmap array (boolean-mask/slice shape mismatch) and `ObjectBlurrer` hits a `cv2` `!_src.empty()` assertion on the empty crop — both reproduced on boats.jpg. So the clip only changes the OBB path, which is the path this PR fixes.

**Tests**

The reason CI never caught this is simple: `tests/test_solutions.py` exercises these solutions only with a detection model. The single OBB case, `ObjectCounterwithOBB`, covers exactly one of the OBB-safe classes — and on `demo_video` the tracker returns zero OBB tracks, so even that one was not exercising the OBB path. Changes:

- A focused regression test `test_solution_obb_boxes`, parametrized over the five affected solutions that consume `self.boxes` (`Heatmap`, `ObjectBlurrer`, `VisionEye`, `RegionCounter`, `ParkingManagement`). Each processes a **single** `parking_video` frame with `yolo26n-obb.pt` and asserts a `plot_im` is returned. The first frame already yields OBB tracks (37 boxes), so one frame is enough to hit each crash site, there is no need to run the whole 82-frame clip. It reuses `parking_video`, `parking_areas` and the `yolo26n-obb.pt` already in the matrix, so no new CI assets.
- `test_left_click_selection_obb` for the latent `DistanceCalculation` path — the mouse callback is hard to drive end-to-end, so it exercises the selection with a (4, 2) box directly.
- `ObjectCounterwithOBB` moved from `demo_video` to `parking_video` so it actually gets OBB tracks (inline comment included) — it stays as the control showing `ObjectCounter` already handles the shape.

**Validation**

RTX 4060, main @ fcb350d (8.4.90):

- On clean main the six solutions fail with the exact errors in the table above (re-verified with a stash/restore cycle); with the fix all of them run clean on OBB input, and 4 detection-model controls give the same output as before.
- OBB test subset (`-k "OBB or obb"`): 7 passed — five single-frame `test_solution_obb_boxes` regressions (~0.08s each), the `DistanceCalculation` unit test, and the moved `ObjectCounterwithOBB` control.
- Full `tests/test_solutions.py`: 40 passed, 1 skipped. `ObjectCounter` with OBB unchanged, and for detection boxes the helper is a passthrough that returns the same object, no copy.
- `ruff format --check` and `ruff check`: clean.

I realise the diff touches 8 files for what started as a Heatmap report, but the six failures share the same root cause, and fixing only two of them would leave the same crash waiting in the other four ..

## 🛠️ PR Summary

<sub>Made with ❤️ by [Ultralytics Actions](https://www.ultralytics.com/actions)</sub>

### 🌟 Summary
Fixes crashes in multiple Ultralytics Solutions when using YOLO26 OBB models by normalizing oriented boxes to enclosing axis-aligned boxes. 🧰

### 📊 Key Changes
- Adds a shared `get_enclosing_box()` helper to handle both standard `[x1, y1, x2, y2]` boxes and OBB corner-point boxes.
- Updates `DistanceCalculation`, `Heatmap`, `ObjectBlurrer`, `ParkingManagement`, `RegionCounter`, and `VisionEye` to safely consume OBB outputs.
- Clips heatmap and blur regions to image bounds to avoid slicing/indexing issues with rotated boxes.
- Adds regression tests for OBB left-click selection and OBB compatibility across affected Solutions using `yolo26n-obb.pt`.

### 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Prevents crashes when users run Solutions with OBB models, improv

author: slawomir-it
body:
## Summary

Makes every Speedwave integration work reliably on any model provider, including small local LLMs. Driven by a full audit of all 233 worker tools, 13 integration skills, the hub, and the shared contracts (3 audit waves + adversarial verification + max-effort code review).

### Local-LLM session support (runtime)
- Local-provider sessions get `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` (stable prompt prefix, KV-cache reuse across restarts) and a skills-recall `--append-system-prompt` nudge (`prompts::local_llm_skills_nudge`, static text, no injection surface). Anthropic/OpenRouter sessions unchanged; prompt replacement stays banned.
- Desktop: tool-input parse warnings suppressed while streaming deltas accumulate (log spam fix).

### Identity-first contract (`_meta` + hub)
- New MCP-spec-compliant prefixed `_meta` keys (`speedwave.pl/...`, SSOT in mcp-shared `META_KEYS`) declare user-scoped tools, their current-user tool, and self-reference params; the hub renders one canonical identity sentence into served descriptions and boosts user-scoped tools for self-reference queries. Legacy unprefixed keys keep working (prefixed-first fallback), so third-party plugins are unaffected.
- New whoami tools: `gitlab.getCurrentUser`, `github.getCurrentUser`, `slack.getCurrentUser` (auth.test); redmine `listTimeEntries` accepts `user_id: 'me'`; gitlab lists gained `scope=assigned_to_me/created_by_me`.

### Teaching errors and no silent failures
- Shared contract in mcp-shared: `teachingErrorResult` (content-block envelope), `teachingToolResult` (Family-A envelope), `clampPageSize` (NaN-safe pagination). Errors name the bad param, the tool that provides a correct value, and the next step.
- Hub search rewritten: tokenized ranked matching (natural-language queries now match), teaching hint on zero results, did-you-mean suggestions for unknown tools, lowered-string caching on the hot path.
- Silent-wrong-result fixes across workers, e.g.: github binary file corruption in `getFileContents` (lossless base64 path), sharepoint permanent wedge after a failed siteId warmup (retry + unwedge), Apple Mail/Outlook `sendEmail` with empty `to` or dropped `bcc`, quote-aware recipient splitting, atlassian `moveIssuesToSprint` silent truncation, office `replace_text` no-op and ignored non-zero exit codes, redmine silently dropped `assigned_to`.

### Skills and docs

body:
**Pixee Scan:** [314dba0f-94bc-48b4-809b-acc05872b28f](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/314dba0f-94bc-48b4-809b-acc05872b28f?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/314dba0f-94bc-48b4-809b-acc05872b28f?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in introduction/views.py ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in `introduction/views.py`. ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application builds an operating-system command string from untrusted input and then executes it through a shell. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters or additional arguments to run arbitrary commands with the application's privileges. This can lead to data theft, unauthorized system changes, or full host compromise. ## Changes Made The `cmd_lab` view in `introduction/views.py` previously interpolated the user-supplied `domain` directly into `nslookup` or `dig` command strings and executed them with `subprocess.Popen(..., shell=True, ...)`, which made the endpoint vulnerable to command injection. The fix removed shell-based command construction and passed the command and domain as discrete arguments to `subprocess.Popen`, which prevents shell interpretation of injected characters. The code also normalized the submitted domain, added strict validation for either an IP address or a hostname matching an allowlist-style regular expression, and returned `Invalid domain` when validation fails. The import of `ipaddress` supports the new input validation path. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the remediation notes: - **Prevent command injection by sanitizing/validating user input**: the patch normalizes `domain`, strips whitespace and trailing dots, and rejects non-hostname/non-IP values using `ipaddress.ip_address(...)` plus a `re.fullmatch(...)` hostname check before any subprocess call. This directly implements the guidance to ensure user-controlled data does not contain malicious commands. - **Do not construct the OS command from user-controlled data**: the patch replaces string interpolation plus `shell=True` with argument arrays (`["nslookup", validation_domain]` / `["dig", validation_domain]`) so the command is executed without shell parsing, which is the correct remediation pattern for `pythonsecurity:S2076`. - **Use input validation as the primary safeguard**: by returning `"Invalid domain"` on failed validation, the change prevents unsafe values from reaching command execution, matching the guidance’s emphasis on validation before command invocation. - **No new external dependency required**: `ipaddress` is part of the Python standard library, so there was no manifest update needed; the fix does not introduce a dependency-management concern. Overall, the patch aligns with the security guidance and appropriately mitigates command injection in the shown flow.

author: ryanseys
body:
`f(**{ ... })` — double-splatting a hash literal at a call site — emitted broken C: `error: unexpected type name 'sp_SymPolyHash': expected expression`.

The call-site double-splat pre-evaluates the spread hash to a temp. A bare variable emits with no prelude, but a hash literal drains its own construction into the prelude buffer, which landed *inside* the temp's declaration line (`sp_SymPolyHash * _t = sp_SymPolyHash *_t2 = ...`).

The fix renders the source into a side buffer first, so a literal's construction lands before the assignment line — a no-op for a bare variable.

Covered by `test/kwsplat_literal.rb` (ruby-oracle): a literal into a keyword-rest param, into explicit keyword params, a literal plus a trailing key, all-supplied keywords, and string-valued kwargs.

author: ghostdogpr
body:
## Problem

`FloatValue.fromStringUnsafe` relied on `s.toDouble` throwing to trigger its BigDecimal fallback:

```scala
try DoubleNumber(s.toDouble)
catch { case NonFatal(_) => BigDecimalNumber(BigDecimal(s)) }
```

But `Double.parseDouble` (behind `String.toDouble`) does **not** throw on out-of-range magnitudes — it silently **overflows to `Infinity`** and **underflows to `0.0`**. So the fallback only ever fired on malformed input, and a parseable-but-out-of-range literal lost its value:

- `1e400` → `DoubleNumber(Infinity)` — renders as the invalid token `Infinity` and throws `NumberFormatException` from `toBigDecimal`.
- `1e-400` → `DoubleNumber(0.0)` — silently collapsed to zero, so e.g. a `BigDecimal` argument receives `0` instead of `1e-400`.

`fromStringUnsafe` is on the query-parsing hot path (every float literal goes through it), so this is reachable from any client-supplied float literal.

## Fix

Take the fast path only for finite, non-zero doubles; otherwise reparse with `BigDecimal` and keep it whenever the literal is actually non-zero (preserving genuine `0` as a `Double`):

```scala
val double = s.toDouble
if (double != 0.0 && !double.isInfinity) DoubleNumber(double)
else {
  val bd = BigDecimal(s)
  if (bd.signum == 0) DoubleNumber(double) else BigDecimalNumber(bd)
}
```

## Tests

Added a `FloatValue.fromStringUnsafe` suite in `ValueSpec`: `1e400` and `1e-400` are preserved as `BigDecimalNumber` (with matching `toBigDecimal`, and no `Infinity`), in-range values stay `DoubleNumber`, and a genuine `0.0` stays `DoubleNumber`.

`core/testOnly caliban.ValueSpec` passes (7 tests).

author: bdfinst
body:
## Summary

Investigated GitHub issue #974 — a 900s single-file `/code-review` timeout in `evals/code-review-benchmark/` on `defects4j-Lang-23`/`defects4j-Lang-56` — via a live dispatch experiment rather than guessing at a cause.

**Root cause (confirmed, not hypothesized):** `/code-review`'s `SKILL.md` step 3 dispatches its full ~14-agent review roster regardless of file count — the harness's `fix-only` scope narrows which *files* are reviewed, not how many *agents* run. Every dispatched agent gets the complete file content (step 4). I confirmed this live: a trivial 15-line single-file review (via `runner.py`'s own `isolated_dispatch.py`/`copy_auth_state()` machinery, no shortcuts, real Claude Code OAuth dispatch) still cost **28 turns, 1.28M input tokens, $1.29, 234s**. A real Defects4J case sampled independently the same session (`defects4j-Lang-29`) measured even higher: **58 turns, 846s cumulative nested-call API time (vs. 368s wall clock), $4.48**. Neither hit 900s at the concurrency each happened to run under, but the numbers make clear that Lang-23's (536-line) and Lang-56's (1744-line) real ground-truth files, reviewed by the same full roster under the harness's original `--workers 4`, can plausibly exceed 900s without any hang — the aggregation step itself (`SKILL.md` step 5) is deterministic parsing with no LLM call, ruled out as a hang source.

**Fix:** raise `cli.py`'s `--timeout` default 900→1800 and lower `--workers` default 4→2 to reflect this now-measured real cost, and document the finding in code/README so it isn't rediscovered blind. Deliberately does **not** touch `/code-review`'s agent roster or `SKILL.md` — trimming the roster to "fix" the timeout would change what the benchmark measures.

## Quality Gate
- [x] New unit tests (`tests/scripts/test_code_review_benchmark_cli.py`) pin the new defaults + confirm overrides still work, via a new `cli._build_parser()` extraction
- [x] Full plugin test suite: 2999 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing, documented opt-in skip unrelated to this change)
- [x] `scripts/citation_lint.py`, `scripts/check_registry_sync.py`, `scripts/check-python-only.py`, `scripts/check_md_references.py` — clean
- [x] `scripts/ci-local.sh` (full local CI mirror) — all checks passed
- [x] Plan reviewed by Acceptance Test Critic + Design & Architecture Critic before implementation (both approved with fixes folded in); `doc-review` + `arch-review` dispatched against the final diff (doc-review found and I fixed two real issues — a markdown-heading-breaking line wrap and a stale `--workers 4` usage example; arch-review passed with two non-blocking suggestions, already noted as deferred follow-ups below)

## Decisions & Assumptions

- **This is a benchmark-harness-only change.** No production `/code-review` behavior changed — the roster fan-out this investigation found is real, intended production behavior; the harness's defaults were simply undercounting its real cost.
- **Not reproducing Lang-23/Lang-56 in full isolation** against a live `--workers 1` Defects4J run — the two live experiments run this session (a deliberately trivial single-file case, plus an independently-running real sweep's `Lang-29` case landing mid-investigation) already gave a confident, evidence-backed root cause without needing that heavier infra investment.
- **A new, separate finding surfaced during this investigation, explicitly out of scope for this PR:** the concurrently-running live sweep's `Lang-29` case reproduced issue #967's finding #1 (a completion claiming JSON was emitted with none present in the final text) — after PR #975 was merged specifically to fix that pattern. This suggests #975's fix isn't fully holding and deserves its own follow-up issue/investigation; not folded into this PR since #974 is specifically about the empty-stdout timeout, not the narration-instead-of-emission pattern.
- **Two non-blocking suggestions from arch-review, deferred rather than addressed here:** (1) `cli.py`'s and `runner.py`'s timeout/workers defaults are two independently-maintained literals rather than a single shared constant (the file already has this same pattern for `--model`'s default, so it's consistent with existing local convention, not a new inconsistency); (2) no total-sweep cost budget/warning exists despite now-measured $1.29–$4.48/case real costs — worth a future `--max-cost-usd`-style guardrail.

## Test Plan
- [x] `pytest tests/scripts/test_code_review_benchmark_cli.py tests/scripts/test_code_review_benchmark_runner.py` — 27 passed
- [x] `pytest plugins/dev-team/tests tests/repo tests/agents tests/commands tests/docs tests/knowledge tests/bats tests/skills tests/scripts` (excluding the two known C# subprocess-heavy exclusions) — 2999 passed, 1 skipped
- [x] `scripts/ci-local.sh` — all local CI checks passed

## Evidence Bundle
**Checks run**
- Full test suite (see above)
- `doc-review`, `arch-review` dispatched directly against the diff — both pass after two doc-review findings were fixed (README markdown-heading line wrap, stale `--workers 4` usage example)
- Two live, real `/code-review` dispatches used as investigation evidence (not simulated): a controlled trivial single-file case, and an independently-running real Defects4J sweep's `Lang-29` case

**Scope notes**
- No `/code-review` skill/agent/roster files changed — this diff is entirely benchmark-harness config + docs + a new unit test

**Untested regions**
- The new `--timeout`/`--workers` defaults are not re-verified against a live Defects4J sweep in this PR (would require the same heavy infra this investigation deliberately avoided provisioning) — the values are evidence-based, not re-confirmed empirically at scale

**Residual risks**
- A future sweep could still occasionally exceed even 1800s for an unusually large/complex file under real concurrency — this is a headroom increase grounded in measured evidence, not a guarantee. The two arch-review-flagged follow-ups (shared-constant refactor, cost-budget guardrail) and the newly-discovered #967-finding-#1 recurrence are known, tracked residual items for separate follow-up, not silently dropped.

Closes #974

body:
💡 **What:** 
Updated `SmartOilGaugeDataUpdateCoordinator` to store tank data as a dictionary keyed by `tank_id` rather than a list of dictionaries. This allows `SmartOilGaugeEntity._get_tank_data()` to retrieve the tank's specific data using an O(1) `dict.get()` lookup instead of an O(N) list iteration.

🎯 **Why:** 
Previously, every time an entity's state was read (e.g. `native_value`), `_get_tank_data` iterated over the entire list of tanks returned by the coordinator to find the matching `tank_id`. By converting the coordinator's stored data to a dictionary, we eliminate this redundant list iteration, reducing CPU overhead during state updates, especially for users with multiple tanks.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
I measured the performance of finding an item in a list vs. looking it up in a dictionary for different sizes of `coordinator.data`. The list iteration used the worst-case scenario (finding the last item).

| Items      | List (s)        | Dict (s)        | Improvement    |
|------------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| 1          | 0.11425         | 0.00416         | 27.44x faster  |
| 5          | 0.15472         | 0.00411         | 37.63x faster  |
| 10         | 0.20017         | 0.00418         | 47.95x faster  |
| 50         | 0.55163         | 0.00405         | 136.18x faster |
| 100        | 0.99397         | 0.00440         | 226.15x faster |

*(Measured over 100,000 iterations).* 
Even for a single tank, the O(1) dictionary lookup is significantly faster.

Also fixed a minor ruff typing error in `pyproject.toml` targeting `py314` instead of `py312`.

Cadastro de profissional com acesso ao sistema, disponibilidade e ajuste de permissões por perfil (critérios de aceite #1–#5, #31).

## App
- **createProfessionalWithAccess** (admin client): cria o acesso no Supabase Auth (e-mail + senha) → `profiles` (via trigger) → `memberships` (papel `professional`) → `professionals` → serviços que realiza → disponibilidade padrão → regra de pagamento (comissão/salário). Exclusivo do dono.
- **Novo formulário de profissional**: nome, e-mail, senha inicial, telefone, comissão (%), salário, serviços (checkboxes) e disponível/indisponível.
- **Disponibilidade** (`public_visible`) com toggle para dono, gerente e secretária. Profissional indisponível não aparece no agendamento público (já filtrado na `get_public_barbershop` e revalidado na RPC `create_public_appointment`).
- **Permissões**: `professional` passa a ter `appointments:manage`, mas a RLS o restringe aos próprios atendimentos (`is_own_professional`) — vê e gerencia só a própria agenda. O filtro por profissional na Agenda só aparece para quem enxerga a equipe toda.

## Banco (migration aplicada no Supabase)
- `employee_pay_settings.commission_rate` (regra de pagamento por profissional).
- Política RLS: secretária pode alterar a disponibilidade do profissional.

## Observação de configuração
- O cadastro com login usa `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (admin client). Ela precisa estar configurada no ambiente da Vercel para o fluxo funcionar em produção.

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` e `npm test` (10 testes) verdes. Advisor de segurança sem pendências novas.

💡 What: Refactored the `publishOptimistic`, `revertOptimistic`, and `connectSseHub` event listeners in the Silcrow JS runtime (`silcrow/src/silcrow.js`) to consolidate redundant DOM scans.
🎯 Why: Previously, optimistic mutation handlers iterated through every key in a payload dictionary, performing a separate `querySelectorAll` pass for each key. This caused unnecessary DOM traversal overhead that scaled O(N) with the payload size during high-frequency mutations.
📊 Impact: Consolidates sequential queries into a single DOM pass. Reduces redundant queries and layout recalculations, providing a smoother, lower-latency optimistic update loop.

## C-2 · Per-tenant chat-auth for Callisthenes (EPIC-2.4 Move 0)

Owns `units/callisthenes/auth/` only. Implements the console-less chat-auth pattern via **OAuth 1.0a PIN (`oauth_callback=oob`)** — CD-3 DECIDED (X has no device-code; PIN is the only "visit x.com, paste the PIN" path).

### Deliverables
- `__init__.py` — `ChatAuth` engine + `register(mcp)` shared contract (`from auth import register as register_auth; register_auth(mcp)`). Supports FastMCP `@mcp.tool(name=)`, `add_tool(fn, name=)`, and a plain-registry fallback when `mcp` is None.
- `oauth1_pin.py` — OAuth1.0a oob request_token → canonical authorize URL → access_token exchange; HMAC-SHA1 signing (stdlib, mirrors upstream xmcp); HTTP behind an injectable `HttpClient` seam.
- `token_store.py` — per-tenant storage keyed by `sha256(mcp_token)`; `SqliteTokenStore` (default, under `CALLISTHENES_DATA_DIR`) + `InMemoryTokenStore`.
- `test_chat_auth.py` + `test_token_store.py` — 31 tests, X HTTP mocked, no network/creds.
- `README.md` — surface + security invariants + **OPEN SEAM**.

### Tools
`connect(service="x")` · `complete_connect(pin, service="x")` · `connections()` · `revoke(service|token)` · `usage()`

### Security (BINDING)
- Canonical x.com URLs only — `_assert_canonical()` refuses non-`x.com/twitter.com` hosts.
- Per-tenant isolation — tokens keyed by hashed MCP token; cross-tenant reads impossible (proven in tests).
- No secret in any result or log — package has zero print/log statements.
- Loud structured `{code, message}` errors (SEAM-SPEC §5 codes).

```
31 passed in 0.08s
```

(`python -m pytest` in `units/callisthenes/auth/`, all X HTTP mocked.)

`usage()` — live per-tenant ledger (`/data/usage.sqlite`, C-4-owned) is not reachable in-unit. Interface is fixed + pluggable: inject `usage_reader(mcp_token) -> {calls, sends, cost_usd}`. Without it, `usage()` returns an explicit `{source: "unavailable", usage: {calls: null, sends: null, cost_usd: null}}` — nulls, not faked zeros. Hand-back documented in README `## OPEN SEAM`.

author: softwaremill-ci
jeremydmiller
body:
Now that the E3 Weasel 9.16 consumption (#4901) is on master, this folds the sharded tenant-removal partition drop back onto Weasel's native path — the cleanup deferred while E3 was in flight.

## What changed
`ShardedTenancy.dropPartitionsForTenant` hand-rolled a quoted `DETACH`/`DROP` loop only because the pre-9.16 native `DropPartitionFromAllTables` interpolated the partition name unquoted and 42601'd on hyphenated/GUID/uppercase tenant ids. weasel#338 (in 9.16) fixed the native drop to **sanitize the suffix symmetric with the create path**, so this replaces the ~50-line loop with the database-scoped native call `DatabaseScopedTenantPartitions.DropPartitionFromAllTablesForValue(...)`.

## A latent bug this fixes
The old loop matched the **raw** (quoted) partition name (`"…_tenant-a"`) while the create path (`AddPartitionToAllTables`) **sanitizes** (`…_tenant_a`). So for a hyphenated/GUID tenant the loop's `to_regclass` check found nothing and **silently orphaned** the sanitized partition on removal. The native by-value drop resolves the sanitized suffix from the shard's own registry, so it drops the real table and clears the raw-keyed registry row. New test `remove_drops_the_sanitized_partition_for_a_hyphenated_tenant_id` pins this.

## Resilience preserved
The former loop's `to_regclass` pre-check made it resilient to a configured-but-not-physically-present parent table (registered tenant whose tables were never migrated to that shard). The native drop throws `42P01` there, so this keeps a **targeted catch** of that one SqlState. Filed **weasel#344** to harden the native drop; the catch can be removed once that lands.

## Tests (net9.0, Marten docker PG)
- `sharded_tenancy_remove_lifecycle_tests` **11/11** (incl. the new hyphenated case)
- all sharded `MultiTenancyTests` **34/34** — including `sharded_tenancy_soft_delete_tests.lifecycle_…` which removes a hyphenated tenant and surfaced the resilience gap (failing without the catch, green with it)
- `TenantPartitionedEventsTests` **228/228**

## Why

You said it plainly: *"an app that has global areas and trails in those areas."* This is the missing link — until now the pipeline produced a flat trail layer and a separate area-polygon layer that were **never connected**. This joins them.

## What
`build/assign_areas.py` (shapely): for each trail, point-in-polygon of its representative point against the OSM area polygons (plus any polygon its geometry crosses, for trails spanning multiple parks) → attaches `area_ids` to every trail and emits an **areas index** (`area → trail count + total miles`), mirroring the production seed pipeline's shape.

- Boundaries come from the **OSM areas layer we already extract** (ODbL, attributed) — **never WDPA** (commercially prohibited, per the research).
- Wired after the inclusion guard: tiles now carry `area_ids`, and the run uploads `<region>-areas-index.json`.
- 5 new tests (inside / outside / crossing-two / index counts / empty); **80 total**, pass locally.

Verified locally: trail inside a park → assigned; outside → ungrouped; crossing two → both; index ranks areas by trail count.

Pipeline-only, no iOS/CI impact. After this merges, the next dispatch produces **areas with their trails** for any country — the data model your app wants.

author: mmaclay
body:
## What does this change do?
  Adds the top-level save/load orchestration that ties the per-item persisters into a working feature — the first code that writes and reopens a real `.wiserproj` end-to-end. A full session round-trips: dataset + ROI + spectrum + stretch + user CRS + band-math expressions + run records, save to disk and reopen into a cleared session.

  ## What type of PR is this? (check all applicable)
  - [x] Feature
  - [ ] Bug Fix
  - [ ] Documentation Update
  - [ ] Style
  - [ ] Code Refactor
  - [ ] Performance Improvements
  - [x] Test
  - [ ] Hot Fix
  - [ ] Build
  - [ ] CI
  - [ ] Chore
  - [ ] Revert

  ## Why is this change needed?
  Every per-item persister (#618–#625) was only unit-tested in isolation — nothing wrote a real bundle or reopened one. Saving is only half the feature; opening a project must rebuild the session in dependency order so every reference resolves (datasets must exist, with their original ids, before the stretches/spectra/run records that reference them; ROIs before ROI-average spectra). Done wrong, a load produces cross-wired references or missing-dependency crashes.

  Closes #627 (load/restore orchestration). Implements the **save-flow half of #626** — the dependency-aware Qt Save dialog and menu wiring remain as a follow-up. Depends on the foundation #616, the resolver #617, and all item persisters #618–#625.

  **Stacked on #625** (`feat/proj-625-bandmath`, PR #679). This PR is based on that branch, so its diff shows only the orchestrator — review/merge the stack below it first, after which this rebases onto main.

  ## How did you implement the change?
  New `project/orchestrate.py`:
  - **`save_project(app_state, dest, resolver=None)`** — writes every item into one manifest (plus dataset/array sidecars via the bundle) by calling the eight `save_*` in dependency order (datasets first — they're the roots and own the sidecar I/O). A `dest` ending in `.wiserproj` is packaged as a zip (built in a temp dir); any other path is a bundle directory. Without an explicit resolver, every dataset is treated as saved (the #626 dialog will supply a user-driven one).
  - **`load_project(src, app_state, extract_dir=None)`** — opens a bundle (unzipping a `.wiserproj` into `extract_dir`, which must outlive the session since  one).
- **`load_project(src, app_state, extract_dir=None)`** — opens a bundle (unzipping a `.wiserproj` into `extract_dir`, which must outlive the session since sidecar datasets are read lazily), calls `bundle.read_manifest()` (which already migrates up / raises `ProjectTooNewError`), **clears the session**, then restores in topological order: datasets → CRS/band-math → ROIs → stretches → spectra → libraries → runs. Returns a load report of the entries that couldn't be restored, per section.

Two audit findings made this simpler than the issue anticipated: the UI reload signals **fire inline** (each `load_*` restores through the signal-emitting `add_*`/`set_*` accessors), and `_all_spectra` **self-rebuilds** via `collect_spectrum`/`set_active_spectrum` — so no separate `emit_session_reload_signals`/rebuild-index pass is needed.

Also adds two small shared-state pieces:
- **`ApplicationState.clear_session()`** — resets to an empty session using the normal `remove_*` methods so removed-signals fire and the UI clears. Verified safe: `remove_dataset → delete_underlying_dataset → delete_dataset` only `driver.Delete`s scratch `IN_DISK_NOT_SAVED` temp rasters — it never touches a user's source file.
- **`RunHistoryManagerBase.clear_records()`**.

Main-view dataset selection (which dataset is displayed) is derived UI state on the MainView widget, not `[SOURCE]` app_state, so it isn't persisted here — the main view defaults to `add_dataset`'s view pick on load. Restoring the exact saved view is a small follow-up if wanted.

## Added tests?
- [x] yes

`test_project_orchestrate.py` (3): a full-session round-trip through a real `.wiserproj` **zip** and through a bundle **directory** (asserting the dataset restores with its original id and its pixels, plus the ROI / spectrum / stretch / CRS / band-math / PCA record), and a **clear-session-first** test (a load discards unrelated state already in the destination). Full project suite green — 66 passed, no regression from the `app_state.py`/`run_history.py` additions; ruff + ruff-format clean.

One coverage note: the round-trip is proven via a comprehensive fake `ApplicationState` (matching the pattern the other persister tests use — a real Qt `ApplicationState` needs an app + cache). The real `clear_session` is mechanical and exercised through the app rather than unit-tested here.

## Added to documentation?
- [x] no documentation needed

## Checklist
- [x] There is an issue associated with this pull request (#627, #626)
- [x] Code compiles/builds without errors
- [x] No new lint/style issues introduced (ruff + ruff-format clean)
- [ ] Branch is up-to-date with main/master — stacked on `feat/proj-625-bandmath`; rebases onto main after the stack below it lands
- [ ] All CI checks passed — pending CI

## [optional] Are there any post-merge tasks we need to perform?
- Merge order: the persister stack merges bottom-up; after #679 lands, re-parent/rebase this onto main.
- Remaining epic work: the #626 dependency-aware Qt Save dialog + Save/Save-As menu wiring, and the #628 golden-file version gate.

## Summary

- Adds a product-contract checklist for Noisegate maintainers: context value first, exact context protection, fail-open behavior, artifact boundaries, and thin Hermes integration.
- Hardens command classification so package/build/log slop is compacted only when the command intent is clear.
- Expands regression coverage around exact source reads/searches, shell wrappers, package-runner wrappers, Docker build/log output, package-manager failures, artifact notices, and unknown/protected tool surfaces.

## Why

Noisegate should make agent context better, not just shorter. This PR tightens that contract: noisy terminal output gets smaller, but source reads, diffs, searches, retrieval payloads, and future unknown tools stay exact unless deliberately allowed.

## Validation

- `uv run ruff check .`

- `git diff --check`

## Risk / impact

- Conservative by design: new compaction paths are command-intent based and covered by tests.
- Exact-context paths are protected more broadly, especially source reads/searches through common wrappers.
- No LLM summaries, no raw-output archive behavior, no broad host framework layer.

Noisegate is stricter about what it is allowed to compact and more explicit about what must stay exact.

The product contract, source/search protections, Docker log/build separation, package-manager slop handling, and regression coverage for real agent workflows.

author: benjibushes
body:
## What

Money-path hardening from the 47-agent product-suite audit (every finding adversarially verified before fixing).

1. **CRITICAL — paid orders could land with no address + no email.** Settlement read `pi.charges.data[0]`, which is empty on modern charges-less Stripe payloads. Now fetches `pi.latest_charge` on the connected account (`event.account`) to recover ship-to/billing; operator signal screams `NO SHIP-TO CAPTURED` if still blank.
2. **Partial refund ≠ cancelled order.** A partial refund used to flip the order to Refunded, restore stock, and fire stop-ship. Now: loud PARTIAL REFUND alert, order stays live. Disputes still stop-ship at any amount.
3. **Oversell window closed + surfaced.** Sessions expire in 30 min (was 24h), and settlement rings OVERSOLD when an order lands with stock already 0 (the decrement clamp used to swallow it).
4. **$2,000 price ceiling** with a typo hint — "1999" instead of "19.99" listed (and could charge) a $1,999 jerky.
5. **Stored-XSS guard**: `jsonLdSafe()` escapes `<` in every rancher-content JSON-LD emission (PDP + ranch page + FAQ) — `JSON.stringify` alone lets `</script>` in a product description break out on the ad landing pages.

**Headline: the trained 4B (1.000) exceeds haiku+harness (0.80)** at ~$0.04/episode.
Round spend ≈ $85 of the $250 cap. RLVR declined by user decision — no post-SFT gradient
remains on this portfolio (round-5 material with the widened suite).

Key machinery (all pre-registered; one declared contract bump):
- **REV 4.9**: `scoring.training_reward` joins the grading contract (correct ∧ fully grounded;

author: paulfidika
body:
Fixes the two integration tests that have kept master CI red (tracker #792). Both reproduce on clean master; both are TEST-FIXTURE bugs, no product code touched.

## 1. TestRootOperatorBoundary_ReachNotMerchantCapability (internal/controlplane)

Failed with `2fa_enrollment_required`: authkit v0.84.0 (#49 login gate) fails closed when assigning an MFA-required root role to a user without enrolled 2FA — the fixture granted `root` owner to a fresh user who never enrolled.

Fix: new `enrollTestMFA` test helper (hentai0's pattern) inserts the exact DB state authkit's `userHasEnabledMFA` checks — an enabled `profiles.mfa_settings` row plus a default email `profiles.mfa_factors` row — before the Genesis role grant. The gate itself is untouched.

## 2. TestReconcileAdoptPreservesScheduledProviderActions (internal/reconcile)

Failed with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_prices_merchant_key_current"`.

**Verdict: fixture bug, not a product bug in price convergence/adopt.** The violation fires on the fixture's own seed INSERT (integration_test.go seed block), before any reconcile/adopt code runs: it inserts two prices for the same product with no explicit `key`, both defaulting to `auto_renew=false` / `access_duration_hours=NULL`, so the `trg_prices_default_key` trigger derives the SAME `<product>-onetime` key for both rows — colliding on the #774 partial unique index within a single statement. Product convergence code is not on the failing path at all.

Fix: distinct explicit keys (`sa-price-<suffix>-current` / `-scheduled`), per the documented `insertPriceIfAbsent` pattern in tests/seed_data.go.

## Verification

- Both tests reproduced red on clean master, green after.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, full unit `go test ./...` green.
- Full integration suite (`scripts/test_integration.sh ./...`, 44 tagged packages) green; `./tests` hit its 25m timeout once while ANOTHER worker's integration run contended for the shared Postgres (stuck live NMI HTTP call), and passes in 9s standalone — unrelated to this change.
- Re-verified both target tests after rebasing onto 421c1f62.

Fixes a misroute where a house-number destination went to the wrong town. Root cause chain: the model passed its own recalled to_coords (the street name exists in more than one town), so the server geocoder - which resolves the address house-number precise - never ran.

- **check_route**: destination geocoding now returns candidates; matches >15km apart return needs_clarification + options instead of a guess.
- **Demo prompt**: never pass to_coords for street addresses/landmarks; on needs_clarification, emit an options block and stop.
- **Frontend**: options blocks render as a bordered clarify card with clickable choices; a click resubmits the question with the exact place.
- **Photon token guard**: fuzzy hits sharing no real token with the query are rejected (it once matched a house-number query to an unrelated street).
- Geocoder User-Agent derives from package metadata instead of a hardcoded 1.1.

Tests: ambiguity surfacing, clarification response shape, fuzzy-hit rejection.

body: ## Summary Fixes incorrect attack timers on cards generated by the Library **New batch** action. Combined/evolved cards can retain a stale `timer` value from an earlier combine step while their `attack` stat reflects later stat boosts. That mismatch showed up on Level 2 and Level 5 cards in freshly generated batches. ## Changes - Add `normalizeCardTimer()` in `shared/baseCardStats.js` and use it when building test library evolved cards and during profile migration - Stamp each new batch with `libraryBatchId` and remount the library card grid so React refreshes card stats after replacement - Clear stale evolved-card entries from the offline lookup before registering the new batch, and keep the lookup in sync whenever the profile changes ## Test plan - [x] Open Library → **New batch** → Replace - [x] Verify every card’s displayed timer equals `Math.round(ATK × 1.5)` - [x] Verify stored `evolvedCards[].timer` matches the same formula in `localStorage` - [x] Start a battle with the new batch and confirm field card cooldowns match library previews

author: sprachzentrum
body:
## Zusammenfassung

Die Zambretti-Skala erwartet Meereshöhen-Druck — auf ~1000 m ü. NN ist die Prognose also nur so gut wie die Kalibrierung des relativen Luftdrucks der Ecowitt-Station. Dieser PR ergänzt einen automatischen Kalibrierungs-Check.

### Backend
- Neue Funktion `barometric.calibration_offset()`: paart die letzten 24 h Stationsdruck (30-min-Serie) mit den stündlichen `pressure_msl`-Werten von Open-Meteo (max. 45 min Zeitabstand, min. 6 Paare) und liefert die mittlere Abweichung in hPa. Ein konstanter Offset verschiebt nur die absolute Position auf der Zambretti-Skala — der 3-h-Trend bleibt unberührt.
- `/api/local-forecast` liefert neu `calibration: {offset_hpa, status}` — `status: "check"` ab 3 hPa mittlerer Abweichung. Kein zusätzlicher API-Call: `pressure_msl` steckt bereits im gecachten Forecast-Abruf; Zeitzonen werden über `utc_offset_seconds` abgeglichen.

### Frontend
- Warnbox in der Karte „Lokale Prognose", nur sichtbar bei `status: "check"`: „⚠️ Barometer prüfen: Ø +X hPa Abweichung zu Open-Meteo – rel. Luftdruck in der Ecowitt-App kalibrieren" (de/en/es).
- Service-Worker-Cache auf `wog-v12` gebumpt, damit Clients das neue Frontend laden.

### Tests
- 4 neue Unit-Tests für `calibration_offset` (Bias-Erkennung, kalibrierter Fall, zu wenige Paare, Zeitfenster) — Suite jetzt 21 Tests, alle grün. Endpoint-Smoke-Test (Offline-/No-Data-Fall) weiterhin grün.

author: greeshv03-ops
body:
## Summary

Geometry no longer has to be a NACA code, a `.dat` file, or hand-drawn points. This adds SVG import at three levels, letting us look at 2D aerodynamics for arbitrary shapes (cars, buildings, bridge decks) drawn in Inkscape/Illustrator:

- **`foil.ParseSVG`** — a dependency-free SVG reader (`foil/svg.go`) supporting `path` with the full command set (M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z and relative forms), plus `rect`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `polygon`, `polyline`. Curves are flattened to polylines at the editor's density, the y-axis is flipped to y-up, and the drawing is normalized as a group into the `.dat` convention (x in [0,1], vertical center at 0) so multiple subpaths keep their drawn relative positions.
- **`(svg "path" chord leadX leadY [subpath])`** scene source in `sceneio`, alongside the existing `(naca ...)` and `(dat ...)`.
- **File → Import SVG…** menu item — loads a drawing as a new scene, one editable/animatable object per subpath, placed like the interactive foil.

The solver is untouched: imported outlines flow through the existing `Place → Rasterize → mask` pipeline.

Also included:
- `examples/car.afoil` + `examples/car.svg`: a car silhouette (cubic-curve body + two circle wheels) verified end-to-end through `cmd/anim` — the rendered flow field shows the body with a proper wake.
- Fix for pre-existing `TestDATSource` failure on Windows (backslash temp paths inside Filo strings read as escape sequences).

## Known v1 limitations (documented in README)

- `transform` attributes are not interpreted — flatten transforms before exporting.
- Holes become solid (subpaths are unioned into the mask), which is fine for external aero.

## Test plan

- 15 new tests, written test-first: parser coordinate mapping, implicit linetos, multi-subpath normalization, cubic/quadratic/arc flattening, basic shapes, terse number tokenization, degenerate-geometry handling, error cases, end-to-end rasterization, the `(svg ...)` builtin (placement, missing file, bad index), import placement/naming, and a guard test that loads `examples/car.afoil`.
- Full suite green on Windows: `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l` clean.
- Headless smoke test: `go run ./cmd/anim -scene examples/car.afoil` renders the car in the flow.

author: vaipakam
body:
## What

Moves the two **view-only guards** in `DeployTestnetMocks.s.sol` — the
`FAUCET_SWAP_ADAPTER` reuse probe (`owner()` version gate + the price-aware
`tokenUsdPrice8` getter check) and the `MWETH_USD_FEED` live-feed freshness
validation — from **inside** the broadcast block to a **pre-flight** block
ahead of `vm.startBroadcast`.

## Why

Both checks are pure staticcalls, but running them after `startBroadcast` meant
that on a misconfigured rerun (a stale/incomplete live feed, or a pre-#1095
swap adapter passed by env) the script broadcast every *other* mock deployment
first and only *then* reverted — leaving orphaned mock contracts on-chain and
burning operator gas. Now a bad config fails fast with **zero on-chain writes**
and the same actionable message. Follow-up deferred from #1095 (Codex).

## What's deferred (intentional)

The state-writing pieces the guards feed — the static snapshot `MockChainlinkFeed`
deploy and the fresh `MockSwapAdapter` deploy — **stay inside** the broadcast,
driven by the values the pre-flight resolved (`wethQuotePrice8`, and whether to
reuse `swapAdapter`). Only the failure ordering moved; the happy path is
byte-for-byte the same behaviour.

## Verification

- Restructure is behaviour-preserving: `wethQuotePrice8` and `swapAdapter` now
  have single declarations in the pre-flight and are consumed unchanged inside
  the broadcast (feed deploy, pool `sqrtPrice` derivation, `setTokenPrice`,
  adapter registration). Every `require` message and probe is preserved verbatim.
- `TestnetMockPricesTest` inherits `DeployTestnetMocks` only to reuse the
  internal `_poolSqrtPriceX96` (untouched) and mirrors the wiring manually — it
  does not call `run()`, so the reordering doesn't affect it.
- No facet ABI / selector change → `contracts-fast` + `predeploy-check` cover
  the compile. (forge isn't available in the authoring env; CI validates.)
- `contracts/script/` only — no `src/` logic, no functional-spec / e2e-coverage
  surface.

## Closes

Closes #1102

author: yooleee
body:
## KI-28 Stage 2 (Slice 0) — comments retired outright, folded into the discussion model

Folds C2 **comments** into the E2 Inc 5 **discussion** loop and retires the comment
system at parity. Comments and discussion were two near-identical conversation surfaces
doing one job; the discussion loop is the matured, identity-first, two-way successor.
Per the 2026-07-07 addendum, comments are retired **outright** — no `report_id` tag (bias
to simplicity; the tag stays a later additive option).

Built unit by unit off `docs/stage2-comments-discussion-consolidation-kickoff.md`:

- **0.1 — migration tool** (`relay/migrate_comments.py`, `262b029`): a standalone,
  idempotent tool with two deliberate invocations. `migrate` folds `report_comments` →
  `relay_discussion_items` (role `supervisor`, `author_id` NULL, blank author → `anonymous`,
  body prefixed `[re: report N]`, timestamp preserved). Idempotent on the
  `(project, author_name, created_at, migrated_body)` four-tuple. `drop` is parity-guarded
  (refuses while any comment is unmigrated or orphaned). Orphan comments are reported
  loudly, never silently dropped. Hardened to no-op on a DB with no `report_comments` table.
- **0.2 — SPA retirement** (`2ffa251`): deleted `CommentList`/`CommentComposer` (+ tests),
  the report page's conversation section, `postComment`, and the `Comment` type / `comments`
  fields. The project-level Discussion thread is the one conversation surface.
- **0.3a — relay backend** (`0516468`): removed the `report_comments` store (functions +
  the table/index from `_SCHEMA`), the three comment endpoints, and the serializers'
  `comments` field.
- **0.3b — CLI / delivery / state / bot** (`5b5cd1d`): removed `orion comments`,
  `pull_comments`, and the comment-watermark accessors (the `comment_watermark` table is
  kept orphaned per the no-local-drops idiom). The Slack **bot is parked** — its write
  target (`POST /api/comments`) retired, so `orion bot` prints a parked notice and exits;
  the pure decision core + Slack shell are kept as the revival seam (repointed at the
  discussion write once per-user keys land in the follow-on slice).
- **0.4 part 1 — docs sweep** (`683dd51`): API contract, auth doc, commands, slack-bot
  guide, and known-issues updated to match.

### What is NOT in this PR (deliberate)

- **The live production migration.** The `migrate`/`drop` run against the deployed relay
  DB (back up → dry-run → verify parity → migrate → drop) is a separate, explicitly
  authorized step. **KI-28 is not yet marked resolved** and there is no CHANGELOG
  "Resolved" entry — both wait for the live migration + merge, so the docs don't overclaim.
- **Bot revival.** Repointing the bot at the discussion write needs per-user keys (the
  Bearer discussion path stamps role `developer`, but chat replies are supervisor speech) —
  that lands in the two-person-shared-base slice.

### Verification

- Backend suite **733 passed**; web suite **48 passed**.
- The migration tool exercised end-to-end against throwaway DBs: dry-run writes nothing;
  real migrate produces faithful rows; re-run is idempotent; drop refuses on an orphan,
  then removes the table once parity holds; no-ops cleanly on a fresh DB.
- Real CLI confirmed: `orion comments` → argparse exit 2 (gone), `orion bot` → exit 1
  (parked notice), `orion discussions` → present.

Note: `plans/orion-plan.md` + `docs/parallelization.md` (gitignored internal planning docs)
are updated locally and not part of this diff.

author: omar-amerah
body:
The user reported the server was sending large amounts of information per second, specifically citing the map which shouldn't change after game start.

I found that the `broadcastSnapshot` function in `src/server/messages.js` had a broken condition for `sendStatic`: `const sendStatic = room.phase !== "active" || ...;`
This meant that during the lobby and design phases, `sendStatic` was ALWAYS true, causing the server to broadcast the full world map, safe zones, relays, asteroids, and rule objects 15 times a second to every client. 

Additionally, `src/server/snapshots.js` was ignoring the `sendStatic` parameter entirely for the `ship.design` array, appending full design lists for every ship in the game, on every tick.

I've redefined `sendStatic` to securely enforce the 2-second rate-limit on static fields at all times. To prevent clients from waiting for the timer when data *does* change, I strategically placed `room.lastStaticSnapshotAt = 0` invalidation triggers where players connect, deploy ships, or rules are modified, ensuring snappy updates without bandwidth bloat.

author: kudratsingh
body:
## Summary

Completes Sprint 2 item 5 (item 5b): synthesizer prefers `state.evidence` over `paper_analyses` when the reader produced grounded claims. Adds an `EVIDENCE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` variant that carries **grounding rules**: every factual sentence must trace to a provided excerpt, missing coverage goes to "Open Questions" rather than being filled from abstracts, paraphrase OK but new facts are not.

Same `settings.enable_evidence_store` flag as ADR 0016 (5a), no new config or flag combinations to sweep.

## Design highlights

- **Base path byte-identical to Sprint 1 baseline.** `_use_evidence_path` returns `False` when the flag is off *or* when `state.evidence` is empty. The fall-back-to-base is automatic — a run with the flag on but all PDFs failing still produces the same report shape as the baseline.
- **User prompt keeps the analyses block on the evidence path.** Paper "shape" context (methodology / limitations) stays useful even when factual claims come from the evidence bank. Analyses have never been the factual source in the report — they've always been context — so keeping them doesn't invite fabrication.
- **Evidence bank grouped by `supports_question` in planner order**, sorted by `relevance_score` within each group. Claims with an empty `supports_question` land under a dedicated "(unassigned)" heading rather than being dropped.
- **Response schema unchanged.** No claim IDs embedded in the report text. Downstream metrics (completeness / citation-accuracy / faithfulness) and the verifier keep reading `draft_report` + `citations` without modification.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q --ignore=tests/e2e` — 358 passed (was 342; +16 new).
- [x] Base path stays byte-identical: dedicated test asserts the exact header lines (`--- Paper N ---`, `Title:`, `Authors: ... et al.`, `ID:`, `URL:`, `Key findings:`, `Methodology:`, `Results:`, `Limitations:`, `Relevance:`) that the Sprint 1 baseline prompt used.
- [x] Path-selection matrix covered: (flag off, ignored) / (flag on, empty evidence → base) / (flag on, evidence populated → evidence path).
- [ ] Nightly eval CI picks up flag defaults (all off). No baseline change until we flip the flag.
- [ ] Follow-up: paired-diff eval run with `enable_supervisor=true, enable_verifier=true, enable_evidence_store=true` vs. the prior config. Watch for "Open Questions" section growth eating into completeness scores.

## Not in this PR (deferred)

- Evidence-aware **completeness / citation-accuracy metrics**. Offline substrate stays abstract-based (ADR 0007) so cross-config comparability holds during the substrate rollout.
- `open_questions` / `evidence_gaps` **state fields with producers**. Report body still surfaces open questions in-markdown.
- **Claim IDs embedded in the report text**. Discussed and rejected in the ADR — would break the citation-accuracy regex and the verifier's cite-key match without a substantive win.

body:
**Root cause of the duplicate meds reminders** (live-confirmed today): the Telegram long-poll loop reset `offset = 0` on every boot and never persisted it. Telegram retains unconfirmed updates ~24h, so each restart (a deploy — today had ~5) re-fetched and re-processed recent updates, **re-sending old reminders/nudges/replies**. The user got a meds ping at the exact minute a deploy restarted the container.

## Fix
- **Persist the offset** in `app_state`: `_load_offset()` on boot, `_save_offset()` after `_poll_once` advances it (only when changed). Fresh/corrupt value → 0.
- **Drain in-flight handlers on shutdown** (`_drain_pending`, bounded 8s, from the poll loop's `CancelledError`) — addresses the prod-support **HIGH**: because dispatch is fire-and-forget and the offset is persisted right after dispatch, a deploy in that window would otherwise **DROP** an update (a lost Done-tap → a reminder that keeps nagging) instead of the old re-send. Slow chat relays may still be cut at the timeout — acceptable residual.
- **Observability** (prod-support MEDIUM): unconditional resume log (incl. fresh-0) + a `bgw_telegram_update_offset` gauge so a reset/stuck offset is visible on a graph.

## First-deploy note (prod-support HIGH #2)
The deploy shipping this boots with an unpersisted offset once. In practice the replay is **bounded to the restart-gap, not 24h** — the *old* running bot confirms updates server-side as it polls, so Telegram's unconfirmed queue is near-empty at cutover. Steady state (next deploy onward) is fully correct.

Also **cancelled the stale one-off reminder `fb05856a`** (a leftover from an earlier buggy chat that would have fired tomorrow 7am).

## Review + validation
code-reviewer (PASS, recommend merge) + prod-support (2 HIGH, both addressed). Tests: +3 (offset round-trip, corrupt-value default, drain-awaits-inflight). Full suite **1651 passed**; ruff clean.

This PR enhances the `InstallModal` component to follow standard accessibility and UX patterns for modals.

### 💡 What
- Added ARIA attributes (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby`) to ensure screen readers correctly identify the modal.
- Implemented keyboard navigation (Escape key closure) and focus management (scroll locking).
- Refactored the installation steps to use a semantic ordered list (`<ol>`).

### 🎯 Why
The previous implementation was a generic `div` that couldn't be closed with the keyboard, allowed background scrolling, and lacked the necessary ARIA attributes for assistive technologies, making it difficult for some users to navigate the installation instructions.

### 📸 Before/After
The visual appearance remains consistent with the brand design, but the underlying behavior is now significantly more robust and accessible. (See attached verification screenshot/video).

### ♿ Accessibility
- Full screen reader support for the modal dialog.
- Keyboard support for closing the modal.
- Focus containment via scroll locking.
- Semantic structure for the installation process steps.

author: acedatacloud-dev
body:
## What

Fix the Kling Motion Control pricing shown in Studio so it reflects how the service is actually billed: **per second of the generated video**.

- `MotionPanel.vue`: `consumption` now evaluates the cost rule with `duration: 1`, i.e. the per-second rate (`1.2`/std, `1.6`/pro) instead of a 5-second estimate.
- `Consumption.vue` (shared): two **optional** props `rateUnit` and `note` (empty defaults → byte-identical rendering for all other call sites). Motion now renders `1.20 Credit/second` plus a muted note.
- i18n: `name.perSecond` + `message.motionPricingNote` added to all 18 locales; `check_i18n_coverage.py` passes.

## Why

The Motion Control panel had no duration selector yet displayed a fixed `6.00 Credit`. That number is the cost rule (`1.2 × duration`) evaluated with the rule's **default** `duration = 5`. But Motion Control output length ≈ the reference video length (up to 30 s), so real charges were 15–34 credits — 2.5–5.7× the displayed estimate. A customer budgeted against the `6.00` and was surprised by the actual deduction.

Since the true output duration is unknown before generation, the honest display is the **per-second rate** + a note that the final amount scales with the reference video length, rather than a fixed number that structurally understates the charge.

Actual billing is unchanged (it happens server-side, per second); this only corrects the pre-generation estimate shown to the user.

## Test

- `Consumption.vue` / `MotionPanel.vue` type-check clean; ESLint clean.
- All 18 i18n locale files parse; `check_i18n_coverage.py` → exit 0 (17 locales × 44 namespaces match zh-CN).
- beachball change file included.

## 🤖 对抗评审

Reviewer: independent `general-purpose` subagent (Codex not installed on this host). Verified against the live cost rules and the shared component's other ~15 call sites.

- Confirmed the motion cost rules are linear (`1.2×d` std, `1.6×d` pro, no fixed term), so `duration: 1` yields the exact per-second rate; rule 1 defaults `mode` to `std`.
- Confirmed the optional props keep all other `<consumption>` call sites byte-identical; `note` is text-interpolated (no `v-html`) → no XSS; inline `<template v-if>` in the `<span>` is valid.
- **NIT** — if `character_orientation` were unset no rule matches and the block would show a transient `0.00`; benign because `CharacterOrientationSelector` seeds `image` on mount before paint and `canGenerate` is false meanwhile, and real billing is server-side. Not gating.

`VERDICT: CLEAN`.
