Images are loaded from IndexedDB after the DOM renders, using the same `testName::nwImageRef` composite key and `getNwImageB64()` resolver as the Clash Register modal. ## Changes **working.html:** - Updated `rDedup()` comment to clarify that viewport thumbnails now hydrate asynchronously (lines 8391–8393) - Added `.dq-img` slot markup to each candidate pair cell with fixed 4:3 aspect ratio, placeholder styling, and `data-dq-uid` attribute for lookup (line 8421) - Scheduled `_fillDedupImages()` via `setTimeout(..., 0)` after `rDedup()` returns to allow DOM insertion before async fill begins (lines 8449–8451) - Implemented `_fillDedupImages()` function (lines 8453–8481): - Queries all `.dq-img[data-dq-uid]` slots in parallel - Maps clash UIDs to clash objects for lookup - Calls `getNwImageB64(c)` per slot (reuses existing IDB round-trip logic) - On success: renders `` with data URI, dark background, and `openImgLightbox` click handler - On failure (missing ref, missing composite key, or missing blob): renders "No viewpoint available" placeholder - Wraps in try/catch to prevent unhandled rejections **tests/dedup-queue.spec.js:** - Added three new test cases covering the image hydration path: 1. **Both cells render `` tags** when both `nwImageRef` and IDB blobs are present — validates successful image rendering with correct base64 data URIs 2. **Placeholder on one side, `` on the other** when only one cell has a reference — validates mixed-state rendering 3. **Placeholder + no console errors** when `nwImageRef` is set but IDB blob is missing — validates graceful degradation and error suppression ## Implementation Details - **Timing:** `setTimeout(..., 0)` yields the current tick so `nav()` completes its synchronous innerHTML swap before slots are queried - **Error handling:** Console errors and network noise (CDN tunnel failures) are filtered; missing images fail silently with a user-facing placeholder - **Styling:** Slots use fixed aspect ratio (4:3) and max-width (220px) to stabilize layout while async fill is in flight; images use `object-fit: contain` to preserve aspect - **Reuse:** Leverages existing `getNwImageB64()` and `openImgLightbox()` to maintain consistency with the Clash Register modal - **Parallel execution:** All slots fill concurrently via `Promise.all()` https://claude.ai/code/session_01DnrTrgw498Fg4tVJBQff8a

author: eliezeravihail
body:
The design proposed in chat: **search each content space in its own pool, filter by relevance, hand the survivors to the model.** Replaces global RRF and all three of its crowding patches (reference channel, reserved seats, distance gates — deleted).

- Each kind (`api` / `tutorial` / `guide`) is searched as its own pool: dense + keyword, RRF-merged **within** the pool. No kind can crowd another out of the results — the failure class is gone structurally, not patched.
- **Relevance threshold**: candidates farther than `RELEVANCE_GAP` (0.15) from the best hit are dropped — junk that merely won its own pool (the RNNT-on-an-SGD-question case) never reaches the context. Keyword-only hits (no distance) are kept: an exact lexical match on a rare term is a signal of its own.
- **Interleave, strongest pool first**: pools take turns filling the top-k, ordered by their best candidate's distance — a tutorial-shaped question still leads with tutorials, but every relevant space is represented. The answering model does the final relevance judgment.
- Exact-symbol pin unchanged; the symbol pool leads the interleave when present. The planner's explicit `kind` (#61) searches only that pool.

**Why (benchmark runs 2→4):** the reference channel fixed q04 but its RRF mass displaced q10's tutorial hit; the gated reservation changed nothing (runs 3 and 4 were byte-identical — the reservation wasn't even the active mechanism). One kind's wins kept costing another kind's seats. Structural problem, structural fix.

**Measure after merge**: run "Eval retrieval" — compare against run 2 (0.808/0.594, pre-channel) and runs 3-4 (0.769/0.660). Watch q04 (api pool should keep it), q10 (tutorial depth vs. diversity trade), q06/q13 (expected to stay red — semantic gap, next experiment is the embedder swap).

Tests: 156 pass — within-pool RRF, interleave shares, strongest-pool-leads, threshold drops far candidates / keeps keyword-only, per-pool library filter, symbol pin + escaping, explicit-kind single pool.

author: vikrantpuppala
body:
## Summary

Reachable use of the stdlib `html/template` in package `auth/oauth/u2m` disabled the Go linker's public dead-code elimination (DCE) for the **entire binary** of any application that imports `databricks-sql-go`. `html/template` builds on `text/template`, whose reflection-based field evaluation forces the linker to retain code it would otherwise strip. This bloats consumer binaries — up to ~20% (40 MB) in multi-library binaries like [`xo/usql`](https://github.com/xo/usql), as reported in #343.

This PR rewrites the mostly-static OAuth callback page as plain string building with explicit `html.EscapeString` on the dynamic fields (the same approach [`xo/tblfmt`](https://github.com/xo/tblfmt/commit/c8da2821c2c334f51dac261563158550bbb6a6ac) used for a similar issue), removing `html/template`/`text/template` from the reachable graph. The now-unused embedded `templates/simple.html` is deleted.

The dynamic fields remain HTML-escaped, so the escaping behavior of the previous `html/template` implementation is preserved.

## Impact

Measured with a minimal `main.go` that imports the driver (the repro from the issue):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `text/template`/`html/template` symbols (`go tool nm`) | 615 | **0** |
| Binary size | 23.7 MB | **14.4 MB (~39% smaller)** |

The size delta is larger than the driver's own footprint because re-enabling DCE benefits the whole binary, including other libraries.

## Test plan

- Added `auth/oauth/u2m/html_template_test.go`:
  - `TestRenderHTML` (table-driven): basic field rendering + escaping of `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`; the conditional action-link block; the conditional code block; and that each page is a complete, well-formed document.
  - `TestInfoHTML`: success page title/heading/content, no code block.
  - `TestErrorHTML`: error page title and that the error message is HTML-escaped (no raw `<script>` leaks through).
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./auth/oauth/u2m/`, and `gofmt -l` are all clean.
- `go test ./auth/oauth/u2m/` passes.
- Verified via `go tool nm` on a consumer binary that the template symbols are gone (615 → 0) and the binary shrinks as shown above.

## Notes

- No other `html/template` or `text/template` usages exist in the codebase — this was the sole occurrence of the pattern.
- CHANGELOG updated under an `Unreleased` section.

Closes #343

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

body:
## What changed

First slice of the Phase 4 list page: the three leaf facet controls that the faceted rail will compose. `CheckboxFacet` (multi-select with counts and optional color swatches), `SearchFacet` (debounced text input via the shared `useDebouncedValue` hook), and `SelectFacet` (native select with a consumer-provided empty label) land in `src/v1/components/list/`, styled by a new `facets.css` partial and demonstrated on the `/_dev/components` showcase. The branch also carries the Phase 3 close-out updates to the planning docs under `projects/84-ui-ux-design/`.

## Why

Contributes to #373.

Phase 4 replaces the list page's filter row with a faceted left rail. The rail ships in staged PRs; these primitives go first because the FacetPanel (next PR) and the list route compose them. All strings arrive via props, so the consuming panel owns the localized copy.

## How it was tested

- `bun run typecheck` — clean
- `bun run lint` — clean
- `bun run test` — 1146 pass (11 new in `facets.test.tsx`; the known `java-instrumentation-list-page` pagination flake passed on retry)
- Manual: `/_dev/components` with `DEV_SHOWCASE` on renders the three facets interactively in light and dark themes

## Is this a breaking change?

No.

## Special notes for your reviewer

`SearchFacet` syncs external `value` changes (the panel's future "Clear all") during render, per React's documented "storing information from previous renders" idiom. The effect-based alternative trips the repo's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule, so the render-time form is the one that passes lint; there's a code comment explaining this. The `.td-facet-panel*` styles stay in the reference bundle on purpose: the FacetPanel PR extracts them into its own partial.

- [x] Tests added or updated for new behavior
- [x] Screenshots attached for any UI changes

author: steipete-oai
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slack does not let people add an app to an existing people-only group DM, and OpenClaw did not provide a supported way to create the equivalent bot-inclusive conversation. Searching for the app in Slack's **Add people** dialog therefore returns no result, while `/openclaw` starts a session without changing the conversation membership.

Fixes #102038.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an inline App Home flow instead of another slash command or modal:

- a native Slack people picker selects 1–7 other members;
- the authenticated actor and OpenClaw are included automatically;
- `conversations.open` creates or resumes the exact-member MPIM;
- the existing catch-all block-action listener owns the click, preserving one acknowledgement and preventing an agent wake-up;
- existing DM authorization and group-DM configuration remain the gate;
- the generated Socket Mode manifest now enables interactivity.

The Slack guide explains setup, authorization, exact-member resumption, relay limitations, troubleshooting, and the key platform constraint: this creates a separate bot-inclusive group DM and cannot copy history from the original people-only DM. Users who need to preserve that history can instead convert the original group DM to a private channel and invite OpenClaw there.

## User Impact

When Slack DMs and unrestricted group DMs are enabled, an authorized user can open **Apps → OpenClaw → Home**, choose people, and open the resulting group DM. Everyone selected can use the agent in that conversation, which is disclosed in the picker and documentation. Existing configurations with group DMs disabled or concrete-only group-DM allowlists do not expose the control.

Related documentation work in #101944 by @clawSean covers general group-DM membership semantics; this PR preserves that scope and adds only the implemented App Home creation flow.

Release-note context: Slack users can create or resume bot-inclusive group DMs from OpenClaw's App Home.

## Evidence

author: cartelug
body:
A full visual overhaul of 97 LIVE, done entirely through the design-token + class layer (no React logic touched), so it cascades across all ~226 inline-styled elements. Designed via a 3-direction design panel and hardened with a 4-lens adversarial visual critique.

## The problem
The app was competent but **flat and monochromatic**: cards barely separated from the near-black background, budget/receivable meters were invisible, cash-green and credit-teal blurred into one hue, and metadata (`--tx3`) was below AA contrast.

## Color law
- **Green** = realized cash / paid / inflow (brand)
- **Cyan-teal** = potential cash: USD amounts + available credit (shifted off green so they never merge)
- **Amber** = attention / pending / due-soon
- **Coral** = loss / overdue / expense outflow
- **Violet** = AI / Copilot

## What changed
- **`:root` retuned** — deeper base (`#0A0D07`) with three real elevation tiers, stronger hairlines, `--tx3` rescued from ~3.4:1 to ~4.8:1 (AA), sharper accents, and additive depth tokens (`--elev-*`, `--toplit`, `--ring`, `--glow-pos`, `--grad-fab`).
- **Components** — `.card` gains a lit top edge + grounded shadow (depth via box-shadow/border so it survives inline backgrounds); gradient primary button + FAB glow; tinted-coral danger buttons; recessed inputs with a green focus ring; glass nav with a glowing active tab; subtle brand-aura app background; styled scrollbars.
- **Meters** — budget/receivable tracks lifted to `--card3` so rails read even at 0%; fills stay color-coded. JS chart-series palette synced to the new tokens.

## Critique fixes (2nd commit)
- `button{color:inherit}` — account/list-row names inherited the UA-default dark (darker than their subtext); now bright primary text.
- `.wrap` bottom padding — last rows no longer sit under the FAB on long lists.
- Due-soon pill retoned coral→amber so it's distinct from Overdue (urgency now reads coral > amber > cyan > grey).
- Copilot empty-state composer scrim so the API-key hint fades under the input bar instead of hard-clipping.

## Verification
Headless Chromium across all six tabs + add/edit modals, at 844/667/600/540px and with `prefers-reduced-motion`: no JS errors, all action buttons visible/reachable, WCAG AA on text.

author: potsrevennil
body:
## Summary

Every `nvim` startup was silently logging `Invalid plugin spec { _keys = {}, get = <function 1>, set = <function 2> }`. Cause: `{ import = "lazyvim.plugins.lsp" }` imports an entire directory, and that directory has a non-spec helper file (`keymaps.lua`) sitting next to the real spec (`init.lua`) — lazy.nvim tried to import both. Fix: point at `lazyvim.plugins.lsp.init` directly so only the real spec loads.

Also added a CI check for this class of bug: lazy.nvim reports spec errors as log notifications, not a failed build, so this had zero CI signal before — it would only surface if someone happened to read `:messages`. Verified the new check actually catches it (fails on the old import, passes on the fix).

Bonus: this bug was also silently corrupting `lazy-lock.json` for unrelated plugins under some conditions — `lazy-lock.json` picks up two routine version bumps (`catppuccin`, `codecompanion.nvim`) that had gotten dropped as collateral damage.

## Test plan

- [x] `nix flake check --all-systems`, full lint suite
- [x] `packages.lite`: `:Lazy restore` in an isolated env, diffed against committed `lazy-lock.json` — exact match, zero spec errors
- [x] New CI check verified both ways: fails on the old broken import, passes on the fix

author: kalekoi
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent state effects from depending on block arrival order by splitting block acceptance into DAG metadata acceptance and a separate deterministic state rebuild phase for ordered-DAG-based semantics. 
- Preserve legacy behavior while enabling a `ghostdag_dev` path that derives transaction application order from the deterministic ordered DAG.

### Description
- Split block processing into phases and added public helpers: `accept_block_to_dag_metadata`, `refresh_selected_chain_phase`, `refresh_ordered_dag_phase`, `rebuild_state_from_ordered_dag`, and `commit_rebuilt_state`, and exported them from the core crate.
- Implemented an ordered-DAG state rebuild that starts from genesis (or a safe checkpoint), replays accepted blocks in `dag.ordered_dag` order, computes a deterministic UTXO/state root, and returns diagnostics; conflicting transactions are deterministically skipped as a placeholder conflict-handling strategy.
- Added diagnostics/state fields to `DagState`: `ordered_dag_rebuild_total`, `ordered_dag_rebuild_failed_total`, `ordered_dag_state_root`, `ordered_dag_tip`, and `ordered_dag_conflict_diagnostics`, and updated `refresh_ordered_dag` to set `ordered_dag_tip` and `ordering_version`.
- Surface ordered-DAG rebuild counters and state root in the status RPC payload and added unit tests that assert arrival-order independence and deterministic conflict skipping during rebuild.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and it passed.
- Ran `cargo test -p pulsedag-core dag_ordering --locked`, `cargo test -p pulsedag-core replay --locked`, and `cargo test -p pulsedag-core state --locked`, and the test suites passed.
- Ran `cargo check --workspace --locked` and it succeeded.

author: erichowens
body:
## Summary

Rebuilds the Harbor editor (`core/pd-console`) from status-card rendering into a real editor surface. The operator-visible bug: every code line rendered as a bordered, rounded, hover-lit "button", and the pane was slow.

**Root cause (all three confirmed in source):**
1. `editor_pane.rs` emitted `Block::Row(vec![gutter, line.text.clone()])` per line, so `app.rs`'s Row renderer gave every code line full status-card chrome (`mx/my/px/py` + `border_1` + `rounded` + hover) — and cloned every line's `String` on every `view()`.
2. `blocks_for_surface` constructed a fresh `EditorPane` inside **every render frame**: a `pd whoami` subprocess spawn + a full disk read + a Loro doc build per frame, then laid out all (up to 2000) lines flat — zero `uniform_list` anywhere in the crate.
3. A 2-char author tag rendered in every line's gutter even with a single author.

**The fix:**
- **`Block::CodeBuffer`** (new, render-agnostic): pre-tokenized lines behind `Arc<[CodeLine]>`, rebuilt only when the buffer's CRDT stamp (`HarborBuffer::change_stamp`, encoded state VV) moves. An unchanged buffer re-renders from the same `Arc` — a test asserts `Arc::ptr_eq` across views.
- **Virtualization**: the GPUI face renders the buffer as one `uniform_list` with `track_scroll` — only visible lines paint. Fixed 19px line height, zero per-line margin/border/rounding/hover.
- **Syntax highlighting** (new `syntax.rs`): line-local lexer (keyword/type/string/comment/number for Rust/TS/Python/shell; honest about same-line-only block comments). Runs render as `HighlightStyle` ranges on a single `StyledText` per line — batched text runs, no div per token (the isonim-gpui technique). Colors live in `palette.rs` roles (both modes) and `term.rs` Sem mapping — no inline hex.
- **Claim/wedge/region bands** paint as a background wash + 2px rail *behind* the text (last band wins; the conflict wedge is pushed last) — the P3 wedge is a highlight layer, not chrome.
- **Gutter**: line number always, plus an ALWAYS-VISIBLE author column (operator ruling mid-PR, reversing the earlier suppression): operator lines carry a subtle Resting-toned tag, agent lines a distinct Engaged-toned tag. `show_authors` is only the legend hint. `PD_CONSOLE_DEMO_AUTHORS=1` seeds a demo agent replica through the real CRDT merge path so the column is demonstrable on single-author files.
- **Persistent editor state**: `ConsoleView.editors` holds one `EditorPane` + scroll handle per open file, created once at render top — whoami/disk/Loro happen once per open, not per frame.
- **Notify discipline**: `update_panes` now reports whether anything changed and `main.rs` notifies only then (`Block: PartialEq`), so an idle 2s refresh cycle schedules zero repaints.
- The TUI face (`term.rs`) paints the same `CodeBuffer` (runs → `Sem` colors, band bars, same tag rule), keeping the one-pane-two-faces contract.

**Perf, before → after (per frame with the editor open):**
- before: 1 subprocess exec + full file read + Loro doc build + O(lines) String clones + O(lines) bordered cards laid out
- after: 1 stamp compare + `Arc` refcount bump + O(visible≈40) tight rows; idle console repaints zero frames

## Test Plan

- `cargo test` (both bins, no gpui — the CI gate): **471 tests green**, including new proofs:
  - `unchanged_buffer_reuses_the_same_code_arc_across_views` (`Arc::ptr_eq` across views; rebuild on a landed remote op)
  - `claims_and_wedge_render_as_background_bands` (wedge band wins overlaps)
  - `view_yields_one_row_per_line_with_gutter_numbers` now also asserts **no `Block::Row` cards** and that every line carries its author tag (always-visible author column)
  - `syntax.rs` unit tests (coverage invariant, lifetimes vs char literals, UTF-8 safety, merged runs)
- `cargo check --features gpui` and `cargo build --features gpui --bin pd-console` (the macOS CI job): green.
- Named devbuild `pd-console-dev-20260707-2322-editor-fast.app` built via `package-console.sh --devbuild editor-fast`, launched on `--pane "edit …/editor_pane.rs"`; captured PNG committed at `core/pd-console/docs/artifacts/gpui/editor-fast/` with a provenance manifest.
- Note: `cargo test --features gpui` SIGBUSes compiling the test binary — pre-existing (not a CI gate; CI builds, not tests, the gpui feature).
- Note: the canonical pd daemon (`:9876`) was down during this work (known 3.23 outage); `pd begin`/notes were retried and the coordination-guard block was bypassed with the shim's documented escape hatch, recorded honestly in the commit message.

author: qnbs
body:
## Symptom

On **LiveEnergyFlow** (and anywhere a command toast fires — **all** device commands, **both** viewports), clicking a control (KNX lights on/off, EV mode, heat-pump SG-Ready, battery force-charge) inserted an empty field at the **top** of the page and pushed the Sankey down, then reverted a few seconds later. Looked buggy.

## Root cause

Every command dispatch calls `notifyResult` → `toast.success(...)` (`useSafeCommand.tsx`). `sonner` positions its toaster via a **runtime-injected `<style>` tag** (`createElement('style')` + `appendChild`) with **no nonce**.

The app ships a strict CSP **meta tag** in `index.html` (AUD-02):

```
style-src 'self' 'nonce-…'
```

with no `'unsafe-inline'`. The browser enforces this everywhere the built app runs (Pages, preview, Tauri, Docker) and **blocks sonner's injected stylesheet**. Unstyled, `[data-sonner-toaster]` loses `position: fixed` and renders **inline at its DOM location** — which is at the top of `AppRouterTree`, *before* `<AppShell>` — so each toast pushes the whole page down until it auto-dismisses (5 s → "reverts").

(`motion` is unaffected: it mutates `element.style` via CSSOM, which CSP doesn't govern.)

## Fix

Import `sonner/dist/styles.css` in `main.tsx`. sonner 2.x ships this stylesheet; bundling it serves the positioning rules from `'self'`, which the CSP allows — so the toaster is `position: fixed` regardless of the blocked runtime injection. Keeps the CSP strict (no `'unsafe-inline'` reintroduced).

Adds a regression guard (`sonner-csp-styles.test.ts`) asserting the import stays in `main.tsx`.

## Verification

- `type-check` clean; guard test green.
- CI (build + E2E + lighthouse) will exercise the built app with the CSP meta tag in place.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
Two-bead cluster on the **pair-mcp / mcp-conformance** surface.

## rf2-bcayt7 — discover-app port-unresolved rides isError (P3, BUG)

`discover-app` returned `{:ok? false :reason :port-unresolved}` through
`wire/ok-text` when a `:port` mapped to no build — a known-tool failure
shipped as a success envelope, the odd one out among its sibling
precondition failures (unhealthy runtime / `:debug-disabled` /
`:no-frames-registered`, which already use `err-text`). Switched the
port-unresolved path to `wire/err-text` per spec/003's universal "every
`:ok? false` is `isError: true`" rule. Keeping it `isError` also keeps an
unresolved port out of the response cache, so it can never mask a later
valid port→build mapping.

- `discover_app.cljs`: `port-unresolved-result` `ok-text` → `err-text`
- `port_to_build_test.cljs`: flipped the fails-loud test to assert
  `isError`; **added an adversarial** `isError`↔`:ok?` cross-check on a
  distinct port (65535)
- `conformance_test.cljs`: **added** a `:discover-app/port-unresolved`
  corpus fixture pinning the `isError` envelope through the full
  `tools/invoke` wire pipeline
- `spec/003`: made the `isError` contract explicit for `:port-unresolved`

## rf2-6amhbt — closed-world tools answer without nREPL (P3, BUG)

`get-stream-controls` and `get-re-frame2-pair-instructions` read only
server-local state (resource-control atoms / an inline text `def`) — no
nREPL round-trip — yet the server ran them through `ensure-connection!`
first, so on a stock/degraded install they returned
`:nrepl-port-not-found`, contradicting the spec/003 "answers even when the
runtime is down" contract. The conformance end-to-end even encoded that
broken boundary as expected (both in `DEGRADED_TOOLS`).

Added a closed-world pre-connection dispatch, symmetric with the existing
unknown-tool and gated-write pre-connection guards:

- `registry.cljs`: flag both entries `:closed-world? true` + derive a
  single-source `closed-world-tool?` predicate
- `tools.cljs`: re-export `closed-world-tool?` onto the server-facing façade
- `server.cljs`: route closed-world tools to a new `handle-call-local`
  (invokes with the cached, maybe-nil conn) BEFORE `ensure-connection!`;
  extracted the shared `invoke-and-guard` from `handle-call*`
- `closed_world_test.cljs` (**new, adversarial**): both tools succeed
  pre-connection with the session-state pristine (no discovery ran)
- `end-to-end-re-frame2-pair.cjs`: dropped both from `DEGRADED_TOOLS`;
  **added** a closed-world success block asserting `isError:false` +
  object `structuredContent` + `isError`↔`:ok?` cross-check with no nREPL
- `spec/003`: documented the closed-world pre-connection dispatch on both
  tool sections

## Quality gates

Focused artefact tests only (full `test-fast-pr.sh` spine deferred to CI):

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` — `npm test` (`shadow-cljs compile
  server-test && node out/server-test.js`): **PASS** — 1172 tests, 3913
  assertions, 0 failures / 0 errors (includes the new `closed_world_test`,
  the updated `port_to_build_test`, and the new port-unresolved corpus
  fixture).
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` — `npm run build` (`shadow-cljs compile
  server`): **PASS** — 0 warnings.
- `tools/mcp-conformance` — `node test/end-to-end-re-frame2-pair.cjs`
  (degraded, no nREPL): **PASS** — `RE-FRAME2-PAIR-MCP MCP-CLIENT
  CONFORMANCE GREEN`; new line `closed-world tools
  (get-re-frame2-pair-instructions/get-stream-controls) -> success
  envelopes with no nREPL`; callTool coverage ratchet 31/30.

`node_modules` was absent in the fresh worktree; ran a focused per-artefact
`npm install` (pair-mcp + mcp-conformance) rather than the full spine.
The JVM wire-vocab conformance suite (`tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab`)

author: samgbafa
body:
## What

Migrates OpenKey off its hand-written capability URN strings onto the TC-112 single-source-of-truth constants published by the js-sdk:

- **Dep bumps** (`apps/api/package.json`): `@tinycloud/bootstrap` 2.4.1 → 2.5.0, `@tinycloud/node-sdk` 2.5.1 → 2.6.0, `@tinycloud/sdk-core` 2.5.1 → 2.6.0 (`@tinycloud/node-sdk-wasm` stays at 1.7.4, matching node-sdk 2.6.0's own pin).
- **`apps/api/src/routes/delegate.ts`**: `DEFAULT_ABILITIES` and the `capabilities/read` required-action checks now use `KV`/`SQL`/`CAPABILITIES` constants.
- **`apps/api/src/routes/delegate-autosign.ts`**: `tinycloud.space/host` → `SPACE.HOST`.
- **`apps/api/src/services/tinycloud-bootstrap.ts`**: all hardcoded `tinycloud.kv/*`, `tinycloud.sql/*`, `tinycloud.capabilities/read`, and `tinycloud.encryption/network.create` ability strings → constants.

All swaps are value-identical, with **one deliberate exception** below.

## Deliberate change: default delegation no longer grants `tinycloud.sql/export`

Rationale (TC-114, merged): `sql/export` was never a node-dispatched ability — SQL export operations are authorized as `sql/read` — and js-sdk 2.6.0's `exportDb` mints `sql/read`. The export grant in `DEFAULT_ABILITIES` was therefore a dead no-op; dropping it removes a phantom permission from the consent UI without changing what a delegation can actually do.

## Reviewer question: `sql/schema`

OpenKey's default delegation omits `tinycloud.sql/schema`, while the SDK's own default abilities include it. This PR intentionally does **not** add it (that would widen the default grant). Flagging for a reviewer decision: should OpenKey defaults align with the SDK defaults here, or stay narrower on purpose?

## Not migrated (out of scope)

- `apps/web/src/lib/siwe-parser.ts` service-label map keys (`tinycloud.kv`, `tinycloud.sql`, …) — these are service *names*, not ability URNs; the bootstrap constants only export ability URNs, and `apps/web` has no `@tinycloud/*` dependency today.
- `NETWORK_ADMIN_TYPE = 'tinycloud.encryption.network-admin/v1'` in `tinycloud-bootstrap.ts` — a credential type identifier, not a capability URN.
- Test-file literals — left as hardcoded strings so tests keep asserting the exact wire values independently of the constants.

## Testing

- `bun test` in `apps/api`: 53 pass / 0 fail.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/api`: error output byte-identical to `origin/main` baseline (pre-existing workspace-codegen/test-mock noise; zero new errors).

Refs: TC-112 (capability SSOT), TC-114 (sql/export request-kind artifact).

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
## What

The `Install clj-kondo` step in `.github/workflows/lint.yml` fetched the upstream `install-clj-kondo` script from CDN-fronted `raw.githubusercontent.com` with a bare `curl -fsSL`. Under CDN rate limiting this HTTP-429s and dies in ~11s before clj-kondo runs, reddening unrelated PRs (this cost a fix-worker cycle on #5304 / surfaced by rf2-rt13fn).

Fix: add `--retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3` to the curl invocation so transient failures — including the 429 that `-f` alone treats as fatal — retry with a 3s base backoff instead of hard-failing.

## Scope

Single-file, hot-zone (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`). I swept every workflow for the same bare-curl / raw.githubusercontent / install-script fetch pattern (`test.yml`, `portability.yml`, `docs.yml`, `release*.yml`, `expensive-tests.yml`, `post-merge-*.yml`): **`lint.yml` is the only file that fetches an install script this way** — the other `bootstrap` hits are esbuild-bundle references, not network fetches. No other workflow needed the same hardening.

## Diff

```diff
       - name: Install clj-kondo
+        # (comment: rationale — 429 flake, retry with backoff)
         run: |
-          curl -fsSL -o install-clj-kondo \
+          curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 3 -o install-clj-kondo \
             https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clj-kondo/clj-kondo/master/script/install-clj-kondo
```

## Quality gates

- CI itself is the validating gate — the lint workflow cannot be run locally. This PR's own `Lint required` run exercises the modified step end-to-end.
- `lint.yml` validated as well-formed YAML locally (PyYAML `safe_load` parses cleanly).
- Flag support confirmed: GNU curl on `ubuntu-24.04` runners supports `--retry-all-errors` (available since curl 7.71); `--retry` / `--retry-delay` are long-standing.

## Risks

- Low. Worst case on a genuine (non-transient) fetch failure is ~15s of added retry latency before the step fails as before — the retry only re-attempts, it never masks a real error (a persistent 404/network-down still exits non-zero after retries exhaust).

## Stance

Pre-alpha, no back-compat shims; ELEGANCE + CLARITY + CORRECTNESS. Minimal surgical CI-hardening — one step, three flags, a rationale comment.

Closes rf2-cq0s2j.

author: jagpat
body:
## What & why

Answers **"how do we manage drawings shared with the team to execute?"** The app only had progress **photos** (`Media`); issued drawings are controlled documents with a number + revision + status, "latest-rev-wins", and format-specific viewing. This adds a proper **drawings register** (Slice 1).

## Backend
- **`Drawing` + `DrawingRevision`** models (+ hand-written migration). Issuing a revision of an existing `number` **auto-supersedes** the prior ones, so the field always builds from the current `for_construction` set. Files reuse `StorageService` (S3/R2 or DB stub); `MIME_EXT` extended to **PDF/DWG/DXF**.
- `POST /projects/:id/drawings` (issue → **per-role push** to engineer/contractor), `GET /drawings/rev/:id` (serve), `DELETE /drawings/:id` (project-scoped). Snapshot gains **`drawings[]`** (each with `current` rev + full `revisions[]`).

## Frontend
- A **Drawings register** screen (all roles), grouped by discipline: number, title, current rev + status badge, "governs ACT-xx", revision count.
- **Viewer**: PDF/image inline, **DWG/DXF download-only** (paired PDF for the field), revision history with superseded revisions clearly marked.
- PMC **"Issue drawing"** flow (file picker → number/title/discipline/rev). Demo seeds three drawings (mock SVG sheets) and issues locally.

## Format decision
**DWG is a downloadable CAD source, not previewed** — browsers can't render it and the site team needs the PDF. This matches construction practice (issue the PDF "for construction"; DWG for consultants). Server-side DWG→PDF conversion was considered and rejected as too heavy for a small practice.

## Verified
In-browser (demo): switched to PMC → **Drawings** → register grouped by discipline (A-201 Rev C *For Construction* · governs ACT-31 · 3 revisions) → opened the viewer → sheet renders, revision history shows Rev C current + Rev B/A **superseded**. No console errors.

Tests: **api 61** (issue creates entry / adds+supersedes rev / S3 vs stub / tenant-scoped delete), **web 54** (issue + supersede). Typecheck + build + lint green, both apps.

## Not in this PR (planned — see `docs/DRAWINGS.md`)
- **Slice 2**: activity/decision linkage on the schedule + worker job card; **acknowledgement** ("building to Rev C") + audit; RBAC tiers.
- **Slice 3**: offline PDF caching (PWA); **presigned uploads** for large drawings (current path is the 12 MB base64 body).

## Migration note
New models ship with `prisma/migrations/20260708000000_add_drawings` (hand-written, no DB in CI to run `migrate dev`). `migrate deploy` applies it on deploy; the live DB was baselined at `0_init` per `docs/DEPLOY.md`.

body: ## Problem Sign-in across official Oxy apps (Inbox, Accounts, Console, etc.) fails during the password hand-off to `auth.oxy.so`: 1. **Production DB drift** — official `Application` records resolve via `GET /auth/oauth/client/:clientId` but have **empty `redirectUris`**, so `POST /auth/oauth/authorize` returns `redirect_uri is not registered for this client` (verified in prod with curl). 2. **Client flow gaps** — `openPasswordAtOxyAuth` sent the full page URL as `redirect_uri` (must exact-match registered origin), omitted PKCE (required for public client token exchange), and first-party apps never exchanged the returned `?code=` back into a device-first session. 3. **IdP signup link** — "Create account" dropped OAuth params, causing "No authorization request found" after signup mid-flow. ## Fix ### API (`packages/api`) - **`reconcileOfficialRedirectUris`** — on boot, restores `redirectUris: [origin(websiteUrl)]` for official apps with an empty allowlist (self-heals prod without a manual seed run). - **`POST /auth/oauth/token`** — calls `finalizeDeviceLogin` and returns `deviceId` + `deviceSecret` so the RP can persist zero-cookie credentials. ### Core / Services SDK - **`openPasswordAtOxyAuth`** — async; uses registered `authRedirectUri` / origin normalization, PKCE, and `sessionStorage` handshake persistence. - **`exchangeOAuthCode`** on `OxyServices` + **`tryCompleteOAuthReturn`** in `OxyProvider` cold boot — completes password sign-in when the RP lands with `?code=&state=`. - Shared OAuth handshake helpers exported from `@oxyhq/core` (re-used by `OxySignInButton`). ### Auth IdP (`packages/auth`) - Signup link preserves OAuth query params from the login page. ## Verification - `packages/core` accountDialogController tests: 27 passed - `packages/api` oauthCode.service tests: 10 passed - Prod curl before fix: `POST /auth/oauth/authorize` with `redirectUri: https://inbox.oxy.so` → **403 FORBIDDEN** ## Deploy notes After merge + deploy to ECS, the boot reconciler should repair empty `redirectUris` automatically on the next API restart. Optionally still run `packages/api/scripts/seed-oxy-applications.ts` as a one-shot to fully reconcile all official app metadata.

author: notashwinii
body:
## BB-14 — Search has no recovery for a bad page; Retry doesn't recover

Visiting a deep/out-of-range results page (e.g. a stale `/search?...&page=9999`) makes the unified search API return an error (a `SearchError` → HTTP 400 beyond the 10k offset window). The error alert's **Retry** button called `refetch()` with the **same** `page`, so it re-errored forever — the reported "Retry doesn't recover."

### Fix (frontend)
`src/pages/ArchiveSearch.tsx` — the recovery action now resets to **page 1** when `page > 1` (escaping the bad page), and keeps a plain `refetch()` for genuine errors on page 1. The message/label also adapts ("That results page is out of range… / Back to first page").

`readParams` already clamps the lower page bound; in-app pagination is already bounded by `PaginationControls`. The remaining trigger is a hand-typed/stale URL, which this recovery handles.

### Scope note — deferred backend half
Making the API return an **empty page (200)** instead of 400/404 for an over-range page — so the MCP client and all callers degrade gracefully (also relates to the `MCP-V` 404) — is a backend change and will be handled in the backend batch.

### Verification
- `eslint` clean on the changed file. (CI runs `bun run lint` + `bun run build`.)

Part of the Jawafdehi bug-bash FE quick-win batch.

author: yuki-zik
body:
## Problem

`master` CI (run 28922137830) failed **only on `windows-latest`**; `ubuntu` and `macOS` passed. Failing test: `extension applies on-demand stable ID tracking policy` (`test/extension.tests.js:158`), `expected true, actual false`.

The push that triggered it (`05bb7a7`, a glass/alpha highlight fix) is **not the culprit** — it just happened to be the first `master` push to run CI on Windows and expose a pre-existing cross-platform test defect introduced in `9ae1b2b`.

## Root cause

The assertion does `fs.readFileSync('src/extension.js','utf8').indexOf('...\n...forceStableIds...\n...')`. The repo has **no `.gitattributes`**, so with Git's default `core.autocrlf=true` (true on GitHub's Windows runners), `extension.js` is checked out with **CRLF**. The `\n`-joined multi-line search then never matches on Windows.

Reproduced locally on Windows (CRLF working tree): LF checkout → `indexOf` matches; CRLF checkout → no match.

## Fix

- **`.gitattributes`** (`* text=auto eol=lf` + explicit LF for `*.js/*.json/*.md/*.yml/*.svg`, `binary` for images/fonts) — forces LF checkout on every platform, ending this class of Windows-only test breakage. Index blobs were already LF, so there is no content churn.
- **`readSource()` helper** in `test/extension.tests.js` that strips `\r\n` → `\n` before scanning; the 12 source-scanning assertions now go through it, so existing CRLF working copies also pass without needing a re-checkout.

No runtime code changed — test/tooling only.

## Verification (Windows, CRLF working tree)

- Reproduced the failure first, then after the fix:
  - `node qunit test/extension.tests.js` → **15 passing / 0 fail** (was 14/1)
  - `npm test` → **145 passing / 0 fail**
  - `npm run webpack` → build succeeded
- `git check-attr` confirms `text: set, eol: lf`; staged diff is only `.gitattributes` + `test/extension.tests.js` (+ governance docs).

## Summary
- Removes the gateway API-version probe (`GET {gateway}/session`) and all `_isV1` branching from the datamesh client — the v0 API is deprecated and no longer deployed, so the client now always operates in v1 (session-aware) mode.
- Root cause this fixes: the probe was auth-gated and fired unawaited from the constructor, so any non-200 / CORS block / transient network error silently flipped the client to v0, stripping `X-DATAMESH-SESSIONID` from every request. Staging works session-less but the zarr query view does not, so gridded queries failed with `{"detail":"Session ID required"}` (observed in the EIDOS auv-demo GEBCO bathymetry layer).
- Changes: a session is always acquired before the first request (`getSessionHeaders`), the zarr view is always addressed via `/zarr/query/{qhash}`, and the v0 dummy-session branch in `Session.acquire` plus the v0 bypass in `Session.close` are removed.
- Tests: new `session-zarr.test.ts` (session always attached to zarr requests; v1 query path always used; `CachedHTTPStore` forwards the session header per chunk); `getdataobject.test.ts` updated to stub session acquisition instead of relying on the removed v0 escape hatch.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** legacy v0 (session-less) datamesh gateways are no longer supported.

- [x] `vitest run` (datamesh package): 85 passed / 7 failed — all 7 failures are pre-existing integration tests hitting `https://gateway.datamesh.oceanum.io` which currently presents a self-signed certificate (verified identical failures on the unmodified tree)

author: plasticparticle
body:
## Why

You couldn't install Mneme to an Android home screen because two prerequisites for a real PWA install were missing: there was **no service worker** (the Workbox plugin was still on the "later" list), and the dev server is reached over `http://<LAN-IP>:5173`, which is not a **secure context** — install and service workers require HTTPS or `localhost`.

While here, this also adds an iOS-specific caveat notice, since iOS is the one platform where a PWA can't fully deliver an offline-first journal.

## Part 1 — Installable PWA

- Wire `vite-plugin-pwa` (Workbox `generateSW`, `registerType: 'autoUpdate'`) in `apps/client/vite.config.ts`. It precaches the app shell — JS/CSS/HTML, the wa-sqlite wasm, bundled fonts, icons (~3.3 MiB) — and injects its registration into `index.html`. The existing `public/manifest.webmanifest` stays the source of truth (`manifest: false`).
- Paired with the manifest this satisfies Chrome/Android installability and enables offline launch. **Production HTTPS hosts get install with no extra config.**

**Dev HTTPS (for testing install on a phone)**
- `pnpm --filter client dev:https` → self-signed HTTPS via `@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl` (good for `localhost` verification).
- `DEV_TLS_CERT` / `DEV_TLS_KEY` → serve dev under a locally-trusted `mkcert` cert — the only kind a phone's Chrome registers a service worker under (a cert *error* blocks the SW → no install).
- The dev SW is **off in ordinary `pnpm dev`** so day-to-day development isn't fighting cached assets; it turns on only in the HTTPS test mode.

## Part 2 — iOS storage-eviction notice

iOS clears a web app's offline storage (OPFS/IndexedDB) after ~7 days of inactivity. For a local-first journal that's worth flagging — framed as the **privacy safeguard it is**, not a complaint.

- `platform/shell.ts`: `isIOS()` (covers iPadOS's desktop-Safari UA via the touch-capable `MacIntel` heuristic).
- `ui/IOSNotice.tsx`: a small, dismissible top banner shown **only** when `isIOS() && !isTauri()`; dismissal persists in device-local `localStorage`. **Never** shown on Android/desktop (they don't evict) or in the Tauri shell (persistent storage).
- Copy reassures that entries stay end-to-end encrypted on the relay and restore on next sign-in.
- i18n: `shell.iosNotice.{body,dismiss}` translated across **all 12 locales** (register-correct — French formal, the rest informal); coverage back to 636/636.
- Preview on a non-iOS dev machine: `localStorage['mneme.iosNotice.force'] = '1'`.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter client build` passes (`tsc` + `vite build`); `dist/sw.js` + workbox emitted, shell precached.
- HTTPS dev mode smoke-tested: serves 200 over TLS, `registerSW.js` served.
- iOS notice driven in a real browser via the force flag: renders with correct copy, dismiss persists, and confirmed it does **not** render on desktop Chrome (no force flag) — proving Android/desktop suppression.

## Docs
New `docs/PWA.md` (install recipe, phone-testing paths, the iOS eviction note, DevTools debugging), plus notes in `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/FEATURES.md`, and the docs index.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Part 3 — Relative manifest paths (fixes install under `/mneme/`)

The production web build serves the app under `/mneme/` (`deploy/web`: `vite build --base=/mneme/` + Caddy). Vite rewrites `index.html` asset paths for the base but copies `public/manifest.webmanifest` **verbatim**, so its absolute `start_url: "/"` and `/favicon-*.png` icons resolved to the site **root**, not `/mneme/` — all three icons **404'd**, and Chrome refuses install when no manifest icon loads. This was the actual reason install wasn't offered on the deployed site (`https://…/mneme/`).

Fixed by making the manifest paths relative (`"./…"`) so they resolve against the manifest's own URL — `/mneme/favicon-192.png` under a subpath, `/favicon-192.png` at root — correct for any deploy base. Added explicit `"scope": "./"`.

Validated against a real `--base=/mneme/` build served under `/mneme/`: `start_url` and `scope` resolve to `/mneme/`, all icons return 200, and `start_url` is in scope. (Diagnosed on the live deploy: icons were 404 before, 200 after.)

## Summary
Migrates the blueberry grading system from a size-based scheme (Small, Medium, Jumbo, Super Jumbo) to a quality-based scheme (Normal, Red Bums, Rejects). All historical size-graded fruit is consolidated into the 'Normal' grade, while 'Rejects' remains unchanged and 'Red Bums' is introduced as a new grade.

## Key Changes
- **Database migration (071)**: Updates all blueberry grades across reaping_data, packhouse_movements, packhouse_intake_lines, packhouse_sale_lines, and packhouse_consignment_lines tables, consolidating Medium/Jumbo/Super Jumbo/Small into 'Normal'
- **Harvest grades**: Updates HARVEST_GRADES constant to reflect new blueberry grades (Normal, Red Bums, Rejects)
- **Grade colors**: Remaps color assignments—Normal inherits the dark teal from Super Jumbo, Red Bums gets a new orange-brown color
- **Packhouse grades**: Updates GRADES constant to match the new blueberry grading scheme
- **Version bump**: Increments to v1.0.56

## Implementation Details
- Migration is idempotent and scoped by produce_type where applicable to avoid affecting citrus grades
- Color scheme maintains visual hierarchy while introducing a distinct color for the new Red Bums grade
- Changes are consistent across both field-level (harvest) and packhouse-level grade definitions

author: slightc
body:
Follow-up to the merged #25. The `@sequio/engine` publish run failed at the
final step:

```
npm error 422 Unprocessable Entity - Error verifying sigstore provenance bundle:
Unsupported GitHub Actions source repository visibility: "private".
Only public source repositories are supported when publishing with provenance.
```

npm only accepts provenance statements from **public** source repositories, and
this repo is private. This removes provenance from the Release workflow so
`pnpm publish` succeeds.

## What changed

- Drop `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'` from the publish step.
- Drop the now-unneeded `id-token: write` permission.

## Notes

`@sequio/engine@0.1.0` was **not** published (the 422 rejected the whole

author: mesox
body:
Implements the #275 RFC: replaces the fixed security-guard catalog with two free-text system-prompt fields.

## What changed

- **`provider.securityGuardrails`** (`text`, ≤8000) — free-text security directives appended **last** in the system prompt (recency strengthens injection resistance) for every run on the provider, **including sub-agent runs resolved to it**. Append-only and non-suppressible; the escape hatch is pointing the agent at a different provider.
- **`organization.identityContext`** (`text`, ≤4000) — free-text org framing rendered **early**, beside the workspace context. Explicitly **not** a security control, and deliberately **not adjacent** to the security block.

Prompt render order: `agentPrompt → agentIdentity → organization → workspace → user → userContext → memories → … → security (last)`.

## Sub-agents (the key correction from the RFC)

Sub-agents build their instructions from the raw agent `systemPrompt` and **never call `renderSystemPrompt`**, so provider guardrails silently missed them before. Each sub-agent now appends its **own** resolved provider's security text — including onto the **canned fallback instructions** when the sub-agent has no `systemPrompt`, so the guarantee is genuinely non-suppressible. No parent inheritance, no org text.

The shared renderer lives in a leaf module (`security-prompt.ts`) so the top-level prompt path and the sub-agent path produce **identical** wording without a circular import.

## Docs

- `concepts/providers.mdx` — documents `securityGuardrails`; preserves the 7 former catalog directives verbatim as **paste-in starter snippets**; adds the honest **three-layer model** (steer / detect / enforce) and the `baseUrl`-fronting proxy pattern. The in-prompt layer is a **floor, not a guarantee**.
- `concepts/memory-and-context.mdx` — documents org `identityContext` as framing, not a security control.
- `self-hosting/providers-and-auth.mdx` — the three-layer model + proxy pattern for the enforce/detect layers.

## Schema / migration

Additive and nullable — existing orgs and providers are unchanged.

```sql
ALTER TABLE "organization" ADD COLUMN "identity_context" text;
ALTER TABLE "provider" ADD COLUMN "security_guardrails" text;
```

No dead catalog column lands in history: this branch is a single clean commit off `main`, carrying **only** the free-text feature (no `guardrails` jsonb column, no `security-guards.ts`, no catalog migration).

## Frontend

- Provider form: catalog Switch loop replaced with an `ExpandableTextarea` (char counter, `maxLength=8000`, markdown preview) bound to `securityGuardrails`.
- Organization form: `ExpandableTextarea` for `identityContext` (update-only; the create schema accepts `name` only).

## Tests

All green: `system-prompt.test.ts`, `tools/sub-agent.test.ts`, `routes/organization.test.ts` (70), and `packages/schemas/index.test.ts` (41). Coverage includes: security text renders last; org block renders before workspace and not adjacent to security; sub-agent guardrails appended even on the fallback-instructions path; org text and parent-provider text are **not** leaked into sub-agents; length bounds reject over-limit input.

Closes #275

author: groeneai
body:
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/110048
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/97411


### Changelog category (leave one):
- Bug Fix (user-visible misbehavior in an official stable release)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Constant folding during query planning no longer executes a function whose argument type differs from the type the function was resolved for during analysis. Such a mismatch used to raise a `LOGICAL_ERROR` while the output header was being computed, which is an assertion failure in debug and sanitizer builds. Folding is now skipped instead, and a genuinely invalid query still reports a recoverable `ILLEGAL_TYPE_OF_ARGUMENT` error from the normal execution path.


### Description

`ActionsDAG::updateHeader` matches header columns to DAG input nodes **by name only**, then runs `evaluatePartialResult` to compute the output header. A function node, by contrast, is resolved once during analysis: the overload is picked and the return type computed for a fixed set of argument types. If partial evaluation is handed an input column whose type differs from the one the function was resolved for, `executeActionForPartialResult` used to execute the function anyway. That trips a `LOGICAL_ERROR` inside the function body (for example `FunctionUnaryArithmetic`: "`negate`'s argument does not match the expected data type"), and because `handle_error_code` routes `LOGICAL_ERROR` to `abortOnFailedAssertion`, a debug or sanitizer build aborts the whole server process during planning rather than failing the one query.

**Fix.** Before executing a `FUNCTION` node in partial evaluation, compare each argument column's type against the type recorded in `function_base->getArgumentTypes()`. If any of them differs, skip the fold: it is only an optimization, and the node's declared result type is already known from analysis.

- With `input_rows_count == 0` (header computation) an empty column of the declared result type is produced, so header computation proceeds.
- With `input_rows_count == 1` (the callers reached from JOIN rewrites, shard skipping and virtual-column path extraction) the column is left null. Those callers treat any non-null output as a definitive folded value, so a fabricated one could silently change a JOIN rewrite or skip the wrong shards; a null routes them through their existing "unknown value" path.

The comparison is exact rather than wrapper-stripped, because `isNullable` derives its value from the argument type alone: its result type is `UInt8` either way, so a wrapper-only difference would produce a definitive but wrong value that no result-type check can catch.

`ALIAS` and `ARRAY_JOIN` need the same treatment, because both used to pass a value through while keeping the declared type computed during analysis. That hid the mismatch from the check above and let a downstream function execute on an incompatible column anyway. Both now carry the argument's actual type, which is what `ExpressionActions::executeAction` already does in its own `ALIAS` and `ARRAY_JOIN` cases.

One result type cannot be instantiated: `DataTypeFunction`, the result type of a captured lambda, inherits `IDataTypeDummy::createColumn`, which throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`. The column is left null in that one case. Since a capture is normally a child of the higher-order function consuming it, that function then reports a recoverable `NOT_FOUND_COLUMN_IN_BLOCK`, whereas executing the stale capture raises `Cannot capture column N because it has incompatible type`, another `LOGICAL_ERROR` abort. (`DataTypeNothing` and `DataTypeSet` derive from the same base but do override `createColumn`, so they are built normally.)

**Scope.** In production the mismatch was produced by a concurrent `EXCHANGE TABLES`. The query does hold its table object, lock and metadata snapshot for its whole lifetime (`InterpreterSelectQuery.cpp:635-656`), so the held storage is never swapped. What drifts is that the old analyzer resolves the table name a second time for the analyzed column types (`getTableExpressions.cpp:118`, reached from `joined_tables.resolveTables()`), and an exchange changes what that second resolution returns. The per-query storage cache from #97411 is what keeps those two resolutions consistent; #108728 defeated it and #110048 restored it, which is what `03915_exchange_tables_race` races for. This change is therefore no longer the fix for that race; it hardens the planning path itself so that any argument-type mismatch degrades to "do not fold" instead of aborting the server. I left the changelog category as `Bug Fix` because the abort was user-visible on released builds before #110048, but I am happy to move it to `Not for changelog` if you prefer, given that the root cause is now fixed upstream.

**Testing.** Coverage is a unit test rather than a functional one, because the race is an inherent TOCTOU and cannot be reproduced deterministically. Since `updateHeader` binds header columns by name only, the mismatch can be injected directly, single-threaded, with no race at all. `src/Interpreters/tests/gtest_actions_dag_partial_result_type_drift.cpp` covers a strict function (`Float64` resolved, `Int256` supplied), a wrapper-only difference through `materialize`, the same mismatch behind an `ALIAS` and behind an `ARRAY_JOIN`, the wrong-value hazard via `isNullable` at `input_rows_count == 1`, a captured lambda both as a terminal output and consumed by `arrayMap`, and a non-mismatched constant that must still be folded.

Verified in both directions on a debug build. Against master's `executeActionForPartialResult` the first case aborts the test binary with `Logical error: 'Unexpected return type from negate. Expected Float64. Got Int256'` through `updateHeader` -> `evaluatePartialResult` -> `executeActionForPartialResult`; with the fix all eight cases pass. Each hunk was also reverted individually and fails only its own case, and forcing the guard to fire unconditionally fails only the still-folds-a-constant case. Full unit suite: 22357 tests pass. `03915_exchange_tables_race` passes 10 out of 10 runs.

**Known residuals, both pre-existing on `master` and deliberately not addressed here.** I measured each one against a build with this branch's `ActionsDAG.cpp` replaced by master's, and the behaviour is identical, so neither is caused or widened by this change:

- The add-time fold in `tryFoldFunctionToConstant` does not perform this check. Handing `addFunction` a `function_base` resolved for one type together with a differently typed constant child raises `Unexpected return type from negate. Expected Float64. Got Const(Int256)`. This diff does not touch that path, and adding the check there would alter DAG construction for every query on a scenario I could not reach from SQL.
- At `input_rows_count == 1` with `allow_unknown_function_arguments`, a type-sensitive folder above a node whose column is unknown can still fold from the type alone. Two shapes: `identity -> isNullable` over a `Nullable(String)` yields `0` where the real chain would yield `1` (unchanged from `master`), and an `ARRAY_JOIN` whose argument stopped being an array leaves the declared nested type in place, so `isNullable` above it also folds to `0`. Closing this properly needs an explicit "unknown" marker propagated through descendants, which changes the `evaluatePartialResult` contract for every caller. I tried the two local shortcuts and neither works: clearing the type outright makes the unit-test binary abort and then segfault, because a null type in a `ColumnWithTypeAndName` breaks downstream consumers; handing up the argument's own type does not help, because the parent compares against the type it was itself resolved for. So this is a separate design decision rather than part of an abort-avoidance fix. Happy to fo

author: cfarvidson
body:
## Why

Switching views on mobile felt slow and glitchy. Three root causes:

1. **No `loading.tsx` anywhere.** Every `(mail)` page is fully dynamic (`auth()` + DB per navigation), so a tab tap gave zero visual feedback until the whole RSC payload arrived — the app looked frozen for the entire server roundtrip.
2. **Tab highlight waited for the server.** `MobileTabBar` derived the active tab from `usePathname()`, which only updates when navigation commits, so the tapped tab stayed grey during the roundtrip.
3. **Stale unread state on back-navigation.** Opening a thread marks it read server-side, but the `["messages", category]` react-query cache never learned about it (fresh server `initialData` is ignored when a cache entry exists). Within the 30s `staleTime`, a just-read row still rendered bold under "New For You" when returning to the list.

## What's included

- **Loading skeletons for every mail view** — per-route `loading.tsx` for all 13 list views, 8 thread-detail (`[id]`) routes, and compose. A shared `MailListSkeleton` / `ThreadSkeleton` renders the real masthead (eyebrow + serif title) instantly with shimmer rows below, so navigation reads as "arrived, content loading". New `Skeleton` primitive in `ui/` uses the design-system `animate-shimmer` sweep (DESIGN.md: skeletons shimmer, they don't pulse) and semantic tokens, so it themes for free.
- **Optimistic active tab** — `MobileTabBar` tracks a `pendingHref` set on tap (tabs, More-sheet items, Settings, Admin) and cleared on pathname change; the tapped tab highlights terracotta immediately.
- **Optimistic read-state** — `MessageRow` gains an `onOpen` callback; `InfiniteMessageList` writes `isRead` into the query cache when a thread is opened and decrements the tab-bar unread badge by the thread's actual unread *message* count (badge counts are per-message, not per-thread; first real user of the existing `badgeUpdate()` helper). The cache write is deferred 300ms: react-query updates are urgent while navigation is a transition, so an immediate write would visibly regroup the row into "Previously Seen" before the thread skeleton takes over.

## Usage

No user-facing configuration — behavior change only. On mobile (and desktop sidebar navigation), switching views now shows the destination masthead + skeleton immediately, and the tapped tab highlights at once. Reading a thread unbolds the row and decrements the badge without waiting for the next sync refresh.

## Configuration

None. No new environment variables, dependencies, or schema changes.

## Notes

- Verified visually against a local dev server over CDP with an iPhone-sized viewport: pending-tab highlight and the Screener/list skeletons captured mid-navigation; thread open and archive list render correctly after.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint 0 errors, all 812 tests pass.
- searchParams-only updates (typing in search) do not re-trigger `loading.tsx`, so search behavior is unchanged.
- Known leftovers (pre-existing, not touched): the More-sheet unmounts abruptly on drag-dismiss (no exit animation); `contacts/[id]` has no tailored loading state (falls back to the contacts list skeleton).

author: abhi1992002
body:
### Why / What / How

**Why.** AutoPilot's baseline copilot path runs one expensive model for both planning *and* every tool-call round. For multi-step requests that means the top-tier model does a lot of cheap, mechanical tool orchestration — costly and not obviously better. This PR lets us split the work so the expensive model plans once and a cheaper model executes, then measure whether that holds quality at lower cost.

**What.** A two-phase **planner → executor** architecture on the baseline path, gated by the `copilot-planner-executor` LaunchDarkly flag. When the flag is on for a user and the message looks multi-step:
1. **Planner** (advanced model, Opus by default) makes one call and returns a structured `Plan` (steps, tools, success criteria).
2. **Executor** (standard model, Sonnet by default) runs the normal tool-call loop with the plan injected into its system prompt.
3. **Re-plan** escalation revises the plan (bounded per turn) when the executor stalls — an explicit `[[REPLAN]]` signal or a run of consecutive tool failures.

Everything **fails open** to today's single-loop path: flag off, non-multi-step message, or any planner error all leave `plan = None` and the path stays byte-identical to current behaviour.

**How.**
- New `copilot/planner/` package: `models.py` (Plan / usage / token-breakdown Pydantic models), `service.py` (`generate_plan`, `plan_to_executor_prompt`), `triggering.py` (multi-step heuristic), `replan.py` (`ReplanController`, bounded at `MAX_REPLANS`).
- Per-role models resolved via `copilot-model-routing[planner|executor]` LD cells with config fallbacks (`planner_model` / `executor_model`), following the existing `title_model` / `simulation_model` precedent, including the local-Ollama rewrite.
- Plan is appended to the **end** of the executor system prompt (after the session-stable suffix) so the per-session plan doesn't bust the cross-user cached prefix.
- Planner + re-plan tokens/cost are folded into the turn totals (same `StreamUsage` / billing path as the executor) and also bucketed separately via `token_breakdown()` for A/B measurement.
- Observability: `observability.py` best-effort Langfuse span helpers; one root span per turn plus per-tool spans, a `planner-split` trace tag, and per-phase token/cost metadata.
- Plan is persisted on `ChatSessionMetadata.plan` (JSON column default, no migration).

### Changes 🏗️

- **New** `copilot/planner/` module (models, planner service, triggering, re-plan controller) + tests.
- **New** `copilot/observability.py` — Langfuse span helpers (degrade to no-op).
- **New** `copilot/eval/planner_executor_suite.py` — eval harness for the A/B comparison.
- **Flag** `copilot-planner-executor` added to `Flag` enum; `is_planner_executor_enabled` resolver in `model_router.py`.
- **Config**: `planner_model`, `executor_model`, `planner_executor_enabled` fields. `planner_executor_enabled` **defaults to `True` while under active testing** (the LD flag still governs per-user rollout when LD is reachable; env override `CHAT_PLANNER_EXECUTOR_ENABLED`).
- **Baseline** `baseline/service.py`: planner phase, executor model swap, plan-into-prompt injection, bounded re-plan between rounds, per-phase token accounting, trace spans.
- `model.py`: `ChatSessionMetadata.plan` field.

> **Note:** this is a **draft** — `planner_executor_enabled` defaults to `True` deliberately for testing/eval. Flip back to `False` (flag-only rollout) before marking ready for review.

### Checklist 📋

#### For code changes:
- [x] I have clearly listed my changes in the PR description
- [x] I have made a test plan
- [ ] I have tested my changes according to the test plan:
  - [x] Unit tests for planner models, service, triggering, re-plan controller, model router, config (`poetry run pytest backend/copilot/planner backend/copilot/model_router_test.py backend/copilot/config_test.py::TestPlannerExecutorConfig` — green)
  - [x] Baseline path suite passes with the split wired in (`backend/copilot/baseline/`)
  - [ ] Manual: multi-step AutoPilot prompt with the flag ON — confirm one planner call then executor tool loop (Langfuse `planner-split` trace) and a coherent result
  - [ ] Manual: flag OFF — confirm behaviour is unchanged vs current baseline
  - [ ] Manual: force a stall (repeated tool failure) — confirm bounded re-plan then best-effort continue

#### For configuration changes:
- [ ] `.env.default` is updated or already compatible with my changes
- [x] `docker-compose.yml` is updated or already compatible with my changes
- [x] I have included a list of my configuration changes in the PR description (under **Changes**)

Config vars: `CHAT_PLANNER_MODEL`, `CHAT_EXECUTOR_MODEL`, `CHAT_PLANNER_EXECUTOR_ENABLED` (all optional, sensible defaults). New LD flag `copilot-planner-executor` and LD routing cells `copilot-model-routing[planner|executor]`.

body:
## Schema gate — Cycle J-D platform half (FEAT-PD005). HELD: not merged, not applied, awaiting the nod.

**Migration `20260708150000`: no new tables, columns, indexes, RLS policies, or triggers.** One `consent_purposes` catalog row (data), one internal read-standing helper, two contract re-issues (`get_player_state`, `get_my_enrollments`), two new SECURITY DEFINER contracts (`set_journey_progress_sharing`, `get_group_journey_progress`). No permission seeding (see Q2).

### The board — Q1–Q9 (defaults recommended; a "yes to all" applies them as written)

1. **Contract shape.** One read (`get_group_journey_progress`) serving JRN-16+17 in one payload, one consent write, one additive `get_player_state` re-issue. One gate, one payload to keep honest.
2. **Role gate — revised by live evidence.** The decomposition assumed a NEW permission; the live catalog already carries the pair, template-wired (Steward + Guide) with **97 instantiated role grants**: `view_group_progress` ("View aggregated group progress") admits the window; `view_others_progress` ("View other members' journey progress") additionally opens per-member marks. The migration seeds nothing and uses the catalog's own grain. 42501 for members without the base key; P0002 conceals for non-members.
3. **Consent mechanism — refined to Amendment-1 conventions.** `journey_progress_visibility` joins the `consent_purposes` catalog (withdrawable, `policy_version` server-stamped); flips ride the house `decision` column, append-only, latest-wins **per enrolment** via `capture_context.enrollment_id`; PC007's effective-state idempotency kept. Accepted wrinkle: `get_own_consent_state()`'s per-purpose projection stays coarse for this enrolment-scoped purpose — the precise per-walk state is `get_player_state.progress_sharing`; the history stays exact.
4. **Aggregate basis.** Sharing members only, with `members_meta {total, sharing}` serving the honesty label. Aggregating over everyone is refused on invariant-4 grounds (a count over a two-member party is a member's data).
5. **No timing in leader reads, v1.** Completion marks only. The red suite bans every timing-shaped key by regex — including any `*_at` key — across the whole progress payload.
6. **Non-sharing members' representation.** Listed (membership is already group-visible) with exactly `{member_group_id, display_name, sharing: false}` — nothing else, and excluded from every aggregate number. Pinned by an exhaustive payload-key walk.
7. **Freeze surfacing.** Additive `freeze {reason, frozen_at}` on `get_player_state`, verbatim from `progress_data` (open vocabulary — all four live reasons render; unknown reasons fall back surface-side). No backfill, no normalization.
8. **Closed-vs-archived last-leader asymmetry — disposition: working-as-intended.** Demonstrated both ways by the suite (green pin): a raw last-leader-role delete is admitted on a `closed` group (native `RETURN OLD` bypass in `prevent_last_leader_removal`), refused on `archived` ("Cannot remove the last Steward") — `delete_group` scopes its own bypass to the transaction-local `app.hard_delete_in_progress` flag, so last-leader protection stays in force for any other archived-group mutation. Closed = ran its course; archived = deliberately-retired tombstone. Recorded here per the Groups-plan verbatim commitment; no fix.
9. **Lived-record read standing (found by the decomposition payload walk; the J-C bridge routed this interplay here).** Two of the four freeze reasons exist because membership ended; today the departed traveller gets P0002 on their own frozen walk (demonstrated: the two intended-red Q9 tests). Default: **reads only** — `get_player_state` + the `get_my_enrollments` via-group arm admit a caller whose own instances live on a **frozen** enrolment; every write keeps the unchanged gate; non-frozen enrolments keep membership-only (rejoin restores — the J-C truth stands everywhere else).

### Dev pre-check evidence (live, 2026-07-08)

- Enrolments: **8 active / 3 completed / 7 withdrawn / 0 frozen** — the freeze block, Q9 loosening, and progress read affect zero existing rows.
- Consent purposes in flight: `transcendence`, `product_analytics` only — the new key collides with nothing.
- Permission catalog: `view_group_progress` + `view_others_progress` present, 2 template wirings each, 97 instantiated role grants each (the Q2 evidence).
- Red-suite pinned cascade truths: MEM-5/6 freeze the member's own self-enrolments in the group's non-public journeys (`removed_from_group`/`left_group`); MEM-8/GRP-9 freeze the group-level enrolment (`group_closed`/`group_archived`); **`active` rows only — a `completed` enrolment is never swept**; frozen = read-OK/write-P0001.

### Red suite (lead-verified first-hand)

`hub/tests/integration/journeys/journey-group-progress-frozen-contracts.test.ts` — **27 tests: 15 red / 12 green pins.** Reds: 10 missing-function (PGRST202), 3 missing-key, 2 Q9 intended-red (today's standing gate, evidence above). Pins: 7 freeze-cascade truths, Q8 both-ways, append-only 42501 (UPDATE + DELETE), `get_player_state` byte-shape (additive-tolerant), house-path erasure (`erase_fim_account`, DeusEx-called). Siblings **88/88** untouched. Lead fixes at the join: the Q8 role lookup made permission-derived (role instances take template names — name-matching found nothing, the exact anti-pattern the tier rules ban), two Q9 test names now state their assertions.

### ADR-U038 direct-caller answers

- `set_journey_progress_sharing`: a direct PostgREST caller (incl. an anonymous-session Mist) can only append their OWN consent row for this one catalogued purpose, policy-version server-stamped, on an enrolment they have traveller standing on; P0001 on solo; no UPDATE/DELETE path exists (append-only trigger untouched).
- `get_group_journey_progress`: membership, permission, and consent shaping all enforced in-function; `journey_steps`/`journey_step_instances`/`consent_records` remain contract-only at the row layer — nothing widens.

### Apply commands (post-nod)

```
node scripts/apply-migration-temp.js 20260708150000_feat_pd005_group_progress_sharing_frozen_contracts.sql
bash supabase-cli.sh migration repair --status applied 20260708150000
npm run test:integration:journeys   # expect 27/27 + siblings green
```

Then: merge this PR, full sweep, Hub half (TASK-JD-03/04), E2E close-out (TASK-JD-05).

author: moloka-store
body:
## Qué cambia

El trackeador usaba `comision_pct`/`comision_envio` de la ficha como fuente principal, pero la pestaña **Rotación** antepone la **comisión/envío efectivos de las transacciones** (`app_datos → clave 'rentabilidad' → venta_actual[asin]`). Este PR alinea el snapshot con Rotación.

### Nuevo orden de la cascada (SOLO ES)
1. **`real_tx`** → `app_datos.contenido.venta_actual[asin]`: `comision_pct_mediana` (comisión) y `envio_mediana` (envío)
2. **`real`** → `comision_pct` / `comision_envio` (ficha `productos`)
3. **`keepa_bd`** → `comision_pct_keepa_es` / `keepa_fba_fee_es`
4. **`keepa_csv`** → `ref_pct` / `Tarifa FBA Pick&Pack` (CSV de Keepa)

**IT/FR** se quedan **como estaban** (ficha → keepa): el dato real de transacciones es solo-ES (`rentabilidad.json` es solo-ES).

## Detalle técnico
- **Nuevo lector `leer_venta_actual_supabase(sb)`** en `moloka_tracker_snapshot.py`: lee la tabla `app_datos` (`clave='rentabilidad'`, campo `contenido`) y devuelve por ASIN `{comision_pct_mediana, envio_mediana}`. Si `app_datos` no está disponible, avisa y devuelve `{}` (degrada a la cascada anterior).
- **`construir_snapshots(..., venta_tx=None)`**: acepta el dict de transacciones y solo lo aplica si `pais == 'ES'`.
- **Auditoría**: `comision_fuente`/`fee_fuente` pueden valer ahora **`real_tx`** (además de `real` | `keepa_bd` | `keepa_csv` | `null`).
- **Unidades**: `comision_pct_mediana` ya viene en porcentaje (15.04); la normalización existente (`< 1 → ×100`) lo deja igual. `envio_mediana` en euros.
- **Wiring**: tanto el CLI (`main`) como el wrapper de nube (`moloka_tracker_snapshot_nube.py`) leen `venta_actual` y lo pasan a `construir_snapshots`.

## Verificación (test directo, precio 18,99 €, PVD 1 €, IVA 21 %)
**ES** (con `venta_tx` solo para el ASIN `TX`):

| ASIN | com_usada | fuente com | fee | fuente fee | margen |
|------|-----------|-----------|-----|-----------|--------|
| TX | 15.04 | **real_tx** | 3.81 | **real_tx** | 41.03 % |
| FICHA | 15.5 | real | 2.0 | real | 50.09 % |
| KEEPABD | 15.5 | keepa_bd | 5.0 | keepa_bd | 34.29 % |
| CSV | 15.03 | keepa_csv | 9.99 | keepa_csv | 8.5 % |

**IT** (mismo `venta_tx`): NO usa `real_tx` → fuente `real` (`comision_pct_it`/`envio_it`). ✓

## Alcance
- Solo `moloka_tracker_snapshot.py` y `moloka_tracker_snapshot_nube.py` (el wiring del wrapper era necesario para que el robot lo use). Nada más tocado; la fórmula y la tabla `monitor_snapshots` no cambian de esquema.

## Nota
El robot corre en GitHub Actions con `SUPABASE_URL`/`SUPABASE_KEY`, que ya dan acceso a `app_datos` (la misma vía que usa la app). No hace falta ningún secret nuevo.

author: openrung-admin
body:
## What

PR B of the telemetry storage upgrade (follows #22). When `OPENRUNG_TELEMETRY_STORE=postgres`, the admin dashboard's overview and sessions endpoints now aggregate in SQL over `telemetry_events` instead of loading every record in the window into Go — and the broker no longer holds telemetry records in memory in postgres mode at all. JSONL mode (the dev/self-host default) is untouched. Retention/partition drops remain PR C.

## Design

**Query abstraction** — the dashboard consumes a new `TelemetryQuerier` interface mirroring its two admin API endpoints (`TelemetryOverview(now, window)` and `TelemetrySessions(now, window, offset, limit)`). The JSONL path is an adapter running the unchanged `buildTelemetryOverview` over its `TelemetryReader`; `NewServer` wraps `Config.TelemetryReader` automatically, so existing embedders keep working. Response JSON shapes are byte-compatible — `dashboard.html` needed no changes.

**SQL aggregation** — a handful of readable queries sharing two CTEs (`events` extracts the payload fields, `sessions` groups per session), always bounded by the dashboard window. `received_at` prunes the daily partitions, widened by the ingest clock-skew allowance so the `occurred_at` filter (what the in-memory path keys on) loses nothing. The subtle accumulator semantics are reproduced: latest-non-empty attribute wins ordered by `(received_at, occurred_at)`, the `android_api`/`ios_version` OS fallbacks, `country_code` fallback, source-IP preference (client_seen-observed > reported `client_ip` > any transport source), cumulative byte MAXima, last `connection_ended` duration with heartbeat-running fallback, status precedence, and heartbeat-based activity against `activeSessionTimeout`.

**Drift-proofing** — everything stylistic happens in shared Go code on both paths: the per-session finalization (`sessionAccumulator.finalize`), `sortedCounts` top-10 tiebreaks, relay ranking, and speed-test ordering are extracted and used by both backends. SQL returns raw grouped rows; Go assembles them exactly like the in-memory aggregator does.

**Stopgap removal** — `PostgresTelemetrySink` no longer keeps the PR-A retained set or does the startup backfill; startup reads no old events. The small write buffer for batched INSERTs stays, and dashboard queries flush it first so just-ingested events are visible. The sink still implements `TelemetryReader` — the periodic network-status log in `cmd/broker/main.go` consumes it over a 5-minute window — but as a short-window SELECT, not memory.

## Testing

- **Parity tests** (the core of the PR): one synthetic event set covering attribute precedence, multi-client sessions, status transitions, byte maxima, running-vs-final duration, IP preference, events occurring after "now", events received before the window opened (partition-pruning margin), and speed tests — pushed through both backends, asserting **byte-identical JSON** for the overview across the 1h/24h/7d windows and for paginated sessions (first/middle/tail/beyond-total pages), plus an empty-window case.
- Postgres-backed tests follow the existing `OPENRUNG_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` skip-guard convention; reworked PR-A tests cover the SQL-backed reader (window-bounded, flush-before-read, cross-instance read-back).
- Full `go test ./internal/broker/` against a real Postgres 16 (including `-race` and `-count=2`), `gofmt`, `go vet`, whole-repo suite.
- Manual smoke test: broker booted with `OPENRUNG_TELEMETRY_STORE=postgres` + dashboard token; login, `/admin/api/telemetry/overview`, and `/admin/api/telemetry/sessions` all served correct SQL-aggregated data for freshly ingested events.

## Out of scope

Retention/partition dropping (PR C), the ingestion API, further write-path changes, anything deploy-related.
