author: mylordkaz
body:
## Summary

The max-from-the-phone phase: capture everything the phone delivers, never lose a lap, and render a continuous line per lap from phone GPS alone. Docs: `docs/line-continuity.md`, `docs/kalman/phase-2-imu-fusion.md`, `docs/telemetry_improvements.md`.

**Confirmed on device** (TestFlight, 2026-07-20): all 13 laps of the 2026-07-19 Tsukuba session render as continuous lines starting and ending exactly on the start/finish line, no overlap. Timing consistency against the circuit transponder: clean laps within 64 ms (mean 25 ms), best lap within 2 ms — on a day the transponder itself missed two passings that trakio caught.

### Line continuity (Fixes A, B, C)

The 2026-07-19 Tsukuba session (13 laps) proved the mid-session line holes are **self-inflicted**: the capture quarantine caught 4 m-accuracy fixes rejected straight through both holes because one displaced-but-accepted fix had become the jump-filter anchor (implied 138/188 km/h steps vs reported 51/78; the rejected chain matches reported speeds).

- **A — display merges the quarantine** (`mergeQuarantinedPoints`): render-time, read-only, applies to every stored session with quarantine data. All 13 laps single-segment (was: laps 1–2 with holes).
- **B — capture cascade re-anchor** (`JUMP_REANCHOR_ENABLED`): a second consecutive `impossible_jump` consistent with the previously rejected sample re-anchors onto the rejected chain. Merged-stream replay: cascade holes 5.0 s → 2.0 s, lap times within 1 ms of device — timing untouched.
- **C — laps clipped at the crossing line**: each lap starts and ends exactly at its own S/F crossing (boundary segment intersected with the line, the detector's own geometry via `segmentTimingLineFraction`); consecutive laps share the clip point. Every rendered lap endpoint 0.00 m from the line (13/13 July, 14/14 April), overlap impossible by construction.

Invariant held throughout: lap timing and line rendering are decoupled — no display work influences a lap time.

### Crossing recovery — never lose a lap

Hole-spanning segments (> 4 s) crossing the gate extension within the measured ±1.25 margin recover the crossing, flagged `≈`. `bench/recovery-acceptance.ts`: all four real sessions byte-stable flag on/off; masked boundaries **0/14 laps lost at 8 s and 11 s** (was up to 14/14); pit-lane, gate-edge, and parked-jitter synthetics correct.

### Capture everything

- IMU capture at 50 Hz (`imu_samples`, migration v14) — 49.5 Hz delivered, 100% field coverage.
- GPS quarantine (`rejected_gps_points`, migration v15) — every rejected fix stored with its reason.
- Export v3 carries both; `bench/imu-quality.ts` classifies every hole as TRUE SILENCE vs SELF-INFLICTED.

### Estimation bench + phone-IMU verdict

Masked-GPS baseline locked on the April session (11 s mask = every lap lost, naive). Fusion prototype passes all synthetic mechanics checks (11 s accelerating mask: 1 ms vs naive 1058 ms). **On real captures the phone path is killed**: CoreMotion's own filter absorbs sustained acceleration into its gravity estimate, so bridged trajectories err 57–131 m vs the ≤12 m requirement. Shipping behavior stays honest: naive + `≈` flags. The bench (`bench/replay.ts` production-fidelity replays, `bench/mask.ts`, `bench/reconstruct.ts`) remains the standing harness for any future estimator.

## Test plan

- [x] `bench/continuity-validation.ts` — A/B/C checks pass on the real sessions (endpoints on the line, shared clip points, cascades shrunk, lap times ±1 ms)
- [x] `bench/recovery-acceptance.ts` — full table green
- [x] jest 43/43, `tsc` clean, lint 0 errors
- [x] Replays of all four real sessions reproduce stored lap times within 2 ms
- [x] On-device TestFlight validation at Tsukuba (2026-07-19 session + 2026-07-20 build): continuous per-lap lines, clipped at the line, timing verified against the circuit transponder

body:
## Description
Rewrite the model guidance in go/cmd/ralph/prompts/task-manager.md and go/cmd/ralph/prompts/bead-creation.md so the task manager always sets explicit model metadata on every bead and never presents or relies on an implicit default.

In task-manager.md, section 'Model reference': replace the two-branch guidance (set model=sonnet for mechanical work / 'Leave the metadata unset' for judgment work) with: set model explicitly on EVERY bd create — model=sonnet for mechanical, fully-specified work; model=opus for judgment, design, multi-file reasoning, or diagnosis. Remove the claim that working_model is 'typically opus' — it is factually wrong: the built-in default is ModelSonnet (flags.go, ConfigKey working_model), overridable per project in .ralph/config.toml. If the prompt mentions the fallback at all, it must instruct reading the project's .ralph/config.toml working_model rather than assuming a value. This caused a real incident: the task manager echoed 'default (opus)' for judgment beads that would actually have run on sonnet.

In the same file, update the 'Create (always owned)' command bullet and the release-gate echo passage ('model: default (working_model)') to match: the echo always states the concrete model set on the bead.

In bead-creation.md, echo-back rule: the Model column shows the explicitly set model; remove 'or `default` when unset' and change the example tables (create/update/close/multi-bead) to show concrete models (sonnet/opus), never 'default'.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. task-manager.md 'Model reference' instructs setting explicit model metadata on every bd create (sonnet for mechanical, opus for judgment work); no 'leave the metadata unset' guidance remains anywhere in prompts/.
2. The 'typically opus' claim is gone; any mention of the working_model fallback states the built-in default is sonnet and that .ralph/config.toml can override it, and instructs checking config rather than assuming.

author: michaelmkraus
body:
## Proposed changes

resolves #6879

The accordion was styled incorrectly compared to the Figma design:

- **Divider variant** (and the default, which Figma labels "(Def) Divider") rendered a `level-1` background on the summary → should be `transparent-full`.
- **Card variant** rendered a `level-1` summary but left the expanded content area transparent while open → the whole card should be `level-1`.

### Root cause

The `summary` background was hardcoded to `level-1` for **every** accordion item in `accordion-item.scss`, regardless of variant (introduced in #3263 as a blanket fix for the card variant). Because `data-variant` lives on the `.db-accordion` (`<ul>`) while the background was set on the variant-agnostic `.db-accordion-item`, the item styling could not distinguish variants, and the fill only covered the summary — not the open content area.

### Fix

- `accordion-item.scss`: base `summary` background → `transparent-full` (default/hover/pressed), the correct divider/default appearance.
- `accordion.scss`: scoped the `level-1` fill to `[data-variant="card"]`, applied to the whole `.db-accordion-item` (summary + open content), with `level-1` hover/pressed states on the summary.

This fixes the cause at the source rather than swapping symptom values, and also corrects the default variant.

### Validation

- `pnpm run build` passes; compiled CSS confirms divider → `transparent-full`, card → `level-1`.
- `stylelint` on both changed files passes.
- Playwright screenshot snapshots intentionally not regenerated locally (handled in CI).
- Visual comparison against Figma still recommended as a final check.

## Checklist

- [x] I have reviewed my own code (self-review), including the screen- and snapshots

author: jhosm
body:
## In plain English

Backstage now stores its catalogue in a lightweight in-process database (SQLite, in-memory) instead of a separate PostgreSQL pod — saving memory on the 16GB demo box. Its state is rebuilt from the catalogue baked into the image on every start, so nothing is lost. This tears the old `backstage-db` pod out completely — its Deployment, PVC, network policy, backup, and volume-snapshot references all go with it.

## Summary

- `infra/backstage/app-config.yaml` — database → `better-sqlite3` / `:memory:` (baked into the image; re-triggers the backstage image build on merge via the `infra/backstage/**` path filter).
- `infra/k8s/base/backstage.yaml` — delete the `backstage-db` Service + Deployment; real image `ghcr.io/jhosm/babelstone-backstage:latest`; drop the `BACKSTAGE_PG_*` env and the flat catalog ConfigMap mount (the tree is baked in, PR #483).
- `infra/k8s/base/kustomization.yaml` — drop the catalog-descriptor generator.
- staging overlay — delete `backstage-db-pvc.yaml` + `backstage-db-storage.patch.yaml`; sweep every downstream reference: `network-policies.yaml` (drop `allow-backstage-db-ingress`, renumber), `backup-cronjobs.yaml` (drop the backstage `pg_dump`), `volume-snapshot-cronjob.yaml` (drop the `backstage-db` PVC), `resources.patch.yaml`, `cd-deploy-rbac.yaml` comments.
- docs — `infra/README.md`, `infra/k8s/README.md`, `infra/runbooks/staging-ops.md` updated to the SQLite reality (no `backstage-db`).
- `infra/compose.yaml` — remove the compose `backstage-db` service.

Rebased on current `main` (resolved the `network-policies.yaml` + `README.md` overlap with the Logto admin-console change `4f37529` — kept both: the Logto 3002 admin-console allow **and** the backstage-db policy removal, with clean policy renumbering).

**Supersedes #486 and #487** (branch/PR churn from a topology pivot + a mistaken "minimal" detour). This is the correct full teardown, rebased and green.

## Testing

`kustomize build --load-restrictor=LoadRestrictionsNone <overlay> | kubeconform -strict -kubernetes-version 1.31.0` — all green: base 26, overlays/ha 38, overlays/staging 70 valid, 0 errors. No `backstage-db` workload in any render. `docker compose -f infra/compose.yaml config -q` parses.

## ADRs touched/honoured

- **ADR-IC-015** — no-drift held: SQLite is only Backstage's rendering store; the baked `/catalog` descriptor stays the sole catalogue source, restating no schema. The flat-ConfigMap mount is superseded by the baked tree (clause 9's own handoff).
- **ADR-IC-016** — zero-trust posture: complete teardown, no dangling allow-rule / snapshot target / backup reference (adr-conformance-verified).
- **ADR-PC-004 §A1** — the DB credential is *removed* entirely (SQLite has no auth); the secret surface shrinks.
- SQLite topology is the maintainer's explicit resource-driven call on bd zla1.6.1 (no ADR — an infra sizing choice contradicting no Accepted Decision).

## bd issues closed on merge

- Closes babelstone-zla1.6.6

author: ashwani573
body:
## Summary

- Migrates 6 `ciphertrust_cm_key` attributes from package-local modifier types (`StringImmutableModifier`, `Int64ImmutableModifier`, `NameImmutableModifier`) to the shared `modifiers.ImmutableString()` / `modifiers.ImmutableInt64()` implementations in `internal/provider/modifiers`, standardising the diagnostic title to `"Attribute is immutable"` across all immutable fields.
- Adds `modifiers.ImmutableX()` plan modifiers to 33 additional `ciphertrust_cm_key` attributes that are absent from the CM `PatchKey` PATCH body but had no prior enforcement, so Terraform now emits a plan-time error rather than letting CM silently ignore or reject the change at apply time.
- Prepends `(Immutable)` to the `Description` of all 39 affected attributes so the constraint surfaces in `terraform providers schema` output and generated docs.
- Adds 11 acceptance-test functions to `internal/provider/resource_cm_key_test.go` covering `ImmutableString`, `ImmutableInt64`, `ImmutableBool`, and `ImmutableObject` modifier scenarios, plus two mutable-field scenarios confirming no unintended regressions.

## Motivation

Implements TFIN-271: Apply plan modifier to immutable fields for key resource in Group D.

The `ciphertrust_cm_key` resource had two related gaps. First, 6 attributes used ad-hoc, package-local modifier types that emitted field-specific diagnostic titles (`"'algorithm' cannot be changed"`, `"Name cannot be changed"`) rather than the provider-wide `"Attribute is immutable"` title used by every other resource. Second, 33 additional creation-only attributes — absent from the CM PATCH body — had no modifier at all. Users could change those attributes in their Terraform config, observe a successful `terraform plan`, and then receive an unexpected CM API error at apply time. This change catches such mistakes at plan time and gives a clear, actionable message.

## What changed

### Modified file — `internal/provider/cm/resource_cm_key.go`

Adds `"github.com/ThalesGroup/terraform-provider-ciphertrust/internal/provider/modifiers"` to the import block.

**6 attributes migrated from local modifier to shared modifier:**

| Attribute | Type | Old modifier | New modifier | Old diagnostic title |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `algorithm` | String | `StringImmutableModifier{FieldName: "algorithm"}` | `modifiers.ImmutableString()` | `'algorithm' cannot be changed` |

author: sheldon-nadarajah-sft
body:
## Problem

Datadog flamegraphs for AWS Lambda functions with SnapStart enabled can render as a multi-hour (or multi-day) empty timeline with the actual work squeezed into a tiny sliver at each end — even though the real invocation took under a second.

We tracked this down from a production trace on a Java Lambda function with SnapStart enabled: the parent `aws.lambda` span was timestamped correctly (`13:42:21Z`), but its 18 DynamoDB child spans — created by this tracer's AWS SDK instrumentation during the same invocation — were all timestamped `11:45:25Z`, ~1h57m *earlier*. Correlating against CloudWatch logs for that invocation confirmed the DynamoDB spans' timestamp landed squarely inside the *original snapshot-creation* `platform.initStart` window (when the SnapStart snapshot was published), not anywhere near the actual `platform.restoreStart`/invocation time that ran ~2 hours later.

## Root cause

`CoreTracer` computes every span's timestamp from a cached reference pair — `startTimeNano`/`startNanoTicks` — captured once at construction, plus a monotonic-tick delta (`getTimeWithNanoTicks()`). It self-corrects drift periodically, but that correction is gated on **monotonic ticks elapsed** (`nanoTicks - lastSyncTicks >= clockSyncPeriod`, default 30s), not wall-clock time elapsed.

AWS Lambda SnapStart checkpoints the JVM at snapshot-creation time and later *restores* a new execution environment from that snapshot — potentially hours or days later, on different hardware. `System.nanoTime()` does not account for that gap: the restored instance's monotonic clock has no relationship to real elapsed time since the snapshot. A short-lived restore-then-invoke sequence (our production case: restore → invocation within ~14s) never accumulates 30 seconds of monotonic ticks, so the periodic correction never fires, and every span stays anchored near the original snapshot-creation instant.

This is a real, reproducible bug — not a config mistake on the user's side — and it's specific to SnapStart's restore-into-a-new-context semantics: a regular (non-SnapStart) Lambda container merely pauses/resumes the *same* continuously-existing process between invocations, which does not exhibit this clock discontinuity.

## Fix

Resync the cached clock reference from `CoreTracer.notifyLambdaStart()` — already invoked once per Lambda invocation, before any span for that invocation is created (see `LambdaHandlerInstrumentation`'s `@OnMethodEnter` advice, which calls it immediately before the first `startSpan(...)` call). Any real SnapStart restore is always followed by an invocation, so resyncing there catches it without needing to react to the restore event itself.

This is gated behind a new, **opt-in, disabled-by-default** config, `DD_TRACE_LAMBDA_SNAPSTART_CLOCK_RESYNC_ENABLED`. Doing this on every invocation (not just ones following a restore) is deliberate: outside SnapStart there's no clock bug to fix (see above), so it's a correct, cheap no-op there — a few volatile field writes, negligible next to the HTTP round-trip `notifyLambdaStart` already makes to the Lambda extension.

## Alternatives considered

- **Lower `DD_TRACE_CLOCK_SYNC_PERIOD` globally.** The periodic correction is clamped to a 1ms floor regardless of configured value, so setting it to `0` does mitigate most of this today, with zero code changes, and users hitting this can do so immediately. We didn't pursue this as *the* fix because it's a blanket per-tracer-instance setting affecting every span for every user, not just Lambda SnapStart ones, and it only shrinks the bad window rather than eliminating it.
- **A CRaC (`org.crac`) `afterRestore` hook**, reacting to the actual restore event via the JVM checkpoint/restore SPI. We built and tested this first, but self-review turned up real problems specific to that approach: it requires a new runtime dependency that, in our build, ended up shipping a second unrelocated copy of `org.crac` in the shaded agent jar (a class that, it turns out, is *already* present unrelocated via an existing transitive dependency — likely Spring, given Spring Framework 6.1+ ships its own CRaC integration and is a common SnapStart audience); it published `this` from mid-constructor into a JVM-wide static registry; and the registered callback fired on an arbitrary async thread with no test coverage of the actual registration path. The `notifyLambdaStart` hook needs no new dependency, fires deterministically on a known thread at a well-defined point in the invocation lifecycle, and is already exercised by existing Lambda instrumentation tests.

## Known limitation

The resync writes `startTimeNano`/`startNanoTicks`/`lastSyncTicks`/`counterDrift` as four independent volatile fields with no encompassing lock, so a concurrent reader (e.g. the background trace-buffer flush thread) could in principle observe a partially-updated combination. This isn't a new class of risk introduced here: `getTimeWithNanoTicks()`'s existing periodic self-correction already updates `counterDrift` and `lastSyncTicks` independently today, with the same eventual-consistency trade-off (a worst-case redundant correction on the next call). We didn't expand scope to refactor that pre-existing pattern into an atomic holder for this fix, but flagging it here for visibility.

## Testing

- `CoreTracerTest`: a test characterizing the underlying bug in isolation (`getTimeWithNanoTicks` with a stale `nanoTicks` reading stays anchored to construction time), plus tests exercising the real fix end-to-end through `notifyLambdaStart()` — resync happens when explicitly enabled, and (the default) does not happen when left disabled.
- Verified against the original production trace/CloudWatch log timeline that motivated this fix.

korean-law-mcp를 검토해 KOICA 규정 도구에 유익한 3개 기능을 이식하고, 자동 동기화를 브랜치 보호에 맞게 개선합니다.

## 신규/개선 기능
### 1. `compliance_radar` — 규정 정비 레이더 (신규 도구)
시행세칙·지침의 모(母)규정을 이름 규칙/제1조 인용으로 찾아 개정일을 대조 → 모규정이 더 최근이면 정비 검토 대상으로 플래그. korean-law-mcp의 조례 정비 레이더(`ordinance_radar`)를 KOICA 규정 체계(규정↔시행세칙↔지침)에 옮긴 것.
- 현재 데이터에서 **31건 중 12건 정비 필요** 탐지 (예: 임금피크제 운영지침 2020.06 ↔ 인사규정 2026.06, ~72개월 뒤처짐)

### 2. `verify_citation` 제목 환각 탐지
기존엔 조문 실존만 확인 → 이제 `인사규정 제11조(육아휴직)`처럼 **존재하는 조문번호에 엉뚱한 제목**을 붙인 환각을 `content_mismatch`로 탐지 (제목 정규화 + bigram Jaccard).

author: aaryanagrawal
body:
Problem

`RelocalizationModule` corrects `world->map` drift from lidar against a frozen
premap. A robot without lidar, or one operating where lidar degrades
(elevator cabs, glass, feature-poor corridors), has no equivalent. The nav
deep dive is explicit about the gap: "We don't have proper loop closure and
stable odometry... does drift eventually"
(docs/capabilities/navigation/deep_dive.md). This adds the same class of fix
using a camera and known fiducial markers instead of a lidar premap.

What this adds

- dimos/perception/fiducial/marker_localization.py: pure-function core.
  Known marker-map pose (map frame) + a live ArUco detection -> camera pose
  via solvePnP run in reverse, gated on reprojection error and tag count.
- dimos/perception/fiducial/marker_localization_module.py: thin Module.
  color_image In, static CameraInfo, publishes TF world->map -- the same job
  as RelocalizationModule, camera swapped in for lidar.
- dimos/perception/fiducial/test_marker_localization.py: 18 tests on real
  cv2.aruco-rendered frames at known poses, end to end through detection and
  pose recovery, plus the boundaries: empty frames, unmapped tags,
  corrupted-corner rejection, multi-tag selection, map-file errors
  (missing/malformed YAML), and config validation.

3 files, 484 insertions (181 implementation, 303 tests), no changes to
existing code.

What this reuses

create_aruco_detector, estimate_marker_pose (SOLVEPNP_IPPE_SQUARE),
camera_info_to_cv_matrices, marker_reprojection_error, and
rvec_tvec_to_transform, all from marker_pose.py -- no new detection or PnP
code. TF publish + resolve_named_path map-file loading follow
RelocalizationModule's pattern exactly.

Validation

Beyond the in-PR tests: a synthetic ground-truth harness (a rendered room,
15 wall tags, a drifting-odometry model, the same estimator running on real
cv2.aruco detections frame by frame) measures ATE 1.75 m raw odometry ->
0.33 m corrected, a 5.3x reduction. When several tags pass the gate in one
frame, the estimate with the lowest reprojection error wins, and an
order-independence regression test pins that behavior. The demo GIF below
shows the run: detections on the left, raw vs corrected trajectory on the
right. The harness is standalone and not part of this diff; happy to share
it.

![Uploading demo.gif…]()

**81% reduction in trajectory error** (ATE 1.75 m -> 0.33 m, 5.3x) on the synthetic ground-truth run shown above.

Follow-ups

Fisheye intrinsics, multi-tag weighted fusion (currently best single tag by
reprojection error), smoothing/hold-last-good, a demo blueprint + fixture
map.

Limitations

Validated on synthetic ground truth and rendered cv2.aruco frames, not yet
on a physical rig.

author: nhancdt2602
body:
## Summary

Add an optional `FORMAT (TXT | JSON)` option to the `INFO` command:

```
INFO [<section> ...] [FORMAT (TXT | JSON)]
```

- `FORMAT TXT` (the default) keeps the existing Redis-compatible text output.
- `FORMAT JSON` emits the same data as a JSON object keyed by section.

```
127.0.0.1:6666> INFO server FORMAT JSON
{"Server":{"version":"unstable","tcp_port":6666,"process_id":123,...}}
```

Closes #2302.

## Changes

- `CommandInfo`: parse the optional `FORMAT` keyword, separating it from section names.
- `InfoEntry`: store each value as a typed `std::variant`, with `InfoEntry::ToString()` for the text form; `GetInfo` serializes to text or JSON.
- Add `TestInfoFormat` integration tests.

## Implementation Note

Each `INFO` value carries its original type in the `InfoEntry` variant `std::variant<std::string, int64_t, double, bool>`, captured in the constructors, so the collectors stay unchanged and each format renders the value at serialization time:

- **Text** (`InfoEntry::ToString`): booleans as `0/1`, numbers via `std::to_string`, strings verbatim — identical to the previous output.
- **JSON**: native types — numbers unquoted, booleans as `true/false`, strings quoted.

The `FORMAT` keyword is case-insensitive; an unknown or missing value returns `syntax error`.

## What does this PR do?
This PR implements all recent customer feedback and fixes several critical bugs, including the database connection crash due to permissions, Excel export formatting, and UI/UX improvements for database synchronization and configuration.

## What changes were made?
- [x] Added new feature
- [x] Fixed a bug
- [ ] Updated documentation
- [x] Code refactoring

### Details:
- **Critical Fix:** Filtered out system views (`dba_*`, `v$*`) in Trino queries to prevent `permission denied` crashes during background schema caching.
- **Database:** Added missing `export_filename` column to `chat_messages` table to fix a SQLAlchemy crash.
- **Excel Exports:** Auto-fit column widths in Excel exports by tracking max cell widths during streaming, and generated meaningful export filenames based on table names instead of internal Trino hashes.
- **UI/UX:** Added real-time sync status tracking (spinner and checkmark) when adding a new database.
- **UI/UX:** Added timeouts to Trino connection endpoints to prevent the UI from hanging on bad connections.
- **UI/UX:** Made database URL input fields auto-expandable (multiline) for better visibility.
- **UI/UX:** Fixed language toggle z-index/clickability and replaced the purple favicon with the new green SVG icon.
- **UI/UX:** Right-aligned number values in chat tables for better readability.

## How can this be tested?
1. Run `docker compose --profile dev up -d --build` to start the application.
2. Open the UI and add a new database connection. Observe the real-time sync animation ("Синхронизация" -> "Успешно") and test the connection with incorrect credentials to verify the timeout works without hanging.
3. Chat with the database, ask for a table with numbers, and verify that numerical columns are right-aligned.
4. Export the chat result to Excel and verify that the downloaded filename is readable (e.g., `table_name_timestamp.xlsx`) and columns are automatically sized to fit their content.
5. Verify that the language toggle button is clickable and the favicon is green.

- [x] I have updated dependencies (`requirements.txt` / `package.json`) if necessary

- Typed query -> real keyword search; results reveal one-by-one (staggered rise). Label stays honest: 'N results in the demo sample' (it searches the 5 demo videos, NOT '582' — no inflated claims).
- Chip / captured Q&A -> streams the REAL reasoned answer word-by-word with a typing caret (looks like AI thinking), then its real citation. Honest because demoQA holds actual captured Claude answers, not invented text.
- 'Ask another question' resets to the idle state.
- Respects prefers-reduced-motion (renders instantly, no typewriter).
- A new ask cancels any in-flight stream (runId guard) — no overlap.

Verified in-browser against the real demo-index.json: progressive stream (44->151->212 chars) with caret, honest search label, reduced-motion instant, ask-again resets, zero JS errors. 57 tests pass.

body:
## Scope

Focused module: production release operations / GitHub Actions maintenance.

Intended change:
- add a manual `Production Maintenance` workflow for `production` branch disk reports and safe SSH cleanup;
- allow process-only production changes such as `.github/**`, `docs/**`, `tests/**`, and `deploy/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` to skip application deploy while still running CI;
- add contract coverage that blocks unsafe Docker volume pruning and deploy-condition drift.

Explicit non-goals:
- no production application code changes;
- no database volume deletion or Docker volume prune;
- no change to Cloud runtime ownership or WordPress control-plane ownership.

## Boundary

Cloud remains hosted runtime/service-plane/detail only. The maintenance workflow is an operator path for SSH host hygiene and does not create a second WordPress control plane, ability registry, workflow registry, prompt/router truth, or WordPress write owner.

## Verification

- `pnpm run check:release-policy`
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/contract/test_deploy_config_contract.py::test_deploy_bundle_smoke_uses_sample_provider_and_skip_frontend_contract -q`

## Risk

Risk is operational and bounded. The workflow is manual, limited to `production`, bound to the `production` environment, and uses safe prune commands only: stopped containers, unused images, build cache, and old release directories outside the current symlink. It deliberately does not run `docker system prune`, `docker volume prune`, or `--volumes`.

author: ggozad
body:
`create_document_from_source` checks `get_document_by_uri` *outside* the write lock, then inserts a fresh-UUID document inside it. Two concurrent ingestions of the same URI both see `None` and both create , so the lock only serializes the inserts. In `run-batch` this is triggered by the reaper re-claiming a still-running job.

Fix: re-check `get_document_by_uri` inside the write lock in `_store_document_with_chunks`; a colliding create becomes an update. One guard covers every ingestion path.

body:
Adds Muro to **Support & Service Management**, in alphabetical order (between `michaelrice/zendesk-mcp` and `nguyenvanduocit/jira-mcp`).

**What it is:** [Muro](https://muro.chat) is a live chat widget + AI support inbox for people running multiple projects/sites. The MCP server is the official hosted remote endpoint: Streamable HTTP at `https://muro.chat/api/mcp`. The linked repo ([Muro-chat/muro-mcp](https://github.com/Muro-chat/muro-mcp)) contains the open-source stdio bridge (JavaScript, MIT), a Dockerfile, ready-to-paste client configs (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf) and the docs.

**Tools (8):** `list_conversations` (status filter + full-text search), `get_conversation`, `send_reply` (visitor reply or internal note), `update_conversation` (status/tags/assignee), `list_contacts`, `get_contact`, `list_sites`, `update_site` (widget config).

**Auth:** Bearer API keys created in the Muro dashboard, with `read`/`write` scopes; a key can be pinned to a single site so an agent only sees that project's inbox.

**Also published on the official MCP registry** as [`chat.muro/support`](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=muro).

**Format notes:** 🎖️ official + 📇 TypeScript/JavaScript + ☁️ cloud per the legend.

*Re-submission of #8468, closed after bot feedback: the entry now uses the full `owner/repo` format pointing to a public repository, as requested by the name-check bot. A Glama listing (glama-check) is being submitted in parallel via the Connectors flow.*

author: terahashalpha
body:
## SPRINT-ORDER-ONCHAIN-FLOOR — close threat-model P1a (HIGH)

**Fund-flow → needs an Auditor pass before merge.** Phase 0 = keeper-only, **no redeploy**; Phase 1 = **ADR only, no contract change/deploy**.

### Problem (P1a, from PR #277)
DCA signs `minAmountOut=1` → `TeraSwapOrderExecutor.sol:508-509` clamps the per-chunk `minOut` to **1 wei** (a no-op), with `routerDataHash=0`/`priceFeed=0`. The only economic floor was a flat **0.5% `KEEPER_SLIPPAGE`** — *self-referential* to the aggregator's own quote — over the public mempool when `FLASHBOTS_RPC_URL` was unset. A keeper compromise / route-builder bug / self-consistent manipulated quote could drain a chunk **to dust**. DCA is live on Base.

### Phase 0 — interim mitigation (implemented, keeper-only)
- **`order-floor.js`** (pure, 19 tests): reject a DCA fill whose built output is below an **independent fair-value reference × (1 − `DCA_ORACLE_FLOOR_BPS`)** (default 300 bps, clamped [50,2000]). Reference = **Chainlink for the ETH leg** (reuses the trusted `readEthUsd`), else **DefiLlama** by `chain:address`. Fully fail-safe: any reference miss ⇒ the fill is *flagged* (never a false reject). A reject **DELAYS** (unlock + retry), never force-executes — delay ≫ drain — and is not a failure (no `orderRetries`/`failed`/failure-alert). Runs before the existing #248 deviation gate; they don't conflict.
- **`submission-policy.js`** (pure, 9 tests) + fail-closed wiring: replaces the **silent** `FLASHBOTS_RPC ? flashbots : walletClient` public-mempool fallback. Base/OP-stack (8453) submit via their **private sequencer mempool**; Ethereum mainnet / unknown-prod chains **require** a private relay or the explicit `ALLOW_PUBLIC_MEMPOOL=true` override, else the fill is refused.
- **Base MEV finding:** the threat model assumed "Base has no Flashbots → sandwichable"; in fact **Base routes to a single sequencer with a private mempool** (no public pending-tx gossip), so the classic retail sandwich vector is largely absent there. The fail-closed relay requirement hardens mainnet; on Base the interim = private sequencer mempool + the oracle floor.

### Phase 1 — on-chain design (ADR only, NOT deployed)
`docs/ADR/ADR-013-order-onchain-floor.md` (Proposed) designs **OrderExecutor v3**: a real per-chunk floor from a **Chainlink read at execution within a SIGNED `maxSlippageBps`** (replace the 1-wei clamp with a **revert**); resolve `routerDataHash`; and a **Permit2-style unordered/bitmap nonce** as a prerequisite to re-wiring Limit/SL/TP (fixes latent **P1b** sequential-nonce stop-loss block and **P1c** non-DCA `routerDataHash=0` revert). Covers deploy + 48h timelock + keeper/frontend migration + Auditor pass + runbook.
> Numbered **013**: the prompt said ADR-011, but `ADR-011`/`ADR-012` already exist — used the next free number per the no-collision convention (flagged in FEEDBACK).

### Tests / scope
- Keeper `node --test`: **155 pass** (28 new: order-floor 19 + submission-policy 9), auto-gated by `keeper-tests.yml`. RED proven by moving the module aside, GREEN on restore; submission-policy written test-first. `node --check executor.js` parses.
- **No contract deployed or changed**; recipient/router/on-chain gates untouched; no `ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_KEY`, no wagmi-v3. Live end-to-end keeper verification (a sub-floor fill rejected on-chain) requires Supabase+RPC+signer and a pm2 restart on EC2 — an ops deploy step.

The shared bill kept opening Loglinkr blank with no router. Cause: some Android builds **drop the `?sharetarget=1` query** on the multipart share POST, so the service worker's query check missed and the POST fell through to a normal page load.

Now the SW matches **any same-origin POST to `/app`** (the app has no other same-origin POST navigations — all API calls go to supabase.co, which is excluded), so the share is caught regardless of the query. Also falls back to `form.getAll('bill')[0]`. Cache bumped to v14 so the SW updates.

author: paruff
body:
## Problem

PipelineProperty instances lack a dedicated service for lifecycle operations. Stage advancement, kill/hold/reactivate flows, source record resolution, and conversion to Property records are all handled ad-hoc.

## Solution

Created `core/services/pipeline.py` as the authoritative pipeline lifecycle service:

### Core Operations
- **advance_stage()** — moves to next stage, sets corresponding timestamp, saves with update_fields. Raises ValueError for KILLED/ON_HOLD/STABILIZED.
- **kill_property()** — sets status=KILLED, records kill_reason
- **hold_property()** — sets status=ON_HOLD, optional reason
- **reactivate_property()** — returns KILLED/ON_HOLD → ACTIVE at current stage

### Source Resolution
- **get_source_record()** — resolves vrm→VrmProperty, foreclosure→ForeclosureProperty, listing→Listing. Returns None for manual/unrecognised types.

### Creation from Sources
- **create_from_vrm()** — creates PipelineProperty denormalizing VrmProperty fields, runs screen_property() immediately, sets stage=SCREENING
- **create_from_foreclosure()** — same pattern, yield/PTR auto-skipped for lack of rent data

### Acquisition
- **convert_to_property_record()** — creates Property record in transaction.atomic(), sets back-link, marks pipeline as ACQUIRED. Raises ValueError on duplicate conversion.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest tests/test_pipeline_service.py`: **35 passed**
- `python -m pytest tests/test_pipeline_service.py tests/test_screening.py tests/test_pipeline.py prei/pipeline/tests/`: **323 passed**
- `python manage.py test core.tests`: **23 passed**
- Pre-commit: ruff, mypy, bandit, secrets all pass

## Risks

- Low. No new migrations, no schema changes. Depends on PIPE-1 models and PIPE-2 screening service.
- convert_to_property_record runs in transaction.atomic() — partially-applied conversions are rolled back on failure.

## Test Coverage (35 tests)

| Area | Tests |
|---|---|
| STAGE_ORDER | 3 |
| advance_stage | 6 |
| kill_property | 2 |
| hold_property | 3 |
| reactivate_property | 3 |
| get_source_record | 5 |
| create_from_vrm | 4 |
| create_from_foreclosure | 4 |
| convert_to_property_record | 5 |

Closes: PIPE-3 (Build pipeline service)

author: imantaba
body:
Adds a scan section + daemon gauge that surface **Bound PersistentVolumeClaims whose bound PersistentVolume has `reclaimPolicy: Delete`** — the data-loss-prone case where deleting the PVC or PV destroys the underlying storage.

## What it does

- New pure package `internal/pvcreclaim` — `Assess(pvcs, pvs)` flags a PVC when it is **Bound** and its bound PV (via `spec.volumeName`) has `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy == Delete`. Reclaim is read from the **bound PV** (authoritative), so a class *named* `-retain` with a Delete PV is still caught, and a PVC whose PV is missing is skipped.
- Two new read-only `collect` List calls (PVCs namespaced, PVs cluster-scoped), wired best-effort into `scan.Evaluate` (a List error yields an empty report, never fails the scan).
- Text section `PVCs with reclaim policy Delete:` + JSON `pvcReclaim`.
- Watch-daemon gauge `kubeagent_pvcs_reclaim_delete` (last-good on scan error).
- RBAC: `persistentvolumeclaims` + `persistentvolumes` `get`/`list`/`watch` in **both** `deploy/rbac.yaml` and the Helm ClusterRole — no write verb anywhere.

## Invariants

Read-only; advisory only (does not change the cluster verdict, `kubeagent_cluster_healthy`, or exit code); not wired into `--explain`; no new dependency.

## Validation

- `go build ./... && go test ./...` — all packages green (incl. non-vacuous unit tests: Bound+Delete listed, Retain skipped, unbound skipped, missing-PV skipped, empty-report section omitted).
- `helm lint` / `helm template` — RBAC renders `get, list, watch` only.
- `mkdocs build --strict` — clean.
- Opus whole-branch review — **MERGE**, 0 Critical/Important.
- **Live read-only scan on a real cluster (hetzner-nova):** flagged exactly **12** PVCs (`hcloud-volumes`), correctly skipping the `hcloud-volumes-retain` ones — matching the cluster’s 12 Delete / 30 Retain PV split.

Built via brainstorm → spec → plan → subagent-driven per-task implementation + review.

author: alu-developer
body:
## Summary
- `DownloadTracker.FilesPerSecond()`/`MBPerSecond()` divided throughput by `d.sum` (the sum of individual per-job download durations) instead of the wall-clock elapsed time of the download phase.
- When downloads are serialized behind a mutex (e.g. the browser-fallback path's `browserDownloadMu` in `scraper.go`), summed job durations can far exceed wall-clock time, making reported throughput look much worse than reality. A live run on 2026-07-08 printed `0.0 files/sec` for a run that actually achieved 0.051 files/sec wall-clock.
- Both methods now take the wall-clock `elapsed time.Duration` as a parameter; `PrintDownloadSummary` already had that value and now threads it through instead of the methods reading `d.sum` internally.
- `Sum()`/`AverageDuration()` are unchanged — per-file average duration is still a legitimate sum-based stat.

## Test plan
- [x] Updated existing tests in `internal/timing/timing_test.go` to pass an explicit wall-clock `elapsed` to `FilesPerSecond`/`MBPerSecond`, matching the new signature.
- [x] Added `TestDownloadTrackerSerializedJobsUseWallClock`: two `Record` calls each with 1s duration (2s summed) but a 500ms wall-clock `elapsed`, asserting throughput is computed as 4.0 files/sec and 4.0 MB/sec (wall-clock based) rather than 1.0 (sum based, the old buggy behavior).
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` all pass.
- [x] `scripts/dev.ps1 all` (mod tidy, fmt, vet, test, build) passes clean with no unexpected diffs.
- [x] Confirmed no other call sites of `FilesPerSecond`/`MBPerSecond` exist in the repo outside `timing.go` and `timing_test.go`.

author: unisay
body:
Refreshes the three `Plinth_1.65.0.0_Unisay_preview` submissions to the merged source at `6b75b5a` (plinth-cape-submissions PR #30). The new preview build uses the monadic typed decoder that is already the mainnet default (PRs #232 and #234), and adds one preview-only decoder change: for a cursor gap of three or more fields it emits a single `dropList` call instead of a chain of `tailList` steps. The committed preview artifacts are the older asData builds that predate both, so the refresh cuts the happy-path fee by 61 to 69% across the three scenarios.

## Result

Happy-path `total_fee_lovelace` and `script_size_bytes`, new preview vs the currently committed preview:

| Scenario | old fee | new fee | fee delta | old size | new size | size delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| htlc | 77829 | 23830 | -69.4% | 4087 | 591 | -85.5% |
| linear_vesting | 128970 | 49805 | -61.4% | 1283 | 889 | -30.7% |
| two_party_escrow | 223875 | 83342 | -62.8% | 2238 | 1495 | -33.2% |

## What changed

Each `Plinth_1.65.0.0_Unisay_preview` submission is updated in place: the `.uplc`, `metrics.json`, `metadata.json`, and `source/README.md`. The source pin moves from the old asData commits (`3efc19ad` for htlc and linear_vesting, `4b321504` for two_party_escrow) to `6b75b5a`. The compiler (Plinth 1.65.0.0, commit `b2db5126`), the `["Plinth", "BuiltinCasing"]` flags, and `min_plutus_version = 1.65.0.0` are unchanged.

`dropList` is a batch-6 builtin that PlutusV3 accepts only from the van Rossem protocol version, which is not on mainnet, so its emission is gated to the preview build (the same track as `BuiltinCasing`). The production build keeps the pure `tailList` induction and its artifacts stay byte-identical, so nothing on the mainnet lines moves here.

## Source and verification

The preview artifacts are measured with the `measure-preview` evaluator (van Rossem / PV11), since the default verifier rejects them by design (they need `plutus-core >= 1.65`). Every scenario keeps all of its expected evaluation outcomes: htlc 25/25, linear_vesting 29/29, two_party_escrow 47/47, and the happy-path measurements match the table above. Both JSON files validate against the repo schemas, and all twelve changed files are `treefmt` clean.

author: praveenvijayan
body:
Closes #13

Hardens the `plan-sync` compiler against silent frontmatter mistakes that corrupt the queue's triage order. Previously a typo'd `priority` (e.g. `P1`) created a nonstandard label that sorts as lowest priority with no warning; the compiler's own regression test even used `P1`/`P2` and passed.

## Changes
- **Invalid priority is a hard skip.** A `priority` not in `high|medium|low` is skipped with a loud warning naming the file and the offending value, rather than compiled into a bogus label.
- **Missing `blocked_by` warns.** The field is documented as required; its absence now warns (naming the file) and is treated as no blockers (distinct from an empty list).
- **Unknown frontmatter keys warn** but never block the sync.
- **Fixtures fixed + coverage added.** The regression fixtures now use valid priorities (`high`/`medium`); a new invalid-priority fixture asserts the rejection path, and assertions cover the missing-`blocked_by` and unknown-key warnings.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A plan file with an invalid `priority` is skipped with a loud warning naming the file and the invalid value
- [x] A plan file missing `blocked_by` gets a warning naming the file and is treated as having no blockers
- [x] Unknown frontmatter keys produce a warning but do not block the sync
- [x] The regression test's fixtures use valid priorities and cover the invalid-priority rejection path

## Gates
| Gate | Command | Result |
|------|---------|--------|
| test | `node scripts/plan-sync.test.mjs` | ✅ PASS (10 assertions) |
| format / typecheck / lint / build | — | n/a (TODO in GATES.md — zero-dependency markdown + Node scripts, no manifest) |

author: sparkpipe
body:
Prefill passthrough is fixed: the traced B1024 run shows every rank transforming every token with clean hop integrity. The remaining accuracy failure produces live, prompt-sensitive but wrong tokens, so the next comparison must be numeric per stage against the serialized reference, which already exists in-repo for the exact matched prompt: diagnostics/glm52_pp13_diff_20260708/serialized_spark2 holds all thirteen after_layer boundaries at 61440 bytes, five tokens by 12288, the identical byte layout the hidden transport ships. Because that reference came from the HF-path serialized run, exact hash equality is not expected from a correct FP8 ring; the signal is numeric: small depth-growing drift is healthy, a discontinuous jump at one stage is the bug's address.

The transport gains SPARKPIPE_HIDDEN_DUMP_DIR: when set, each rank writes every sent and delivered hidden payload as
rank{r}_{tx|rx}_seq{s}_tok{t}.bin at the exact sites the hashes already print. The comparator gains --numeric SERIAL_DIR DUMP_DIR: per token and rank it converts bf16 to f32, reports max_abs, rel_l2, and cosine against after_layer_{6r+5}, and flags relative-error jumps above four times the previous stage. Selftest covers the bf16 conversion and stats.

Transport change is device-side and rides the next resident restart; the comparator is host-only.

author: cipherwebllc
body:
## 概要

旅行者の AI (Claude/ChatGPT 等) が日本の店のメニューを母国語で相談して注文を組み、支払いは「決済画面 URL を開いて自分のウォレットで払う」BYOW 1 タップにする **インバウンド・エージェント注文 Phase A** (`plans/inbound-agent-order.md` v3 §2)。エージェントは財布を持たず、注文を組む手に徹する。

## 変更点

### 1. `packages/x402-mcp` 0.5.3 → 0.6.0: `createOrderLink` ツール
- **鍵なしで動作** (wallet-optional)。URL を組むだけで署名も送金もしない (`order_menu`/`order_quote` と同じ流儀)。
- 出力: `${origin}/@<handle>?cart=<base64url>[&table][&pickupAt]`。
- cart は `{id, qty, options}` のみを運び **受取先・価格を URL に載せない** (メニュー文字列が受取先/金額に影響しない・レビュー **M2**)。
- **自己完結 `/order?s=` トークンは生成しない** (レビュー **CRITICAL C1**: receiver スプーフィング回避)。受取先・価格は `@handle` の KV レコードから server が再解決する。
- cart 直列化は `order_quote` と共通化した `normalizeCartItems` + `encodeCart` = server の `lib/agentOrder.encodeAgentCart` と同形式。

### 2. `@handle` ページ + `MobileOrderView`: `?cart=` 事前充填
- server (`app/[locale]/[handle]/page.tsx`) が `?cart=` を **`decodeAgentCart` で検証**し、検証済みカートを `MobileOrderView` に `initialCart` で渡す。
- 新規純ロジック `lib/prefillCart.ts` の `resolvePrefillCart` が menu と突合し `qty`/`optionEntries` を初期化。
  - **グレースフル劣化 (L2)**: 未知 id / オプション不整合 / required 未選択は **該当行だけ drop** し解決分のみ反映 (全体を落とさない)。
  - **改ざん無害化 (M2)**: cart は金額を運ばず、価格は menu (KV 権威) から再計算。
- **フラグ/env なし**: `?cart=` 不在では従来挙動と完全同一 (構造的 inert・掟9 の対象外を保つ)。
- **人間の最終確認面 (M2 の砦)**: 事前充填時はカート明細を既定で開き、通知バナー `prefillNotice` を表示 (店名 + 明細 + 合計が可視)。

### 3. リファクタ (挙動不変)
- strict なオプション解決を `lib/menuOptions.resolveStrictSelection` に集約 — `computeAgentOrder` (server 権威注文) と `resolvePrefillCart` (URL 事前充填) の単一情報源。

### money-path 不変 (掟12)
支払い・fee・受取先の制御フロー (`CheckoutForm` / `mobileOrderFee` / relay 系) は一切変更なし。事前充填はカート選択状態の初期化のみ。

## 検証

| 項目 | 結果 |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | ✅ 0 errors |
| `npx eslint <変更ファイル>` | ✅ 0 |
| full vitest (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`) | ✅ **328 files / 6889 tests pass** (exit 0) |
| `npm run build` | ✅ exit 0 (page export 検査含む・掟3) |
| i18n parity | ✅ `prefillNotice` は `MobileOrder` namespace のみ (掟5) |
| 実機スクショ | ✅ dev サーバ (port 明示・掟11) で `?cart=` 事前充填を確認 (店名+明細+合計 3560 JPYC + バナー + 明細既定オープン) |

**新規テスト**: `createOrderLink` (URL 形 / handle 正規化 / 直列化 / 鍵なし動作 / `?s=` 非生成) ・ **MCP⇄server cart フォーマット互換フェンス** (drift 防止・複数カート形で byte 一致 + `decodeAgentCart` 往復) ・ `resolvePrefillCart` (decode / menu 突合 / grace 劣化 / 改ざん無害化 / cart 不在) ・ `MobileOrderView` 事前充填 (充填 / 改ざん drop / options / grace / 従来挙動不変)。

**e2e**: `@handle` storefront の `?cart=` 事前充填を張る既存 e2e spec は無く、KV に公開店舗の seed が必要なためローカル実行は不可。掟2 に従い **CI を e2e の権威**とする (可視文字列 `prefillNotice` はこのパス限定で、既存 spec の描画には影響しない)。実機描画は上記スクショ + component テスト (実 `MobileOrderView` render) で担保。

## 出荷ノート
- npm publish は **未実施** (user 承認事項) — version bump + CHANGELOG/README 更新のみ。
- **merge は user 承認待ち** (掟・自律運転の型)。

author: sentacraft
body:
## Why (and why not the circuit breaker)

A hung/unreachable DeepSeek would otherwise hang **every** `/api/chat` request to the 120s total-stream timeout, then the client nudges a retry into the same wall. The abandoned circuit breaker (#425) addressed this but is a poor fit at this traffic — it's passive, so it only protects requests *after* it has learned from ~4 failures, and it adds global KV state.

A **connect-layer timeout** is the cheaper fix and strictly better at what actually hurts: it's per-request and stateless, so it helps *every* caller immediately.

## What

`connectTimeoutFetch` wraps the prod DeepSeek provider's `fetch` (via `createDeepSeek({ fetch })`):

- Aborts a call whose response **headers** haven't arrived within **18s** — a dead connection.
- `fetch()` resolves on headers, *before* the body, so clearing the timer there caps **time-to-first-response**, not total stream time. A legit long turn (headers fast, then streaming) runs unaffected under the route's existing 120s total backstop.
- Chains the caller's own abort signal (the total timeout / client disconnect) through, so upstream aborts still cancel.

Two complementary layers now: **18s connect** (per model call, catches a hung start) + **120s total** (catches a mid-stream stall after a good start). No backup model — OpenAI stays out of the prod path.

## Tunable

`CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 18_000` — a judgment call in the 15–20s range.

## Test plan

- `connect-timeout.test.ts` — pass-through when headers arrive in time, TimeoutError abort when they don't, upstream-abort propagation (fake fetch + fake timers). `npm test` → 392 passed (18 files).
- `tsc` + `eslint` clean.
- Live happy-path smoke against `/api/chat` (200, streamed tool calls + text) confirms the custom-fetch provider still authenticates (apiKey from env) and streams normally.

author: raymundmt
body:
Docker sends SIGKILL 10s after SIGTERM if the container hasn't stopped. If bisync is mid-transfer when the container shuts down, the transfer gets nuked — corrupting the sync state and forcing a full `--resync` on next start.

Two changes:

- Add `stop_grace_period: 120s` to `charon-sync` — gives bisync enough time to finish its current cycle before Docker escalates to SIGKILL
- Track `SYNC_IN_PROGRESS` in the entrypoint — trap handler now logs whether bisync is actively running vs sleeping, so the user can see why shutdown is taking time

The entrypoint already doesn't interrupt bisync (SIGTERM is trapped, not forwarded to the child), but without `stop_grace_period`, Docker's default kill timeout made that protection meaningless.

author: nvartolomei
body:
Removes the `stm::raft()` accessor from the L1 LSM metastore STM and hardens
two externally-called STM entry points against lifetime issues.

The STM does not own the raft consensus, so handing out the raw pointer via
`raft()` let callers dereference it with no lifetime guarantee. This resolves a
use-after-free where `db_domain_manager::gc_loop` accessed the consensus's log
via `stm_->raft()->log()` after the consensus had been freed. Callers that need
the consensus now hold a `consensus_ptr` themselves (`db_domain_manager`,
`replicated_database`, and the test fixtures). Holding the consensus keeps its
log alive, so the fixtures release it before tearing down the raft fixture,
letting the log close while storage services are still up.

Separately, `stm::sync()` now holds the STM gate for its duration, as the base
`persisted_stm` contract requires of externally-called async methods; without
it, resuming after the awaited base `sync()` could touch a destroyed STM.

## Backports Required

- [x] v26.1.x

## Release Notes

### Bug Fixes

* Fixed a potential broker crash (use-after-free) in the cloud topics metastore when accessing Raft state during leadership changes.

author: jhfnetboy
body:
## A1#6 — derive the audit watchlist from on-chain Registry role membership

The DVT auditor no longer depends on a hand-curated `AUDIT_WATCHLIST`. When
`AUDIT_ROLE_DERIVE=true`, it enumerates the CURRENT members of `AUDIT_ROLE_IDS`
(default `DVT,ANODE`) from the SuperPaymaster Registry and UNIONs them with the
static `AUDIT_WATCHLIST` (now an additive manual override — it never subtracts).
**Default OFF → behavior unchanged.**

### How
- **`blockchain.service.getRegisteredOperators`** — getter-first (`getRoleMembers`,
  gated behind `AUDIT_ROLE_USE_GETTER`, default off) → event-scan fallback
  (`RoleRegistered|RoleGranted` add / `RoleExited|RoleRevoked` remove, replayed in
  `(block, logIndex)` order). Derived to a caller-supplied **finalized** `toBlock`,
  adaptive chunk-halving on getLogs errors, 100k-event cap, refuses a from-genesis
  scan. Fail-loud.
- **`audit.service`** — throttled + single-flight `refreshDerivedOperators` (a failed
  refresh keeps the previous set, never empties); `effectiveWatchlist` union; loud
  `ROLE_DERIVE_UNHEALTHY` event when the set is stale/never-confirmed;
  `getStatus` exposes `roleDerive`/`derivedSetFresh`/`lastRoleRefreshAt`.
- **Slash safety** — `confirmSlashableAtBlock` gates every irreversible slash on BOTH
  the requester (`coordinateQuorumCoSign`) and responder (`verifyViolationForCoSign`):
  static-listed → always; derived-only → the set must be fresh AND `hasRole==true`
  pinned to the **evidence block** (cheap eth_call, no re-scan); any read error →
  fail-closed. The responder also rejects an unfinalized `req.epoch`.
- **`GossipQuorumCoSigner`** — dropped its own static watchlist; operator authorization
  is delegated to the single authority (`verifyViolationForCoSign`), so derived-only
  operators can reach BLS quorum.
- **config** — `AUDIT_ROLE_DERIVE/_IDS/_FROM_BLOCK/_LOG_CHUNK/_REFRESH_MS/_USE_GETTER/_MAX_STALE_MS`.

### Review
Codex adversarial review, **4 rounds** (2 High + several Medium found and fixed across
rounds; final verdict **APPROVE**, only Low/Nit which are also closed). **400 tests**
(+19), 0 lint errors, type-check clean.

### Ops note
Set `AUDIT_ROLE_FROM_BLOCK` to the Registry deploy block before enabling
(Sepolia Registry `0xf5Bf37ca…8E71` = block **11151002**). Enabling `AUDIT_ROLE_DERIVE`
is an arming decision (pairs with the existing `AUDIT_EXECUTE_SLASH` gate).

Closes the A1#6 gap in `docs/RELEASE_READINESS.md`.

author: hayssams
body:
## What & why

quack-on-demand ran on Linux/macOS only — the JVM was already portable, but the runtime edges assumed a POSIX shell and Unix-only native binaries. This makes the manager **run natively on Windows** (no WSL, no Docker) and makes CI publish **one cross-platform uber-jar** that runs the native client on Windows *and* Linux/macOS.

## Changes

**Runtime (Scala)**
- `LocalQuackBackend` spawns nodes via `powershell.exe -File spawn-quack-node.ps1` on Windows and tears down the process tree with `taskkill /T` (reaps the `duckdb.exe` grandchild instead of orphaning it); Unix path unchanged.
- `QuackNativeBridge.platformDir()` resolves `windows-x86_64` → `quackwire.dll`.
- New config `spawnScriptWindows` (`QOD_SPAWN_SCRIPT_WINDOWS`).

**PowerShell scripts (new)**
- `spawn-quack-node.ps1` — mirror of the bash spawn; keeps DuckDB alive by holding stdin open instead of a FIFO.
- `run-jar.ps1` — self-installs DuckDB 1.5.4 windows-amd64, prepends to PATH, runs the jar.
- `stop-jar.ps1`.

**Native `quackwire.dll`**
- Cross-platform CMake `DUCKDB_HOME` discovery.
- 5th `windows-x86_64` classifier, gated behind `QOD_WITH_WINDOWS_NATIVE` (default **off** → existing Linux/macOS/CI builds are byte-identical).

**CI (cross-platform published jar)**
- `quackwire.yml` gains an MSVC `build-windows` job and publishes all 5 classifiers.
- `snapshot.yml` + `release-jar.sh` set `QOD_WITH_WINDOWS_NATIVE=true` so the single published jar bundles the Windows native alongside Linux/macOS.

**Misc**
- `UiBuild` uses `npm.cmd` on Windows (otherwise `sbt assembly` fails at the UI step).
- `LocalQuackBackendSpec` made cross-platform (Unix-only timing assertion guarded).
- Docs: `RUNNING.md`, `install.md`, `quickstart.md` Windows sections; `CLAUDE.md`.
- `.gitattributes` to normalize line endings (LF text, CRLF for Windows scripts).

## Verified live on Windows
- `spawn-quack-node.ps1` end-to-end: `quack_serve` binds, stdin keep-alive holds the node, `taskkill /T` clears it with no orphaned `duckdb.exe`.
- `INSTALL quack; LOAD quack;` works on Windows with DuckDB 1.5.4 (the make-or-break).
- All PowerShell scripts parse; changed Scala files report zero diagnostics.

## Client paths on Windows
- **Native wire (default)** — needs the bundled `quackwire.dll` (published cross-platform jar, or a local build with `QOD_WITH_WINDOWS_NATIVE=true`).
- **Embedded DuckDB-JDBC** — `QOD_NATIVE_CLIENT=false`, works with any jar out of the box (no native build).

## Rollout note
The `quackwire native build` workflow must run once (publishing the `windows-x86_64` classifier) before `snapshot.yml` resolves it — its existing `workflow_run` trigger handles that ordering automatically.

author: varnasr
body:
## What does this PR do?

Wires the companion validator into CI as a blank-page regression guard, so a future companion with broken `DATA` can't silently ship as a blank page.

**New CI job `book-companions`** (in `ci.yml`, runs on every push/PR) executes `scripts/check-book-companions.py`, which for each `BookSummaries/*-companion.html` verifies the inline `const DATA` object:
- parses as valid JSON,
- has a non-empty `title` and non-empty `sections`,
- contains no `</script>`, `U+2028`/`U+2029`, or raw C0 control character (the deterministic causes of a blank client-rendered page).

It's intentionally lenient about schema variation (older companions omit `southAsia`, use `summary` instead of `ideas`, or ship as a compiled bundle with no `const DATA`), so it has **zero false positives on the current 105 companions** — verified — and **fails (exit 1)** on an injected `</script>` break — also verified.

Also adds `scripts/validate-companions.mjs` — the deeper headless-Chromium render check (visible-text length + JS errors across every page) used to validate this batch — as a manual/optional tool, and documents both in `.claude/rules/testing.md` (item 9). The browser check is kept out of CI because it's heavier/flakier than the static guard.

body:
## What
A lightweight offline layer for the buyer surfaces. They're server-rendered (no React Query), so this is a small client-side enhancement, not a data-layer rewrite.

## Changes (frontend-only)
- `lib/recently-viewed.ts` — localStorage cache of the last 8 viewed listings (SSR-safe, dedupes by id, caps + newest-first, never throws on corrupt/absent/quota).
- `<RecordView>` — seeds the cache from the server-rendered listing detail page without making it a client component.
- `<RecentlyViewedCard>` — hydrates the cache into a dashboard sidebar strip, so a last-viewed fallback still renders when the live feed can't load.
- `<OfflineBanner>` — buyer-layout banner via the browser online/offline events; a failed fetch reads as “you’re offline” rather than a hard error.

author: avrabe
body:
Fixes #642.

## The hole

The Thumb-2 (and A32, #596) `call_indirect` expansion was three unguarded instructions off a runtime index:

```
lsl.w  ip, idx, #2
ldr.w  ip, [r11, ip]
blx    ip
```

No `cmp`/bounds branch, no type comparison — an out-of-bounds or wrong-typed index performed an **uncontrolled indirect branch** where WASM Core §4.4.8 mandates a deterministic trap. In-bounds dispatch was correct (the #594/#597 arc only ever fixed *indexing*), which is exactly why index-valid probes never saw it.

## Guard design

**Bounds check — runtime, both ISAs.** The expansion now prepends:

```
movw ip, #table_size   ; (+ movt when size > 16 bits)
cmp  idx, ip
blo  +1                ; skip the trap when in bounds
udf  #0                ; §4.4.8 OOB trap (same idiom as the div-by-zero guards)
```

Where does the table size live at runtime? **Nowhere** — the table is a raw array of 4-byte code pointers linked at `r11` by the runtime/harness, with no size field. The size is therefore a **compile-time immediate**, and it is *sound and exact* for a defined table: `table.grow`/`table.set` are unsupported ops whose functions loud-skip at decode, so nothing synth compiles can resize (or retype) the table. An imported table only yields a bound when its limits pin the size (`max == initial`); otherwise the lowering **declines loudly** (a guard against `initial` on a growable import would trap spec-valid calls).

**Type check — discharged at compile time (closed world).** The raw code-pointer table stores no type ids, so a runtime tag compare is not implementable with the current layout. Instead `DecodedModule::call_indirect_guards()` verifies, per expected type `t`: every slot in `[0, table_size)` is initialized by a const-offset active element segment with a plain `ref.func`, and every entry's signature **structurally** equals `types[t]` (signature comparison, not index comparison — duplicate types stay interchangeable). Under that property no runtime mismatch is possible; the check compiles away. Any hole — an uninitialized (null-funcref) slot, a heterogeneous entry, a passive/computed segment, a non-zero table index — records a reason and the lowering **declines loudly with it**. The unchecked branch is never left behind:

- `CompileConfig::call_indirect_guards` **defaults to decline** (no module context ⇒ no `call_indirect`),
- the optimized path now declines `call_indirect` **explicitly** (it previously fell through `wasm_to_ir`'s `_ => Opcode::Nop`),
- both direct selectors (`select_with_stack` + `select_default`) gate on the verdicts.

This is the (b) strategy from the issue triage: dissolved images have homogeneous fully-covered tables (the repro verifies), and extending table *emission* with type ids is moot while synth doesn't emit the table at all.

## Red → green evidence

`scripts/repro/call_indirect_642_differential.py` (new CI job `call-indirect-642-oracle`): unicorn vs wasmtime on **both ISAs**, table at `r11`, and — non-vacuity — the words *past* the 3-entry table seeded with a valid decoy function (`movs r0, #0x5A; bx lr`), so an unguarded build doesn't fault, it *calls the decoy*.

**origin/main (a1541c0), both ISAs red:**
```
[Thumb-2] f(5,3)  = 0x5a — the DECOY past the table was CALLED: uncontrolled indirect branch, no bounds guard (#642) MISMATCH
[Thumb-2] f(5,5)  = 0x5a — … MISMATCH
[Thumb-2] f(5,99) = 0x5a — … MISMATCH
[A32]     f(5,3)  = 0x5a — … MISMATCH   (+5, 99)
ORACLE: FAIL — 6 case(s) diverged from wasmtime (#642)
```

**this branch, 12/12 green:**
```
[Thumb-2] f(5,0)=0xf f(5,1)=0xfffffffb f(5,2)=0x32  (= wasmtime)
[Thumb-2] f(5,3)/f(5,5)/f(5,99) = udf trap (wasmtime: trap) OK
[A32]     same 6/6 OK
ORACLE: PASS
```

## Both-ISA status

- **Thumb-2** (cortex-m3): guarded, encoding pin updated (`test_encode_thumb_call_indirect_lsl2_597` + new `_guard_shapes_642` covering the high-reg CMP T2 form and the >16-bit MOVT arm).
- **A32** (cortex-r5): guarded, `test_encode_arm32_call_indirect_is_real_call_594` updated + new wide-size pin; the #594 A32 differential stays green (now executes the guard in-bounds).
- **RISC-V / AArch64**: no `call_indirect` lowering exists (falls to `Unsupported` → loud-skip) — no shared gap.

## Gates

- `cargo test --workspace`: **2012 passed, 0 failed** (was 2004; +5 decoder closed-world tests, +3 selector decline/emit tests, +2 encoder pins, net of split assertions)
- Frozen anchors: `frozen_codegen_bytes` **10/10 untouched** (fixtures carry no `call_indirect`)
- `estimator_encoder_agreement` (#511): green — `CallIndirect` is a direct-selector-only op, already in the oracle's not-on-optimized-path exclusion list, and the direct path's `resolve_label_branches` sizes by *actual encoding*, so the bigger expansion is measured, not estimated
- `#594`/`#597` differentials: green on the fixed build
- `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

author: lautaropetaccio
body:
## What

Two small changes to the retry-failed-deployments catch block (`src/logic/deployments/component.ts`):

1. Remove the redundant `logs.error(error)` call, keeping only the structured error line.
2. Narrow the catch variable when building the error description so a non-`Error` throw can't produce the string `"undefined"`.

## Why

### 1. Log noise
`retryFailedDeploymentExecution` re-attempts **every** failed deployment on each cycle. Most failures are permanent — invalid schema (e.g. emotes missing `emoteDataADR74`) or missing parcel access — so they re-fail every cycle. Each failure was logged twice:

```ts
logs.error(`Failed to fix deployment of entity`, { entityId, entityType, errorDescription })
logs.error(error) // full Error object → full stack trace
```

Since the retry loop moved to a `p-queue` (bounded parallelism), that second call's stack now bottoms out in `p-queue/dist/index.js` and carries no useful signal — while the parallelism makes the same permanent failures land in dense bursts, flooding the logs. The remaining structured line already carries `entityId`, `entityType`, and `errorDescription`, so no diagnostic information is lost.

### 2. Robust error description
`const errorDescription = error.message + ''` produced the literal string `"undefined"` if a non-`Error` value was thrown, persisting a useless reason into the failed deployment. Removing the `logs.error(error)` fallback (change 1) also removed the only place the raw thrown value was captured, so this is now narrowed:

```ts
const errorDescription = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
```

`error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)` is used rather than plain `String(error)` to keep the exact message format for `Error` instances (no `"Error: "` prefix), which preserves the existing `IGNORING_FIX_ERROR` match.

## Notes / out of scope

This only reduces log noise and hardens the error description. It intentionally does **not** change retry behavior — permanent failures are still re-reported and retried every cycle. Making the job classify permanent vs. transient failures (or add the long-standing `TODO: exponential backoff`) is a separate follow-up.

author: falinor
body:
## Summary

In the housing bulk-edit side menu, updating a batch while leaving status/sub-status empty (e.g. only adding a note) silently wiped every selected housing's `sub_status` to `NULL` and emitted a spurious `housing:status-updated` event — corrupting housings whose status requires a sub-status. The `fix-housing-sub-status` repair script found this fingerprint on ~1,557 of 1,618 damaged housings.

**Root cause (server-side only — the frontend already omits an untouched sub-status):** the batch-update schema ended with `.default(null)` on `subStatus`. The request validator `validateSync`-casts the body, so an *omitted* sub-status became `null`, which the repository persisted and the controller diff turned into a status event.

A naive "drop `.default(null)`" would have broken intentional clearing: Yup 1.7.1 **skips custom transforms when the input is `undefined`** (`_cast`), so the `.when(...).transform(() => null)` branch never fires on an omitted field — the null-clear relies on the default.

## What changed (`packages/schemas/src/housing-batch-update-payload.ts`)

- **Move `.default(null)` into the no-sub-status branch of the `.when()`.** An omitted sub-status stays `undefined` → the repository skips it (no-op). Setting a status that takes no sub-status (`NeverContacted`/`Waiting`) still clears it to `null`.
- **Require a sub-status when the payload sets a status that has sub-statuses** (defense-in-depth matching the frontend, which already `.required()`s it).
- **Reject a sub-status provided without a status.** A sub-status is meaningful only relative to a status, so a value — or an explicit `null` — without a `status` is a 400. This closes the last vector for the original bug (an explicit `subStatus: null` with no status would otherwise still null the column + emit an event).

Behaviour by case (keyed on the payload's `status`):

| Payload `status` | Payload `subStatus` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| absent | absent | untouched (no-op) — the bug |
| absent | value or explicit `null` | **400** (a sub-status needs a status) |
| `null` / invalid number | any | 400 (rejected by the `status` field) |
| no-sub (NeverContacted/Waiting) | absent or any | → `null` |
| sub-requiring | valid | kept |
| sub-requiring | invalid | 400 |
| sub-requiring | absent | 400 (required) |

No frontend change needed — `HousingListTab` maps an untouched sub-status to `undefined`, and `HousingEditionMobilizationTab` disables/requires the field per status.

Independent of the `fix/housing-sub-status` repair branch (that cleans up existing damage; this stops recurrence).

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn nx test schemas` — property + unit tests (omitted → `undefined`; NeverContacted → `null`; sub-requiring without sub → throws; sub-status without status → throws, value and explicit `null`)
- [x] `yarn nx test server` — `housing-api.test.ts` (65 passed): note-only update leaves sub-status untouched & emits no status event; sub-requiring status without sub → 400; sub-status without status → 400
- [x] `yarn nx typecheck schemas server`
- [x] `yarn lint`

# Add WebRTC-Based Audio Rooms for Live Peer Reviews

## Description

This PR introduces **WebRTC-based Audio Rooms** to enable real-time voice communication during peer reviews. The implementation uses **WebRTC** for peer-to-peer audio streaming and **Django Channels WebSockets** for signaling, ensuring low backend overhead while providing seamless live collaboration.

A new `WebRTCSignalingConsumer` handles signaling messages between peers, while the frontend introduces a reusable `AudioRoom` component that manages microphone access, peer connection setup, signaling, and call controls. Comprehensive frontend and backend tests have also been added to validate functionality and edge cases.

Closes #1241 

## Type of Change

* [x] New feature
* [ ] Bug fix
* [ ] Refactoring
* [x] Test improvement
* [ ] Documentation update

## Checklist

* [x] Code follows project conventions
* [x] Existing functionality preserved
* [x] WebRTC signaling consumer implemented
* [x] WebSocket routing added
* [x] Audio room UI implemented
* [x] Peer Review page integrated
* [x] Frontend tests added
* [x] Backend WebSocket tests added
* [x] Edge cases covered
* [x] Ready for testing

---

# What Was Implemented

## WebRTC Signaling Backend

Implemented a dedicated WebRTC signaling consumer using Django Channels.

### New File

* `backend/apps/chat/webrtc_consumers.py`

### Updated File

* `backend/apps/chat/routing.py`

The implementation provides:

author: adaworldapi
body:
Fixes the `/garmin/iceland` needle field and adds atmosphere to the terrain scenes. **Client-side only** (`GeoHelix.tsx`) — no asset regeneration, no new parser. Two commits.

### 1 — The needle field was over-exaggeration, not quantization

The "dequantize" framing turned out to be a misnomer. I decoded the live v8-grid and measured it:

- **16,515,072 verts** (the full DEM, not downsampled)
- **10,192 distinct height levels** (median step ~0.02% — fine, not stair-stepped)
- **~zero isolated spikes** (0 cells poke >5% of span above their neighbours)

So the height data is fine. The needles were the client's auto-exaggeration: `0.11/span` drives Iceland's tiny true-scale span (~0.0067) to **~16×**, versus the canyon's **2.2×** — and at 16× Iceland's genuinely rugged ~100 m fjord/ridge detail frays into needle-hair.

**Fix: cap the auto-exaggeration at 4.2×.** Iceland clamps 16×→4.2× and reads as a clean island with real relief (mountains, glacier caps, fjords, highland valleys); the canyon (2.2×) sits below the cap so it is **unchanged** — verified by re-render (walls still read as walls, drape intact). No `.DEM` reparse needed — rebaking from a different DEM source would have given the same rugged data.

### 2 — Terrain atmosphere: drifting clouds + KIND-gated sun-glint / ice-sheen

The "Fresnel/specular for ice caps + waves" direction, layered on the crisp relief:

- **Drifting cloud shadows** — a world-fixed 2-octave value-noise field scrolled by `uTime` dapples soft moving shade over the terrain (atmosphere + a real sense of scale). Terrain scenes redraw for the motion, **throttled to ~15 fps** so the continuous redraw of a heavy DEM stays cheap; anatomy/buildings stay fully on-demand (zero idle cost).
- **Sun-glint + ice-sheen** — a Blinn specular term **gated by KIND on the raw `aColor`** (not the hypsometric render): ocean (blue-dominant, `[26,62,104]`) → tight bright sun-glitter that brightens where clouds part; ice/snow (near-white, `[238,244,252]`) → broad soft sheen. The canyon's grey terrain KIND (`[150,150,150]`) triggers **neither**, so its hypsometric-white peaks stay matte — no false glacier shine.

### Verify

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- **Canyon (864 K verts, headless render):** cloud shadows visibly dapple the plateau; the rim stays matte (KIND-gating works); the OSM⊕Garmin drape overlay is intact; 2.2× relief unchanged.
- **Iceland (16.5 M verts):** the animated scene is too heavy for headless swiftshader, so captured **static** — the 4.2× relief reads crisp (no needles) and the cloud shadows dapple ocean + land. The ocean sun-glitter is view-angle-dependent (subtle at the aerial default); its gating mechanism is confirmed on the canyon. **Honest note:** the animated Iceland scene was not headless-verified in motion — it needs a real GPU (the deploy) to confirm the drift + glitter live.

The third of the Garmin terrain arc (after #93 shader, #94 surfel, #95 drape).

## Summary
- Treat editor-only Markdown serialization changes as clean when checking dirty state.
- Normalize known equivalent visual serialization shapes: intraword escaped underscores and tightened simple list spacing, including blockquote/callout lists.
- Ensure native close confirmation checks fallback Markdown equivalence before prompting.

## Why
Visual editor serialization can rewrite unchanged Markdown, such as `x_p` to `x\_p`, which caused clean documents to prompt for unsaved changes.

- `pnpm --filter @markra/app test -- src/hooks/useMarkdownDocument.test.tsx` passed: 68 tests
- `pnpm --filter @markra/app build` passed
- `pnpm --filter @markra/app typecheck:test` passed

## Risk
- Low. Scope is limited to dirty-state equivalence and close-prompt logic.
- Source-only edits that only add equivalent intraword underscore escapes may be treated as no semantic change.

author: praveenvijayan
body:
Closes #7

Two plan files blocking each other were a silent deadlock — both stuck at `state:blocked` forever, `unblock-dependents` never firing, nothing warning. This closes that hole at both ends: the sync that creates issues, and the status diagnosis that reads them.

## What changed
- **`scripts/plan-sync.mjs`** — plan files are now parsed *before* any GitHub call, then a DFS cycle gate runs. On any `blocked_by` cycle among plan files it prints a clear, user-facing error naming **every slug in each cycle** (ordered path) and exits non-zero **before creating or editing a single issue** — a deadlocked plan set changes nothing. Cycle-free sync behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **`ratchet-status` skill** (canonical `.agents/` + regenerated `.claude/` and `plugin/` mirrors via `setup.sh`) — new *Blocked cycles* diagnosis: builds the graph from `Blocked by #N` links among open `state:blocked` issues, reports each deadlock cycle naming every member, surfaced as a root cause above ordinary blocked chains.
- **`scripts/plan-sync.test.mjs`** — subprocess test asserting a two-file cycle exits non-zero and names both slugs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] `plan-sync` detects any `blocked_by` cycle among plan files and fails loudly, naming every slug in the cycle
- [x] A cycle-free plan set syncs exactly as before (existing 6-assertion regression still passes)

Most MiSTer cores read relative PS/2-style mouse movement, so trackpad mode is the reliable path; absolute mode is best-effort per core. Verified with `tsc` and `vite build`.

author: mattmcalister
body:
Closes #33, #34

## F10.2 — agentOS verify warns on Apps for no-App roles (#33)

`bootstrap/verify.py`: new `_check_no_app_roles()` function added to the verify pipeline.

For every role declared `create_app: false` in `agentOS.yaml` (currently: `archaeologist`, `planner`), it queries `/repos/{repo}/installations` and checks whether any installed App's slug contains the role id. If one is found, the check **fails** with a `SECURITY WARNING` message explaining:
- The role is declared with no App identity (SPEC.md §13 — confused-deputy protection)
- The installed App silently defeats that design
- The App should be uninstalled or its permissions reduced to none

**Field incident this check catches:** operator provisioned a fifth App for the archaeologist by the same pattern as builder/reviewer/watcher/janitor. Nothing in the setup path stopped them; the security guarantee was defeated with no error.

## F11.3 — Static token-write audit (#34)

`scripts/audit_token_writes.py`: static analysis of all workflow files in both `.github/workflows/` and `bootstrap/templates/workflows/`.

For each non-orchestrator job, checks if the job both:
- calls `addLabels` with a `status:*` value, **AND**
- uses `github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (bare token)

If both are true, it flags a violation — GitHub does not fire `issues.labeled` events for bare `GITHUB_TOKEN` writes (loop-prevention, platform-level). This is exactly the class of bug fixed in v1.2.2 F11 (`/approve-intent`). Currently **clean** on all workflow files (the v1.2.2 fix is in place). Wired into `test.yml` to catch future regressions.

Note: this PR also adds the CI script calls from PR #37 (F9.4 + #35) to `test.yml` — they'll become a clean no-op after #37 merges first.

author: code-alexander
body:
## Summary
- `run_benchmark` and `run_metric_benchmark` gain `max_concurrency` (default 1 — serial, behavior-identical to today). Above 1, solver calls (the network-bound half) fan out on a `ThreadPoolExecutor`; execution and scoring stay serial in case order because platform adapters hold a single DB connection that isn't thread-safe (sqlite3 enforces it; the other connectors hold single cursors/sessions).
- Reports return in case order regardless of solver completion order (`pool.map` + `zip(strict=True)`).
- Errors-as-values preserved: solver error values flow into case reports exactly as in the serial path; genuine exceptions still propagate.
- `--max-concurrency` wired onto `bench`, `dbt-bench`, and `sl-bench`.
- `evaluate_case` split into solve + `_score_output` halves (same shape mirrored in the dbt vertical; the two runners deliberately stay parallel copies, not a shared abstraction).

## Design notes
Comparable harnesses (inspect-ai's `max_connections`, openai/evals' thread fan-out) cap concurrency at the model-call layer and record per-item failures rather than aborting — this matches that shape without an async rewrite, since our LLM path wraps litellm's sync `completion`.

The run accumulator (`reporting/collector.py`) is untouched by this path — only pytest's `assert_eval` records to it, and that isn't reachable from `run_benchmark`.

## Tests
