author: scottstultz
body:
## Summary

Adds a frontend unit/component test suite (Vitest + React Testing Library on jsdom) with a first batch of 24 tests covering the optimistic-update and lifecycle paths most likely to break silently under refactoring: `AuthContext`'s session bootstrap/expiry/tab-restore behavior, the suggestion dismiss/undo flow, and thumbs-rating flip/revert.

## Changes

- Installed `vitest`, `jsdom`, `@testing-library/react`, `@testing-library/dom`, `@testing-library/jest-dom`; added `npm test` (`vitest run`) and `npm run test:watch` scripts to `frontend/package.json`
- `vite.config.ts` gains a `test` block (`environment: 'jsdom'`, `setupFiles: './src/test/setup.ts'`)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: new "Run tests" step in the frontend job, between `npm ci` and `npm run build` — a failing test now fails the build
- `frontend/src/test/setup.ts`: shared setup — jest-dom matchers, per-test `cleanup()`/storage clearing, a `ResizeObserver` stub (used by `DiscoverPage`'s shelf scroll rows), and an in-memory `Storage` polyfill for both `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` (Node 22+'s experimental `localStorage` global shadows jsdom's and is non-functional without a Node flag)
- `AuthContext.test.tsx` (10 tests): bootstrap with valid/expired/missing token; `getCurrentUser` failures — token cleared only on a confirmed `UnauthorizedError`, kept on a transient network error (#242); `pageshow`/`visibilitychange` re-validation including the hidden-tab no-op; the `setTimeout`-driven expiry sign-out under fake timers; adopting a token via the `wewatch:token-refreshed` event
- `DiscoverPage.test.tsx` (5 tests): optimistic tile removal + recorded dismissal, Undo restoring the tile, revert when `dismissSuggestion` rejects, re-hiding when `undoDismissSuggestion` rejects, snackbar auto-hide after 6s
- `LibraryPage.test.tsx` (4 tests) + `ThumbsRating.test.tsx` (5 tests): optimistic flip with `rateTitle`/`clearTitleRating`, revert on API failure, un-rate via `DELETE` when tapping the active thumb, plus pure component behavior (`aria-pressed`, `disabled`)
- `frontend/README.md` (new): documents `npm test`/`npm run test:watch` and the established conventions — colocated `<name>.test.ts(x)` files, mocking at the `apiFetch`/`ApiClient` service layer (never global `fetch`), rendering real providers (e.g. `WatchlistProvider`) on top of a mocked `useApi`, no vitest globals
- Root `README.md`: refreshed feature list and test counts to match the current state of the app (suggestion shelves, ratings, watch providers, etc.), and moved "Frontend unit tests" from Planned to done

## Why

The backend carries 429 tests, but `tsc && vite build` catches zero logic errors — it only checks types compile and the bundle builds. The frontend now has real optimistic-update and session-lifecycle logic (dismiss/undo, rating flip/revert, the #242 tab-restore fixes) with real failure modes, and those are exactly the paths that regress silently under refactoring without a human noticing in manual testing. This also establishes the test-file location, rendering, and mocking conventions so future features add tests instead of inventing structure each time.

## Testing

    cd frontend && npm test

- [x] `npm test` — 24 tests, 4 files, all passing
- [x] `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — 17 pre-existing errors, all in files untouched by this change (react-hooks rules); no new lint errors introduced

Closes #287

author: rajnishkhatri
body:
## ACT-English bank Phase B — governed practice-item bank + hint ladders

Grows the served ACT-English practice bank from **8 → 171 cascade-verified items**, each with a full **3-rung hint ladder** (513 rungs), giving every one of the 32 syllabus topics ≥1 practice item. Built through the authored-seed → cascade → frozen-corpus → deterministic-emit pipeline (SDD Stage 6, spec [`act-english-bank-phase-b.spec.md`](docs/plan/act-english-bank-phase-b.spec.md)).

### What ships

| Layer | Artifact | Result |
|-------|----------|--------|
| Question bank (source of truth) | `docs/plan/coach-item-bank-live.promoted.json` | **171 items**, all `reviewed=true`, 32/32 standards, key balance A/B/C/D = 16/54/52/49 |
| Hints (source of truth) | `docs/plan/coach-bank-hints.seed.json` | **513 rungs, 0 waivers** |
| Served plane (items) | `frontend/lib/adapters/engine/_test_item_bank.ts` | emitted wholesale from promoted corpus |
| Served planes (hints) | `frontend/lib/adapters/engine/_hint_bank.ts` + `components/subject_coach_bank_hints.py` | emitted wholesale |
| Emitter (new) | `scripts/emit_test_item_bank.py` | ADR-0014 seam sibling of `emit_hint_bank.py` |
| Sub-decisions folded in | D3 syllabus substrate (ADR-0022) · D2 Test-01 practice/test split | — |

### How correctness is guaranteed (fail-closed)

Every served item survived the **test-item verifier cascade** (ADR-0015): schema → **independent-solver answer-key gate** (a separate model picks the letter with the answer *withheld*) → duplicate (Jaccard ≥0.85). `reviewed=true` is earned only in-cascade — 21 of 192 candidates quarantined (solver disagreement) and are **never served**. Every hint rung passed the deterministic leakage predicate (`components/hint_leakage.py`); answer-revealing rungs quarantined.

### Notable in-flight findings (all recorded in `docs/adr/decisions.md`)

- **Tier-routing defect** (`d944b6b`): the `--capable-difficulty` knob was dead code — the router read `difficulty`, but the cascade fed the solver the answer-blind `_solver_view` which strips it, so all d≥4 items silently ran on the fast tier. Fixed route-before-view; 176 capable-tier calls confirmed on the final run.
- **Floor cleared honestly** (`a8ca29f`): reached ≥170 by fixing 6 genuinely-broken items + grading d2 on the capable tier — **not** by weakening items to satisfy the fast solver.
- **Zero hint waivers** (`a1ca0fe`): 4 atomic items that couldn't get a leak-free rung-2 were reworded (one via `why_correct_md` → method-language) rather than waived.

### Gates

- `make check`: **all checks passed** (ruff · ruff-format · pyright 0/0/0 · cite-lint clean · hygiene · pytest) — re-run on the branch tip for this PR.
- `tests/architecture/`: green (within `make check`).
- frontend vitest (engine): **80 passed** — provenance confinement (FR-B2), coverage ratchet (FR-E1), serving path (FR-C1).
- Bank serves 171 ≥ 170; every standard ≥1 item (matrix test green).

### Scope / what this does NOT include

Serving code is unchanged (FR-13). **D4** (topic taxonomy — FSRS `StandardState` + unlock, emitter gains `standard_id` on the wire) and **D5** (`rule_type`) are deliberately deferred to their own ADR-gated specs.

Evidence log (verbatim run outputs, red→green, gate results): [`docs/plan/act-english-bank-phase-b.impl.md`](docs/plan/act-english-bank-phase-b.impl.md).

author: martinhoefling
body:
## Summary
Makes the web interface listen port configurable instead of hardcoded to `8000`, so it no longer clashes with other services on the same host.

The Docker deployment hardcoded uvicorn's `--port 8000`. This unifies on the `BIND_HOST`/`BIND_PORT` convention already used by the Debian service and Windows launcher, so every deployment method shares one knob.

## Changes
- **`Dockerfile` / `backend/Dockerfile`** — CMD expands `BIND_HOST`/`BIND_PORT` (defaults `0.0.0.0:8000`). Uses `sh -c "exec …"` so uvicorn stays PID 1 and keeps receiving signals for graceful shutdown.
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — passes `BIND_HOST`/`BIND_PORT` into the container and lets the published host port follow `BIND_PORT`.
- **`.env_example` / `README.md`** — document `BIND_HOST`/`BIND_PORT`.

The HA add-on port stays fixed at `8000` by design (internal to Ingress).

## Testing
`BIND_PORT=9100 docker compose config` confirms the container target, published port, and env var all resolve to `9100`; default remains `8000`.

Closes #147

author: alonzoricardo
body:
## What this PR does (in one line)
Lets you send two or more transactions from the same wallet **without waiting for each one to mine first** — back-to-back or concurrently. Today the second send collides on the nonce and fails.

## The bug this fixes
Every send derives its nonce from the **mined** on-chain EntryPoint nonce, which doesn't move until a UserOperation is included in a block. Fire a second send before the first mines → both ops build at the same nonce → the bundler accepts one and rejects the other. Affects `sendTransaction` and `transfer`.

## How it fixes it
The account keeps an in-memory set of EntryPoint nonces it has handed out but that haven't mined yet (`_reservedNonces`). Each send allocates the next free nonce — `max(mined nonce, highest reserved + 1)` — so concurrent/rapid sends get **sequential** nonces (N, N+1, …). Allocation is serialized behind a lock (`_nonceLock`) so two simultaneous sends can't grab the same number. The allocated nonce is threaded into the abstractionkit build (`createUserOperation`'s `nonce` override) on every path, **including the EIP-7702 delegation rebuild** in `_sendUserOperation`.

## Failure handling (so it stays safe)
- A send **rejected before reaching the chain** (pre-acceptance: AA validation errors, `nonce`, `underpriced`, insufficient funds) hands its nonce back so the next send reuses it — no gap.
- A send that fails **ambiguously** (e.g. a network timeout) keeps its nonce reserved — we never risk double-sending the same operation.
- Mined nonces are forgotten automatically (reserved values below the mined nonce are dropped on the next allocation).
- The on-chain nonce read is bounded by a 30s timeout.

## Adapted from the erc-4337 module
Ports tetherto/wdk-wallet-evm-erc-4337#101 to the 7702 gasless module. Differences from that PR: EntryPoint v0.8 + `this._provider` (failover provider) rather than v0.7; the built op field is `sponsoredOp`; the allocated nonce is additionally threaded through 7702's delegation-rebuild path (the 4337 Safe flow has no such rebuild); fees reuse the module's existing `_getUserOperationGasCost`. This **supersedes** the consume-at-send check added in #14 (`_consumeFreshQuote` is removed) — `_prepareForSend` now reuses a cached quote only when its nonce equals the freshly-allocated nonce.

## What this PR does NOT change
- **Common path is identical:** quote → immediately send the same tx is still a single cache hit with one nonce read.
- Does **not** coordinate nonces across separate wallet instances or external clients sharing the account (the future `nonceKey` lane-isolation idea, out of scope).

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Verification
- `standard` lint clean.
- Unit suite (mocked) **72/72**, including a new `should allocate sequential nonces for back-to-back sends` test.
- Integration suite (real bundler + paymaster) green, including a new `should send two concurrent transactions with sequential nonces` test.

Builds on #14. Ports tetherto/wdk-wallet-evm-erc-4337#101.

author: gustavofbassani
body:
## Description
This PR addresses critical bugs regarding camera positioning, entity visibility, and SwiftUI state updates inside RealityKit's Attachment API on visionOS. It also refactors the immersive scene navigation UI for a more reliable architecture.

1. RealityKit Attachment Reactivity (Tab Bar Refactor)

Issue: SwiftUI state updates (via @Observable or @State) were failing to invalidate and redraw the UI inside RealityKit Attachment views in the immersive scene, causing the navigation buttons to remain visually frozen (disabled) despite underlying logic changes.
Solution: Dismantled the single VisionNavigationButtons component into individual 3D Attachment entities directly in SceneView.swift (moveToLeftTsuru, moveToRightTsuru, doneTsuruTab, tabBarBackground).
We now toggle the .isEnabled property of these 3D entities directly within the RealityView's update: closure, successfully bypassing the SwiftUI observation bug.


2. Camera Positioning Bug on Newly Created Tsurus

Issue: In visionOS, when focusing on a newly created Tsuru, the camera would move to a completely wrong offset location (the scene's origin or out of bounds) instead of properly focusing on the bird.
Solution: Updated CameraManager.swift (repositioningCameraNewToTsuru). For visionOS, if the target entity passed is the root container, the manager now dynamically intercepts the target and extracts the exact world position (position(relativeTo: nil)) of the inner child mesh (flappingBird___0PercentFolded). This circumvents a RealityKit bounding box bug on dynamically added root entities without breaking the shared iOS dictionary state.


3. Tsuru Visibility Bug (Overlapping Canvas)

Issue: When opening a newly created Tsuru to view the Canvas, the 3D model would not disappear, remaining visible and overlapping the Canvas UI.
Solution: Fixed the hide logic inside setCanvasPresented in SceneViewModel.swift. The dictionary (dict) uses the child mesh as the key for loaded tsurus, but the root container for newly created ones. The logic now intelligently verifies the entity name: if it's the child mesh, it disables the .parent; if it's already the root container, it disables the entity directly, preventing accidental disabling of the entire scene tree.


Visual Changes
The immersive scene navigation is now composed of individual, responsive glass attachments that mimic a single capsule tab bar.

author: pen-pal
body:
Closes #64. The group generalization of Signal's pairwise ratchet (Apex had the 1:1 ratchet + X3DH, not the group case).

Keeping a shared key fresh in a big group pairwise is O(n) per change. **MLS** (RFC 9420) puts members at the leaves of a binary **ratchet tree** with the group key at the root, so any change re-keys only the committer's **direct path** (leaf→root) — **O(log n)** — each node's new secret encrypted to the sibling subtree (copath).

**Produce & break** on an 8-member SVG tree: click a member to **update** or **remove** it.
- Only its direct path lights up (teal) + copath (amber): **4 re-keyed nodes, 3 encryptions vs 7 pairwise** — or **10 vs 1023** at 1024 members.
- **Remove** → its leaf blanks (red) and it's **locked out** of the new root (post-compromise security); everyone else recomputes it from the copath.

**Honesty:** `treekem.ts` computes the exact direct path / copath / cost; `treekem.test.ts` (7) pins the tree math with an independent oracle. Crypto in prose, not faked.

- [x] typecheck / full suite (3104) / anti-slop green
- [x] verified update-path + removal in dark & light; tree indices exact
- [x] count → 489
- [x] Signed off, no tool attribution

author: korjavin
body:
Follow-up to #482. A post-merge audit of the vault against `internal/store/migrations/` + `internal/seeddemo/wipe.go` found four gaps in the "seamless server migration" guarantee — three of them **silent data loss on replace-import**, because `WipeUserTx` deletes tables the exporter never wrote.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-08-vault-coverage-gaps.md`. Executed by ralphex (8 tasks) + codex external review.

## What was lost

1. **`bp_reminder_state` / `weight_reminder_state`** — wiped, never exported. A replace-import reset the BP/weight reminder enabled flag, snooze, don't-remind-until and preferred hour. `med_reminder_pref` was already in the vault; these were the missing siblings.
2. **Gamification** (`gamification_targets` — user-editable via `PUT /api/gamification/targets` — plus `ledger` and `state`) — neither exported *nor* wiped. A restore lost HP/level/streak/targets **and** could leave the previous user's state in place. Now exported and added to `WipeUserTx`.
3. **tz transition plans** — only the current plan was exported, but the wipe deleted every row. Past plans (needed for history analysis) are gone. `tz.transition_plan` → `tz.transition_plans[]`, oldest first, carrying the fields the old export dropped (`plan_hash`, `inputs_json`, `user_action`, `notified_at`).
4. **`api_tokens`** — a server move forced re-minting every MCP/API token. Exporting `token_hash` is what makes existing tokens keep working on the new host.

Also fixed on the way in (reported on #482): **weight goal history** — `weight_goals` is append-only and reachable via `GET /api/weight/goals/history`, but only the latest row was exported. `weight.goal` → `weight.goals[]`.

## Secrets toggle

New checkbox, **checked by default**: *"Include API keys and external provider settings"*. Unchecked → `settings.integrations` and `api_tokens` are omitted (`GET /api/export?include_secrets=0`; cloud passes `{includeSecrets:false}`).

One deliberate asymmetry: on import an **absent** secrets block leaves the destination's existing keys alone; a **present** one replaces them. A secrets-free vault must not silently unconfigure a working server. Codex caught that `Get("include_secrets") != ""` treated `?include_secrets=` and bare `?include_secrets` as absent — i.e. shipped the keys anyway. Now `Query().Has()`, fail-closed on any non-truthy value, both cases pinned.

## The guard

`TestVaultWipeAndExportAgree` pins `WipeUserTx`'s table manifest against a declared vault-coverage set + a skip list where every entry carries a `Reason`. Fails in **both** directions. This is what would have caught the original omission.

Skip list, with reasons: `push_subscriptions` (device-bound), `intake_reminders` (Telegram message ids), `change_events` (SSE tag stream), `miband_gps_tracks` (nested under `workouts.miband[].gps`), `workout_schedule_snapshots` (**write-only** — `CreateGroupSnapshot` is called from `workout_handlers.go:77,130`, `ListGroupSnapshots` has zero callers anywhere, so nothing can read the data).

Format stays `version: 1` — v1 shipped in #482 and nothing in the wild has exported it, so no compat shim.

## Cloud parity

`web/domain/vault.js` maps the new blocks: reminder prefs onto the existing `bpreminderpref`/`weightreminderpref` records (carrying the bot-only `snoozed_until`/`dont_remind_until` verbatim for round-trip fidelity), gamification/api_tokens as passthrough records like `tzhistory`, non-current tz plans as `tzplanhistory-<idx>` while the active one stays at `tzplan-current`. `managedTypesForImport` narrows `VAULT_MANAGED_TYPES` per-file so a secrets-free vault doesn't wipe the destination's keys — the client-side mirror of the asymmetric rule.

## Rebase note

Rebased onto master after `628b854c` (export/import timeouts + wire gzip). Three conflicts, all mechanical: the deadline + gzip wrapper coexists with `include_secrets`, and `importexport.js` sends both `?include_secrets=` and `timeoutMs`.

## Testing

Golden fixture `tests/fixtures/vault-v1.json` carries ≥2 rows per new list, so a dropped row fails both the Go (`TestVaultImportRoundTrip`) and Vitest (`cloud.vault-roundtrip.test.js`) round-trip pins. `TZ=UTC go test ./...` clean; `pnpm test` 2938 passed.

Closes bd med-j2b.3 follow-up. Remaining: med-4pw (gzip the saved file before age encryption).

author: emmiekehoe
body:
## Summary
- Adds `completeCustomProfile(dflt, profile)` in `assistant/src/config/profile-materialization.ts`: materializes a partial custom profile into a complete, standalone override by baking in what it inherits from `llm.default` under the current deep-merge resolver — including the resolver's parity quirks (winning-profile-scoped `temperature`/`topP`/`logitBias` are never inherited; nested `thinking`/`contextWindow`/`openrouter` merge leaf-by-leaf; model-only profiles get the `withImpliedProviders` provider; `provider_connection` is inherited only when the effective provider matches the default's).
- Inert: no production consumers yet. This is PR 1 of the M6 plan — the write-path normalization (PR 2) and workspace migration 128 (PR 3) build on it.
- Tests include a resolver-equivalence suite pinning that partial and completed profiles resolve identically when the profile is the only profile layer above `llm.default` (profile-less call site) — the contract that lets migration 128 rewrite profiles without behavior change, plus idempotency, nested-merge, implication, and passthrough coverage.

## Original prompt
Milestone 6 of the Inference Management Refactor replaces deep-merge profile resolution with override-or-default semantics (custom profile = complete override; default intents resolve through `llm.defaultProvider` via the code catalog; new resolver ships behind the `override-or-default-resolution` kill-switch flag). Existing custom profiles are partial (omitted fields inherit via merge), so they must be materialized into complete profiles before the resolver flip. This PR is the shared completion helper that the write-path normalization and migration will use. Full plan attached below as the durable papertrail.

<details>
<summary>M6 plan: Override-or-Default Profile Resolution (papertrail)</summary>

# M6: Override-or-Default Profile Resolution

## Overview

Replace the deep-merge cascade in `assistant/src/config/llm-resolver.ts` with override-or-default semantics: resolution picks exactly one complete profile (explicit override, or the call site's default intent resolved through `llm.defaultProvider` via the code catalog), plus at most the call site's own tweak fragment. Prerequisite state (M4 code catalog, M5 `llm.defaultProvider`) is fully merged. The plan front-loads the compatibility work (materializing partial custom profiles, write-path normalization, defaultProvider-aware catalog lookup, error groundwork) so the resolver flip itself is one reviewable PR that must not change behavior for materialized workspaces.

Notion: vellum-ai/Inference-Management-Refactor-38e9035c57bd804d9f92c11f27391856 (Milestone 6). Everything is inside `assistant/` — the resolver has no consumers in gateway/cli/clients/packages, and route contracts do not change (that's M7). No cross-repo work.

## Design decisions (resolved during planning)

- **Materialization baseline**: a custom profile is completed against the layers *below* it — `llm.default` plus the profile itself ("what the profile means standalone"). Call-site layers above it stay call-site concerns. Replicates current merge quirks exactly: `temperature`/`topP`/`logitBias` are winning-profile-scoped today and are **not** inherited from `llm.default`; nested `thinking`/`contextWindow` deep-merge leaf-by-leaf; provider is copied from `llm.default` and the (retained) single-profile model→provider implication corrects it when the model isn't served.
- **Mix profiles survive unchanged**: a mix carries no config fields (schema-enforced), it's a weighted pointer. Expansion at dereference stays; the chosen arm (a complete profile post-materialization) is the winner. Mixes are not materialized.
- **Model→provider implication is retained** as a live, code-owned resolution step applied to the single winning profile (`withImpliedProviders` semantics collapse to one check). This keeps the materialization migration free of a frozen model-catalog snapshot.
- **`forceOverrideProfile` collapses**: under override-always-wins there is no "float above" distinction. The resolver option becomes a documented no-op alias; the three drivers (scheduler opportunity-wake, memory-retrospective fork, subagent advisor) and agent-wake's string-form convention keep working untouched. Removal is M9 scope.
- **`activeProfile` becomes mainAgent-only**: it is the mainAgent call site's selection, second in that site's chain. It no longer folds into other call sites (today it back-fills profileless sites). `advisorProfile` is unaffected (enters as `overrideProfile` via subagent spawn).
- **Profileless call sites (`vision`, `workflowLeaf`) re-anchor to the default provider**: they resolve balanced-intent through `llm.defaultProvider` plus their fragment tweaks, instead of `llm.default` + activeProfile-backfill. This is a deliberate behavior change (see Behavior changes). `llm.default` drops out of live resolution; the completeness base becomes `LLMConfigBase` code defaults. `llm.default` itself stays on disk (delete-guard and legacy readers reference it) — retirement is M9.
- **`LLMSchema.superRefine` stays strict**: config-file profile references are still validated at load (dangling refs are pruned by config recovery). The resolver's deleted-profile fallback covers the refs schema can't see — DB-backed pins (conversation `inferenceProfile`, `cron_jobs.inferenceProfile`) arriving as `overrideProfile`, plus delete races.
- **Auto-recovery connection scans stay in M6** (`connection-resolution.ts:152-176`, `:241-262`): they handle stale-but-recoverable references (compat aliases), which is different from *missing* — missing gets explainable errors. Removing auto-recovery is M9 scope.
- **The small internal `deepMerge` helper survives** for composing exactly three known layers (code-default base → winning profile → call-site tweak fragment) so a tweak like `{thinking: {enabled: false}}` doesn't wipe sibling nested fields. What M6 removes is the multi-profile fragment *cascade* and its provenance machinery (`samplingRef`/`biasRef`, per-layer implied providers, mainAgent's flipped precedence).
- **Release sequencing**: all seven PRs ship in the same release (decided 2026-07-08 — no soak cycle). Ordering is safe: workspace migrations run at boot before traffic, so every install materializes profiles before the new resolver runs. Since there's no field-soak of the migration under the old resolver, the plan compensates with (a) an adversarial fixture matrix in PR 3 covering drifted/hand-edited configs, (b) a structured log from the migration recording exactly which fields it baked into which profiles (so a field report of "wrong model" is immediately attributable to data vs. resolver), and (c) PR 6's before/after resolution-parity fixtures.
- **Kill-switch feature flag** (decided 2026-07-08): the new resolver semantics ship behind assistant flag `override-or-default-resolution`, `defaultEnabled: true`. It gates pure read-time logic only (PR 6's resolver branch + PR 7's preflight); PRs 1–5 ship unconditional because migration/write-normalization/catalog/error-groundwork are valid under both semantics by construction (PR 1's equivalence test). Flag-off instantly restores the merge cascade with no reconcile lifecycle — this is what M5's "no flag" decision deferred to M6. Remote flag sync = fleet-wide kill without a release (fully offline self-hosted installs only get the registry default). The old cascade is therefore NOT deleted in PR 6; deletion of the cascade machinery + this flag is M9 scope (Notion M9 already lists "old deep-merge helper paths"). `usage/attribution.ts` must follow the same flag so attribution never disagrees with the active resolver. Requires a small companion Terraform PR in vellum-assistant-platform to create the flag on the platform (per meta/feature-flags/AGENTS.md).

## Behavior changes to call out in PR descriptions

1. Profileless sites (`vision`, `workflowLeaf`) and BYOK installs whose call site resolved no profile

author: tszaks
body:
## Why

Pallium hardcoded the default worker provider to `codex`, so workers ran codex even when Claude Code (or any non-codex agent) was driving Pallium — and broke entirely when codex was unavailable. Multiple live workflows failed this week for exactly this reason (7/7 agents dead when codex hit its quota). Pallium is meant to adopt the model of whatever agent is steering it.

## What

**1. Auto-provider adoption** (`internal/workflow/provider.go`). `ResolveProvider` precedence: explicit `agent.Provider` > `opts.Provider` > `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_PROVIDER` env > **detected steering agent** (`CLAUDECODE`/`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` → `claude`) > `codex` fallback. Explicit `provider:"codex"` still wins under CLAUDECODE. `DetectSteeringProvider` is structured so more agents (cursor/gemini/…) can be added later.

**2. Built-in claude provider** (`internal/workflow/claude_provider.go`). When the resolved provider is `claude` and no `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_PROVIDER_CLAUDE_COMMAND` wrapper is set, invoke the `claude` CLI directly — adoption works with just the CLI on PATH, no wrapper. Prompt piped over **stdin** (not `-p <prompt>` argv) to avoid `MAX_ARG_STRLEN`. Robust output extraction (envelope / event-stream array / prose / fenced), usage+cost parsed to Pallium's shape.

**3. ARG_MAX fix.** The configured-provider path also stuffed the full prompt into the child **environment** (`PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_PROMPT=`), which blows the exec argv+env past `ARG_MAX` → `fork/exec /bin/sh: argument list too long`. Prompt is now **file-only** via `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE`.

**4. Non-Go repos.** The edit allowlist spans Go/Node/**Deno**/Python/Rust/Make/Apple-Swift build+test runners; repos extend it via `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_CLAUDE_ALLOWED_TOOLS`.

## Security hardening (from a review run *on Pallium itself*, then re-reviewed)

- Dropped `Bash(pallium:*)` from the read-only allowlist — it allowed `pallium workflow run` (nested paid agents / recursion) and `index`/`task` mutations, so read-only wasn't read-only.
- Built-in worker runs with `--safe-mode --strict-mcp-config`: disables all ambient customizations (user/project/local settings + hooks) and MCP, so neither a checked-out repo nor the operator's global config can widen the per-mode allowlist. Permission flags still enforce.
- `claude` `is_error` envelopes now surface as errors instead of being returned as the answer.
- Report/analytics use a display-only provider resolver (no live env detection) so historical codex runs aren't misattributed as claude.
- Error output capped; `buildClaudePrompt` surfaces schema-marshal failures.

## Verification

- `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./internal/workflow/ ./cmd/ -count=1` + `-race` on `internal/workflow` — all green.
- **Live**: ran a no-provider workflow from inside Claude Code → run record shows `provider: claude`, output `PONG`, real usage accounting. Confirms adoption + built-in provider + stdin + safe-mode isolation end-to-end.
- Review + adversarial verify + re-review all run **through Pallium's own engine** (dogfood). Re-review: 3 findings refuted, 1 residual (`--setting-sources user` still trusted operator config) fixed by upgrading to `--safe-mode`.

## Breaking / deferred

- **Breaking (pre-1.0):** `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_PROMPT` env var removed from the provider contract (prompt is file-only). Wrappers read `PALLIUM_WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE` (the reference wrapper already does).
- **Deferred (tracked):** per-run provider pinning for cross-env resume; codex quota-error surfacing + non-zero exit on total failure; JSON-recovery heuristic tightening.

author: barrowsbr
body:
Continuação do #552 (caixa da IBKR no canônico). Depois de somar o caixa, os baldes **Brasil** e **Cripto** batem entre a Home e o canônico (vêm do mesmo snapshot). A diferença que sobra está no **book internacional**: a Home o valoriza pelas posições **reais** da IBKR (OpenPosition, preço da IBKR), enquanto o canônico usa o **FIFO de `meus_ativos`** (preço Yahoo).

## Fix — alinhamento de preço

`buildIbkrOverview` cotava as posições via `fetchCotacoes` mas **nunca carregava o cache `ativos_meta`** antes (ao contrário de `/api/cotacoes`). Como `yahooTicker()` usa esse cache para achar a grafia Yahoo (ex.: `DPM`→`DPM.TO`), sem ele tickers internacionais podiam falhar a cotação ao vivo e cair no **preço estático do extrato** — desalinhando o patrimônio IBKR (Home) do canônico. Agora ambos os lados usam o mesmo preço ao vivo.

## Ferramenta — reconciliação de patrimônio

Nova rota `/api/debug/patrimonio-recon` (própria, `maxDuration 60`, fora do catch-all porque baixa o extrato Flex): casa **ticker a ticker** as OpenPositions reais da IBKR × as posições canônicas (FIFO) e decompõe a diferença em:

- **quantidade** — FIFO ≠ holding real (trade faltando ou errado no ledger `meus_ativos`);
- **preço** — mesma quantidade, preço do extrato IBKR × Yahoo ao vivo (timing).

Devolve o total, a divisão por causa, e a lista das posições com maior `delta_brl` — aponta **exatamente** de onde vêm os "alguns milhares". Também concilia o caixa IBKR já somado via `fixa_aberta`.

## Verificação

Type-check limpo; a rota compila e roda (o 500 no sandbox é só a credencial do Sheets ausente, pré-existente).

Quando subir, é só abrir `…/api/debug/patrimonio-recon` (via conector Vercel) — o campo `resumo.por_causa` diz se o resto é ledger (quantidade) ou timing de preço.

author: brandonrc
body:
## Summary

Adds a `service-account` command group to the CLI, covering the full
`service_accounts` SDK/API surface. Service accounts previously had no
dedicated CLI command.

## Commands (op → command)

| API operation | Command |
|---|---|
| `list_service_accounts` | `ak service-account list` |
| `get_service_account` | `ak service-account show <id>` |
| `create_service_account` | `ak service-account create <name> [--description]` |
| `update_service_account` | `ak service-account update <id> [--display-name] [--active\|--inactive]` |
| `delete_service_account` | `ak service-account delete <id> [--yes]` |
| `list_tokens` | `ak service-account token list <account>` |
| `create_token` | `ak service-account token create <account> <name> --scope <s>... [--expires-in-days] [--repository-id <id>...\|--repo-selector <json>] [--description]` |
| `revoke_token` | `ak service-account token revoke <account> <token> [--yes]` |
| `preview_repo_selector` | `ak service-account preview-selector --selector <json>` |

All 9 operations are covered.

## Implementation notes

- New module `src/commands/service_account.rs` follows the existing
  command-module pattern (clap `Subcommand`, shared `helpers`, spinner,
  `table`/`json`/`yaml`/`quiet` output via `output::render`).
- Token operations are grouped under a nested `token` subcommand.
- `create_token` shows the secret token once (stdout) with a save-now notice,
  and emits just the token in `--quiet`.
- Registration is minimal: `pub mod` in `commands/mod.rs`, one enum variant and
  one dispatch arm appended in `cli.rs`.

## Testing

- `cargo build` / `cargo build --release`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings -A dead_code`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1440 passing (28 new: parse, JSON-object parsing,
  and wiremock handler tests for every subcommand).
- Manually exercised against a live backend: `list`, `show`, `update`, token
  `create`/`list`/`revoke`, `delete`, and `preview-selector` all work and
  render correctly across output formats.

## Known caveat (backend/spec, not CLI)

`create` currently surfaces an "Unexpected Response" error because the live
backend returns **HTTP 200** for `POST /api/v1/service-accounts` while the
OpenAPI spec declares **201**; the generated SDK strictly matches the declared
status, so it rejects the 200 even though the account is created server-side.
This is a spec/backend status-code mismatch rather than a CLI defect (the
handler is spec-faithful and its 201 handler test passes). Aligning the backend
response (or the spec) to 201 resolves it.

author: 100rd
body:
## Root cause (not what it looked like at first)

`knowledge.spec.ts`'s four `test.describe` blocks (Journey A/B/C, Adversarial
gate) each use a lazy seeder (`ensureSeeded` / `ensureComplianceSeeded` /
`ensureAdversarialSeeded`) that creates one workspace + calls
`ensureProjectHeaders(page, baseURL)` **once**, on the first test's page,
gated by a `seeded` boolean. `test.beforeEach` in every block only called
`loginPage()` — never `ensureProjectHeaders()`.

Playwright gives every test a brand-new page/context (fresh `localStorage`).
Because the lazy seeder short-circuits after test 1, every later test in the
block never re-writes `localStorage.project_id`. The client's own
`ProjectContext.tsx` handles a missing `project_id` by auto-selecting
`data[0]` from `GET /api/projects` for the logged-in admin user.

- Running `knowledge.spec.ts` alone: exactly one project exists for the
  whole run (the one cached project all specs in this repo share per
  worker process), so `data[0]` always happens to be the right one — no
  failure, matching the "passes in isolation" symptom.
- Running the **full suite**: other spec files also create admin-owned
  projects (via their own `POST /api/projects` calls or their own
  `ensureProjectHeaders` cache misses), so the account can end up with more
  than one project. Whichever project sorts first in that list is no longer
  guaranteed to be the one that owns this file's workspace. When it isn't,
  every request from that page carries the *wrong* (but valid, so not
  400'd) `x-project-id`, and the server's project-scoped `getWorkspace()`
  correctly returns nothing for that project → `404 {"error":"Workspace not
  found"}`.

This is **not** a server bug — `requestContext`/`withProject` scoping
(`server/context.ts`, `server/db.ts`) is properly per-request via
`AsyncLocalStorage`. It's also not really "one shared `workspaceId`" in the
sense of two journeys racing on the same row — it's a missing per-test
project-header hydration on the client causing an unrelated project to be
auto-selected. Reproduced locally with the exact `404: {"error":"Workspace
not found"}` payload at `knowledge.spec.ts:330`/`:714` on a clean DB, full
suite, before the fix; gone after.

## Fix

Add `await ensureProjectHeaders(page, baseURL)` to each of the four
`beforeEach` hooks in `knowledge.spec.ts`, matching the pattern already
established in `statistics.spec.ts`/`workspaces.spec.ts`. This re-hydrates
`localStorage.project_id` on every test's fresh page before any navigation,
independent of list order or how many other projects exist in the account.
Spec-only change; no product/server code touched. No `waitForTimeout`/sleep
added; existing `networkidle` waits left as-is (unrelated to this failure
mode, out of scope for a minimal fix).

## Verification

Full suite (117 tests, `CI=true`, `workers: 1`), against a scratch
`pgvector/pgvector:pg16` Docker DB, **dropped and recreated before each
run** to mirror a fresh CI job:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Baseline (before fix), run 1 | 106 passed / 11 skipped / 0 failed (flake did not reproduce this time) |
| Baseline (before fix), run 2 | 103 passed / 1 failed / **2 flaky** — `knowledge.spec.ts:330` and `:714` both needed retry #1, exact `404 Workspace not found` payload confirmed in the trace |
| Fix, clean-DB run 1 | **106 passed / 11 skipped / 0 failed / 0 flaky** |
| Fix, clean-DB run 2 | **106 passed / 11 skipped / 0 failed / 0 flaky** |
| Fix, clean-DB run 3 | **106 passed / 11 skipped / 0 failed / 0 flaky** |

`:330` and `:714` green in all 3 post-fix runs, no retries, no new failures.

### Unrelated flake observed once, not fixed here

One run against a DB that had already been used for 2-3 consecutive full
suites (not reset in between) showed `remote-agents.spec.ts:374` "POST
/api/remote-agents registers agent (DB)" fail with a `500` on both the
initial attempt and the retry. It did not reproduce in any of the 3
clean-DB runs above (before or after this fix), and it also does not touch
project/workspace headers, so it looks like state accumulation from reusing
one scratch DB across repeated manual runs rather than a real per-CI-job
flake. Flagging for visibility, not fixing as part of this PR.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on the changed file
- [x] Full suite × 3 on a freshly reset scratch DB, all green, `:330`/`:714` stable
- [x] No product/server files touched (`git diff --stat` shows only
      `tests/e2e/knowledge.spec.ts`)

author: pavel-rp
body:
## What

Adds a **pre-commit self-review seam** to the commit path — an operation-time injection point fired immediately before a commit is recorded, where a future self-review capability (WF-160's `sr`) can inspect the staged change set and gate or annotate the commit. Core defines the seam abstractly; with no self-review capability registered it is **inert** (the commit proceeds byte-identically).

Closes WF-154 (C002 sub-task under WF-153).

## How the seam is defined

- A new SDD phase, **`pre-commit`**, added to the contribution taxonomy in `capability-registry.contract.md` + `capability-registry.ops.md` (heading parity preserved). It is an operation-time seam, **not** a gated artifact phase.
- It **reuses the existing `finding` kind** (no new taxonomy token) — a pre-commit self-review is a set of provenance-tagged findings about the staged change set, exactly the shape `finding` already carries at `verify`. `finding`'s phase(s) become `verify, pre-commit`.
- The `wf:commit` subagent (`plugins/wf/agents/commit.md`) fires the `pre-commit` phase — the way `verify-spec` fires `verify` — as new **Step 4 item 5**, immediately before the Step 4 commit operation (now item 6). It walks the registry, collects `finding` fragments at `pre-commit`, aggregates them; a gating finding aborts the commit, an annotating one proceeds.

## Inert when unregistered

With an empty registry, or no capability attaching a `pre-commit` fragment, the phase produces its empty result: no finding surfaces, no capability term appears, and the commit proceeds byte-identically. In bare-core mode the seam is never even reached — Step 4 item 1 (no-delivery-provider diagnosis) returns before it.

## The three existing layers are preserved

The seam **composes with**, and does not replace, the pre-existing commit-path layers:
- **WF-209** resolved-provider forwarding — the Provider-resolution section and the forwarded `delivery` record are untouched; the seam firing is an independent phase resolution that neither consumes nor alters that record.
- **WF-212** nothing-to-commit short-circuit (Step 4 item 2) — untouched; the seam fires only when a real change is pending, after this short-circuit.
- **WF-201** hedged two-mode write-side diagnosis (Step 4 item 1) — untouched; it returns before the seam is reached when no provider resolves.

## Validation

- `validate-registry.sh` recognizes `pre-commit` in the SDD-phase allowlist.
- New fixtures: `pass-precommit-review` (a `finding` at `pre-commit` validates clean) and `fail-precommit-badkind` (a bespoke `self-review` kind at the seam is rejected, naming the offender).
- Full fixture suite + `check-ops-docs.sh` green (48 passed, 0 failed); every pre-existing fixture stays green.
- Grep-clean of git/gh/stack/domain strings across the changed contract/validator/fixture files and `agents/commit.md`.

Version bump: wf `0.48.0`, marketplace top-level `0.60.0` (reconciled above WF-178's concurrent `0.47.0`/`0.59.0` release).

author: krippler
body:
## What

Stops the container's own health probes from flooding the access log. Docker's `HEALTHCHECK` hits `GET /healthz` every 30s, so the log fills with internal 200s a couple of times a minute — burying real traffic (this is what you were seeing).

## How

- New **`app/gunicorn.conf.py`** with a `logging.Filter` on the `gunicorn.access` logger that drops `/healthz` and `/readyz` lines. It matches on the access-log **`U` atom** (URL path, no query string) — an exact, log-format-independent check — with a substring fallback. Attached in `post_fork` so it's live on the worker that emits the records.
- **Dockerfile CMD** gains `--config gunicorn.conf.py`.

**Log-only** — the health check still runs and still gets its 200; every non-probe request is still logged. The error log is untouched.

## Verification

Ran gunicorn locally with the config and fired 2× `/healthz` + 1× `/readyz` + 2 real requests:

## v0.35.0 (v0.35.0)
buildx 0.35.0

Welcome to the v0.35.0 release of buildx!

Please try out the release binaries and report any issues at
https://github.com/docker/buildx/issues.

### Contributors

* CrazyMax
* Tõnis Tiigi
* Sebastiaan van Stijn
* Areeb Ahmed
* Jiří Moravčík
* Sopho Merkviladze
* Akihiro Suda
* Jonathan A. Sternberg

### Notable Changes

- Local output now supports a `mode=delete` attribute for build and bake commands. This mode replaces the destination directory with the build result instead of merging it. Similar to the `--delete` flag in rsync. For safety, this mode is only allowed if the destination directory is a subdirectory of the working directory. To export to other destinations, `--allow=buildx.local.delete` needs to be provided or the action confirmed by the user in the TUI. When exporting multi-platform results, this mode requires BuildKit v0.31.0+. #3883
- Source policies now support the new exec proxy feature of BuildKit v0.31.0+ that captures the network traffic of your build steps. To opt in to network proxy, your Dockerfile.rego source policy needs to return `caps: { "exec.proxy": true }` in the evaluation decision. After opting in, you can control what network requests are allowed to be made by the run steps with policy rules for regular `input.http` sources, similar to how this was done for direct HTTP build sources before. You can also opt in your whole builder with `--buildkitd-flags '--proxy-network'` in `buildx create`. #3895
- Resource limits can now be set for CPU and memory using the `--resource` flag in `build` and the `resource` key in `bake` commands. This feature requires BuildKit v0.31.0+ and Dockerfile v1.25.0+. #3876 #3900
- Fix possible "closed channel" panic. #3886

Abgleich Patientenbogen (Kundenportal) gegen den SA-Neuanlage-Wizard — Martins Frage "Die Fragen reichen und schoen sortiert?".

**Ergebnis des Vergleichs:** Struktur und Sortierung des Portals (5 kleine Schritte statt einer SA-Riesenseite) sind bereits besser als SA; Demenz-Stufen, Nachteinsaetze, Pflichtfeld-Rot etc. waren schon deckungsgleich. Es fehlten 4 Fragen, die SA stellt und die ein echtes Mamamia-Feld haben:

1. **Hilfsmittel** je Patient (Chips: Gehstock, Rollator, Rollstuhl, Patientenlifter, Treppenlift, Pflegebett, Sonstiges) → `patient.tool_ids` 1–7 wie im SA-Wizard; explizite Auswahl gewinnt gegen die bisherige Ableitung aus der Mobilitaet.
2. **"Was ist in der Nacht zu machen?"** — nur sichtbar wenn Nachteinsaetze ≠ Nein; echter Text ersetzt den generischen Platzhalter in `night_operations_description`. Platzhalter wird beim Wiederoeffnen nicht als Nutzertext angezeigt.
3. **Einkaeufe** (Ja/Gelegentlich/Nein, optional) → `wish.shopping` (bisher hart auf 'no'); bedingtes "Wie werden die Einkaeufe erledigt?" fliesst in die Job-Beschreibung.
4. **Raucherhaushalt** (optional) → `Customer.smoking_household`.

Bewusst NICHT uebernommen (Endkunden-Friktion ohne Matching-Wert): Pausenregelung, TV/Kueche-Checkboxen, interne Kundenbezeichnung, Stellenbeschreibung (macht der Mapper), Sprachkenntnisse (kommt bereits aus dem Kostenrechner, read-only sichtbar).

author: amfiggins
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The distance check in `CombatSystem.lua` evaluating `distSq > maxRange * maxRange` can be bypassed by clients sending spoofed `NaN` coordinates, as any relational comparison with `NaN` evaluates to false.
🎯 Impact: Attackers can exploit this to perform melee attacks from any distance across the map, bypassing the intended range limits and severely impacting the game's economy and fairness.
🔧 Fix: Used inverted logic `not (distSq <= maxRange * maxRange)` for the spatial check to securely validate the boundaries and block `NaN` bypasses.
✅ Verification: Ran the project's test suite, linters, and formatters to ensure the check functions correctly and no regressions were introduced.

body:
The harvest half of the navigation-topology arm (the Core model half is lance-graph #670 / #673). An entity/behaviour transcode captures ClassViews (screens) + DTOs (actions) but not the navigation topology — which screen opens which. This adds the agnostic SPO fact for it.
What lands
ruff_spo_triplet::Predicate::NavigatesTo — one new closed-vocab predicate (count 64→65), default Inferred. The "form→route" edge the ruff_csharp_spo README already anticipated. Round-trips through the shared Triple carrier (compatible with main's new deny_unknown_fields — merged in and green).
ruff_csharp_spo::EmitNavArm (harvester/Program.cs) — a Roslyn pass detecting new TargetForm().Show() / .ShowDialog(), both as a one-liner (new Foo().Show()) and via a two-statement local (var f = new Foo(); f.ShowDialog();). Framework CommonDialogs (OpenFileDialog, etc.) are excluded — they are not screen nodes.
harvester/fixtures/nav_shapes.cs — a synthetic WinForms fixture (no proprietary source): three forms wired Main → Orders → Lines + Main → Settings. The real harvester over this fixture emits exactly the 3 navigates_to edges — verified end-to-end.
Why agnostic / public-safe
Screens = nodes, clicks = edges is a domain-blind graph shape. No app-specific identifiers, table names, or German labels — the fixture is invented. The private edge set (the actual Klickweg of a specific app) is consumed downstream in the consumer repo, never here.
Tests
ruff_spo_triplet 4/4, ruff_csharp_spo 100/100 (after merging current main). Additive: one enum variant + one harvester pass + one fixture.
The other half
The Core consumer — contract::class_view::{screens_reachable_from, nav_is_fully_connected} (reachability with cycles allowed; the level-editor connectivity validator, strengthened to reached == screens per codex P2) — is lance-graph #670 + follow-up #673.

* To use aws s3 api we need access key and secret key which we generate using yandex sdk for the configured yandex cloud service account.
* The generate aws access and secret key is removed on provider.Cleanup()
* We get service account id from sa `key` with `ProviderConfig.Spec.Method == StaticCredentials` and whoAmI function with `ProviderConfig.Spec.Method == WorkloadIdentity`

body:
## False-confidence test remediation — all 10 modules

Removes or rewrites confirmed false-confidence tests (0-assert / tautological / skip-dominated / mock-into-tautology) across the whole Verenigingen suite so that a green run means a real regression would fail — **without ever regressing coverage**.

**Test files only — zero production code changed in this branch.** Dead production code and missing features surfaced during the work were logged to two backlog files rather than fixed here (a separate branch, `fix/test-remediation-backlog`, addresses those).

### Method
A risk-ordered roadmap executed in **waves of 3 module-agents** (Wave 4 was the final single module). Each module ran the identical cycle: triage → disposition (rewrite / delete+backlog) → **mutation-verify every rewrite and new test** (green → break the prod target → confirm RED → revert) → module suite green on a `test_site_N` → coverage-Δ ≥ 0 → commit. After each wave, an independent `skeptical-code-reviewer` adjudicated the rewrites by reading the production code under test.

### Aggregate (Waves 1–4)
- **~18 test files + ~55 standalone tautological/dead methods deleted** (each re-grepped for callers).
- **~85 methods + 4 empty scaffolds rewritten** to call real production code instead of in-test reimplementations / mocks-of-the-function-under-test.
- **~27 new tests added** — ~10 genuine UNHAPPY gap-fill + 17 scaffold tests for previously-untested bookkeeping/tracker doctypes.
- **Coverage-Δ ≥ 0 for every module**; every wave APPROVED by skeptical review (0 Critical/Important).

### Reviews
- Per-wave skeptical reviews: all APPROVED.
- Final whole-branch review: **MERGE-READY** — all deferred minor notes resolved, zero residual false-confidence, zero prod files (verified), backlog completeness confirmed.

Full per-module breakdown, commits, and counts: `verenigingen/docs/testing/test-remediation/REMEDIATION-TRACKER.md`. Audit worklist: `verenigingen/docs/testing/test-inventory/`.

author: sangioletti
body:
## Summary

Makes the ESM-C / ESM3 embedding work **MIT-licence clean**: ESM-C is now served from the 2026 Chan Zuckerberg Biohub MIT-licensed [`esm`](https://github.com/Biohub/esm) fork (the same MIT package that already backs ESMFold2), and **ESM3 is removed entirely**.

Branched from `feat/esmc-esm3-embeddings` (PR #106).

### Why
The previous ESM-C/ESM3 runtime pulled EvolutionaryScale `esm==3.2.3`. ESM3's open weights (`esm3_sm_open_v1`) ship under the EvolutionaryScale Community licence, **not MIT**. This PR keeps only MIT-covered models.

### What changed
- **Renamed the `esm3` model family and runtime image → `esmc`.** ESM-C's runtime image now installs the Biohub `esm` fork (`git+https://github.com/Biohub/esm.git@c94ed8d`) instead of `esm==3.2.3`.
- **Dropped ESM3** everywhere: wrapper, core (`ESM3Core`), registry spec, top-level `boileroom.ESM3` export, docs, and tests.
- **ESM-C models**: `esmc_300m` (default), `esmc_600m`, `esmc_6b`, plus `esmc-*` aliases. Weights are the MIT-relicensed checkpoints `biohub/esmc-{300m,600m,6b}-2024-12`.
- The Biohub ESM-C SDK API (`esm.models.esmc.ESMC`, `esm.sdk.api.ESMProtein`/`LogitsConfig`, `.encode()`/`.logits()`) is identical to what the code already called, so the embedding logic is unchanged in behaviour.
- **bfloat16 fix**: the Biohub ESM-C SDK runs in bfloat16 on CUDA, which NumPy cannot convert directly; floating tensors are now upcast to float32 before `.numpy()`.
- Updated registry, image metadata, README, and docs (`models.md`, `architecture.md`, `backend_support_matrix.md`, `docker_images.md`).

### Breaking changes (acceptable on prerelease per repo policy)
- `from boileroom import ESM3` is removed. `from boileroom import ESMC` is unchanged.
- Internal module path `boileroom.models.esm3.*` → `boileroom.models.esmc.*`; runtime image `boileroom-esm3` → `boileroom-esmc`.

### Testing
- `pytest -m "not integration"` (the unit-tests CI filter): **137 passed, 3 skipped**.
- `scripts/harness/check_repo.py`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` (ruff + ruff-format + mypy): passed.
- The remaining suite failures locally are pre-existing Modal-GPU integration tests (separate workflow), unrelated to this change.

author: graham-williams
body:
## What
Adds a built-in **shared-password sign-in** to the taste-twin web app. Graham hands one password to a friend; entering it grants a long-lived signed session so re-auth is rare. This replaces the Cloudflare-Access emailed-PIN flow at cutover.

## How the gate works
- **Env-gated:** `APP_PASSWORD` set = gate **ON**; unset/empty = **OFF** (app behaves exactly as today). This lets it ship dormant behind Cloudflare Access and be switched on at cutover.
- A `before_request` gate (registered **first**, so it runs ahead of the CF-Access and Host pins) redirects any request that isn't `/login`, `/logout`, a static asset, or `/healthz` to `/login?next=<path>` until a signed session marker is present.
- `POST /login` compares the submitted password to `APP_PASSWORD` with **`hmac.compare_digest`** (constant-time). Success stores only a **signed session marker** (`session['tt_authed']`, signed with `SESSION_SECRET`/`SECRET_KEY` via itsdangerous) — the raw password is never stored in the cookie or logged. Cookie flags: **HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax**, 30-day lifetime.
- `next` is **open-redirect-safe** (local single-slash paths only; rejects `//host`, `https://`, `/\host`).
- Failed logins are **rate-limited per client IP** (`CF-Connecting-IP`, fallback `remote_addr`): ~10 failures / 15 min -> `429`, in-memory with bounded growth.
- Reuses the existing `APP_HOST` Origin/Referer **CSRF pin** for the login POST. `/logout` clears the session.
- **Cloudflare-Access JWT verification is kept intact and env-gated** (`CF_ACCESS_AUD`/`CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN`) — just left unconfigured after cutover.

**Exempt (reachable unauthenticated):** `/login`, `/logout`, static assets, `/healthz` (the container healthcheck).

## Box `.env` vars needed at cutover
```
APP_PASSWORD=<the-one-shared-password>
SESSION_SECRET=<random 32+ byte hex; python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))">
```
Keep `APP_HOST` set (already in `docker-compose.yml`) — it enforces the CSRF pin on `POST /login`. See DEPLOY.md "Sign-in" section for the full cutover steps (add vars -> redeploy -> verify `/login` -> then remove the CF Access app).

## Viewer-mode interaction
The gate sits **cleanly in front of** viewer mode: after signing in, the box gallery is still read-only (username form hidden, `POST /run` refused). Verified by test.

## Security
Parallel skeptical-reviewer panel over the diff (auth-bypass/session/open-redirect/CSRF/injection + secrets/PII/data-exposure/supply-chain): **no exploitable findings.** Two low-severity hardening notes applied: bounded the rate-limiter's per-IP table against an IP flood, and a DEPLOY.md nudge to keep `APP_HOST` set at cutover. No new dependencies (stdlib `hmac`/`secrets` + Flask-bundled session/itsdangerous). Live smoke test confirmed: unauth `/` -> 302 `/login`, wrong pw -> 401, correct pw -> signed marker-only cookie with the right flags. Full suite: **211 tests pass.**

author: phas02
body:
## The bug (verified on live data)

`packages/cockpit/src/duckdb/parts.ts` composes a non-additive metric drill (a ratio like `operating_margin`) by joining the dim-carrying carrier CTEs with `FULL JOIN … USING(dim)`. `USING` treats NULL as **unequal** (`NULL != NULL`), so when the slice dimension has NULL values (e.g. `cost_center` is NULL for 52% of journal rows) the NULL group never matches across carriers: it **SPLITS into two one-sided rows** that each render a dash (`—`) and **discard the real value**.

On the live workspace, `operating_margin` by `cost_center` returned **7 rows for 6 groups** — the NULL group appeared twice, both dashed, true value **46.46% lost**. The additive path was already correct because it uses `GROUP BY`, which folds NULL into one group.

## The fix

Make the carrier join NULL-safe and type-preserving (semantics verified against the real lake in a Python spike):

1. Replace `USING(dim)` with an explicit `ON dim IS NOT DISTINCT FROM dim` per dim (NULL matches NULL). For the chained spine (`carrier1 FULL JOIN carrier2 FULL JOIN carrier3 …`), the **left key of each successive join is `COALESCE(<all prior carriers>.dim)`** — a FULL JOIN can leave either side's key NULL.
2. The output dim projection becomes `COALESCE(c1.dim, c2.dim, …) AS dim` — with `ON` (not `USING`) every carrier alias now carries the dim column, so a bare `dim` would be ambiguous.

The value expression is **unchanged** (bare refs, `NULLIF`-guarded division). The **additive path and every other composition tier are untouched.**

Generated SQL (`rev_over_cogs` sliced by `cost_center`), matching the spike's reference shape:

```sql
... "rev_over_cogs" AS (
  SELECT COALESCE("revenue"."cost_center", "cost_of_goods_sold"."cost_center") AS "cost_center",
         "revenue"."value" AS "revenue",
         "cost_of_goods_sold"."value" AS "cost_of_goods_sold",
         ("revenue"."value" / NULLIF("cost_of_goods_sold"."value", 0)) AS "value"
  FROM "revenue"
  FULL JOIN "cost_of_goods_sold"
    ON ("revenue"."cost_center" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM "cost_of_goods_sold"."cost_center")
) ...
```

3-carrier chained spine correctly COALESCEs over all prior carriers:

```
FROM "a" FULL JOIN "b" ON ("a"."d1" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM "b"."d1") ...
       FULL JOIN "c" ON (COALESCE("a"."d1", "b"."d1") IS NOT DISTINCT FROM "c"."d1") ...
```

## Test hardening

`parts.test.ts` gains a partially-NULL slice dim (`cost_center`, NULL for the `east` rows — both carriers observed in the NULL group and in `cc1`) and a new `NULL-dim non-additive slice (DAT-714)` block:
- NULL group is **ONE row with the real value** (`300/80 = 3.75`), never two dashes; **no duplicate group keys**.
- **pin ≡ group for EVERY group INCLUDING the NULL group** (a NULL-group pin renders `IS NULL`, consumes no param).
- joins NULL-safe (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`), never `FULL JOIN … USING`.

The existing one-sided-ratio test's stale `not.toContain("COALESCE")` string-proxy is replaced by `toContain("IS NOT DISTINCT FROM")` + `not.toContain("USING (")`; its value-fabrication guard (the absent side stays NULL) is unchanged.

**These 4 tests fail against the old `USING` join and pass with the fix** (verified by reverting only the source change).

## Verification

- `bun run test` — **177 files, 1669 tests, all green** (parts.test.ts: 47).
- `bun run check` (biome) — clean.
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean.

```
 Test Files  177 passed (177)
      Tests  1669 passed (1669)
```

- **Link `/support` from `/service`**: a "Product manuals, guides & videos" row in the Documents block, so browsing customers can reach the manuals and MMEXO videos without scanning a QR code.
- - **`/service` copy is CMS-editable**: guarantee, returns steps, FAQ, documents and contact copy moved into Site settings, Microcopy (was hardcoded; only headline/intro were editable before). The current English text stays as in-code fallbacks so the page never blanks. Also the `/support` index headline/intro.
- - **Language tag on support downloads**: every PDF/video gets a structured Language field (da/de/nl/fr/en/es), shown on the download and machine-readable, so the market system can later serve each market its own language. MMEXO videos are pre-tagged.
## Changes
- app/service/page.tsx, app/support/page.tsx, app/support/[slug]/page.tsx: CMS wiring + language label.
- - sanity/schemaTypes/siteSettings.ts (service/support fields), supportPage.ts (Language field).
- - lib/cms.ts: types + projections. lib/help-knowledge.ts + docs/STROXX-editor-guide.md: editor docs.
- - scripts/seed-service-copy.ts (new, `npm run seed:service`): safe setIfMissing populate of the base English copy; seed-home-stores.ts defaults; seed-videos.ts language tags.
## Notes
- English is the reference/fallback language per the market-localisation plan.
- - Base English copy seeded on the dataset via `npm run seed:service` (only fills empty fields).
- - Verified: lint + typecheck clean.

author: majabri
body:
Fixes the enrichment queue throughput bottleneck the diagnostic surfaced (26,087 rows pending, curator producing near-zero exec-security matches).

## Fix 1 — Self-draining enrichment (edge function, `enrich-jobs`)
- `BATCH_SIZE` 100 → **250** (2.5× per invocation).
- New `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 40` constant.
- `runBatch` now returns `remainingPending`; when > 0 **and** `chainDepth < 40`, the function fires-and-forgets a POST to itself with `{ chainDepth: chainDepth + 1 }`.
- **Each 4h cron tick now drains up to 40 × 250 = 10,000 rows** (was 100). Response includes `{ chainDepth, remainingPending }` for observability.

## Fix 2 — Priority lane for fresh ingests
- `runBatch` accepts `{ priorityTitleFilter?: string }` — `|`-delimited word list.
- When set, the batch pulls priority-matching rows FIRST (via OR-joined ilike patterns on `title`), then fills remaining budget from the general queue with a `not-in-ids` exclude to avoid double-processing.
- `ingest-ats-direct` now fires **one fire-and-forget enrichment** post-upsert with `priorityTitleFilter='security|ciso|biso|director|chief|vp|head of'`. Freshly ingested exec titles get classified in the same cron tick as their ingest. Filter is a param — reusable for future patterns.

## Fix 3 — Curator degrades gracefully (Next.js side)
- `queryJobsForRole`: family fast-path drops `enrichment_status='complete'` filter; rows with populated `role_families` qualify regardless of overall status.
- **New third fallback**: if family + enriched-title both return 0, run title tsquery **without** the enrichment filter. Results tagged `queryMethod: 'title_unenriched'` so scoring knows to skip the family fast-path.
- Return type widened to `'family' | 'title' | 'title_unenriched'`.
- `queryByRoleFamilies` + `queryBySeniorityTier` also drop the enrichment filter (same graceful-degrade reason).

## Fix 4 — Widen `security_architect` synonyms
Added `solutions architect security`, `security solutions architect`, `principal solutions architect security`. Elastic's *"Principal Solutions Architect, Security"* was falling out of every family because the existing synonyms all led with `"security architect"` (wrong word order). Word-boundary matching from PR #359 handles the new synonyms correctly.

## Tests

**16 new** in `enrichmentThroughput.test.ts`:
- Fix 1: chainDepth cap, empty-queue stop, `40×250=10K` budget
- Fix 2: `priorityTitleFilter → OR ilike` conversion (3-token / empty / trimmed / 7-token)
- Fix 3: source-code assertions that enrichment filter was removed + `title_unenriched` fallback added
- Fix 4: `Principal Solutions Architect, Security → security_architect`, negative test `Software Solutions Architect NOT classified`, 3 new synonyms present in `ROLE_FAMILIES.security_architect`
- Regression: Field CISO → `ciso`, Director of Security → `director_of_security`

**Full suite: 1100/1100 pass** (+16 new). Type-check clean.

## ⚠️ Deployment — hand to Platform

Fixes 1 + 2 touch the edge functions. **Per Amir 2026-07-06 process note: do NOT deploy from Jobs Cowork.** Platform will push v15 of both `enrich-jobs` and `ingest-ats-direct` after this PR merges. Fixes 3 + 4 are Next.js-side and go live automatically with the Vercel deploy on merge.

## Exact deploy note for Platform Chat

> **PR #365 (`fix/jobs-enrichment-throughput`) is merged. Please deploy v15 of two edge functions:**
> - `enrich-jobs` — from `supabase/functions/enrich-jobs/index.ts` at merge SHA. Runtime change: batch=250, self-invokes on remaining pending up to chainDepth=40. First 4h cron tick after deploy should drain the current 25K pending queue in one pass.
> - `ingest-ats-direct` — from `supabase/functions/ingest-ats-direct/index.ts` at merge SHA. Runtime change: fires priority-lane enrich POST after upsert.
>
> Deploy commands:
> ```bash
> supabase functions deploy enrich-jobs         --project-ref kuneabeiwcxavvyyfjkx
> supabase functions deploy ingest-ats-direct   --project-ref kuneabeiwcxavvyyfjkx
> ```
>
> **Post-deploy verification:** `POST /functions/v1/enrich-jobs` with body `{}` — response should include `chainDepth: 0, remainingPending: N, processed: <=250`. Poll `SELECT enrichment_status, count(*) FROM ats_jobs GROUP BY 1` — should hit `pending ≈ 0` within one cron tick or one manual trigger.

body:
## Resumen

`v8.6.79 (BF.RANGE-FIX)` — sustituye el límite superior fijo (2019) del rango prioritario de recogida de tags del backfill por `datetime.now().year`, recalculado en cada pasada.

## Contexto

BF.PRIO (v8.6.78) fijó el rango prioritario en `debut_year` 1960-2019. Eso dejaba fuera de la cola prioritaria a los artistas 2020-2026+. No bloqueaba la generación de música actual (el gate de era y las décadas "20s" —`DECADE_YEARS["20s"] = (2020, 2029)`— funcionan con normalidad), pero sí retrasaba que esos artistas tuvieran tags en `artist_info_cache` y, por tanto, que aparecieran como candidatos en `_artist_info_tag_pool` (TAGS.1) para pipes de música actual. Detectado por Alberto (2026-07-08).

## Cambio

```python
# antes
_tag_filter = {"debut_year": {"$gte": 1960, "$lte": 2019}, "tags_checked": {"$ne": True}}
# ahora
_tag_filter = {"debut_year": {"$gte": 1960, "$lte": datetime.now().year}, "tags_checked": {"$ne": True}}
```

Un literal → una expresión dinámica recalculada en cada pasada, así que se autoactualiza cada año sin mantenimiento. `datetime` ya estaba importado a nivel de módulo. No toca gate, scoring ni selección (regla 19).

## Archivos

- `main.py` — `_backfill_run_pass`: `_tag_filter` con límite superior dinámico; `BOT_VERSION` → v8.6.79.
- `changelog.py` — entrada v8.6.79.
- `ESTADO.md` — versión en producción v8.6.79.
- `backups/kurator_v8.6.78.py` — backup del original v8.6.78.

## Aceptación

`python -m py_compile main.py` → OK.

author: lcj-claude-coder
body:
## Problem

`set_breakpoint` speaks **TypeScript** coordinates, but the only source-reading tool, `get_script_source`, returns **compiled JS**. Agents read a line number off that JS and pass it to `set_breakpoint` against the `.ts` filename — a JS line used as a TS line — binding the breakpoint at the wrong TS line, frequently one where a supplied `condition` can never be true. The never-firing conditional breakpoint then fails **silently**: `wait_for_pause` reports only a generic timeout.

Observed (opus-4.8, `node-conditional-bp`): a conditional bp set at `conditional-bp.ts:14` with `condition: "i === 3"` slid onto the loop header, the condition never held, the target ran to completion, and the wait timed out → thrash.

## Fix — three layered changes

**1. `get_source` (new tool)** — fetch the original **TypeScript** by TS path/fragment (symmetric with `set_breakpoint` / `resolve_source_position`). Resolves via the map's embedded `sourcesContent`, falling back to an on-disk read for loopback sessions (`tsc --sourceMap` emits `sources` but no `sourcesContent`), reusing the loader's `file://` loopback security gate. `get_script_source`'s description now warns its line numbers are compiled JS, **not** `set_breakpoint` coordinates, and points here.

**2. `set_breakpoint` line-drift warning** — the response envelope now echoes `requested` and adds a `warning` when CDP binds on a different TS line than requested (the fingerprint of a JS line used as a TS line), naming the trap and pointing at `get_source`.

**3. `wait_for_pause` timeout diagnostics** — a bare timeout becomes a `pause_timeout` error that lists never-fired conditional breakpoints (resolved TS location + condition, with remediation) and, when detectable, reports that the owned Node target already exited.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` + `npm run build` clean
- **Unit: 1017/1017** — new L1 resolver tests; L2 `get_source` / warning / `pause_timeout` tests; contract tool count 51 → 52
- **Full L3 e2e: 42/42** — including two new real-Node-inspector cases in `node-conditional-bp.e2e.test.ts` (`get_source` returns the real TS; `wait_for_pause` surfaces the `pause_timeout` diagnostic)
- Manual real-inspector drive reproducing the failure end-to-end: `get_source` returned the actual `.ts` (with type annotations), the wrong-line bp produced the drift warning, and `wait_for_pause` surfaced the diagnostic instead of a bare timeout

Fixes #46.

author: aekdahl
body:
## Problem

A real agent could reach `finalStatus=done` with its change **uncommitted and unintegrated** — the fix landed in the worktree, the agent declared success, yet no integration branch was created and the diff artifact was empty. Reproduced via `evals/run.ts exec bugfix-failing-test` (intermittent, ~4/5 runs).

## Root cause (both prior hypotheses disproven by instrumentation)

Not a clean worktree (`git status` was dirty and `commitAll` committed a real sha every time) and not a file-flush race. It's a **status race in the runner→orchestrator handoff**:

Every runner's `finish()` emitted `onStatus("done")` **synchronously before** `onCompleted` triggered `complete()`. Trace (timestamps):
1. `finish()` → `onStatus("done")` → store shows **done** immediately.
2. An observer (the eval poll) sees `done`, captures `git diff main...branch` — but `complete()→commitAll` advances the branch **~950ms later**.
3. Branch still at the fixture commit → **empty diff**; `complete()` then commits and moves to `review`, too late.

All five runners shared the defect (`claude`, `mock`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `cli-runner`=codex+gemini).

## Fix — `done` is the orchestrator's decision

- `events().onStatus` **ignores a runner-emitted `"done"`** — terminal state only via `complete()`/`completeMerged`.
- `complete()`'s plain/no-change path sets `agentStatus("done")` itself; a `commitAll` **error** now routes to `review` (needs-attention), never a silent done that drops real edits.
- Removed the premature `onStatus("done")` from every runner's `finish()`.

## Regression guard

`skynet/tests/agent-completion-integrity.test.ts` drives the real orchestrator with a fake provider that reproduces the exact defect (edits the worktree, then reports `done`+`onCompleted`) and asserts **no `done` precedes the diff review** and the edit is committed. Verified it **fails on the pre-fix orchestrator** and passes after.

## Verification

- Repro loop: `done + empty diff` (4/5) → **5/5 full 230-char diffs**.
- Full test suite: 2 new tests pass, all previously-passing tests still pass. The 5 `contracts`/`assign-and-chat` failures are **pre-existing** (identical on pristine baseline).
- `pnpm -r typecheck`: clean.

Scoped to the orchestrator drop-commit bug; the eval-infra fixes remain on `fix/eval-diff-capture`.

author: abdulberk
body:
…s) no longer hard-fail

The default grid placement is size-blind: it packs each part on a fixed pitch, so a physically large part (e.g. a 14mm 6-pin ICSP header, or a 32-pin TQFP) lands in a cell smaller than its courtyard and tscircuit rejects the WHOLE board with pcb_courtyard_overlap_error → layoutCircuit returned LAYOUT FAIL (no board at all). But the failed eval still carries every part's REAL geometry, so we now re-run the courtyard-aware placement engine (placeParts, which legalizes with real courtyard extents) off that geometry and re-evaluate, adopting ANY valid result — there is no valid grid baseline to beat on HPWL. Guarded: only fires when parity is otherwise ok and EVERY error is a courtyard overlap (a pure placement-geometry fault a re-place can fix), so it cannot mask a real electrical/connectivity failure.

attemptAutoPlacement gains an adoptOnValidity flag (skip the HPWL-improvement gate in rescue mode).

Measured (gauntlet): atmega328-min went LAYOUT FAIL → produces a routed board (parity 56/56, 64 traces). No regression: the 6 previously-clean boards are unchanged (the rescue never fires for them). Routing the dense rescued board fully DRC-clean is a separate, harder problem (freerouting headroom) — this fix is the placement half: dense boards are now producible instead of a hard failure.

author: quintinshaw
body:
## Summary

Consolidate the hand-rolled SentencePiece/metaspace decode logic (metaspace `_`->space, `<0xXX>` byte-fallback, bracketed special-token handling, trimming) into one shared `SpmDecoder`, removing per-family duplication and its drift risk.

## Changes

- New `models/spm_decoder.rs`: `decode_spm_pieces(pieces, config)` with 4 orthogonal knobs (word-marker join, special-token policy, byte-fallback, trim) + named presets.

author: waleedlatif1
body:
## Summary

Fixes a class of structural editing + serialization bugs in the rich-markdown (`.md`) editor, discovered while fixing the reported "deleting a bullet leaves a weird space" bug. A deep audit (parallel subagents + a real-browser ProseMirror harness) found the original fix was **not isolated** — the same class spanned other boundary keys, node types, and the serializer. This PR eliminates the whole class.

### Tier 1 — Empty-wrapped-block boundary keys (`keymap.ts`)
`joinBackward` on an empty list item left a stray empty paragraph inside the previous item (flat lists), no-op'd on nested items (leaving them stuck), and never handled blockquotes (which split in two). Replaced with a `walk-up-and-delete` that removes the whole emptied wrapper, generalized to **list items, task items, and blockquotes** at every position. Added an **Enter** handler: pressing Enter on an empty *non-trailing* list/task item previously split the list around a stranded, non-round-trippable empty paragraph; it now removes the empty item. A *trailing* empty item still exits the list via the default (unchanged).

### Tier 2 — Verbatim node isolation (`raw-markdown-snippet.tsx`)
`footnoteDef` and `rawHtmlBlock` hold exact source text but were neither `isolating` nor `atom`, so a single Backspace/Delete at their boundary merged their raw markdown into an adjacent paragraph as HTML-escaped prose — **silently destroying the node and corrupting saved markdown**. Marked the block variants `isolating`.

### Tier 3 — Paragraph serialization guard (`extensions.ts`)
`BlockSafeParagraph` guards a paragraph's leading characters so it can't re-parse into a different block on the next load:
- **Leading block markers** (`#`, `-`, `+`, `1.`, `1)`, bare `---`) are backslash-escaped (the upstream serializer escaped inline delimiters — so `*` bullets and `>` quotes already round-tripped — but not these).
- **Leading indent** (4-space/tab) is stripped — it never renders in a paragraph and would otherwise re-parse as an indented code block. (Real indented/fenced code blocks are `codeBlock` nodes, untouched.)
- Replacing StarterKit's Paragraph also drops the upstream ` ` empty-paragraph marker: **consecutive empty paragraphs now round-trip via blank lines** — count-preserved, idempotent, and no longer tripping the read-only safety gate (which flags ` `).

All escaping/stripping is idempotent (parsing consumes it) and never over-escapes non-markers (`#hashtag`, `-5`).

## Testing
Real-browser ProseMirror harness + committed Vitest (CI):
- Tier 1: bullet/ordered/task/blockquote/nested, Backspace + Enter, all positions, regressions.
- Tier 2: boundary corruption (footnote + raw HTML) + in-place editing + whole-node deletion + round-trip.
- Tier 3: marker escaping, indent stripping, no over-escape, and empty-paragraph count preservation (1–4).
- **Regression: round-trip fixtures stay byte-identical idempotent** (headings, marks, all list types, quotes, code blocks, mermaid, tables, images, footnotes, raw/inline HTML, mentions, real indented code, full mixed docs), verbatim nodes still edit/delete, input rules (`# `/`- `) still autoformat — confirming the paragraph replacement and `isolating` changes have no side effects.

## Note
An empty blockquote (a `>` with no content) normalizes away to blank lines on reload. This is a benign one-time normalization (idempotent, no data loss, not read-only) — preserving an empty quote has no clean CommonMark representation and would reintroduce the ` `→read-only problem, so normalizing is the correct behavior.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/dapper-kataifi-28be88/agent-runs/6a4ea7c34912291b26776a5a

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** The Netlify deploy errored, with the following guidance provided:

Diagnosis
- Relevant error lines: [line 11](#L11), [line 12](#L12), [line 13](#L13) and [line 16](#L16). These show pip reading requirements and failing to find a matching wheel for t...

✅ **Result:** The deploy was failing during the dependency installation step because pip could not find a wheel for `torch==2.4.1+cpu`. The Netlify build environment was resolving Python to version 3.14.3 (from a `python = "latest"` setting), and PyTorch 2.4.1 was never published with wheels for that Python release — only much newer torch releases (2.9.x) have wheels built against it, and this project intentionally stays on 2.4.1 to match the pins used everywhere else (numpy, scipy, and the Docker image).

Rather than bumping the pinned torch version (which would ripple into every other pinned dependency that was chosen to match it), the fix pins the Python version used by the Netlify build to 3.12 — the same version the project's Docker image already uses. This keeps the existing `torch==2.4.1+cpu` requirement valid, since PyTorch does publish CPU wheels for Python 3.12, and keeps the Netlify build environment consistent with the Docker build environment instead of drifting to whatever the newest available Python happens to be.

This was done by adding a project-level mise configuration file that pins Python to 3.12, overriding the "latest" default that was picking up an unsupported Python version.
