body:
💡 **What:** 
Replaced redundant `for` loops appending to a list with Python list comprehensions and tuple-based `startswith()` checks in form data parsing loops. Used `FormData.multi_items()` to properly handle multi-file uploads of identically named keys.
🎯 **Why:** 
Appending to lists dynamically via loop iterations in Python is computationally heavier than evaluating comprehensions in C. Furthermore, standard iteration over `FormData` in Starlette drops files when multiple uploads have the identical key `name` (e.g., standard HTML array `<input multiple>`), which `multi_items()` corrects.
📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
Baseline code processing 100 mock files took ~1.34s for 10,000 iterations.
Optimized code took ~0.71s for the same iterations.
Resulted in a **~46.77% performance improvement** on the form data parsing hot path.

author: michaelleungadvgen
body:
💡 What: Replaced `_operationCounts.Values.Sum()` and four separate `.GetValueOrDefault()` calls in `WriteConcernManager.GetStatistics()` with a single lock-free `foreach` loop over the `ConcurrentDictionary`.
🎯 Why: Accessing `.Values` on a `ConcurrentDictionary` allocates a new `ReadOnlyCollection` snapshot array, causing unnecessary O(N) memory allocation and garbage collection overhead. Furthermore, doing four separate dictionary lookups immediately afterward for specific keys multiplied the CPU lookup cost and contention.
📊 Impact: Eliminates array allocation overhead (O(N) to O(1) allocation) and reduces dictionary lookup overhead (5x queries down to 1 pass) when gathering metrics, reducing GC pressure during statistics tracking.
🔬 Measurement: Run a memory profiler during a high-throughput load test querying stats, and observe zero array allocations originating from `WriteConcernManager.GetStatistics()`.

author: khatchad
body:
Implements wala/ML#702. Adds `testDiagnosticLoggingVolumeBounded`, a self-contained guard against the class of bug fixed by the `Loggables` sweep (#544): a bare render of a `Context`-bearing value in a log or exception message, whose cyclic `Context.toString()` exhausts the heap on large graphs (wala/ML#697; upstream root cause wala/WALA#1992). That class is invisible in CI, which logs at `WARNING` so the `FINE`/`FINEST` message strings are never built; that gap let ~56 sites accumulate unnoticed.

## How It Works

The test reruns the nlpgnn generation analysis (the cyclic-closure call graph behind #697) with every `com.ibm.wala.cast.python` logger at `FINEST`, routing records through a new `DiscardingFormattingHandler` that formats and discards them while summing the formatted volume, then asserts the total stays under a bound.

## Why a Volume Assertion, Not a Heap Cap

The issue proposed a capped-`-Xmx` `FINEST` run that OOMs on regression. Investigation showed that is fragile: the heap exhaustion happens in the publish path and is cumulative, so it only reproduces with real output writing (hundreds of MB to over a GB) and its timing depends on heap size and output backpressure. A volume assertion is deterministic instead: correct code renders through the bounded `Loggables.describe(...)` (~0.6 GB of formatted `FINEST` output here), while a bare render inflates that by more than an order of magnitude (~14 GB measured). The handler discards output, so the guard needs no capped heap, no gigabytes of log files, and no CI-workflow changes; it runs in the normal suite.

On a violation the failure names the likely cause (a value logged without `Loggables.describe(...)`) and points at `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s Diagnostic Logging section.

author: gocarisrael-hub
body:
Four related order-wizard changes on the honoree-name step. They all touch the name validation and/or the create button, so they ship in one PR.

## 1. Single-word honoree name (no spaces)
`isValidHonoreeName` now rejects any internal whitespace — the honoree name is ONE word. Hyphen `-` and apostrophe `'` stay allowed (e.g. `Anne-Marie`, `O'Neil`). Digits/symbols still rejected. Inline error copy updated (`site/options.html`).

## 2. Numbers-only for numeric extra fields (AGE / YEARS)
New pure `isValidIntegerField(v, min, max)` in `configurator.js` — digits-only integer within the input's min/max (stricter than `parseInt`: rejects `12abc`, `3.5`, `1e3`, spaces). `extraFieldsValid()` now blocks Next on a non-integer, and an inline error shows per numeric field. `step="1"` added to the AGE/YEARS inputs.

## 3. Enforce name language per template (from theme data)
- `designs.js`: new `LANGUAGE_BY_THEME` mirroring `generator/themes.json` `language` (kept in sync like `THEME_EXTRA_FIELDS`/`VISIBILITY_BY_THEME`, covering all 8 themes), plus `languageForDesign(id)` (defaults unknown ids to `hebrew`, the Hebrew-first product default; accepts a map override for testability).
- `isValidHonoreeName(v, language)` gains an optional `language` param (backward-compatible when omitted): an `english` design rejects Hebrew names / requires Latin; a `hebrew` design rejects Latin / requires Hebrew.
- Wired through `validateStep` / `refreshNameError` / `createCollection` via `currentLanguage()`, plus the couple NAME1/NAME2 fields (anniversary = hebrew). Clear Hebrew inline hint distinguishes a language mismatch from a format error.

## 4. Gate the "create the game" button on the preview
On the preview step the create/next button stays disabled until the name-preview has rendered on screen (`markPreviewShown()` on the real images OR the settled graceful fallback), with a 20s backstop (`armPreviewFallback()`) so a valid client is never permanently stuck. Field validity still gates as before.

## Tests
- Unit: `tests/unit/honoree-name.test.js` (single-word / hyphen-apostrophe / digits / empty / both language directions / integer-field digit-only + bounds) and `tests/unit/design-language.test.js` (`LANGUAGE_BY_THEME` mirrors themes.json for every theme; `languageForDesign` resolution, default, override).
- E2E: new `tests/e2e/wizard-name-gate.spec.js` (button disabled until preview shows; failed preview still unlocks; english design rejects Hebrew + spaced names; hebrew design rejects Latin, with the right inline error). Existing wizard specs updated to English honoree names on the english-default design and to stub `/api/preview` so the gate opens deterministically.

## Checks
`npm run format:check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test:unit` (454 passed) all green. Ran the affected Playwright specs in isolation on Desktop Chrome — all pass (configurator 23, gate/rules 4, collect 24, theme-extra-fields / gender-bleed / chasers / name-preview 20, preview-fit/zoom/noscroll 37).

author: etienneprx
body:
Closes #120

## Diagnostic

Le signalement de problème (`IssueReporter.tsx`) ne se déclenchait que via l'événement `contextmenu` (clic droit). Or **iOS Safari ne déclenche jamais `contextmenu` sur un appui long** pour un élément DOM quelconque — c'est une limitation connue de WebKit (contrairement à Android Chrome, qui simule bien `contextmenu` au appui long). Résultat : sur Safari mobile, le menu « Signaler un problème » n'apparaissait jamais, la fonctionnalité était donc totalement inaccessible — d'où le signalement de Yannick (#120).

## Changement

- `components/interactive/IssueReporter.tsx` : ajoute un bouton flottant (`.issue-fab`, bas-droite, `position: fixed`) qui ouvre directement la modale via un tap standard.
- **Affiché uniquement sous 900px** (mobile/tablette) : sur desktop, le clic droit (`contextmenu`) fonctionne déjà et suffit — le bouton n'y apporte rien de plus qu'un contexte moins riche (pas de section/extrait ciblés). Le clic droit desktop est conservé tel quel (`handleContextMenu` inchangé).
- Prend en compte les safe-area-insets (`env(safe-area-inset-bottom/right)`) pour éviter que le bouton soit masqué par l'indicateur d'accueil sur les iPhone à encoche.
- `app/globals.css` : styles `.issue-fab` (cohérents avec `.share-btn`).

## Tests

- `npx vitest run` : ✅ 31/31
- `npm run build` : ✅ compilation stricte
- Vérifié en local : bouton caché sur desktop (`display:none`), visible et fonctionnel sur mobile (375×812), clic droit toujours fonctionnel en parallèle sur desktop

author: poszu
body:
## Why

Companion to podnetwork/pod#1479, which changes native-token bridge withdrawals to move the coin via `tx.value` (standard EVM value path) instead of burning it internally. The existing docs tell users to *"set `tx.value` to `0`, even for native token withdrawals"* — that's now incorrect and would make every native withdraw revert.

## Changes

**`doc/api-reference/guides/bridge-from-pod.md`**
- Rewrote the warning hint: native token → `tx.value` = `amount` scaled up to Pod's 18 decimals (e.g. 1 USDC → `amount=1e6`, `tx.value=1e18`); ERC20 → `tx.value=0`.
- Updated the TypeScript and Rust examples to compute `value` from the token + its Ethereum decimals (native → scaled, ERC20 → 0), and the Rust example now passes `.value(value)`.

**`doc/protocol/native-bridge.md`**
- Extended the Pod → Ethereum decimal-scaling note: native withdrawals carry the coin as `tx.value` (= amount scaled to 18 dec), subject to the usual `native >= tx.value + gas` check, so you can't bridge your whole balance and leave nothing for gas.

`amount` remains in the destination chain's decimals (unchanged) — only the `tx.value` guidance changes.

body:
Dashboard half of Phase 3D.

## What's here
- **Diagram manager** on the aviary page: view, relabel, reorder (earlier/later), remove (draft-only — published versions keep frozen copies), and upload. Uploads run three steps — mint presigned URL → PUT bytes browser→bucket → attach via the replace-set — with client-side type/size guards before minting and the server's messages (incl. the uploads-not-configured 503) surfaced inline.
- **New Aviary page** (lean form, design §5 rethought): name + auto-derived slug + clone-or-blank; on create it lands on the aviary editing page. New aviaries start **inactive**.
- **ActivationControl**: activate/deactivate an aviary — the deliberate final step before an inactive draft can reach observers (still only on publish).

## Contract note (why the API PR must go first / together)
The presigned PUT is signed with `Content-Type` AND `If-None-Match:*` (the storage-layer overwrite guard). `uploadToBucket` sends both exactly — a 412 (object exists) surfaces as a failed upload and the caller re-mints a fresh version rather than clobbering.

## Review
Manual adversarial read (the API branch got the multi-agent pass). Contract points verified against the just-changed API (minted-URL attach, replace-set payload shape, activation). One considered-and-dismissed item: a sequential-upload race that would need a full file-select-and-label cycle to fit inside one reload round-trip — human-unreachable, and a dropped object is recoverable.

## Verification
79 tests (was 61), lint (oxlint), build, prettier all green. Pairs with ethogram-api #51.

author: evrydayimruslin
body:
## Bug

PR #83's stale-run reaper built one PostgREST filter with a nested `or(...)` inside an `and(...)`, all under a top-level `or=(...)`:

```
or=(and(status.eq.running,lease_expires_at.lt.X),
    and(status.eq.running,lease_expires_at.is.null,started_at.lt.Y),
    and(status.eq.queued,created_at.lt.Z,or(next_attempt_at.is.null,next_attempt_at.lt.X)))
```

That query **silently matched zero rows** in prod — PostgREST returned an empty set (not a 400), so the `.catch` never fired and no error surfaced. A run wedged in `"running"` since a prior deploy stayed stuck across many cron cycles, its `max_concurrency` slot held forever. The unit test passed because the mock replicated my *assumption* of how the filter parses, not PostgREST's actual behavior.

## Fix

Two **flat** filters — the same shape `queuedRunCandidates` / `activeRunCount` already use in prod (plain `status` + column params, no `and`/`or` grouping):

1. `status=eq.running & lease_expires_at=lt.<now>` — a live lease that expired
2. `status=eq.running & lease_expires_at=is.null & started_at=lt.<now-lease>` — a lease-less run stuck past the window

Disjoint (lease non-null-and-past vs lease null) → nothing counted twice. Dropped the `"queued"` backstop: a queued run is never orphaned (`queuedRunCandidates` re-dispatches it every cron; a lost `EXEC_QUEUE` message is near-impossible with at-least-once delivery + DLQ).

## Verification (prod)

The run stuck in `"running"` since `18:03Z` flipped to `failed` (`ServerTimeout`) within a few crons of deploying the flat filter, freeing its slot. The test mock now keys off the `lease_expires_at` filter param (unique to the reaper), so it exercises the exact flat queries the code issues.

- `routine-executor.test.ts`: 11/11 · `tsc` clean · knip baseline

`useProjectedEarnings` now derives and returns a `currency` from the eligible tokens it sums over (instead of consumers reading `selectCurrentCurrency` separately), so the projected-earnings total and the currency label can never drift apart. - author: underminedsk
body:
## What

Repo-split phase 1, PR 4 of 4: separate the CI/release workflow surface into public-persistent files and private-bound files, so whole workflow files move at cut time instead of job-level surgery inside `ci.yml`/`release.yml`.

**ci.yml (public, trimmed):**
- `unit-tests` no longer installs `bobi_deploy` and runs only `tests/` (public product).
- `lint` keeps actionlint only (renamed `Lint (workflows)`).
- `package-smoke` and `integration-wrangler` moved out (below).
- The public event-server gates (`npx tsc --noEmit` + vitest over events-core and `local.ts`), e2e, and non-Claude integration jobs are untouched.

**New private-bound files (same triggers as ci.yml, so coverage is unchanged):**
- `deploy-package.yml`: bobi-deploy unit tests (3.12/3.13 matrix) + the two-wheel install smoke (the phase-1 exit criterion).
- `worker-integration.yml`: the wrangler-dev integration job, moved verbatim.

**container.yml** gains an `image-lint` job (hadolint + `docker build --check`, both build modes), moved from ci.yml's every-PR lint job. Every input to those checks (Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, `docker/**`, `pyproject.toml`) is already in this workflow's path filter, so a lint regression cannot arrive on a path that skips the job. No branch-protection required checks reference the old job name (the active ruleset enforces deletion/non-fast-forward only).

**release.yml** keeps the public release (subscription-login smoke, build-wheel, PyPI trusted publishing, Homebrew) and calls two new reusable workflows:
- `release-fleet.yml` (`workflow_call`): deploy-event-server + build-canary, exporting the `smoked` output. `publish` now gates on the `fleet` caller job - the same failure set as before (an event-server deploy failure still cascades; the FLY-token-unset skip still lets publish proceed with PyPI's trusted-publisher backstop).
- `release-image.yml` (`workflow_call`): publish-image + publish-manifest, with the `IMAGE` env definition moved in. Deliberately not in `publish`'s needs, preserving "a GHCR failure never blocks PyPI". The caller `image` job carries the smoked + release-tag-shaped gates and the `packages: write` permission cap.
- PyPI publish stays a native job in release.yml (trusted publishing rejects reusable workflows).

At cut time: `deploy-package.yml`, `worker-integration.yml`, `release-fleet.yml`, `release-image.yml`, `container.yml`, `team-images.yml` move to the private repo whole; release.yml drops the two caller jobs and re-gates `publish` on the public jobs.

## Tests

- `tests/test_release_workflow.py`, `test_gitops_c22.py`, `test_ci_workflows.py` follow their jobs into the new files and additionally pin the new cut-time contract: caller wiring, `secrets: inherit` on fleet, `smoked` output plumbing, publish gated on fleet but not image, called workflows consuming build-wheel outputs only via inputs.
- `tests/test_tool_guides.py` now resolves bobi-deploy plugin commands from the plugin's on-disk `bobi.commands` entry-point declarations, so the public unit suite passes without the plugin installed (with it gone at cut time, stale `bobi deploy` doc references fail the contract check again, as they should).
- Shared `workflow_on()` helper added to `tests/workflow_utils.py` (PyYAML bare-`on:` workaround, previously duplicated).

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean across all seven workflow files.
- Public unit suite (3042 tests) passes with bobi-deploy **uninstalled** (the new `unit-tests` environment).
- `bobi_deploy/tests/` (95 tests) passes under the new `deploy-package.yml` install.
- Full combined unit run: 3137 passed.

Part of the repo-split phase 1 restructure (follows #699, #701, #702). No version or changelog changes.

Adds the **smoke suite** — the test infrastructure the Report Health Gate's `smoke` / `form-e2e` audits will consume once a producer workflow lands.

Generated by the `smoke-suite` maintenance recipe ([reddoorla/reddoor-maintenance#371](https://github.com/reddoorla/reddoor-maintenance/pull/371), formatting fix [#373](https://github.com/reddoorla/reddoor-maintenance/pull/373)), formatted to this repo's own prettier config. - `tests/smoke/routes.ts` + `tests/smoke/pages.spec.ts` — the smoke specs

- A `playwright.config.ts` that honors `REDDOOR_SMOKE_PORT` (R1.1) — only when absent or an exact pre-R1.1 shared-base config

**No runtime/user-facing change**: only test files, `package.json` scripts, and (if missing) the `@playwright/test` devDep — nothing under `src/routes`, so the deployed site is unchanged.

author: bbrak
body:
## Problema

O instalador era **check-and-print**: para as ferramentas externas ele só rodava `<tool> --version`, e se faltasse, **imprimia** o comando e seguia (`"NAO instala nada sozinho"`, `failSoft: true`). Resultado: `rtk`, `graphify` e `agent-browser` nunca chegavam instalados no dia 1 — o colaborador terminava com o hook `rtk hook claude` no `settings.json` mas **sem o binário**, e a economia de tokens do RTK não valia (falha silenciosa em todo Bash).

Descoberto ao diagnosticar uma máquina onde `which rtk` → not found apesar de todo o config assumir o rtk presente.

## Mudança

Nova **fase 5** nos dois instaladores: para cada ferramenta externa ausente, **pergunta `[Y/n]` e instala** o comando do SO. Fail-soft preservado (recusar/falhar → aviso e segue).

| SO | rtk |
|---|---|
| **macOS** (`install.sh`) | `brew install rtk` (método oficial recomendado; fallback `curl \| sh`) + `rtk init -g` |
| **Windows** (`install.ps1`) | sem winget/scoop → baixa `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` do release, extrai `rtk.exe` p/ `~/.local/bin`, adiciona ao PATH do usuário + `rtk init -g` |

`graphify` e `agent-browser` reusam os comandos `uv`/`npm` já existentes.

**Flags novas:** `--yes`/`-Yes` (não interativo, aceita tudo) e `--skip-tools`/`-SkipTools` (pula a etapa).

**manifest.json:** rtk mac agora é `brew install rtk` (antes era `curl|sh`, desatualizado); adicionados `installFallback`, `postInstall`, `autoInstall`.

**README:** seção de instalação atualizada.

## Validação

- ✅ `bash -n install/install.sh`
- ✅ `manifest.json` JSON válido
- ✅ **dry-run macOS ponta a ponta** — fase 1 sem os externos, fase 5 detecta `rtk (ja instalado)` e avisa graphify/agent-browser, fase 6 extras OK
- ⚠️ **Windows:** `install.ps1` revisado manualmente (PS 5.1-safe: usa `;` não `&&`, `Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing`, `Expand-Archive`, try/catch fail-soft). **Pendente smoke test em Windows real** — vale confirmar que o `.zip` do release traz `rtk.exe` na raiz.

author: joaofelipe93
body:
Closes #17

Ao enviar o relatório (GUI ou CLI), depois de criar o quadro, o webhook do Trello é **registrado automaticamente** para esse quadro — sem `webhook:registrar` na mão a cada mês.

## Como funciona
- O pipeline já cria o quadro e agora devolve o `quadroRef` (com **id**) no resultado.
- `TrelloDestino.garantirWebhook(quadro, callbackURL)` faz **find-or-create idempotente**: usa o id do quadro como `idModel`; se já existir um webhook igual, não cria outro.
- `server.ts` (GUI) e `index.ts` (CLI) chamam isso após processar, **se `WEBHOOK_CALLBACK_URL` estiver no `.env`** da máquina. Se não estiver, apenas pula (nada quebra).

## Requisito
A máquina que roda a GUI precisa ter `WEBHOOK_CALLBACK_URL=https://webhook.thesmart.com.br/webhook/trello` no `.env` (o registro é só uma chamada à API do Trello; não precisa rodar na droplet).

## Verificação
- `npm run typecheck` limpo; `npm test` com **35 testes** (asserção do `quadroRef` adicionada).

## Observação
Webhooks de meses anteriores **não são removidos** automaticamente (cada quadro tem o seu). Se quiser limpeza automática do mês anterior, dá pra adicionar depois.

author: markd2lp
body:
# Feat: Minimum Loading Capacity & Initial Inventory Support

## Overview

This pull request introduces comprehensive support for **minimum loading constraints** and **initial inventory management** in the jSprit routing engine. The changes enable vehicles to carry pre-loaded inventory, apply minimum load requirements to shipments, and properly handle multi-location pickup scenarios with thread-safe concurrent insertion evaluation.

## Key Features

### 1. Minimum Loading Constraints
The routing engine now enforces minimum loading requirements for shipments, ensuring that vehicles meet load thresholds before departing. This feature integrates with the capacity constraint system to prevent underutilized routes.

### 2. Initial Inventory Support
Vehicles can now be configured with initial inventory (products already on board). The system treats these as zero-cost pickup locations, allowing the optimizer to leverage existing vehicle stock without incurring additional transport costs.

### 3. Multi-Location Pickup Handling
Shipments with multiple pickup options are now properly evaluated, with the selected pickup location stored on the activity instance rather than the shared job object, preventing concurrent mutation issues during multi-threaded insertion evaluation.

## Technical Changes

### Core Algorithm Enhancements

#### VehicleRoutingAlgorithm.java
- Added `algoListeners.bestSolutionUpdated(bestEver)` callbacks whenever a new best-ever solution is found, enabling real-time monitoring of optimization progress.

#### BestSolutionUpdatedListener (New Interface)
- Introduced a new listener interface for receiving notifications when the optimization discovers an improved solution.
- Fired inside `memorizeIfBestEver()`, called at most once per iteration when the solution actually improves.

#### VehicleRoutingAlgorithmListeners.java
- Added `bestSolutionUpdated()` method to dispatch best-solution events to registered listeners implementing `BestSolutionUpdatedListener`.

### Insertion & State Management

#### InsertionData.java
- Added `selectedPickupLocation` field to store the pickup location chosen during multi-pickup insertion evaluation without mutating the shared Shipment object.
- Provides getter and setter methods for thread-safe access to the selected location.

#### Inserter.java
- Enhanced to apply the selected pickup location to both the activity instance (`PickupShipment`) and the shared `Shipment` after insertion is confirmed.
- Includes detailed comments explaining the thread-safety rationale: evaluation occurs concurrently, insertion is single-threaded, and downstream components (AffectedJobTracker, AdaptiveSpatialFilter) require the updated Shipment state during ruin.

#### ShipmentInsertionCalculator.java
- Refactored to avoid mutating the shared Shipment during concurrent evaluation; instead, sets the location on the activity instance.
- Updated `getInsertionData()` to store the best pickup location in `InsertionData` rather than directly on the Shipment.
- Enhanced `getAllInsertionPositions()` to set the location under test before constraint evaluation, ensuring `HardActivityConstraints` see exactly which pickup option is being evaluated.

#### ShipmentInsertionCalculatorFlex.java
- Introduced `bestPickupLocation` tracking to properly record which location was selected during flexible insertion evaluation.
- Enhanced to set the selected location on both the activity instance and `InsertionData` for consistency.

### Capacity & Load Management

#### MaxLoadStateUpdater.java
- Added `copyDimensions()` method to properly copy multi-dimensional capacity data when building adjusted capacity objects.
- Ensures that all dimensions (not just dimension 0) are preserved during capacity calculations.

#### MinLoadAdjustmentProvider (New Interface)
- Extension point for querying adjusted pickup sizes that account for minimum load requirements and initial inventory consumption.
- Provides `getAdjustedSize()` method to retrieve the effective pickup size for a given route, vehicle, and job combination.
- Enables the private project to inject custom logic without modifying the core fork.

#### VehicleInventoryProvider (New Interface)
- Extension point for managing vehicle inventory during insertion evaluation.
- Provides methods to query available inventory, commit consumption when splits are confirmed, and release inventory during ruin phases.
- All methods are thread-safe, supporting concurrent multi-threaded insertion evaluation.

#### PickupAndDeliverShipmentLoadActivityLevelConstraint.java
- Enhanced to consult `MinLoadAdjustmentProvider` for effective pickup sizes, unifying minimum load increases and initial-inventory reductions.
- Improved delivery constraint logic to avoid double-counting shipments: uses the effective pickup size instead of blindly inverting the delivery size.
- Includes detailed comments explaining the capacity calculation rationale.

### Pickup Location & Route Identification

#### PickupLocation.java
- Added `onVehicle` boolean flag to mark pickup locations representing initial inventory.
- Provides `isOnVehicle()` getter and builder method `setOnVehicle()` for configuration.
- When marked as `onVehicle`, the location represents product already loaded; no physical pickup activity is needed and transport cost is zero.

#### PickupShipment.java
- Added `selectedPickupLocation` field to store the activity-local selected location, avoiding concurrent reads from the shared Shipment.
- Updated `getLocation()` to prioritize the activity-local selected location over the Shipment's state.
- Enhanced copy constructor to propagate the selected location to activity copies.

#### VehicleRoute.java
- Fixed route ID generation to preserve the original `routeId` in the copy constructor, ensuring external maps keyed by `routeId` (e.g., compartment results) remain valid after solution copying during best-ever memorization.
- Moved UUID generation to the builder constructor only, preventing unintended ID changes during route copies.

## Version Updates

| Component | Previous Version | New Version | Reason |
|-----------|------------------|-------------|--------|
| jsprit-core | 2.0.11-local | 2.0.20-inventory | Capacity constraint fix & multi-pickup support |
| jsprit-analysis | 2.0.11-local | 2.0.20-inventory | Aligned with core module |
| jsprit-fleetpanda (parent) | 2.0.11-local | 2.0.20-inventory | Version bump for inventory features |

## Testing

The implementation includes:

- **InventoryRoutingScenarioSpec**: Comprehensive test suite validating minimum loading and initial inventory scenarios.
- **Thread-safety validation**: Multi-threaded insertion evaluation with concurrent pickup location selection.
- **Capacity constraint tests**: Verification that effective pickup sizes are correctly applied to capacity checks.
- **Route copying tests**: Ensuring route IDs are preserved during solution memorization.

## Backward Compatibility

All changes are backward compatible:

- The `MinLoadAdjustmentProvider` and `VehicleInventoryProvider` are optional; if not registered, the system falls back to standard behavior.
- Existing shipments without multiple pickup locations continue to work unchanged.
- The `onVehicle` flag on `PickupLocation` defaults to `false`, preserving standard pickup semantics.

## Integration Points

This PR establishes extension points for the private project:

1. **StateManager**: Register `MinLoadAdjustmentProvider` and `VehicleInventoryProvider` implementations.
2. **CustomSerializers**: The private project's JSON serialization logic now has corresponding Circe decoders in FPApi.
3. **Listener System**: New `BestSolutionUpdatedListener` enables real-time monitoring of optimization progress.

## Related Issues

- **Target branch**: main
- **Source branch**: min_loading_changes
- **PR**: Fleet

author: ckatalay
body:
## What

Makes the `Cache SwiftPM build` step in `.github/workflows/swift.yml` immune to the workspace-path poisoning that broke the Swift job after the `a11y-checker-plugin` → `a11y` rename:

- The cache `key` **and** the `restore-keys` prefix now carry `${{ github.repository }}`, so a cache entry can only ever be restored into the same repo name (and therefore the same runner workspace path) it was built under. A future rename changes the key and the job falls back to a clean from-scratch build instead of a poisoned restore.
- A comment block on the step records why the key/paths are shaped that way — including the explicit warning not to "simplify" the restore-keys back to a bare `swiftpm-${{ runner.os }}-` prefix — so the next rename doesn't regress it.

## Ops already performed (AC 1)

- Verified via `gh cache list` and deleted the three stale pre-rename cache entries: ids `5540350288`, `5375714600`, `5375694438` (all keyed `swiftpm-macOS-8855e1d5…`). Only `node-cache-*` entries remain.
- Re-triggered PR #297's failed Swift run (run `28968768676`); with the poisoned entries purged it rebuilds from scratch.
- This PR itself touches `.github/workflows/swift.yml`, so the Swift job runs here too and exercises the new key end to end.

## Why key-shape over dropping the `.build/` cache

The issue allowed either fix. Keeping the `.build/` cache preserves the fast-run intent of the original step (a scratch SwiftPM build of swift-syntax on macOS runners is multi-minute); scoping the key by `github.repository` removes exactly the poisoning vector (the PCH-embedded workspace path is derived from the repo name) without giving up the artifact cache.

Fixes #299

author: cyberpunk042
body:
## What

The third greenfield cockpit engine (after SDD-048 approvals #26, SDD-049 model-runtime #27). Makes the **D-08 rollback-points** snapshot/rollback write buttons **functional** through the SDD-047 R10274 `control-exec-api` rail. The manual `sovereign-osctl rollback …` command stays the documented fallback.

## Why this shape

The D-08 **read** side already existed — `sovereign-osctl rollback {snapshot,preview,commits}` → `scripts/lifecycle/rollback-points.py`, served at `/api/d-08/snapshot` + `/api/d-08/preview?to=`. Several "planned" buttons were actually *mislabeled* (they emitted a fake `sovereignctl snapshot …` clipboard string). The genuine **greenfield write** is `snapshot create` (`zfs snapshot <ds>@<tag>`) and `snapshot prune` (`zfs destroy` aged snapshots) — neither existed. And arbitrary-snapshot rollback wasn't web-functional (arbitrary ids carry `/`+`@` that the exec allowlist's `_SAFE_VALUE` forbids; the `rollback-apply` control is latest-only).

## Stages in this PR

- **Stage 0** `docs/sdd/050-snapshot-rollback-actuation.md` (+ INDEX + mandate E11.M17) — the spec, lead commit.
- **Stage 1** extends `scripts/lifecycle/rollback-points.py` (+ `tests/unit/test_snapshot_ops.py`, 14 scenarios) — `_DATASETS` enum, `create()`, `prune()`, recent-N in `apply()`. The read methods (`snapshot()`/`preview()`) the API imports stay untouched.
- **Stage 2** 3 new controls in `config/control-systems.yaml` (registry 21→24, local 19→22), sudoers NOPASSWD entries, lint bumps, and the honest d-08 button re-wire.

## Operator decisions realized

- **Prune = floor + refuse-by-default** (Q-050-C): destroy snapshots older than `--retain-days`, EXCEPT a hard floor — never the very latest (absolute), and never the newest 3 per dataset unless `--force` (a logged, **CLI-only** escalation). Old-but-floor-protected snapshots are withheld + reported (`refused=true`), not destroyed.
- **Arbitrary rollback = bounded recent-N enum** (Q-050-F): a new `rollback-recent` control (`--to {recent-1..recent-5}`). The token resolves to the live `@`-name **internally**, so the `/`+`@` id never crosses the exec allowlist; the dry-run plan shows the `resolved` target before confirm (TOCTOU mitigation). `rollback-apply` (latest one-click) is left **untouched** — its `--to latest --confirm` change_cli is a pinned security contract (`test_sovereign_osctl_rollback_apply.py`).

## The `/`-in-dataset landmine

`--dataset` carries `/` (`rpool/sovereign-os`, `tank/context`), which `_SAFE_VALUE` forbids. So the control passes an **enum of short keys** (`{os|context|models|agents}`) resolved to the real dataset path **inside the engine** — exactly the SDD-049 model-load id-resolution pattern. `--tag` is a free arg validated `_SAFE_TAG`-clean (no `/`, `@`, whitespace, metacharacters).

## R10212 preserved

`selfdef`/`perimeter` untouched (proxy-only, absent from sudoers); `state_path` free of `selfdef`/`tetragon`; `rollback-api.py` stays **read-only** (405 on writes — no new API surface added). `zfs snapshot/destroy/rollback` are the **only** host mutations, each gated by the two-gate exec rail (placeholder validation → sudoers) + operator-key presence + type-to-confirm + DRY-RUN default. ## 背景

#350 已合并后实机踩到的新坑，修复未赶上合并，单独补这个 PR。

`UnityWndClass` 是所有 Unity 游戏共用的窗口类名。用户同时开着另一个 Unity 游戏（Steam、4K 全屏）时，`_find_game_hwnd` 只按类名枚举会先撞上它：

- `PC_ResizeWindow` 对着别人家的游戏调分辨率 → 被全屏顶回 → 循环误报"游戏可能锁定了分辨率"（实测调整后客户区恒 2560×1440，MFA 报"pc窗口未找到或调整失败"）；
- `PC_StopApp` 在该状态跑则会**误杀用户正在玩的另一个游戏**。

## 改动

`_find_game_hwnd` 枚举条件由 仅类名 改为 **类名 + 标题含 `BrownDust`** 双条件；找不到时的报错文案带上标题便于排查。

## 验证

实机两个 UnityWndClass 窗口共存（BrownDust II 窗口化 + 另一 Unity 游戏 4K 全屏）：新逻辑正确选中 BrownDust II，不再碰另一窗口。

author: ymoussatt
body:
### PR Category
Bug fix

### Summary

Quasar arch-enablement. Across the runtime, code branched on `ARCH::BLACKHOLE`
(or `== WORMHOLE_B0`) as a *proxy* for a capability that Quasar actually shares, so a
Quasar device was silently excluded, either crashing (`TT_THROW`/`TT_FATAL`) or getting
Wormhole's (wrong) settings. This is the same class of gap as the missing
`get_string_lowercase` QUASAR case fixed in #48155. Each fix either uses the real
capability predicate or adds `QUASAR` explicitly; none change Wormhole/Blackhole behavior.

Eight gaps fixed (grouped by commit):

**FP8_E4M3 guards** (Quasar supports FP8; only Wormhole doesn't)
- `jit_build/data_format.cpp`: FP8 pack-format selection FATAL'd unless Blackhole; now
  gates on `is_data_format_supported(Fp8_e4m3, arch)` (the support table = source of truth).
- `impl/tensor/mesh_tensor.cpp`: FP8 tensor device-binding guard now allows `BLACKHOLE || QUASAR`.

**Device init**
- `impl/device/firmware/risc_firmware_initializer.cpp`: the virtual PCIE/DRAM
  addressable-core table (feeds the device NoC watcher/sanitizer) was populated only for
  Blackhole; now gated on a new HAL capability, `hal.virtualizes_non_worker_cores()`.
  DISPATCH cores (Quasar-only) are now always registered in the physical list. Also adds
  a bounds guard on the fixed-size `virtual_non_worker_cores` mailbox array to fail
  loudly instead of overrunning.
- `risc_firmware_initializer.cpp`: the harvested-COL-column virtual coordinate used a
  Blackhole-only formula; Quasar is COL-harvest with an identical virtual-grid layout
  (`VIRTUAL_TENSIX_START_X/Y`), so it now uses the same formula.

**ttnn NoC size/alignment** (Quasar uses DRAM align 64 / L1 align 16 like Blackhole, but a larger NOC max burst size (65536))
- `matmul` `get_max_page_size_and_num_pages`: DRAM-sharded matmul `TT_THROW`'d on Quasar;
  now `noc_max_page_size = 65536`.
- `concat_s2s_tiled`: burst size defaulted Quasar to Wormhole's 8192; now 65536.
- `interleaved_to_sharded` / `interleaved_to_sharded_partial`: the Blackhole-only alignment
  path now also covers Quasar.

Tests added:
- `test_blockfloat_common.cpp`: host-side `DataFormatFp8ArchGuard.Fp8E4m3PackSrcFormatPerArch`
  (QUASAR/BLACKHOLE allowed, WORMHOLE_B0 still rejected).
- `test_mesh_tensor.cpp`: `MeshDeviceSingleCardFixture.AllocateFp8E4m3OnDevice`.

### Notes for reviewers

**Verification status:**
- FP8 pack guard: host test **passes**.
- FP8 tensor guard: **passes on the Quasar emulator** (`emu-quasar-1x3`, slow dispatch).
- The device virtualization fix runs on every Quasar boot (exercised by the tensor test).
- The **harvest** fix and the **4 ttnn** fixes are **compile-clean + verified against the Quasar
  HW headers** (`tt-2xx/quasar/noc/noc_parameters.h`, `qa_hal.cpp`) but **not run end-to-end**.

**No Wormhole/Blackhole behavior change**

author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Erdős #666 (C₆ in hypercube subgraphs) is a **completion** problem whose gallery entry was already at 0 sorries / 1 axiom. The lone remaining axiom `chung_no_threshold` (Chung's explicit 4-partition of Qₙ into C₆-free subgraphs) is genuinely deep and absent from Mathlib — eliminating it needs a >1000-line combinatorial construction (BLOCKED).

This PR adds the highest-value **verified** content available: the hypercube's structural invariants, grounding the previously-bare numeric definitions `hypercubeVertices`/`hypercubeEdges` in the actual graph `Hypercube n`.

## New theorems (all VERIFIED, 0 sorries)

- **`hypercube_degree`** — Qₙ is `n`-regular: every vertex has exactly `n` neighbours (the `n` bit-flips `x ⊕ 2ⁱ`, `i<n`). Explicit injection `Fin n ↪ neighborFinset x`: well-definedness from `Nat.xor_lt_two_pow`, injectivity from xor left-cancellation + injectivity of `i ↦ 2ⁱ`, surjectivity from the adjacency characterisation.
- **`hypercube_isRegular`** — packaged `IsRegularOfDegree n` form.
- **`hypercube_card_edges`** — `(Hypercube n).edgeFinset.card = hypercubeEdges n = n·2ⁿ⁻¹`, from `n`-regularity via the handshake lemma `sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges`.

These carry no assumptions beyond the ambient `Classical.choice` (adjacency `DecidableRel`), and are independent of the irreducible cycle machinery, so they avoid the `Nat.card·edgeSet` / `HasCycle` co-unfolding crash documented in the file header.

## Axiom status (unchanged)

Still exactly **1 axiom**: `chung_no_threshold`. No new counted axioms.

## Build

`docker-build.sh Proofs.Erdos666Problem` — **succeeded** (Lean v4.26.0; first attempt hit a transient exit-135 volume corruption, clean on retry).

File 326 → 412 lines, `theoremCount` 5 → 8, 0 sorries, 1 axiom. Gallery `meta.json` counts/sections/contributions updated to match.

author: yashmayya
body:
Follow-up to #18237 and #18924; closes out the rollout planned in https://github.com/apache/pinot/issues/18201.

## What

1. **Enables broker segment pruning by default on the MSE logical planner path** — flips `pinot.broker.multistage.logical.planner.use.broker.pruning` (`DEFAULT_LOGICAL_PLANNER_USE_BROKER_PRUNING`) from `false` to `true`, matching the physical optimizer path (`pinot.broker.multistage.use.broker.pruning`), which has defaulted to `true` since it was introduced. The flag is unchanged and can still be set to `false` cluster-wide, and `SET useBrokerPruning=false` still disables pruning per query.
2. **Fixes two latent bugs in the routing-query construction** that the default flip exposed (both were reachable before this PR only with `SET useBrokerPruning=true`; enabling by default is what surfaced them in CI). See "Bug fixes" below.

## Why now

The logical-planner flag was introduced in #18237 with a `false` default explicitly so the rollout could proceed independently, path by path. That rollout is complete:

* Non-partitioned leaf path: #18237
* Partitioned leaf path + logical tables: #18924
* All-segments-pruned short-circuit: #18538

With every leaf path supported, the `false` default now just means MSE queries fan out to servers that provably hold no matching segments — the motivating problem of #18201 (a single unhealthy server degrading nearly all queries on a tenant).

## Bug fixes bundled with the flip

Both live in the leaf-stage → routing-query builders (`LeafStageToPinotQuery` for the physical optimizer's Calcite `RelNode` trees, and its `PlanNodeRoutingQueryBuilder` counterpart for the logical planner's `PlanNode` trees). Enabling pruning by default routes every leaf filter through the broker segment pruners, which surfaced these:

1. **Boolean scalar-function predicates hard-failed planning.** A predicate that is a boolean scalar function used directly (e.g. `WHERE contains(col, 'x')`, `regexpLike(...)`) reaches the pruners as operator `"contains"`; the pruners resolve operators via `FilterKind.valueOf`, which threw `No enum constant FilterKind.contains` and failed the whole query. The single-stage engine never hits this because `PredicateComparisonRewriter` canonicalizes such predicates to `EQUALS(fn, true)` at parse time — the MSE routing builder now does the same. Additionally, the non-partitioned and logical-table routing paths gained the same fail-open `try/catch` the partitioned path already had, so a pruner throwing can never fail a query that would route fine unpruned.

2. **Filters above a leaf boundary corrupted the routing filter (silent wrong results).** The builder folded every `Filter`/`Project` it found in the leaf chain while silently skipping other node types. With `aggOptions(is_partitioned_by_group_by_keys='true')` the aggregate is a DIRECT (un-split) node with no exchange, so a `HAVING` filter lands in the same leaf fragment *above* the aggregate — its `InputRef`s index the aggregate's output row space, not the scan columns. The builder resolved them against the scan columns and *overwrote* the genuine `WHERE` filter, so pruning could eliminate segments holding matching rows. Fixed by stopping the fold at the first non-`Filter`/`Project` node (a leaf boundary) and AND-combining stacked filters instead of overwriting. Strictly conservative: the routing filter can now only shrink (less pruning), never wrongly extend. Applied to both builders.

## Scope / risk

* **Pruning only activates on tables with segment pruners configured** (`routing.segmentPrunerTypes` etc.). Those tables already get identical pruner behavior on the single-stage engine today; this brings MSE routing in line with SSE routing for them. Tables without pruners get the same segments back from the filtered routing query — results and routing unchanged.
* The pruning implementation is fail-open throughout (unsupported plan shapes, routing failures, all-pruned, pre-partitioned/colocated-join leaves), so the residual failure mode is unpruned-but-correct routing.
* **Observable changes** on pruner-enabled tables: `numServersQueried`/`numSegmentsQueried` drop, `numSegmentsPrunedByBroker` is now populated, and filters matching zero segments short-circuit at the broker (#18538). Worth a release-note callout since dashboards keyed on these stats will shift.
* Broker-local planning behavior only — no wire format or mixed-version concerns.
* **Validation basis**: the physical-optimizer path has run with pruning default-enabled since its introduction; the segment pruners themselves are the same ones SSE has always used at the same spot in routing; and the logical-planner implementation is covered by unit tests for every fallback (disabled, unsupported shape, routing failure, all-pruned, unavailable segments, pre-partitioned gate) plus end-to-end integration tests on a real partitioned realtime table and logical tables.

**Release-note callout**: MSE (default planner) now performs broker-side segment pruning by default on tables with segment pruners configured. Disable cluster-wide with `pinot.broker.multistage.logical.planner.use.broker.pruning=false` or per query with `SET useBrokerPruning=false`.

## Testing

* **Default flip** — `WorkerManagerTest`: default-on is asserted directly (filtered routing query without any `SET`; partitioned leaf prunes without any `SET`), and the disabled path stays covered via explicit `SET useBrokerPruning=false` variants. Integration tests from #18924 that used a bare query as the "unpruned" baseline now disable pruning explicitly, and the partitioned-table test doubles as an end-to-end regression test of the new default (a plain query must report `numSegmentsPrunedByBroker > 0`).
* **Boolean scalar-function fix** — `LeafStageToPinotQueryTest` covers wrapping at top level and under AND/OR/NOT, and asserts genuine `FilterKind` functions (IN/RANGE/TEXT_MATCH/IS_NULL/…) are *not* wrapped; `WorkerManagerTest` drives a real `WHERE contains(...)` query end-to-end and asserts the routing request carries `EQUALS(contains(...), true)`; a fail-open test asserts a throwing routing manager falls back to unfiltered routing. The mock routing managers validate filters via the same `FilterKind.valueOf` walk the real pruners use, so a non-canonical routing filter fails the unit tests.
* **Leaf-boundary fix** — `PlanNodeRoutingQueryBuilderTest` asserts a `HAVING` above an `AggregateNode` is not folded (routing filter = `WHERE` only) and that stacked leaf filters are AND-combined; `LeafStageToPinotQueryTest` adds the `RelNode`-path mirror for the physical optimizer builder (both verified to fail without the fix).
* Three `EXPLAIN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN` snapshots in `ExplainPhysicalPlans.json` are updated: in the planner-test fixture, the partitioned tables' segments all live in the first partitions, so with pruning on by default the *filtered, shuffle-feeding* leaf drops its segment-less partitions (4 workers → 1). The diffs demonstrate the safety gates: the unfiltered scan, the join-bearing leaf (unsupported shape → fail-open), and the `[PARTITIONED]` direct-exchange chain are all untouched; only shuffle/broadcast-feeding filtered leaves compact.

author: muhannadnouri
body:
## Summary

This PR enables Arabic Libtashkeel text preprocessing for iOS native TTS builds.

Previously, iOS native TTS packaged the Piper/Sherpa runtime with static libraries, but did not include the Libtashkeel preprocessing path used by Arabic audiobook generation. As a result, Arabic bundles or setups that referenced `libtashkeel-1.5.0` could report the preprocessor as unsupported on iOS.

## Changelist

- Added a dedicated `native-tts-ios` Cargo feature for iOS native TTS builds.
- Split native text preprocessing into shared/dynamic and static modes.
- Kept desktop and Android using dynamic ONNX Runtime loading.
- Enabled iOS to initialize ONNX Runtime through the statically linked archive.
- Updated iOS build scripts to pass `ORT_LIB_LOCATION`.
- Updated iOS native TTS build checks to use the new `native-tts-ios` feature.
- Updated README and docs to describe iOS Libtashkeel support.
- Documented the remaining imported-bundle validation shortcoming: completed bundles already contain WAV audio, but current validation can still reject bundles if their stored preprocessor is not supported by the active runtime.

## Dynamic vs Static Linking

Dynamic linking means the app loads a shared library at runtime, such as a `.so`, `.dylib`, or `.dll`. In practice, this is useful on desktop and Android because the app can package ONNX Runtime as a shared library and load it when the native TTS/preprocessing runtime starts.

Static linking means the library code is linked directly into the app binary during build. In practice, this is better suited for iOS because iOS distribution is stricter about runtime-loaded native libraries, and App Store/TestFlight builds generally need native dependencies bundled and signed as part of the app itself.

For Papercut, this means:

- Desktop/Android keep using dynamic ONNX Runtime loading for Libtashkeel.
- iOS uses the prepared static ONNX Runtime archive already used by the native TTS build path.
- The app gets the same Arabic preprocessing capability, but through the linking model expected by each platform.

## Reviewer Notes

This change is focused on packaging/linking support for Arabic preprocessing on iOS native TTS builds. It does not yet change the imported-bundle validation behavior for bundles that already contain generated WAV audio. That validation issue is documented as a known follow-up because playback of completed audio bundles should not strictly require the original text preprocessor to be available.

Local validation was limited by the Linux environment because full iOS linking has to be proven through CI or an Apple build environment.

## Manual Testing

- Run iOS native TTS CI/build and confirm the app builds with `native-tts-ios`.
- Install on iOS and open the Audiobooks tab.
- Select the Arabic Piper Kareem model.
- Confirm Auto Diacritization / Libtashkeel preprocessing is available.
- Generate a short Arabic audiobook using the Libtashkeel preprocessor.
- Confirm generation completes and playback works.
- Export the generated audiobook bundle.
- Delete and re-import the bundle.
- Confirm the imported bundle can be played.
- Regression test English Kokoro generation and playback.
- Regression test Arabic Piper generation without preprocessing / original text mode.
- Regression test desktop or Android Arabic preprocessing still works through the existing dynamic runtime path.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Updated iOS native text-to-speech builds to use the latest iOS-specific packaging and configuration flow.
  * Enhanced Arabic diacritization preprocessing coverage for iOS and shared native builds.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved offline narration extraction rules (including footnote reference handling and wrapper-text preservation).
  * Strengthened compatibility when imported bundle highlight/rebuild data is missing or mismatched, with more reliable fallback playback.

* **Documentation**
  * Refreshed iOS build and setup instructions to reflect the new native TTS iOS workflow and configuration options.

- Body: pass it straight to the creation tool's `body` arg (GitHub MCP `create_pull_request` body, or `gh pr create --body-file -` via stdin) — don't write it to a temp file first; the arg preserves markdown and newlines verbatim.
- Public OSS repo: no internal customers, incidents, or operational metrics.
- Draft by default: open new PRs as drafts (`gh pr create --draft`) — drafts run only a narrow CI subset and save runner credits. Fix CI and run affected tests locally before marking ready for review.
- Labels: apply `skip-agent-review` for trivial/chore PRs that don't need Copilot or Greptile review.
- When a human directed the work, the PR must be attributable to that person, even if agent-assisted.
- If a human directed this work, assign them as the PR assignee (the DRI) — actually set the assignee, don't just name them here. Leave a PR unassigned only when it is fully autonomous with no human driver (set Autonomy to "Fully autonomous").
- Never write a GitHub @mention or username you have not verified this session. Resolve a real handle from `gh api user` (current user) or the PR's actual author/assignee via `gh pr view --json author,assignees` — never infer a handle from a display name.
- Do not add a human Co-authored-by just for the sake of attribution — if no human was involved in the changes, own it as agent-authored.
- Agent-authored PRs always require human review — do not self-merge or auto-approve.
- Do NOT claim manual testing you haven't done.
- GitHub PR descriptions render markdown, not fixed-width text. Do not hard-wrap prose at a column width or use space-aligned tables — use real markdown tables, headings, and fenced code blocks, and let GitHub flow the text.
- Use GitHub's rich markdown when it makes review faster, never as decoration:
  - If the change alters a flow or topology (CI wiring, pipelines, state machines, request paths), include before/after mermaid diagrams as two separate `flowchart` blocks, before first. Pick `TD` (tall pipelines) or `LR` (wide paths). Keep them simple; a syntax error renders as an error block. Skip for trivial changes.
    - Brand the nodes with PostHog colors: use the hex directly (mermaid can't read CSS vars), and pair every `fill` with a text `color` so nodes stay legible in GitHub light and dark.
      ```
      classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
      classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
      classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
      classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
      ```
      Assign by role (`class NodeA,NodeB phBlue;`): `phBlue` agents/primary, `phRed` APIs/external, `phYellow` entry+exit, `phGray` data/artifacts. Shape by kind: `{{hexagon}}` agents, `[rect]` steps.
  - Use alerts (`> [!WARNING]`, `> [!NOTE]`) for behavior changes and risk callouts.
  - If you have to include long supporting content (test output, logs), collapse it in `<details>` blocks.
  - Use fenced `diff` code blocks for config before/after.
  - Line-range permalinks to code in this repo render as embedded snippets: prefer them over pasting existing code.
- Write with a crisp, direct Silicon Valley communication style. Use concise language that gets straight to the point. Sentences that are easy on the reader, paragraphs that are each about one thing. Prioritize clarity and brevity over elaborate explanations. Avoid corporate jargon, buzzwords, and unnecessary embellishments. Communicate as if you're explaining a complex concept to a smart colleague over coffee, keeping the tone light but substantive. No em-dashes, only en-dashes if needed. Spare use of inline code. Limited use of the colon and semicolon.
- Write from a first person perspective of the author of a human-driven PR. Although if something was done by an agent (i.e. you), make that clear with something like "I (or, actually Claude/Codex/etc.) did blah".
- For titles, headings, or bolded parts use "Sentence case" rather than "Title Case" (i.e. only capitalize the first word of the title/heading/bold text).
-->

author: tomrford
body:
Closes #81.

Replaces the app sidebar with a signal selector popover that mirrors the settings popover: database squircle trigger on the left of the header, centered load-trace title button, plot toolbar and settings on the right. Deletes the vendored `ui/sidebar` library (28 files), `app-sidebar.svelte`, and the `sidebarOpen` preference. Net −821 lines.

## Relationship to the old branch

This is a clean reimplementation of the design from `cursor/sidebar-signal-selector-popover-cc84` (draft PR #82), which forked before the #87–#91 refactors and would have needed a heavy rebase (inlined toolbar vs `plot-toolbar.svelte`, pre-`session.ts` store calls, a DBC dedup guard superseded by #89). The remote fix from that branch (#85 — hide trigger while open, load DBC library at app init) is incorporated here, with the trigger/close-button overlap solved structurally instead of via CSS.

**Once this PR is approved and merged as the definite successor, delete `cursor/sidebar-signal-selector-popover-cc84` and close draft PR #82.**

## Notable mechanics

- No `forceMount`: the popover content unmounts when closed, but filter/expansion state survives because the component instance inside `Popover.Root` persists; scroll offset is saved on scroll and restored in an `$effect`. `forceMount` was actively harmful — its always-mounted `position:fixed` floating wrapper sat over the closed trigger and swallowed clicks.
- Header control groups drop their `z-10` so the portaled popover paints above the trigger; the destructive close X lands exactly where the squircle was and is genuinely clickable (this also fixes the same latent overlap on the settings cog).
- `dbcFiles.loadLibrary()` runs at app init rather than on first selector mount.
- Settings popover gains the help dialog and GitHub link; help copy typo fixed.
- Store `sidebar*` identifiers renamed to `selector*` (theme tokens `--sidebar-*` untouched); stale "DBC side panel" empty-state copy updated.
- Unused `.scroll-fade-b` / `.scroll-fade-none` CSS variants pruned.

## Testing

- lint, svelte-check (0 errors), 99/99 unit tests
- Driven end-to-end in Chrome: cold open, tree expand, fuzzy filter, active-only toggle, close via X, reopen with state intact, trace load, signal selection → WebGPU plot render
- Codex read-only closeout review: GO

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large UI shell refactor (~800 lines removed) changes how users discover and select signals; DBC load timing moved to app init, but plotting/session logic is largely unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the persistent DBC/signal **sidebar** with a **header popover** opened from a database squircle on the left, matching the settings popover pattern. The main shell is now a single full-width column: centered **load-trace** title button, plot toolbar and settings on the right—no `Sidebar.Provider`, inset, or collapse shortcut.
> 
> **Signal selector** (`signal-selector-dialog.svelte`) is `Popover.Content` with the same DBC tree (search, active-only filter, drag-drop add, collapsible DBC/message/signal checkboxes). Filter and expansion state survive closes because the component instance stays mounted; **scroll position** is saved on scroll and restored when the popover reopens. A **scroll-fade** utility is added for overflowing lists.
> 
> Removes the vendored **`ui/sidebar`** package (~28 files), **`app-sidebar`**, and the persisted **`sidebarOpen`** preference. `dbcFiles` APIs rename `sidebar*` → **`selector*`**; **`dbcFiles.loadLibrary()`** runs at app init on `+page.svelte` instead of on first selector mount.
> 
> **Settings** popover gets a top bar with **help** (alert dialog) and **GitHub** links; help copy now says “signal selector.” **Search** form uses generic `Input` instead of `Sidebar.Input`. Plot empty state copy updated accordingly.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b2342b67822f7d3b349bece61c8ce8418d165edb. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: jackli921
body:
## What

Flips the web Content-Security-Policy from `-Report-Only` to **enforcing**, after a static audit of every resource `packages/web` loads. The audit found the policy was **factually wrong** — `img-src` omitted the two hosts the app loads on nearly every page — so flipping it as-is would have broken production.

Closes out the last step of #500 (the hash-pinning + `unsafe-inline` drop shipped earlier).

## Audit result (why it was blocked, now unblocked)

#500 was deferred pending a "live preview" (#1009) to verify the policy against OAuth/Unsplash. A code audit gave that verification without infra:

| Directive | Verdict |
|-----------|---------|
| `script-src` | safe — `'self'` + the one hashed inline bootstrap, no `unsafe-inline` |
| `connect-src 'self'` | safe — every fetch is the same-origin `/api`/`/auth` proxy; OAuth is a 302 navigation, not XHR; no Stripe.js/WebSocket |
| `style-src`, `font-src`, `form-action`, `frame-ancestors` | safe |
| **`img-src`** | **the only gap — 2 active + 1 flag-gated hosts missing** |

## Changes

- **`img-src`** += the R2 public bucket (operator **vehicle photos**, `wrangler.toml` `VEHICLE_PHOTOS_PUBLIC_URL`), Google's **avatar** host (`lh3.googleusercontent.com`, OAuth `profile.picture` in `nav/UserMenu`), and the **GSI tile** host (`cyberjapandata.gsi.go.jp`, the flag-gated search map — added proactively so a future flag flip doesn't break).
- **Flip** `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` → `Content-Security-Policy`.
- **`connect-src` stays `'self'`** — a `NOTE (#1042)` in `_headers` flags that the Sentry ingest host must be added there when the browser SDK gets a prod DSN.
- **Drift guard** (`csp-script-hash.test.ts`): pins the R2 + Google img hosts and asserts the header is served enforcing — a later edit can't silently drop a host and break every photo/avatar.

## Verification

- web `tsc` clean; `csp-script-hash` source test **7/7** (incl. the 2 new guards, RED→GREEN); `wrangler-pages-config` **11/11**
- post-build `lint-csp-hash` guard run against a **real `vite build`** → OK; confirmed `dist/_headers` serves the enforcing header

## Recommended before prod GA

This lands on `develop` → beta. Smoke on beta before promoting to prod: **sign in** (avatar loads), **open a vehicle** (R2 photos load), **complete a booking**. Leaving **#500 open** until that beta smoke confirms enforcement — flip to closed then.

Refs #500.

author: dev48v
body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Fixes #301

### 📚 Description

The `modulate` handler declared `args: [VArg]`, so `parseArgs` only pulled the **first** value out of the URL segment. Its `apply` takes three (`brightness, saturation, hue`), so `saturation` and `hue` were always `undefined`.

A request like `/_ipx/modulate_2_1_1/example.png` then failed with:

```
[IPX_ERROR] Expected number above zero for saturation but received undefined of type undefined
```

Fix: declare all three arg mappers — `args: [VArg, VArg, VArg]` — matching the sibling multi-arg handlers, so every value is parsed and forwarded to sharp. One-line change plus a regression test.

Thanks to @wuiyang for pinpointing the exact location (`src/handlers/handlers.ts`).

### ✅ Test

Added a test that drives the handler through `applyHandler` (i.e. through `parseArgs`, not `apply()` directly) so it covers the arg-count contract:

```
modulate parses all three args (brightness, saturation, hue) (#301)
```

- `vitest run test/handlers/handlers.test.ts` → 53 passed (incl. the new test)
- `eslint .` → clean

The existing `modulate.apply() returns expected values` test called `apply()` with three args directly, so it didn't exercise the parsing gap; the new test does.

## Summary
- Adds `ArchitectureContractFamilyDescriptor`, a record capturing per-family catalog metadata: family id, strict/audit YAML group names, baseline-capability flag, strict/audit contract accessors, an informational owned-CLR-types list, and an unused `AdditionalValidation` hook reserved for future family-decomposition work.
- Adds `ArchitectureContractFamilyRegistry.All`, the single ordered source of truth for all 25 contract families, in the exact order the old hand-written `AddGroup` calls used.
- Refactors `ArchitectureContractCatalog.Build` to iterate the registry instead of ~40 near-identical hand-written `AddGroup` calls, and replaces the hardcoded `IsGroupResolvable` name-exclusion list with a registry lookup on `IsBaselineCapable`.

## Architecture notes
- No behavior change: family discovery, dispatch order, baseline-capable groups, and all public `ArchitectureContractCatalog` members produce identical output for every existing policy document — pinned by the pre-existing `ArchitectureContractCatalogTests` suite (unmodified) plus new `ArchitectureContractFamilyRegistryTests`.
- `layer_template` contracts continue to be expanded via `LayerTemplateExpander.Expand` inside the descriptor's accessor, matching prior inline behavior.
- `OwnedContractTypes` and `AdditionalValidation` are inert in this change — extension surface reserved for future family-decomposition tasks under issue #208, not read by any production code path yet.

## Scope / non-goals
- The YAML DTO model (`ArchitectureContractGroups`) is unchanged — still typed lists.
- Contract handlers, DI registration, `ArchitecturePolicyDocumentLoader` validation, `ArchitectureAnalysisSession` check methods, CLI behavior, diagnostics, and exit codes are unchanged.
- No runtime plugin loading introduced.

## Tests run
- `make fmt` — clean.
- `make acceptance` — full build + test suite: `ArchLinterNet.Core.Tests` (926 passed), `ArchLinterNet.Cli.Tests` (112 passed), `ArchLinterNet.Unity.Tests` (3 passed), 0 failures.
- `openspec validate --all --strict` — 75/75 specs pass, including the new `contract-family-registry` capability.

## Risks / follow-ups
- Low risk: purely a data-driven refactor of an existing dispatch path, fully covered by pre-existing regression tests plus new registry tests.
- Follow-up (tracked under #208): future tasks can wire `OwnedContractTypes` / `AdditionalValidation` to actually decompose per-family validation logic out of the god-file extension points; this change only lays the groundwork.

author: digitie
body:
## 무엇을 / 왜

Feature 지도 pan 반응성 개선 (사용자 배치 #12의 **클라이언트 개선분**).

`useFeaturesInBbox`의 outer query key에 들어가던 viewport 서명이 `.toFixed(4)`(~11m)로
과도하게 정밀했다. tile 최소 폭이 ~9.7km(zoom 12)이라 **tile 집합이 fetch 결과를 완전히
결정**하는데도, 이 정밀 서명이 sub-tile 작은 pan마다 새 outer key를 만들어 tile cache가
전부 hit인데도 outer query를 재실행(재merge·재렌더)시켰다.

## 변경

- viewport 서명 `.toFixed(4)` → `.toFixed(2)`(~1.1km) + zoom 성분 제거 → tile 내부 작은
  pan은 순수 cache hit.
- outer `staleTime` 5s → 30s (tile fetchQuery와 정렬; 기존엔 outer만 조기 만료돼 tile이
  fresh한데도 refetch).

순수 클라이언트 캐시 튜닝 — **데이터·API 계약·렌더 결과 불변**. `live.test.ts`의 무효화는
`["features","viewport"]` prefix에만 의존하므로 영향 없음.

## 잔여(별도 인프라 과제)

필터 적용·대형 pan의 잔여 지연은 **서버 병목**(4코어 박스에서 밀집 bbox tile 조회, 1M
feature). 근본 해법은 **저zoom 서버측 region clustering**(기존 `/v1/features` `cluster_unit`
엔드포인트 활용 — 저zoom에서 개별 feature 대신 sido/sigungu 집계 렌더) 또는 MV/박스 증설.
UX(군집 방식) 변경이라 별도 스코프.

## 검증

- 타입 변경 없음(배열 원소 제거 + 리터럴 변경). CI type-check + next build로 검증.
- Playwright e2e는 CI 없음 — 동작 변화 없는 캐시 튜닝이라 라이브 e2e 비필수.

## Summary Implements KadoMoco v0.1, a desktop-resident pixel pet, from scratch (the repository previously contained only a README). - **Electron main process** (`electron/main.ts`): frameless transparent 180×180 window (min 120 / max 240), initial position at the bottom-right of the primary display with off-screen recovery, drag-to-move via cursor polling, position persistence, system tray with programmatically drawn icon (show / always-on-top toggle / quit), close-to-tray behavior, `electron-store` persistence, and power-resume notification. - **Game logic** (`src/game/`): vitals (0–100 clamped integers), 4 care actions with cooldowns and restrictions, 10-minute-chunk time decay with up to 12h offline catch-up, priority-based state machine, EXP/levels 1–5 with unlock rewards, 3 random daily tasks with rewards, daily personality-tendency evaluation (changes after 2 consecutive days), low-frequency random events, versioned save data with sanitization. - **UI** (`src/components/`, Zustand store): sprite-sheet CSS animation (4×8 grid, 64px frames, `steps(4)`), CSS fallback blob when the sheet is missing, left-click reactions, double-click status panel, right-click care menu, subtle speech bubbles, dev-only DevTools panel (`import.meta.env.DEV`). - **Placeholder asset**: `scripts/generate-placeholder-sheet.mjs` generates a committed placeholder sprite sheet (pale round unclassified creature, 8 colors) at `src/assets/pet/pixel/kadomoco_sheet.png`; replace with real art at the same path/spec. ## Verification - `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` all pass. - Smoke-tested under Xvfb: startup at bottom-right, right-click menu, feeding (hunger 70→100, EXP +5+8 task reward, task marked done), double-click status panel, drag + position save, restart restoring position/EXP/tasks, DevTools panel including +12h time simulation (auto-sleep behavior confirmed). - Bundled logic smoke test verified offline cap (12h), cooldown blocking, play blocked when sleepy, rest→sleeping→wake decay, level-up unlocks, and day rollover with personality history. [Status panel restored after restart](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-0651af34-6e46-42fe-9ec1-e004e4c474a7/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fkadomoco-restored.png) [Right-click care menu](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-0651af34-6e46-42fe-9ec1-e004e4c474a7/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fkadomoco-menu.png) [DevTools panel](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-0651af34-6e46-42fe-9ec1-e004e4c474a7/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fkadomoco-devpanel.png) ## Notes - Sprite sheet is a generated placeholder; real pixel art can be dropped in at the same path. - Tray icon visibility could not be visually confirmed under Xvfb (no system tray), but tray creation runs without errors. - Volume setting is persisted but unused (no audio in v0.1, per spec). To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
  
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * ペット育成アプリの基本機能、常駐表示、設定保存、トレイ操作、ステータス/メニュー/デバッグ画面を追加しました。 * 日次タスク、レベルアップ、性格変化、ランダムイベント、会話吹き出しなどの遊び要素を追加しました。 * ペットの見た目、アニメーション、フォールバック表示を含む新しいUIを追加しました。 * **Bug Fixes** * ウィンドウ位置やサイズを保存・復元し、再起動後も前回の状態を維持しやすくしました。

author: erwinislasegura
body:
### Motivation

- Prevent incorrect URLs produced when the project is served from XAMPP (paths that include `/htdocs/<project>`), so the app can redirect to the proper web path instead of failing with 404.  
- Ensure `redirect()` and `base_url()` produce correct paths for installations that are not at webroot and provide consistent front-controller routing.  
- Clarify XAMPP usage in `README.md` and ensure the default directory index and rewrite base are set for the `muni` deployment.

### Description

- Modified `.htaccess` to set `DirectoryIndex` to `index.php` only and added `RewriteBase /muni/` so rewrites resolve under the `muni` subdirectory.  
- Extended `README.md` with a new "Uso con XAMPP" section that explains correct URLs to use when the project is copied under XAMPP `htdocs` and how to avoid incorrect filesystem-style URLs.  
- In `app/bootstrap.php` added `canonicalize_xampp_filesystem_url()`, `normalize_xampp_filesystem_path()`, and `app_base_path()` helpers to detect and normalize requests that include `.../htdocs/<project>` and to compute the application base path.  
- Updated `redirect()` to handle absolute URLs and normalize XAMPP filesystem paths, changed the authentication guard to use `redirect('auth-2-sign-in.php')`, and updated `base_url()` to use `app_base_path()`.  
- In `index.php` added `front_controller_base_path()` and logic to strip the computed base path from `REQUEST_URI` so front-controller routing and direct file includes work when the app is served from a subdirectory such as `/muni`.

### Testing

- No automated tests were run for these changes.

author: rennf93
body:
Closes the one gap the X/video subsystem review found, per the CEO's direction: a dedicated aggregated surface instead of history buried inside queue cards.

## Backend

- `GET /x/posts/history` and `GET /video/posts/history` — CEO-gated exactly like their queue siblings, `limit` 1-200 (default 50), newest-acted first. Rows carry the draft body/captions, kind, outcome, acted timestamp, posted platform ids (`x_posted_tweet_id`; the video draft's per-platform `*_posted_id` keys, extracted generically), and reject reasons.
- Route tests assert membership by identity rather than emptiness — the approve/reject services commit the whole session, so prior tests' rows legitimately persist in the shared test DB (an existing test-pollution trap this work documented and sidestepped).

## Panel

- New **Social** page in the dashboard nav: the existing X Post Queue and Video Post Queue compose at the top, with one unified **History** section beneath — both platforms interleaved newest-first, kind badges (X post / X reply / Feature spotlight / Video), Posted/Rejected badges, X ids linking to the live tweet (`x.com/i/status/<id>`), TikTok inbox-upload ids shown raw (no public URL exists), reject reasons displayed. Collapsed by default, lazy-fetches only on expand.
- The Command Center's two full queue cards are replaced by a compact pending-counts card linking to `/social` — one home for the queues, no duplicated surfaces. React Query deduplicates the count queries against the page's own.

Out of scope by design: retention/TTL, editing history rows, re-posting from history.

## Verification

Branch carries current master (incl. #342). Full gate green: ruff/mypy (1094 files)/xenon, e2e smoke 40/40, backend suite **12308 passed, coverage 94.79%**, full panel suite **53 files / 326 tests**. New coverage: service, route (incl. CEO-gate 403), and component tests for the page, history section, and summary card.

author: martinotten
body:
## Summary
- `MutantIdentity.stable_id` collided for distinct mutants sharing operator/description/unparsed-mutation (e.g. two `MethodExpression`→nil mutants at different call sites in one method); observed 19 mutants → 13 ids, with a `CompileError` aliasing a `Killed` verdict.
- Add a `site_offset` identity component: mutation start_line/start_col relative to the subject's own `source_range.begin`, not absolute file coordinates — disambiguates same-signature call sites while still surviving line drift elsewhere in the file.
- Mark `docs/backlog/2026-07-08-stable-id-collisions.md` done with resolution notes.

## Trade-off
Every stable id changes; `mutation-history.sqlite3` per-mutant history restarts going forward. Accepted per the ticket's documented trade-off — ids are opaque hashes, no schema migration needed.

## Test plan
- [x] `mutant_identity_spec.rb`: distinct call-site mutants get distinct ids; identity unchanged under whole-subject line drift
- [x] `mutant_history_store_spec.rb`: stable-id assertion delegates to `MutantIdentity.stable_id` instead of duplicating the hash formula
- [x] `incremental_filter_spec.rb`: regression proving two previously-colliding real mutants now get distinct ids and reuse verdicts independently
- [x] `rubocop`, `steep check` clean
- [x] Full suite green except 3 pre-existing infra failures (`devcontainer_spec`, `pre_commit_hook_spec`) already present on `main` HEAD, unrelated to this change

author: chtruong814
body:
## Summary
- Use `job.workflow_repository` when checking out the copyright checker source
- Use `job.workflow_sha` so the checker comes from the exact reusable workflow revision that is running
- Remove the incorrect `github.workflow_ref` parsing step

## Why
The labs-molt run at https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/labs-molt/actions/runs/28978959566/job/85992909027 showed that `github.workflow_ref` resolves to the caller workflow (`NVIDIA-NeMo/labs-molt/.github/workflows/copyright-check.yml@refs/heads/pull-request/2`) inside this reusable workflow. That made the checkout try to fetch `NVIDIA-NeMo/FW-CI-templates@refs/heads/pull-request/2`, which does not exist.

GitHub documents `job.workflow_repository` and `job.workflow_sha` as the reusable workflow identity fields for checking out files co-located with the reusable workflow.

## Validation
- Confirmed the failing log tried to fetch `refs/heads/pull-request/2` from FW-CI-templates
- Checked GitHub context docs for reusable workflow source checkout fields
- Diff is limited to `.github/workflows/_copyright_check.yml`

author: barrettruth
body:
closes #40631

## Problem

`'background'` auto-detection currently treats `SID_LUA=-8` as its own provenance (I use "provenance" here to refer to "originating source of data"). This works iff automatic OSC 11 writes & use Lua writes (i.e. `se bg=...`) can collapse to the same source.

This explains #40631; setting from `VIMINIT`, `--cmd`, `-c`, `nvim_exec_lua()` or `:luafile` can look like a value set by `defaults.lua` and is not picked up on by the bg detection, sotThe next OSC 11 response is then free to replace the user's choice.

## Solution

Make `SID_LUA` mean a **plain Lua chunk**, and add a `SID_DEFAULTS` for **internal writes that `defaults.lua` is allowed to replace**. A few examples best demonstrate this:

```
source                         last-set SID
automatic OSC 11 background    SID_DEFAULTS (-11)
Lua in VIMINIT                 SID_ENV (-4)
Lua in --cmd                   SID_CMDARG (-2)
Lua in -c                      SID_CARG (-3)
nvim_exec_lua()                SID_LUA (-8)
:luafile                       real script SID
```

`SID_LUA` is still the fallback for plain Lua chunks. Lua API calls now preserve the active startup/source context when one exists. Explicitly for example, this means `:luafile` uses a file-backed Lua script context instead of collapsing to `SID_LUA` as it did before.

author: markusneusinger
body:
## Summary
- **Fixes the critical audit finding**: since at least 2026-06-12 (30-day log retention boundary), every crawler UA — googlebot, bingbot, twitterbot, discordbot, whatsapp, … — received **HTTP 502 on every page**, a de-facto site-wide noindex plus dead social previews, while human traffic saw a healthy site.
- **Root cause** (fully diagnosed against production): nginx's `@seo_proxy` hop runs `proxy_ssl_verify on` against `https://api.anyplot.ai`, whose certificate chain is **4 deep** (leaf → Let's Encrypt YE1 → ISRG Root YE cross-sign → ISRG Root X2). nginx's default `proxy_ssl_verify_depth` is **1** → Cloud Run logs show `upstream SSL certificate verify error: (20:unable to get local issuer certificate)` for every Cloudflare upstream IP. Fix: `proxy_ssl_verify_depth 4;` in both `@seo_proxy` and `@seo_proxy_python`.
- **Adds `bot-serving-check.yml`**: daily synthetic monitor (plus `workflow_dispatch`) curling production with Googlebot/Twitterbot UAs and a human-UA control, failing on non-200 or missing per-route `<title>`. This serving path is invisible to humans, Plausible, and CI — which is exactly how the outage persisted ~4 weeks. Also institutionalizes the check in the nginx.conf comment and docs/workflows/overview.md.

## Evidence
- `curl -A Googlebot https://anyplot.ai/scatter-basic` → 502; normal UA → 200 (verified live, also directly against the Cloud Run origin bypassing Cloudflare)
- Upstream healthy: `https://api.anyplot.ai/seo-proxy/scatter-basic` → 200 with correct per-route HTML, even with a bot UA
- `openssl s_client` confirms the 4-deep chain; earliest matching log entry 2026-06-12T18:09Z

## Verification plan
- `nginx.conf` has no local verification loop (no docker in this environment) — `proxy_ssl_verify_depth` is a standard `http/server/location`-context directive; the change is two identical one-liners.
- The new monitor script was **dry-run against current production**: it correctly reports 3× FAIL (bot 502) + control OK, exit 1 — i.e. it detects the current outage.
- **After merge + Cloud Build deploy**: re-run the same three curls (must all be 200 with per-route titles) and trigger `bot-serving-check.yml` via `workflow_dispatch` (must be green). I will do both and report.

## Test plan
- [x] Workflow YAML validated; monitor logic dry-run against production (correctly red pre-fix)
- [x] CHANGELOG updated (Fixed + Added)
- [ ] Post-deploy: `curl -A Googlebot https://anyplot.ai/scatter-basic` → 200 with `Basic Scatter Plot | anyplot.ai`
- [ ] Post-deploy: `gh workflow run bot-serving-check.yml` → green
