author: gemini2350
body:
## New Features

### 🎧 Audio Monitor (experimental, off by default)
- Headphone button next to every audio sender on the Details page
- The server joins the sender's multicast group on demand (IGMP join), depacketizes RTP (L16/L24/L32), encodes Opus 48 kHz stereo and streams it to the browser via WebRTC
- Channel-pair selector for multichannel streams (8ch/16ch AES67), mute/volume overlay
- Instant teardown when the tab closes (new `onClientDisconnect` hook)
- Fully disableable in Setup; **requires access to the multicast network** (Docker: `--network host` or a macvlan interface in the media VLAN)

### Node grouping (Details + Crosspoint)
- Devices sharing an NMOS node are grouped under a common node header on the Details page (status dot, PTP clock and web-UI link shown once globally; collapsible to a single line with one click)
- In the matrix: subtle node bands above the sender columns and a vertical strip left of all receiver rows of a node
- Labels follow the rule node = node, device = device; single-device nodes keep the combined label as before
- BCP-002-01 grouphint groups cluster under their node the same way (incl. label deduplication)
- Node names are renamable (persisted node alias, applied everywhere incl. DDNS)

### DDNS replaces pfSense/Unbound
- RFC 2136 Dynamic Updates + RFC 8945 TSIG (hmac-sha256/-sha512/-sha1/-md5) over TCP — BIND9, Knot, PowerDNS, Windows DNS
- New: unsigned mode ("none") for zones with IP-based `allow-update`
- Keeps its own inventory of pushed records; Forget also removes the DNS record

### Color scheme & Crosspoint
- Green = active, violet = prepared/preview, orange = working, red = errors only
- Staged disconnects (AutoTake off) mark the crosspoint with a dashed violet ring, orange while executing

### Details page
- Card layout with hover-revealed actions, merged media column, side-by-side legs, DUP badge naming the conflicting senders, connected sender in the toggle tooltip

### Other
- Virtual NMOS Node now defaults to **OFF** (explicit opt-in in Setup; configs that already saved `enabled:true` stay on)
- Logs button in the navigation; TAKE/Autotake always reachable (scrollable nav)
- Performance: structured-clone worker messaging, lease-snapshot change detection, shallow-copy filter pipeline, rAF-coalesced rebuilds
- Dead code removed (configState, dnsPushService, service.ts, unused UI components), `.dockerignore` restored, `.DS_Store` untracked
- Dockerfile: libopus build/runtime deps, node_modules taken from the builder stage (glibc-compatible native bindings)

## Verification
- Server `tsc` clean, `svelte-check` 0 errors, Vite build ✓
- Extensively tested in the test copy (NMOS-Crosspoint-responsive) against a real registry and devices

## Migration
- `settings.json` migrates itself (`dnsPush` → `ddns`, new `audioMonitor` block, `virtualNode.enabled` defaults to false)
- New server dependencies: `@discordjs/opus`, `werift` (native builds happen inside the Docker build)

author: benevolentfutures
body:
Fixes the two v0.58.0 staging-smoke blockers in **C11-171**, restoring the Truth & Stability cycle's TEL/EVT contract. Both root causes confirmed against code **and** the live event logs (`liveness.derived` had fired 3× ever, all in one C11-167 dev instance — zero in any staging/prod log).

## Defect 1 — `set-status` / `set-progress` bypass the evented canonical store
`upsertSidebarMetadata` / `setProgress` wrote only the tab-scoped sidebar display store (`tab.statusEntries` / `tab.progress`), never `SurfaceMetadataStore`. So no `metadata.changed` event fired and no canonical last-updated `ts` was recorded (`get_metadata` showed nothing) for the command agents actually use. The visible pill decay already worked off the display entry's own timestamp; the gap was the canonical store + event stream.

**Fix:** mirror canonical keys (`status`, `task`, `role`, `model`, `progress`) into `SurfaceMetadataStore` at the `.explicit` tier, targeting the explicit `--surface` (now resolved by the CLI) or the tab's focused surface. `status` emits `metadata.changed`; `progress` records a `ts` but stays out of the event stream (deliberate flood-control — `EventEmitter.canonicalMetadataEventKeys` unchanged). Threading preserved: the mirror rides the existing main-async display write via `setInternal` (store's own serial queue) — no new `main.sync`.

## Defect 2 — derived liveness never fires in Release
Shell integration reports `report_shell_state --tab=$CMUX_TAB_ID --panel=$CMUX_PANEL_ID`, and `CMUX_TAB_ID` is a legacy alias for the **surface** uuid — but `explicitSocketScope` treated `--tab` as the workspace id, so `tabManagerFor(surfaceUUID)` returned nil and the report silently no-op'd, never reaching `SurfaceLivenessDeriver`. Every other `report_*` fast path has an app-side fallback (git polling, OSC-7 PWD, ps sweep); liveness had none.

**Fix:** resolve the workspace from the **panel** via `AppDelegate.workspaceContainingPanel(...)`, through a pure `resolveShellActivityTarget` helper, in both the v1 (`TerminalController.reportShellState`) and v2 (`SocketDispatch.reportShellStateWorker`) handlers. Backward-compatible with callers that pass a real `--tab` workspace (tests, C11-167).

## Tests (c11-logic, green)
- `resolveShellActivityTarget` contract: resolves by panel, ignores the surface-uuid `--tab` hint, nil when unowned, still honors a real workspace/panel pair.
- Canonical-mirror key selection + `ts` stamping; the mirror's `metadata.changed` emission (`status`) and non-emission (`progress`).
- Full `c11-logic` suite: 1261 passed (1 unrelated flaky perf benchmark — `CommandPaletteSearchEngineTests`, timing-sensitive under concurrent build load).

## Recorded proof (RELEASE staging `rel-v0.58.0-fix2`, `reloads.sh`)
Transcripts in `notes/c11-171-proof-*.txt`:
- **(a)** `set-status status "…"` → `metadata.changed` (seq 14, `source=explicit`) + canonical `status` key with a last-updated `ts` on the surface store.
- **(b)** PTY output burst → `liveness.derived` `working` (seq 15) → `idle` (seq 17) on the driven surface.

## Post-merge note
`skills/c11/references/metadata.md` was updated for the mirror semantics — run `scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh c11` **after merge** to refresh the installed copy (not synced pre-merge to avoid shipping an unmerged skill change to live installs).

### Motivation
- Branded composer previously returned only an initial "Queued N recipients" message and did not surface progress or rejection reasons when the server always queues sends.\
- Fully-rejected background jobs (e.g. dead API key, unverified sender) were invisible to the composer UI.\
- The marketing dashboard poller could hide the rejection reason in jobs that finish with an error, reducing observability for users and operators.\

### Description
- Add `pollComposerJob` to `src/components/marketing/BrandedEmailComposer.tsx` that polls `/api/marketing/send-jobs/:jobId` and updates the composer message with progress, done, or failure details.\
- Extend the composer send response type to include `jobId` and call `pollComposerJob` when the server responds with `queued`.\
- Update `src/pages/marketing/MarketingDashboard.tsx` `pollSendJob` to append `j.error` to the done status message so rejection reasons are surfaced.\
- Include explanatory comments and a feature flag style comment `BF_PORTAL_COMPOSER_JOB_POLL_v1` for the change.\

author: adaworldapi
body:
## What

Completes the Railway first-run story on top of #2's `ODOO_DB_SETUP` / `ODOO_POPULATE_TEST_DATA` flow. Two additions to `docker/entrypoint.sh`:

### 1. Graceful onboarding when no DB is found
When the DB is uninitialized and `ODOO_DB_SETUP` is unset, the entrypoint no longer boots Odoo into a broken no-schema state. Instead it serves a **static onboarding page on `0.0.0.0:$PORT`** — answering **200 on every path including `/web/health`**, so Railway's healthcheck stays green — showing:
- the live DB state (Postgres reachable vs unreachable, host + db name),
- the exact three variables to set, then redeploy:
  1. `ODOO_DB_SETUP=1` (idempotent first-start; skipped once the schema exists)
  2. optional `ODOO_POPULATE_TEST_DATA=1` (rich demo data)
  3. `ODOO_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<pw>` or `=generate`

`ODOO_ONBOARDING=0` restores the old boot-anyway behaviour. The page also notes PG is this image's system of record (the lance-graph V3 storage lane belongs to the separate odoo-rs deployment, not this container).

### 2. Verified admin credentials (no email confirmation, loud nudges)
After first-boot init:
- the admin password is set, then **double-checked via `res.users.authenticate({'type':'password',…})`** — the same code path the login form uses — **before** being reported;
- `ODOO_ADMIN_PASSWORD=generate` mints a random 20-char password (`python3 secrets`), verifies it, and prints it **once** in the deploy logs;
- verification failure prints an unmissable *do-not-hand-out-this-credential* banner with the recovery path;
- the success banner nudges an immediate password change + 2FA;
- with no password set at all: a loud `admin`/`admin` change-me nudge.

## Verification (honest)
- `bash -n` clean; the embedded onboarding Python `ast`-checked.
- **Onboarding server exercised live in the sandbox**: `curl` returned `200` on `/web/health`, and the page carries `ODOO_DB_SETUP=1`, `ODOO_POPULATE_TEST_DATA=1`, `ODOO_ADMIN_PASSWORD=generate`, and the DB state string.
- Password generator length-checked (20 chars, alnum).
- **Not exercised here**: the full `odoo shell` verify path (needs a live Postgres + built image; registry egress is blocked in this sandbox). The `authenticate` signature was verified against this repo's `res_users.py:784` (Odoo 19: `authenticate(credential, user_agent_env)`).

`docker/README.md` updated: env table (`ODOO_ADMIN_PASSWORD` semantics, new `ODOO_ONBOARDING`), plus "Graceful onboarding" and "Admin credentials" sections.

author: trisiak
body:
## What

When the left sidebar is collapsed, the workspace name is no longer visible anywhere in the UI. This surfaces the current workspace title in the workspace top bar (`WorkspaceHeader`) so the user always knows which workspace they're in — but **only when the sidebar is collapsed**, since an open sidebar already shows the name.

## Details

- The title renders in the header's left cluster, right after the sidebar toggle and before the branch pill, gated on the existing `sidebarCollapsedAtom`.
- It reuses the sidebar's label source (`workspace.description`) and falls back to `"Untitled"` for a null/blank name, so this prominent slot never renders empty.
- Its text metrics mirror the adjacent branch pill (`font-size-1`, medium weight) so the two labels share a baseline and read as one row.
- It truncates with an ellipsis (`min-width: 0`) so a long name can't push the branch pill and right-side controls off the overflow-hidden bar.
- Adds a `WORKSPACE_HEADER_TITLE` element id for testing.

## Behavior

| Sidebar state | Header title |
|---|---|
| Open | Hidden (name shown in the sidebar) |
| Collapsed | Workspace title shown |

## Testing

- Verified end-to-end in the headless-browser QA harness: title absent with the sidebar open, present when collapsed, sharing a baseline with the branch name, and truncating cleanly at a narrow (760px) viewport with all controls still reachable.
- `just format`, `just check`, and `just test-unit` all pass.

A compact **"What happens next?"** explainer for the gap between adding the first source and the first scraped post arriving.

1. We check their recent posts

Rendered **only** when the workspace tracks ≥1 source **AND** a head-count (limit 1, no rows fetched) of posts from tracked accounts is zero. It hides itself once any tracked source has a saved post.

Not a wizard or large onboarding panel — one dashed strip, three lines.

💡 **What:** Optimized the `MiniScoreBar` component by replacing three separate `.filter()` calls with a single `for` loop traversal to calculate score distribution counts.

🎯 **Why:** The original implementation traversed the `scores` array three times to calculate `positive`, `mixed`, and `negative` counts. This was redundant and inefficient. Combining these into a single pass improves performance and reduces CPU usage.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Benchmark results for 10,000 iterations on an array of 10,000 items:
- **Baseline (Current):** 3.92s
- **Optimized:** 705.35ms
- **Improvement:** ~82% reduction in execution time.

The refactored code maintains strict logic parity with the original implementation, ensuring that only valid scores within the specified ranges are counted.

author: doruchiulan
body:
## What

The toolbar branch chip only rendered for **worktree** sessions. It derived its label from the persisted `chat.branchName`, which the daemon sets only when a session runs in a worktree — so on a **main-repo** session the chip disappeared entirely, taking the branch manager with it.

Now the chip reads the **live current branch from git on mount** (`getGitBranch`, which the daemon resolves to the main-repo checkout when there's no worktree). So it shows for every git session — main-repo included — and can switch its branch in place. Non-git projects (branch `null`) still hide the chip.

## Design

Matches the `Workspace Surfaces.html` artboard (`02-chrome.jsx` `MainToolbar`):

- **Worktree session** → accent-tinted chip, `GitFork` glyph, `WT` badge, foreground text.
- **Main-repo session** → neutral chip (no accent even when the popover is open).
- Tooltip names which: `Switch branch · worktree` / `· main repo`.

Also **unifies the worktree glyph** on lucide `GitFork` across the app — the sidebar session-row meta pill used a hand-rolled SVG; it now matches the composer worktree trigger, the git panel `WorktreeSection`, and the new chip.

## Note / tradeoff

On a main-repo session, switching branches via the popover does an in-place `git checkout` on the **shared** main repo, affecting every other main-repo session on that project. That's inherent to git; the chip labels the context so it's not surprising.

## Verification

- MainToolbar + SessionRowMeta suites: **35/35 pass**; UI typecheck clean; ESLint clean.
- **Driven live** (browser-mode renderer → running daemon, real sessions): confirmed the chip renders neutral for a main-repo session (previously absent) and accent + `WT` for a worktree session.

## Files

- `packages/ui/src/layout/MainToolbar.tsx` — mount-fetch, `isWorktree` prop, artboard styling, `GitFork`/`GitBranch` glyphs, `WT` badge.
- `packages/ui/src/app/AppShell.tsx` — passes `isWorktree`.
- `packages/ui/src/features/sessions/sidebar/SessionRowMeta.tsx` — worktree pill → `GitFork`.
- `packages/ui/src/layout/__tests__/MainToolbar.test.tsx` — updated suite.
- changeset (patch, `@qlan-ro/mainframe-ui`).

author: johnpc
body:
## What

Album, playlist, artist, and song detail pages now fade in a **Spotify-style ambient gradient** behind their headers, sampled from the cover art's dominant colour.

## How it works

- `dominantColor.ts` (pure) — `averageColor` walks an RGBA byte array (from canvas `getImageData`), skipping transparent / near-white / near-black pixels so the result reflects the artwork's real hue, with a plain-mean fallback; `darken` keeps it legible; `rgbCss` formats it.
- `useDominantColor.ts` — loads the art into a 24×24 off-screen canvas (`crossOrigin` — Jellyfin serves images with CORS `*`, verified) and samples it; returns null until resolved / if the canvas is tainted.
- `GradientHeader.tsx` — wraps a header in the gradient (`linear-gradient(color → transparent)`), falling back to the neutral surface. Applied via `AlbumHeader`, `PlaylistHeader`, a new extracted `ArtistHeader`, and `SongDetail`.

## Tests

- Unit: `averageColor` (mid-tone average, transparent/near-white/near-black skipping, plain-mean + neutral fallbacks), `darken`, `rgbCss`; `useDominantColor` (null src, samples → darkened rgb via stubbed Image+canvas); `GradientHeader` (renders children, null-item fallback)
- Existing album/playlist/artist/song header + detail suites still green

## 1. Full re-sync — drift is now zero

Every imported repo three-way merged (base = recorded import SHA, ours = mono copy preserving your workspace flattening/retargets, theirs = source `origin/main`), one commit per repo:

| Repo | Range | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| finitecomputer-v2 | `862e6bf..0150dd9` | merged clean |
| finitechat | `f13c973..6bde2cc` | 13 commits, ~18k insertions (Electron app, `finitechat-daemon` — added to root members) |
| finite-sites | `768a0b8..a6d03e9` | source's identity rev bump superseded by the workspace path dep |

| finite-identity | `54a6936..0750e8c` | nip98 + authority work |

nostr/search/skills/auth had **zero drift** (the "reverse drift" we feared was stale local checkouts — your import commits were already pushed to the source repos). The procedure is now `scripts/import-sync` + `scripts/import-sync.toml` (provenance manifest) for any pre-archive stray commits.

**Verification on the synced tree:** `cargo fmt --check` ✅ · `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` ✅ · `cargo test --workspace --locked` ✅ (276 tests) · dashboard `npm test` ✅ (101) · **`just dev smoke` full-stack pass** ✅

## 2. infra/ — the single deploy root

Authored from **read-only SSH captures of all prod hosts today**. Inventory corrections worth knowing: no Traefik on lat1 (host Caddy edge, hardcoded ClusterIP); the live finitechat server runs on **clawland-ovh** (the Jul 7 lat1 deploy was rolled back — leftovers documented); real ovh-vps-smoke is **15.204.56.61**; finite-brain is already NixOS-managed by the legacy fleet flow (port 3015; SilverBullet is gone).

- `infra/hosts/{lat1,lat2,smoke,clawland}/` — unit files, Caddyfiles, k8s manifests (moved from component deploy/ dirs, references updated), secrets-by-NAME inventories, captured-state divergence appendices
- `infra/images/` — core/dashboard/private-limiter Dockerfiles, CI-built digest-pinned (**limiter now builds from this repo — split-brain with legacy closed**)
- `infra/tinfoil/` — satellite-repo pin model
- `infra/runbooks/` — release, per-service deploy, **Postgres restore drill**, break-glass; TODO-marked where first execution must validate a step

Real risks found on the boxes (documented, not fixed — read-only mandate): no backups at all on smoke (brain SQLite unprotected) and lat2's newest sites backup sits in tmpfs; brain's :3015 binds the public IP (possible oauth bypass); lat1 pg_dump is a single overwritten file on the same disk as Postgres.

## 3. Root CI + component-scoped releases

- `ci.yml` — fmt/clippy/tests vs real Postgres, dashboard, finitechat Hermes bridge, nix skills/search checks, devfinity smoke (non-blocking until proven on hosted runners). Born green — all gates verified locally first.
- `release-{finitechat,fsite,fbrain}.yml` — tags `finitechat/v*` etc., **identical asset names** (product contract), plus **mirror jobs** publishing the same assets to the legacy repos so field `releases/latest` URLs keep working (needs `RELEASE_MIRROR_TOKEN` secret). fsite also ships `finitesitesd-linux`, fbrain ships the `finite-brain` server binary (gaps found during the runbook pass).
- `service-images.yml` / `runtime-image.yml` / `hermes-runtime-smoke.yml` — the runtime image's three sibling clones collapse to the single checkout SHA. Self-hosted lanes are dispatch-only until a lat2 runner is registered against this repo (`infra/hosts/lat2/runners.md` has the checklist).
- Superseded component `.github/workflows` deleted (they never executed here).

## 4. Doctrine flip + onboarding

`docs/monorepo-doctrine.md` (the constitution), rewritten root AGENTS/README, `CONTRIBUTING.md` (15-minute clone→stack path), `compat/matrix.toml` (field artifacts mono can't see). The old workspace-level "not a monorepo" files were updated on Paul's machine; v2's "do not vendor" rules restated as "use sibling workspace deps, never copy."

## Going public

Paul opted to make the repo public (GHCR images + release URLs all anonymous). Secrets scan before the flip: gitleaks over the **full git history** + targeted greps — 6 findings, all benign (test fixtures, `.env.example` placeholders, a Cargo.lock checksum). The flip happens after this PR is pushed; branch and history both scanned.

## Manual follow-ups (deliberately not in this PR)

1. Register a lat2 self-hosted runner against finite-mono (checklist in `infra/hosts/lat2/runners.md`)
2. Set `RELEASE_MIRROR_TOKEN` org/repo secret (contents:write on the legacy repos)
3. Cut `finitechat/v0.1.3` from mono, verify a field install through the legacy URL — **the acceptance test**; archive source repos only after that
4. First deploys from `infra/` (supervised): core via CI image, sites via release binary; Postgres restore drill
5. clawland→lat1 finitechat-server cutover (SQLite copy + DNS flip) — separately scheduled
6. Smoke-host fixes: enable borg via backup.json in the legacy repo; verify/close the :3015 public bind

author: rjwalters
body:
## Enrichment pass — denumerability-rationals-oq-05

This q94 entry is already saturated (5 fully-populated annotations, correct line anchors on all 8 mainTheorems, complete conclusion, accurate counts). Per the size-guardrail SKIP rule I did **not** inflate it — added exactly **one** sharp, mathematically-verifiable keyInsight that the existing four do not cover.

### What's added
A 5th keyInsight explaining why the boundary value `#(ℕ → ℚ) = 𝔠` is **base-robust**: it holds not because the base is ℚ but because any base κ with 2 ≤ κ ≤ 𝔠 is squeezed by the Cantor–Bernstein sandwich

487022^{\aleph_0} \le \kappa^{\aleph_0} \le (2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0\cdot\aleph_0} = 2^{\aleph_0} = \mathfrak c.48702

So ℕ→ℚ, ℕ→ℤ, ℕ→ℕ, and ℕ→{0,1} all have cardinality 𝔠; `aleph0_power_aleph0` (ℵ₀^ℵ₀ = 𝔠) is one instance of this collapse. The escape from ℵ₀ is driven by the *countably infinite exponent*, not the base — which is precisely why the proof routes through `aleph0_power_aleph0`.

### Guardrails
- keyInsights 4 → 5 (cap 12)
- meta.json 14.2 KB → 14.8 KB (cap ~60 KB)
- JSON validated; no content deleted, additive only

author: simply-ministry
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [security improvement] Harden OtisTerminal against DoS and UI injection

### 🚨 Severity
MEDIUM

### 💡 Vulnerability
The `OtisTerminal` component lacked resource limits on command history and terminal output, potentially leading to memory exhaustion (DoS). Additionally, the Rich Text sanitization was incomplete (missing `&` escaping), and untrusted user input was echoed directly in the "Unknown command" error message.

### 🎯 Impact
- **Denial of Service:** Maliciously large command histories or terminal logs could degrade performance or crash the application.
- **UI Injection:** Attackers could use Rich Text tags or HTML entities to disrupt the terminal UI or spoof system messages.

### 🔧 Fix
- Implemented strict limits on history and output length with efficient trimming.
- Transitioned to a `StringBuilder` buffer for zero-allocation UI updates via `SetText(StringBuilder)`.
- Enhanced `AppendSanitized` to cover ampersands.
- Sanitized echoes in `GetUnknownCommandText`.

### ✅ Verification
- Ran `dotnet build OtisTerminal.csproj` to confirm build integrity.
- Ran `python3 validate_implementation.py` to ensure core data and file structure remain intact.
- Verified that all interactive UI paths in `OtisTerminal.cs` now flow through the hardened `_terminalBuffer` and sanitization pipeline.

author: ahwrist
body:
Implements ADR-0006. This is PR C: it migrates the relevance gold set's label schema to two independent axes and hardens the harness that guards it.

## What changed

**`evals/relevance_labels.yaml` → `relevance-labels-v2`**
- Every trace gains `request_fidelity` (`faithful | unfaithful | not_observed | unsure`) and `boundary_handling` (`honest | evaded | not_applicable | unsure`).
- `relevance` is retained but is now a derived value: `unsure` if either axis is unsure, else `not_relevant` if the request is `unfaithful` or the boundary was `evaded`, else `relevant`. The harness enforces the derivation.
- `should_have_been` widens from a bare request-or-`unanswerable` sentinel to a `{request?, expect}` object mirroring an intent case minus its question, so a correction can name a denied honest outcome.

**Two verdicts reconciled to their intent keys** (both were already correct in `relevance_intents.yaml`; only the labels were behind):
- `net-revenue-over-time`: `not_relevant` (unfaithful, evaded); corrects to the honest `net_revenue`-by-month request denied `dimension_not_allowed`.
- `customer-count`: `not_relevant` (unfaithful, not_applicable); corrects to the `customer_count` request denied `unknown_metric`.

**`tests/agent/test_relevance_gold_set.py`** gains three checks:
1. each derived `relevance` matches the rule over its axes;
2. each correction replays to its declared `expect` (denials included), replayed under the intent key's caller so `customer-count`'s empty-caller trace still reaches `unknown_metric`;
3. each correction equals the intent key for its `bank_id`.

The correction and intent replays now share one engine.

## Ordering note

The widened corrections include denied honest requests that the old harness (which asserted corrections admit) would reject. So the data migration and the harness update land in a single atomic commit; splitting data-first would leave the tree red.

## Not changed

`evals/relevance_intents.yaml` is untouched.

## Gate

`uv run ruff format --check . && uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` → all green (256 passed, 1 skipped).

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Proposed commit message

Fix a race condition between Filebeat.Run and Filebeat.Stop where Stop could close the done channel before Run had reached the point of waiting on it. This was observable when Filebeat is embedded in the OTel collector, which may call Shutdown before the beater's Run goroutine has finished initializing its shutdown-signal machinery.

What changed

- Added an atomic.Bool running flag on Filebeat.
- Run sets running = true immediately before entering waitFinished.Wait(), signaling that the done channel is now wired up and safe to close.
- Stop polls running for up to 5 seconds (50 × 100ms) before proceeding to close(fb.done). If Run has not started within that window, Stop proceeds anyway to avoid hanging the shutdown path indefinitely.
- New unit test TestStopWaitsForRunReady in filebeat/beater/stop_test.go verifies that Stop blocks until running is set, then completes promptly.

## Checklist

- [ ] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation

- **New Project** now clears undo/redo stacks.
- Fix **chamfer/fillet view crash** and zoom corruption after sketch extrude + view-cube navigation.
- Refresh bundled **`res/ezycad_settings.json`** defaults (layout, theme, grid, dimensions, snap colors).

## Add node fixes

| Bug | Fix |
|-----|-----|
| Escape during distance input still added node | `hide_dist_edit(false)` / `hide_angle_edit(false)` on Escape; route Escape to `on_key` while dist edit is focused |
| Undo empty after anchor + distance/click | Open `Sketch_op_recorder` before `add_new_node` / `get_node_exact` in rubber-band commit paths |
| Redo did not restore placed nodes | `restore_curr_node_at_pt_()` in `Sketch_delta::apply_forward_` |
| Length dimension tool ignored Origin | Remove hard `origin` exclusion from `try_pick_existing_node` |

## Circle / arc undo-redo fix

**Repro:** create a circle (center + radius click), undo, redo — debug pane showed **4 edges** and **3 extra permanent nodes** instead of the original **2 edges**.

**Root cause:** on redo, `restore_curr_node_at_pt_()` revived stencil/bulge nodes from `curr_arc_edges` and then called `split_arcs_at_node_if_interior`, splitting each semicircle in half. Bulge nodes were also revived with `get_node_exact(pt, true)`, promoting them to permanent.

**Fix:** in `restore_curr_node_at_pt_()`, treat nodes matching arc-defining points (`pt_a` / `pt_b` / `pt_c` in `curr_arc_edges`) specially:
- **Bulge (`pt_b`)**: revive without making permanent; skip interior splits.
- **Endpoints (`pt_a` / `pt_c`)**: revive without making permanent (split is already a no-op at endpoints).
- **Add-node placements** (not arc-defining): unchanged — revive as permanent and re-run interior splits.

## View / chamfer fix

Repro: new project, rotate view, view cube **Top** (zoom to origin), zoom out, draw square, extrude, chamfer, then rotate/zoom — view jumped to empty space and `FlushViewEvents` crashed with `Standard_ProgramError`.

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Stale selection/highlight on removed solid after chamfer/fillet | `replace_picked_shape_()`: clear hover/selection, `Unhilight`, remove old shape, `Display` replacement |
| Orthographic sketch extrude -> perspective chamfer corrupted zoom | `apply_camera_projection()` runs at start of `on_mode()` (before shape show/redisplay) |
| Projection switch reset camera scale/distance | Preserve eye-center distance and view scale when toggling ortho/perspective |
| Residual OCCT failures during navigation | Defensive `try/catch` in `flush_view_events()` clears selection/hover and aborts view animation |

| Platform | Path |
|----------|------|
| Windows (live) | `%APPDATA%\EzyCad\ezycad_settings.json` |
| Bundled defaults | `res/ezycad_settings.json` |
| Linux | `~/.config/EzyCad/ezycad_settings.json` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/EzyCad/ezycad_settings.json` |

author: leofang
body:
## Summary

Add `concurrency_limit` to `WorkqueueResourceOptions`, so the user-facing options for `WorkqueueResource.configure()` mirror the driver's user-writable fields on the workqueue config (`sharing_scope` + `concurrency_limit`).

Also fixes `WorkqueueResource.configure()` where the `sharing_scope is None` early return silently dropped any other option that might be set, and moves both `sharing_scope` and `concurrency_limit` validation to `WorkqueueResourceOptions.__post_init__` so bad options fail at construction and are caught on any build (not just CUDA 13.x).

Following the "no speculative sugar" principle, no query-side property is added — `configure()` is the only user-facing setter, symmetric with how `sharing_scope` works today.

## Semantics

An input hint to the driver — "expected maximum number of concurrent stream-ordered workloads" — bounded in practice by `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS` (see [CUDA docs](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/environment-variables.html#cuda-device-max-connections)). Values `>= 1` accepted; per the [green contexts docs](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/green-contexts.html), configurations may exceed the driver-reported cap at the cost of the non-overlap guarantee, so no upper cap is enforced.

## Test coverage

Extended `TestWorkqueueResource` in `test_green_context.py`:
- `configure(concurrency_limit=N)` accepted on valid values
- combined `sharing_scope` + `concurrency_limit` in one `configure()` call
- `WorkqueueResourceOptions(concurrency_limit=0)` and negative values raise `ValueError` at construction
- `WorkqueueResourceOptions(sharing_scope="bogus")` raises `ValueError` at construction (was: at `configure()`)

Extended `TestGreenContextKernelLaunch::test_with_workqueue_resource` to configure the workqueue with both `sharing_scope="green_ctx_balanced"` and `concurrency_limit=4` before green ctx creation + kernel launch, so the end-to-end path is exercised.

Full `test_green_context.py` locally: 35 passed, 2 skipped (arch), zero regressions.

Release notes entry added under 1.1.0 "New features".

Related: #1976 (green context support).

-- Leo's bot

author: nkeleher
body:
# Pull Request Summary 🚀

## What does this PR do? 📝

Hardens the GitHub Actions workflows (release + coverage) following the recommendations in [How to publish to PyPI using GitHub Actions securely](https://snarky.ca/how-to-publish-to-pypi-using-github-actions-securely/), verified with [zizmor](https://docs.zizmor.sh/). `uvx zizmor .github/workflows/` now reports **zero findings** (previously 30+, including several errors).

- Pin all `uses:` action references to full commit SHAs (with version comments; Dependabot keeps them current)
- Fix two template-injection sites in `release.yml` by passing `${{ }}` expressions through `env:` instead of interpolating into `run:` scripts
- Disable the uv cache throughout the release path so a poisoned cache cannot influence published artifacts
- Tighten permissions: `permissions: {}` at the workflow level with per-job grants; add `contents: read` to `coverage.yml`
- Set `persist-credentials: false` on all checkouts
- Replace `softprops/action-gh-release` with a plain `gh release create` step, removing a third-party action from the release path
- Add the official zizmor pre-commit hook (runs locally and in CI via the existing pre-commit jobs)
- Add a 7-day Dependabot cooldown on all ecosystems so freshly compromised upstream releases are likely caught before being proposed here
- Document all of this in a new "Release security" section in CONTRIBUTING.md

## Why is this change needed? 🤔

The release pipeline publishes to PyPI, making it a supply-chain target. The big-ticket protections were already in place (Trusted Publishing via OIDC, separate build/publish jobs, GitHub environments, scoped `id-token: write`), but a zizmor audit surfaced remaining gaps: unpinned actions, template injection, cache poisoning exposure, missing permission blocks, and credential persistence. This PR closes them and adds continuous enforcement so they stay closed.

## How was this implemented? 🛠️

Ran `uvx zizmor .github/workflows/` and fixed every finding. Tag SHAs were resolved via the GitHub API and pinned as `<full-sha> # vX.Y.Z` so Dependabot can continue updating them. The zizmor pre-commit hook was added to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, which both CI workflows already run — no new CI job needed. The hook also audits `dependabot.yml`, which prompted the cooldown additions.

Two follow-ups require repo settings (not enforceable in code, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md):

- Add **required reviewers** to the `pypi` environment (Settings → Environments → pypi) so final releases need a manual approval even after a tag push
- Optionally enable **"Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"** (Settings → Actions → General)

## How to test or reproduce ? 🧪

1. `uvx zizmor .github/workflows/` → no findings, exit 0
2. `uv tool run pre-commit run --all-files` → all hooks pass, including the new `zizmor` hook
3. End-to-end: the next pre-release tag (e.g. `vX.Y.Zrc1`) exercises the full pipeline against Test PyPI, including the reworked `gh release create` step on the following final release

author: kaisong1990
body:
## Summary

Fixes ADO 3236668: https://dev.azure.com/IdentityDivision/_workitems/edit/3236668

`+[MSIDXpcSingleSignOnProvider canPerformRequest:]` has 5 distinct exit points that all collapse into a bare `NO`, making it impossible to root-cause the production spike of this client-side XPC gate rejecting requests without further instrumentation. This PR adds an additive, non-breaking `reason:` overload that reports which branch fired — at both the provider level and the controller level, since production callers (e.g. OneAuth's `MSAIBrokerClient`) call the controller's bare `canPerformRequest` class method directly and never see CommonCore's internal `MSID_LOG_WITH_CTX` output.

## Changes

- **New enum `MSIDXpcCanPerformFailureReason`** (`MSIDXpcSingleSignOnProvider.h`), with one case per failure branch:
  - `None` (success)
  - `NoProviderInstalled` — no MacBrokerApp/CompanyPortal XPC component on device
  - `DeviceInfoRequestCreationFailed` — SSOExtension `getDeviceInfo` request object failed to construct
  - `DeviceInfoHandshakeError` — handshake completed with a hard error
  - `DeviceInfoHandshakeTimeout` — handshake did not complete within the 1s `dispatch_group_wait` window
  - `ValidateCacheProviderFailed` — no installed provider matches cached/available config
  - `UnsupportedOSVersion` — controller-level gate rejects the request on macOS < 13, before ever reaching the provider
- **New `MSIDXpcCanPerformFailureReasonToString(reason)`** helper for non-PII logging.
- **New `+[MSIDXpcSingleSignOnProvider canPerformRequest:reason:]`** overload that sets `*reason` at each return site. The original no-`reason` `canPerformRequest:` selector is kept as a thin wrapper (`reason:nil`) — fully source/behavior compatible with existing call sites and tests.
- **Split timeout vs. hard-error**: both previously fell through to the same generic `validateCacheXpcProvider` failure; they're now tracked separately and reported as distinct reasons (timeout takes priority if both occurred).
- **Updated both callers** — `MSIDXpcSilentTokenRequestController` and `MSIDXpcInteractiveTokenRequestController` `canPerformRequest` — to call the new overload and log the reason (name + int, no PII) via `MSID_LOG_WITH_CTX` when the result is `NO`.
- **New `+[MSIDXpcSilentTokenRequestController canPerformRequest:]`** and **`+[MSIDXpcInteractiveTokenRequestController canPerformRequest:]`** overloads (reason out-param), mirroring the provider-level pattern, so external callers outside CommonCore (e.g. OneAuth) can retrieve and surface the failure reason to their own telemetry instead of only getting a bare `BOOL`. The existing no-arg `canPerformRequest` selectors remain thin wrappers (`canPerformRequest:nil`) — fully source/behavior compatible.
- **Unit tests**: added coverage in `MSIDXpcSingleSignOnProviderTest.m` for all 5 provider-level failure branches and the success path.
- **Changelog**: added/updated an entry under `TBD`.

## Testing

Ran `./build.py --targets mac_library --no-xcpretty --no-clean`:
- Build succeeded.
- All 2496 tests passed (0 failures).

## Notes

- No PII is logged — only the reason enum name/int and class/method name.
- No behavior change for existing callers of any no-`reason` selector (provider or controller level).
- Adoption in OneAuth (`MSAIBrokerClient.m`) to actually consume the new controller-level `reason:` overload and feed it into OneAuth's own telemetry (`MSAIBrokerEligibilityResponseFactory` / `appendExecutionFlow:`) is tracked separately, since that's a different repo/consumer.

author: rtanglao
body:
## Why

On 2026-07-06 the hourly refresh entered a **death spiral**: one run exceeded the CI `timeout-minutes` cap → it was cancelled before `actions/cache/save` → the high-water mark froze → every later run's `updated` window grew ~1h/hour → more days to re-scrape → more of the API's new **HTTP 429s (~12–14 min `Retry-After`)** → cancelled again, forever. The mark advanced **only** on a fully clean run, so a single slow run poisoned all future ones. (The gap data was backfilled separately and the stuck caches cleared; this PR prevents recurrence.)

## What

Graceful **deferral** + **durable partial watermark** so a slow/rate-limited/cut-off run advances the mark over whatever finished and retries only the rest next run — the spiral becomes structurally impossible. (Literally extending `timeout-minutes` per-429 isn't possible: it's static and hourly `cancel-in-progress` caps every run <60 min.)

- **sumo.py** — `RateLimitDeferral` + `DEFERRAL_EXIT_CODE=75`; `SumoBrowser(max_429_wait_s=…)` → `fetch_json` raises instead of sleeping when a 429 demands longer than the threshold. **Off by default** (waits in full).
- **scrape_questions.py / scrape_answers.py** — `--max-429-wait`; on deferral exit 75 **without touching the CSV**. Writes are now **atomic** (tmp + `os.replace`) to survive a hard kill mid-write.
- **find_updated_days.py** — returns `{(slug, day): earliest_updated_dt}` (was a bare pair list) so the mark can be held just below an unapplied change. Iterating keys still yields `(slug, day)`, so callers are unaffected.
- **run_refresh.py** — `--soft-deadline` + `--max-429-wait`; per-day completion tracking; `compute_new_hwm` holds the mark just below the earliest deferred/failed change, else advances fully to `now`. Discovery deferral leaves the mark unchanged.
- **scrape.yml** — incremental run uses `--soft-deadline 40 --max-429-wait 120`; `timeout-minutes` 50 → 55 (backstop above the soft deadline).
- **CLAUDE.md** — documents the mechanism.

## Correctness

`compute_new_hwm` never advances past an unapplied change and always advances over completed ones; re-scrape is idempotent so overlap is harmless. Unit-tested `compute_new_hwm` (advance-fully / hold-below-earliest / cap-at-now) and the `find_updated_days` aggregation, including an **answer edit predating its question's `updated`** correctly lowering that day's floor.

Deferral is opt-in, so manual backfills / explicit-range refreshes still wait in full.

## Problema

Abrir **Temporada** o **Directorio** por primera vez se sentía lento. Causa: la temporada actual encadenaba hasta **11 requests a AniList en serie** (4 páginas de temporada → 3 de "en emisión" → hasta 4 del horario de episodios) = varios segundos de skeleton. Y ambos caches eran solo en memoria: cada recarga de la página volvía a esperar todo.

## Qué cambia

1. **Paralelización** (`anilistService`): la página 1 se pide primero (para saber si hay más) y las restantes salen **todas en paralelo**; la temporada y los "en emisión" también se piden **a la vez**. Peor caso: ~4 round-trips en lugar de 11 (~3× más rápido en frío). Si una página extra falla, se sigue con las demás en vez de perder todo.
2. **Cache persistente en localStorage**: la temporada vigente (`anitracker-season-cache`, TTL 15 min — alineado con la frescura de "hace X horas") y la primera página del Directorio por combinación de filtros (`anitracker-directory-cache`, TTL 30 min). Entre sesiones las pestañas pintan al instante, sin red.
3. **Precarga en segundo plano**: a los 2 s de abrir la app se precalientan Temporada y Directorio, así el primer clic ya encuentra los datos (o la precarga en vuelo). `useDiscovery` ganó dedupe de fetches en vuelo para que el clic durante la precarga no dispare una tanda duplicada, y `loadInitial` del Directorio ya era idempotente.

## Verificación

- `npm run test`: 169 tests pasan (6 nuevos: paginación paralela, tolerancia a página caída, corte en página 1, cache persistente de Directorio y de Temporada, dedupe de in-flight).
- `npm run lint` limpio y `npm run build` OK.
- Playwright contra el build de producción con latencia simulada de 250 ms/request: la precarga dispara ambas pestañas sola; temporada y "en emisión" salen con Δ=0 ms y las páginas 2-4 en paralelo; abrir Temporada tras la precarga tarda ~430 ms y Directorio ~75 ms (sin red); tras recargar, Temporada abre del cache persistente con **cero requests nuevas**.

## Summary
- Harden row-L1 normalization config coercion so non-mapping configs and unknown mapping keys raise controlled `ValueError`s.
- Match the validation behavior already used by the row-L∞ helper.

## Rationale
`normalize_train_test_rows_l1(config=...)` previously passed arbitrary mappings through `row_l1_config(**dict(config))`. A misspelled key escaped as a raw Python `TypeError` instead of a stable user-facing validation error, and non-mapping objects were not normalized through a clear public API error. This made row-L1 less robust than the analogous row-L∞ helper.

author: florianpfaff
body:
## Summary
- reject NumPy `datetime64` / `timedelta64` scalar controls before covariance-helper numeric coercion
- reuse the existing unsupported numeric-value guard for scalar finite and integer validators
- add focused regressions for temporal `atol`, `min_eigenvalue`, `initial_jitter`, `max_attempts`, and `dim`

## Bug fixed
`np.datetime64[ns]` and `np.timedelta64[ns]` scalar values can expose their internal nanosecond payloads through NumPy scalar conversion. In `pyrecest.numerics`, that meant malformed temporal controls could be silently interpreted as ordinary numeric tolerances, jitters, retry counts, or dimensions. For example, `np.timedelta64(2, "ns")` could pass as `dim=2` or `max_attempts=2`, while `np.datetime64(..., "ns")` could pass as a finite `atol`.

The patch blocks temporal scalar arrays and object-wrapped temporal scalars before `.item()` / numeric conversion, matching the module's existing matrix-value validation policy.

## Validation
- `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pyrecest_patch/src python -m py_compile /tmp/pyrecest_patch/src/pyrecest/numerics.py /tmp/pyrecest_patch/tests/test_numerics_temporal_scalar_controls.py`
- `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/pyrecest_patch/src pytest -q /tmp/pyrecest_patch/tests/test_numerics_temporal_scalar_controls.py` → `6 passed`
- GitHub compare: branch changes only `src/pyrecest/numerics.py` and `tests/test_numerics_temporal_scalar_controls.py`.
